title: CR-A6: Fix ORIS SRAA path reporting unconstrained pre-clamp max_error (false convergence)
description:
# CR-A6: Fix ORIS SRAA path reporting unconstrained pre-clamp max_error (false convergence)
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Make the ORIS SRAA (`accelerate=TRUE`) path report `res.base.max_error` (and the other cell metrics) consistent with the RETURNED, capacity-clamped weights — mirroring the honest non-SRAA path — so a tight/infeasible-bounds run no longer reports `status=0, max_error≈2e-16` while returning weights that miss margins by ~35%. In scope: `src/oris.cpp` SRAA branch final-metric assignment (the level-exit region after the mass-preserving clamp ~line 1067) and/or the post-homotopy-loop finalize (~after line 2019). Out of scope: the mass-preserving clamp math itself (verified correct); the ALM Newton step formula (forbidden).
* **Why:** On the SRAA path `res.base.max_error = r.err_rp` (oris.cpp:877) is the UNCONSTRAINED per-step errRp from `f_eval_lf` (the SRAA log/linear sweep applies NO capacity — capacity is enforced ONCE by the mass-preserving clamp at oris.cpp:1039-1070). After that clamp writes capacity-limited masses into `X`, the SRAA path NEVER recomputes the reported metrics on the clamped `X`. The non-SRAA flat-BCD path DOES recompute per-iteration (compute_cell_metrics at oris.cpp:1863 on the live capacity-respecting `X`), so it honestly reports the constrained residual. Net effect measured (forced log path, seed=99, n=1000, 3 margins, min_weight=0.5): `accelerate=FALSE` → status=0 reported=0.2504 achieved=0.2504 (honest); `accelerate=TRUE` → status=0 reported=2.220e-16 achieved=0.3496 (DISHONEST — claims machine-precision convergence on an infeasible problem). A user reads `max_error=2e-16` and believes calibration succeeded when it silently failed. Confidence 92 (empirically disambiguated: non-SRAA path is honest on the same fixture, so this is SRAA-specific, not a tight-bounds/clamp artifact).
* **Reference Data:** Discovered 2026-07-03 during mxcl.4 execution. RED fixture (forced log, but repro also on the natural-dispatch path when M_cell/n selects log): set.seed(99); n=1000; x~c(H .7,L .3), y~c(P .3,Q .7), z~c(M .5,N .3,O .2); targets x(H .4,L .6) y(P .7,Q .3) z(M .4,N .35,O .25); harvest(method="oris", accelerate=TRUE, min_weight=0.5, max_weight in {1.2,1.5,2.0}, max_iterations=500). Env `LBW_ORIS_FORCE_PATH=log` forces the log path (oris.cpp:145). ENTANGLED with mxcl.4 (stale X_cur re-sync) and a `res$kl==0`-always reporting gap on the SRAA path — see mxcl.4 Amendment B.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `src/oris.cpp` (SRAA branch 851-1071, esp. the r.err_rp assignment at 877 and the clamp at 1039-1070; the post-homotopy-loop finalize after 2019 where obs-expansion + best_weights + any final metric write happen — READ it to determine whether to recompute at level-exit or at finalize). The non-SRAA recompute at 1853-1863 is the honesty reference to mirror.
* **Format:** C++ source; testthat R test asserting reported == achieved on the tight-bounds SRAA fixture.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Recompute the 6 cell metrics (`compute_cell_metrics`) on the FINAL capacity-clamped `X` (the masses that produce the returned weights) on the SRAA path and write them to `res.base.{max_error,kl,chi2,mean_error,grake_norm}` — matching the non-SRAA path. Do NOT change the mass-preserving clamp. Do NOT touch the ALM Newton step. Verify the returned weights' achieved margins == the newly-reported `max_error` (rtol tight). Do NOT re-classify status here unless the recomputed metric legitimately changes the convergence rule outcome — if status semantics need change, STOP and file separately (anti-pivot). |
| **Format** | Match existing style; pathspec-form commits `git commit <files> -m "..."`, never `git add -A`; no AI attribution. |
| **Boundary** | `src/oris.cpp` only. Coordinate ordering with mxcl.4 (this fix makes mxcl.4's re-sync observable; land this, then mxcl.4 can be RED-tested). |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Write a failing test first: the tight-bounds SRAA fixture above; assert `abs(achieved_margin_err(returned_w) - res$max_error) < 1e-6` — currently FAILS (reported≈2e-16 vs achieved≈0.35).
2. Read `src/oris.cpp` SRAA branch + the post-2019 finalize; determine the correct single site to recompute metrics on the clamped `X` (level-exit for the final level, or the finalize). Confirm the non-SRAA path (1853-1863) semantics to mirror.
3. Recompute `res.base.*` metrics from the final clamped `X` on the SRAA path.
4. Confirm the RED test now GREEN (reported == achieved). Confirm `accelerate=FALSE` byte-identical (untouched path). Confirm loose-bounds SRAA runs unchanged (reported already == achieved there).
5. `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`, `Rscript -e "devtools::test()"` 0 FAIL, `cd python && pytest` green (rebuild .so via uv; verify symbol landed).
6. Stepstone benchmark (data present at benchmarks/stepstone_fulldata_bench_data.parquet) — no regression (run oris accelerate=TRUE, compare max_error/marginal_kl/weights vs pre-fix baseline; expect max_error to become HONEST, weights unchanged).
7. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
Sub-agent MUST return:
```toon

success: bool
data:
  files_changed: [list]
  tests_run: [commands + results]
  verification: [tight-bounds reported-vs-achieved before/after; accelerate=FALSE byte-identical; stepstone weights unchanged + max_error honest]
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . succeeds
- [ ] Rscript -e "devtools::test()" 0 FAIL
- [ ] cd python && pytest — parity green
- [ ] Tight-bounds SRAA fixture: reported max_error == achieved-from-returned-weights (was 2e-16 vs 0.35); accelerate=FALSE untouched; stepstone weights unchanged with honest max_error; no regression
close_reason: SRAA max_error recomputed on final clamped weights (honest); false status=0/2e-16 convergence on infeasible fixed. RED 0.262 -> GREEN 2.8e-16. R 746/0, Py 50, stepstone honest+weight-neutral. Commit 6036171.

title: CR-E2: Validate calibrate() container sizes vs K before C call
description:
# CR-E2: Validate calibrate() container sizes vs K before C call
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add Python-side length validation for the per-margin containers passed into the `calibrate()` C call so malformed input raises a Python exception instead of causing out-of-bounds reads/undefined behavior.
* **Why:** `_bindings.cpp:49-63` indexes `group_ids_list[k]` and dereferences `targets_list[k].data()` without checking these lists have length `K`, and without checking each `targets_list[k]` has length equal to its corresponding `cat_counts_list[k]`. This is directly reachable from Python (not just internal C++ callers) and exercised raw in `test_python.py:6,14`.
* **Reference Data:** `_bindings.cpp:49-63`: `group_ids_list[k]`, `tgt_ptrs[k] = targets_list[k].data()` unchecked against list length; `targets_list[k].size()` unchecked vs `cat_counts_list[k]` → OOB/UB/segfault from Python, no exception raised. Element-LENGTH of `group_ids` IS checked at `_bindings.cpp:54` — the gap in checking `k`-th list existence and per-margin target length is accidental, not by design.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `python/leafblower/_bindings.cpp` (the `calibrate` pybind11 wrapper, lines ~40-70), `python/leafblower/test_python.py` (existing raw-call test harness at lines 6, 14).
* **Format:** C++ (pybind11).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Check ALL THREE: `len(group_ids_list) == K`, `len(targets_list) == K`, `len(cat_counts_list) == K`; AND for each `k`, `len(targets_list[k]) == cat_counts_list[k]`. Raise before any pointer is taken/dereferenced. |
| **Format** | Use `py::value_error` with the specific parameter name and index in the message (match existing pybind11 error-raising style in the file — check ndim/size checks nearby for the established idiom). |
| **Boundary** | `python/leafblower/_bindings.cpp` only; add corresponding negative test(s) to `python/leafblower/test_python.py` or the appropriate parity test file — do not touch `_harvest.py` or C++ core (`src/`). |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read `_bindings.cpp` lines 40-70 in full to see the existing (partial) `group_ids` element-length check at line 54 and match its style.
2. Add a check that `group_ids_list`, `targets_list`, and `cat_counts_list` (or whatever the K-length containers are actually named — confirm from source) each have length `K` before any per-`k` indexing occurs.
3. Add a per-`k` loop check that `targets_list[k].size() == cat_counts_list[k]` before `tgt_ptrs[k] = targets_list[k].data()` is taken.
4. Raise `py::value_error` naming the offending parameter and index (e.g. `f"targets_list[{k}] has length {len} but cat_counts_list[{k}] expects {expected}"`).
5. Write a TDD test in the appropriate test file asserting these malformed inputs raise `ValueError` (not segfault, not silent corruption) — cover: wrong-length `group_ids_list`, wrong-length `targets_list`, and per-`k` target/cat_counts mismatch as 3 separate cases.
6. Run the existing `test_python.py:6,14` raw-call tests to confirm no regression on valid inputs.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
Sub-agent MUST return:
```toon
task_id: CR-E2
success: bool
data:
  files_changed: [list]
  tests_run: [commands + results]
  verification: [proof]
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] `cd python && pip install -e .` succeeds (clean rebuild — `rm -rf build` caches per stale-.so gotcha; verify symbol via `strings` on built `.so` where new keys added)
- [ ] pytest green (`python/leafblower/test_*.py`)
- [ ] R parity unchanged where applicable (no C API surface change, Python-layer validation only)
- [ ] New negative tests assert `ValueError` (not segfault) for all 3 malformed-input cases: mismatched K-length lists, per-margin target/cat_counts length mismatch, and confirm valid inputs still pass unmodified
close_reason: calibrate() pybind wrapper now validates group_ids/cat_counts/targets list lengths ==K + per-margin targets[k]==cat_counts[k] before any pointer taken (commit 53025be). RED: short group_ids/targets SIGSEGV(139), target/catcount mismatch silent OOB(status=2); post-fix all raise ValueError. 4 tests; Python 63 pass. Python-layer only, no C/R change.

title: CR-E1: Make lbw_config.h hermetic for the Python build
description:
# CR-E1: Make lbw_config.h hermetic for the Python build
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Make `pip install -e .` from a clean clone succeed without ever invoking R's `./configure`, by having CMake generate its own `lbw_config.h` into the build directory instead of relying on a gitignored, R-generated header.
* **Why:** Python build currently depends on an artifact only R's `./configure` produces; when absent, the build fails outright, and when present from a prior R build on a different machine, the `.so` silently inherits wrong feature flags (cross-machine ABI/perf drift).
* **Reference Data:** `python/CMakeLists.txt` includes `src/*.hpp` files that `#include "lbw_config.h"` (`greenkhorn.hpp:3`, `sraa.hpp:5`, `lbw_math.hpp:2`); `src/.gitignore:1` ignores `lbw_config.h`; only R's `./configure` generates it. Clean clone → `pip install -e .` fails with `lbw_config.h: No such file or directory`. When a stale header from a prior R build is present: `.so` silently inherits R-toolchain flags — e.g. `LBW_HAS_GLIBC_MVEC=0` from another machine disables the AVX2 `exp` path that `python/CMakeLists.txt:48-50` provisions `-mavx2` for; `LBW_HAS_OMP=1` in a config compiled with no OpenMP flags present causes mismatched assumptions.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `python/CMakeLists.txt`, `configure` (the R autoconf script, to enumerate which feature macros it detects and writes into `lbw_config.h.in`/`lbw_config.h`), `src/greenkhorn.hpp`, `src/sraa.hpp`, `src/lbw_math.hpp` (consumers of the header).
* **Format:** CMake (`configure_file` + `check_cxx_source_compiles` feature probes).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | CMake must generate `lbw_config.h` into the CMake *build* directory (never into `src/`), prepended to the include path so it is found before any stale committed/leftover copy. Probe for the SAME macro set `./configure` detects — read `configure` first to enumerate exact macro names (e.g. `LBW_HAS_GLIBC_MVEC`, `LBW_HAS_OMP`) rather than guessing. |
| **Format** | Never commit a generated header. R build path (`configure` → `src/lbw_config.h` via Makevars) must remain byte-for-byte unchanged — do not touch `configure` or `Makevars.in` logic, only read them. |
| **Boundary** | `python/CMakeLists.txt` only (plus a new `python/*.h.in` template if needed). Do not modify `src/*.hpp`, `configure`, `Makevars.in`, or any R-side build file. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read `configure` (and `src/lbw_config.h.in` if one exists) to enumerate every macro name it writes (expect at least `LBW_HAS_GLIBC_MVEC`, `LBW_HAS_OMP`, and any others feeding `#ifdef`/`#if` guards in `greenkhorn.hpp`, `sraa.hpp`, `lbw_math.hpp`).
2. In `python/CMakeLists.txt`, add `check_cxx_source_compiles` (or `check_symbol_exists`) probes reproducing each macro's actual detection logic used by `configure` (glibc vector-math symbol presence, OpenMP `find_package`, etc.) — do not just hardcode `1`.
3. Add a `configure_file()` step to write `lbw_config.h` into `${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}` (or a scoped subdir) from a new template.
4. Prepend that directory to `target_include_directories` for the extension target, ahead of `src/`.
5. Verify `rm -f src/lbw_config.h && cd python && rm -rf build **/*.so && pip install -e .` succeeds from a clean state with no R `configure` ever run.
6. Confirm via `strings`/`objdump` on the built `.so` (or a `-E` preprocessor dump) that the AVX2/OMP-dependent code paths reflect flags the CMake probes actually detected on the build machine, not stale/inherited values.
7. Confirm R build path unaffected: `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` still runs `./configure` and produces `src/lbw_config.h` as before.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
Sub-agent MUST return:
```toon
task_id: CR-E1
success: bool
data:
  files_changed: [list]
  tests_run: [commands + results]
  verification: [proof]
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] `rm src/lbw_config.h && cd python && pip install -e .` succeeds (clean rebuild — `rm -rf build` and any cached `.so` per stale-.so gotcha)
- [ ] pytest green (`python/leafblower/test_*.py`)
- [ ] R parity unchanged — `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` still generates its own `src/lbw_config.h` via `./configure`, untouched logic
- [ ] Flags baked into the built `.so` match what CMake's own probes detected on the build machine (strings/objdump evidence attached), not a stale inherited value from a prior R build
close_reason: Python build now generates hermetic lbw_config.h via CMake feature probes (commit d80dd15). Clean-clone pip install -e . succeeds (was: header-not-found); GLIBC_MVEC probed+baked (_ZGVdN4v_exp in .so); stale-header override proven via -include; R CMD INSTALL still regenerates identical header via configure. 63 pytest pass.

title: CR-A5: Add cross-solver returned-weights≡reported-metrics regression gate
description:
# CR-A5: Add cross-solver returned-weights≡reported-metrics regression gate
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add a new testthat test (+ Python mirror) that, for EVERY calibration method, independently recomputes max_error/kl/chi2 from the RETURNED weights and asserts they match the reported result fields — a gate that would have caught CR-A1, CR-A2, and CR-A4. In scope: new test file(s) only. Out of scope: fixing any solver — this is a detection gate, not a fix.
* **Why:** The three Blocking defects in this epic (Cholesky triangle mismatch, chebyshev warm-start pairing, ORIS SRAA stale-iterate) all share one root symptom: the weights returned to the caller do not actually realize the metrics reported in the result struct. No existing test independently re-derives metrics from returned weights across all solvers — each solver's test suite trusts its own self-reported numbers. This ticket closes that structural gap permanently.
* **Reference Data:** Methods to cover: raking, sinkhorn, greenkhorn, logit, greg, chebyshev, newton_kl, oris, oris_soft, auto. Depends on CR-A2 (chebyshev fix) — until CR-A2 lands, the chebyshev case is expected to be RED; use `skip()`-with-reference-comment or `testthat::expect_failure()` explicitly linking the CR-A2 ticket ID, not a silent skip. Confidence: 90 (test design is straightforward; exact tolerance-per-method requires reading `finalize_weights` bounds-adjustment behavior in `calib_dispatch.hpp`, which the sub-agent must do before writing tolerances).
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` (`finalize_weights`/`finalize_weights_buf` — for understanding what bounds-adjustment slack is legitimate per bounds_mode), a mid-size fixture usable across all 10 methods (check `tests/testthat/fixtures/` for an existing multi-method fixture or construct one), the R public API surface (`R/harvest.R`) for how to invoke each method uniformly, `python/leafblower/ (test_*_parity.py files — NOTE: python/parity/ is an empty stale dir; the real parity-test pattern home is python/leafblower/test_solver_parity.py et al.)` for the mirror-test pattern to follow.
* **Format:** New testthat test file (R), new Python parity test file mirroring it.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | The independent re-derivation of max_error/kl/chi2 from returned weights MUST be a fresh R implementation (not calling back into the package's own metric functions) — the point is cross-checking the package's self-report against ground truth, not testing the package against itself. Tolerance must account for legitimate `finalize_weights` bounds adjustments (cell vs. unit bounds_mode) — document the per-method slack explicitly in test comments, derived from reading finalize_weights, not guessed. chebyshev is expected RED until CR-A2 lands — mark with explicit skip/expect_failure referencing CR-A2's ticket ID, not silently. |
| **Format** | Match existing testthat style in the repo; pathspec-form commits `git commit <files> -m "..."`, never `git add -A`; no AI attribution. |
| **Boundary** | New test file(s) only — do not modify any `src/*.cpp` solver code. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read `finalize_weights`/`finalize_weights_buf` in `calib_dispatch.hpp` to determine legitimate per-method bounds-adjustment slack (cell vs. unit bounds_mode).
2. Select or construct a mid-size fixture runnable across all 10 methods (raking, sinkhorn, greenkhorn, logit, greg, chebyshev, newton_kl, oris, oris_soft, auto).
3. Write the R testthat test: for each method, run calibration, independently recompute max_error/kl/chi2 from returned weights via a fresh (non-package) R implementation, assert ≈ reported fields within the documented per-method tolerance.
4. Mark chebyshev as expected-RED via `expect_failure()` or an explicit `skip()` referencing CR-A2, with a comment explaining why.
5. Write the Python parity mirror in `python/leafblower/ (test_*_parity.py files — NOTE: python/parity/ is an empty stale dir; the real parity-test pattern home is python/leafblower/test_solver_parity.py et al.)` following the existing pattern.
6. Run the new tests standalone first to confirm they RED-fail where expected (chebyshev) and PASS elsewhere — this IS the TDD "observe" step since the gate itself is the deliverable.
7. `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`, `Rscript -e "devtools::test()"`, `cd python && pytest`.
8. After creation, run `bd dep add <this-ticket-id> <CR-A2-ticket-id>` to record the dependency.
9. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
Sub-agent MUST return:
```toon

success: bool
data:

  tests_run: [commands + results]
  verification: [per-method tolerance table derived from finalize_weights; chebyshev expected-RED confirmed and linked to CR-A2; all other methods pass]
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . succeeds
- [ ] Rscript -e "devtools::test()" 0 FAIL (chebyshev case explicitly marked expected-failure, not a silent skip)
- [ ] cd python && pytest — parity mirror green (chebyshev case mirrored as expected-failure)

title: CR-A4: Fix ORIS SRAA convergence/best-iterate on stale X_cur
description:
# CR-A4: Fix ORIS SRAA convergence/best-iterate on stale X_cur
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Ensure ORIS's SRAA convergence check and best-iterate tracking evaluate the ACCEPTED iterate, not a stale pre-sweep or rejected-step snapshot. In scope: `src/oris.cpp` `f_eval_lf` log path (~770-796), SRAA convergence/best-iterate check (~957-1004), end-of-level clamp (~1040). Out of scope: the linear (non-log) path's hot per-iteration loop — must remain byte-identical unless explicitly justified.
* **Why:** The `f_eval_lf` log path at `src/oris.cpp:770-796` updates `lf`/`X_tilde` but never updates `X_cur` post-sweep — `X_cur` is only written by `unpack_lf` at line 762, which runs on the PRE-sweep input. Every SRAA convergence/best-iterate check at lines 957-1004 evaluates `X_cur`, meaning it's always one BCD sweep behind `lf_flat`. Separately, after a rejected Anderson-acceleration step, `sraa_step` step 9 has already run `f_eval(X_AA)` — so globals hold `F(X_AA)` while `lf_flat` has been reverted to `F(X_k)`. The convergence check can therefore `mark_converged` on the REJECTED iterate, and the end-of-level clamp at line 1040 (`src_cells = X_cur`) emits that rejected iterate as final output. Additionally, `best.update(...)` uses `w_ratio` derived from `X_cur` while pairing it with `lf_best = lf_flat` (lines 993-1001) — a mismatched (X_cur, lf_flat) pair that feeds the Newton warm-start with inconsistent state.
* **Reference Data:** Confidence: 85 (exact code read at all cited line ranges; the "one sweep behind" and "rejected-step mismatch" mechanisms are directly traced from the log-path code; interaction with Newton warm-start quality is inferred, not independently benchmarked).
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `src/oris.cpp` (full: `unpack_lf` ~762, `f_eval_lf` log path ~770-796, SRAA convergence/best-iterate check ~957-1004, end-of-level clamp ~1040), `src/oris_internal.hpp` (shared state struct definitions for `X_cur`/`lf_flat`/`X_tilde`), any existing `accelerate=TRUE` (log-path) ORIS fixture.
* **Format:** C++ source; testthat R test comparing reported vs. recomputed convergence metrics.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Fix must make the convergence check evaluate the ACCEPTED iterate — either (a) recompute `X_cur` from `lf_flat` (via `unpack`) immediately before the check, or (b) update `X_cur` post-sweep on the log path AND re-sync globals after a rejected AA step. Do NOT add a per-`f_eval` O(M_cell) pass to the hot LINEAR path if avoidable — a check-interval-only re-sync is acceptable and preferred. Do NOT touch the ORIS ALM Newton step formula `X̃(1−λ+μz)/(1+ρ)` — verified correct for the un-normalized-KL generator, forbidden to "fix". |
| **Format** | Match existing style; pathspec-form commits `git commit <files> -m "..."`, never `git add -A`; no AI attribution. |
| **Boundary** | `src/oris.cpp` only (log path + SRAA check + clamp). Linear-path hot loop must be untouched unless the fix is unavoidably shared — if so, justify explicitly in the commit message and DoD. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

2. Read `src/oris.cpp` unpack_lf, f_eval_lf log path, SRAA check, and end-of-level clamp in full; confirm the one-sweep-behind mechanism and the rejected-step mismatch independently.

# CR-A2: Fix chebyshev warm-start expansion pairing — returns ≈design weights
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Fix `src/chebyshev.cpp` so the returned observation-level weights actually realize the reported calibrated cell masses `X_out`, on the (default, unconditional) warm-start path used by both R and Python. In scope: `chebyshev.cpp` warm-start swap (~line 115) and exit-expansion (~lines 727-731). Out of scope: the metrics computation at lines 713-718 (already correct given a correct `X_out`).
* **Why:** `src/chebyshev.cpp:115` `X_warm.swap(X_init)` replaces `X_init` (design aggregates from `solver_setup_ct`: `X_init[c] = Σ_{i∈c} st.weights[i]`) with clamped warm ORIS masses, but `st.weights` (the per-observation weights) remain the ORIGINAL design weights — they are never updated to match the warm start. At exit, `src/chebyshev.cpp:727-731` computes `mult = X_out[c] / X_init[c]` and does `st.weights[i] *= mult`. Since `X_init` now holds warm masses (not design masses) while `st.weights` still holds design-weight values, the returned cell mass is `X_design · X_out / X_warm ≠ X_out`. With a good warm start `mult ≈ 1`, so the returned weights are approximately the UNCALIBRATED design weights, while the metrics at lines 713-718 are computed from `X_out` and report calibrated quality — a silent mismatch between what's returned and what's reported.
* **Reference Data:** Warm start runs UNCONDITIONALLY for `method="chebyshev"` in `r_bridge.cpp:738-757` AND the mirrored logic in `c_api.cpp` (~lines 352-402) — this is the default path for both R and Python, not an edge case. Option (a) full symmetric fill in compute_normal_equations remains unconditionally safe for every caller and is the default recommendation; choose (b)+uplo-param only if the half-fill perf win (the original G2 motivation) is measurably material — decide with interleaved bench::mark. title: T-M: Stage-1 calibrate coarse_margins only + cell-aggregate multiplier (FIX-1+7)
description:
# T-M: Stage-1 calibrate coarse_margins only + cell-aggregate multiplier (FIX-1 + FIX-7)
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** Coarse-only sub-CalibState in Stage-1 branch (analogous to fine-only sub-CalibState in Stage-2 branch); replace per-obs `stage1_multipliers[c] = ratio` overwrite with cell-aggregate `Σ(weights)/Σ(w_init)` over each coarse cell.
**Forbidden:** modifying `raking_solve` / `sinkhorn_solve` / `greenkhorn_solve` themselves; touching `cell_id >= 0` Stage-2 branches; touching outer-loop convergence logic in `calib_dispatch.hpp`; per-obs multiplier semantics.
**Audit:** new test `tests/testthat/test-stage1-coarse-only.R` proves Stage-1 calibrates coarse only AND Stage-2 measurably reduces fine-margin residual (positive rescue assertion).

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: 3 hierarchical wrappers (`raking_solve_hierarchical`, `sinkhorn_solve_hierarchical`, `greenkhorn_solve_hierarchical`). Out: Stage-1 (`cell_id == -1`) calibrates coarse_margins only via coarse sub-CalibState; sparse-cell `stage1_multipliers[c]` = `Σ(weights[i] for i in cell) / Σ(w_init[i] for i in cell)`.
* **Why:** Spec §6 Strategy A: Stage-1 = coarse-margin repair only. Code calibrates ALL margins. Sinkhorn comment self-incriminates ("full-data Sinkhorn on all margins"). Per-obs multiplier overwrite arbitrary (last-i wins).
* **Reference Data:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-2-stage-hierarchical-method-assessment-design.md` §6; `src/raking.cpp:568-727`; `src/sinkhorn.cpp` analogous; `src/greenkhorn.cpp` analogous; `vignettes/hierarchical-calibration.Rmd`.
* **Philosophy:** Atomic. Algorithmic correctness fix. May unblock T-W (rescue seed-sweep).

## II. Input Specification
* `st.K` margins; `p->hierarchical_coarse_mask[k]` ∈ {0, 1}.
* `partition.cell_id_per_obs[N]`, `partition.obs_indices_by_cell[K_cells]`, `partition.n_cells_total`.
* `w_init[N]` snapshot from before Stage-1.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Stage-1 branch (`cell_id < 0`) MUST construct coarse-only sub-CalibState (mirror existing fine-only pattern at `cell_id >= 0`): `sub.K = K_coarse`, `sub.group_ids = coarse_gids_ptrs.data()`, `sub.targets = coarse_tgt_ptrs.data()`, `sub.cat_counts = coarse_cats.data()`. Pass to solver. After return, copy weights back. Then: `stage1_multipliers[c] = (Σ_{i ∈ cell c} weights[i]) / (Σ_{i ∈ cell c} w_init[i])` with guard `Σw_init > 0` else `1.0`. |
| **Boundary** | TOUCH ONLY: `src/raking.cpp:568-727` (Stage-1 branch + multiplier compute), `src/sinkhorn.cpp` analogous Stage-1 region (~lines 322-475), `src/greenkhorn.cpp` analogous (~lines 268-460). Tests: `tests/testthat/test-stage1-coarse-only.R`, `tests/testthat/test-stage1-multiplier-aggregate.R`. Vignette: `vignettes/hierarchical-calibration.Rmd` — update Stage-1 description to reflect coarse-only semantics (CLAUDE.md "docs bundle WITH method WUs"). DO NOT touch `calib_dispatch.hpp`, `cell_table.hpp`, `validate_calibrate_inputs`. |
| **Lambda [&]** | All bool guards (e.g., `stage1_done`) MUST stay declared before `auto fn = [&]`. New buffers (`coarse_gids_buf`, `coarse_weights_buf`, `coarse_gids_ptrs`, `coarse_tgt_ptrs`, `coarse_cats`) declared at function scope before lambda definition (CLAUDE.md mandate; bug re-introduced twice). |
| **No post-normalize** | Post-Stage-1 weight write-back MUST NOT renormalize Σw=N. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. **Add regression tests FIRST** (Strict TDD per CLAUDE.md):
   1. `test-stage1-coarse-only.R`: DGP with measurable fine-margin residual after coarse-only Stage-1 (i.e. fine-margin residual `Σ|w·X_fine − target_fine|/N > 1e-3` post-Stage-1, pre-Stage-2). Verify CURRENT code FAILS this test (residual ≈ 0 because Stage-1 secretly fits all). Document RED on un-patched code.
   2. **Positive rescue assertion** (Completeness reviewer requirement): same test asserts `fine_residual_post_stage2 < fine_residual_post_stage1 / 10` — proves Stage-2 actually fires and reduces fine residual. A trivially-passing fix that just shrinks Stage-1 scope without making Stage-2 work would FAIL this clause.
   3. `test-stage1-multiplier-aggregate.R`: instrument or compute equivalent — for cells with non-uniform per-obs ratios after Stage-1, expect cell-aggregate value, NOT last-obs value.
2. **Per solver** (raking, sinkhorn, greenkhorn — symmetric patches):
   1. Pre-allocate buffers at function scope (BEFORE lambda): `coarse_idx` (analogous to `fine_idx`), `coarse_gids_buf(K_coarse, std::vector<int32_t>(N))`, `coarse_weights_buf(N)`, `coarse_gids_ptrs(K_coarse)`, `coarse_tgt_ptrs(K_coarse)`, `coarse_cats(K_coarse)`.
   2. Inside Stage-1 branch (`cell_id < 0`): pack full-data weights + coarse-only group_ids; construct `CalibState sub = st`; override `sub.K = K_coarse`; redirect pointers; call solver on `sub`; for greenkhorn copy `sub_res.base.best_weights` → `coarse_weights_buf`; scatter back.
   3. Replace per-obs multiplier compute with cell-aggregate:
      ```cpp
      std::vector<double> num(partition.n_cells_total, 0.0), den(partition.n_cells_total, 0.0);
      for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { int c = partition.cell_id_per_obs[i]; num[c] += st.weights[i]; den[c] += w_init[i]; }
      for (int c = 0; c < partition.n_cells_total; c++) stage1_multipliers[c] = (den[c] > 0.0) ? num[c] / den[c] : 1.0;
      ```
3. **Update self-incriminating comments**: raking.cpp:638, sinkhorn.cpp ~393, greenkhorn.cpp ~343 — replace "full-data X on all margins" → "full-data X on coarse margins only (Stage-1 per spec §6)".
4. **Update vignette** `vignettes/hierarchical-calibration.Rmd` — Stage-1 example section: change description from "calibrates all margins on full data" (if present) to "calibrates COARSE margins on full data; fine margins are repaired Stage-2 within cells". Single-method example sufficient (Designer plan iter-1: bundle docs WITH method WU).
5. Verify: `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`; `Rscript -e "devtools::test()"`; tests added in step 1 transition RED → GREEN.
6. **T-W handoff**: in BD comment on `leafblower-6ycz.1.23` (T-W), record rescue rate observations on the original §8 v0 DGP under T-M-fixed algorithm.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{
  "task_id": "T-M",
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "files_modified": ["src/raking.cpp", "src/sinkhorn.cpp", "src/greenkhorn.cpp", "vignettes/hierarchical-calibration.Rmd"],
    "tests_added": ["tests/testthat/test-stage1-coarse-only.R", "tests/testthat/test-stage1-multiplier-aggregate.R"],
    "verification": {"r_install": "ok", "devtools_test_new_fail": 0, "python_pytest": "ok"},
    "tw_re_test_handoff_data": "<rescue rate %, residuals, statuses on §8 v0/v1/v2/v3 DGPs>"
  },
  "error_log": null
}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Both new testthat tests added BEFORE fix; RED on un-patched code (verify by stash + run).
- [ ] All three solvers patched symmetrically (no algorithmic divergence).
- [ ] Lambda [&] rule preserved: bools + buffers declared before lambda defs.
- [ ] Vignette Stage-1 description updated.
- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` succeeds.
- [ ] `Rscript -e "devtools::test()"` — zero new failures; both new tests PASS.
- [ ] `cd python && pytest` — Python parity unchanged at rtol=1e-6.
- [ ] T-W re-test data captured into bd comment on `leafblower-6ycz.1.23`.
- [ ] No hallucination.
close_reason: T-M (commits 33416bf + 264bb1c): Stage-1 coarse-only sub-CalibState across 3 solvers + cell-aggregate multiplier; vignette updated; 16 new tests RED→GREEN. Strategy B sparse_inheritance added (spec §6 compliance). Quality reviewer flagged dead coarse_weights_buf in greenkhorn — fixed in 264bb1c. T-W handoff data recorded on .1.23. Both reviewers PASS.

title: fix(sinkhorn): bisect_capacity target_mass should be n not W_after_clamp
description:
## I. Objective
Fix sinkhorn.cpp ~line 202-203: target_mass passed to bisect_capacity_fast is Sigma X[c] (which can be < n when capacity bounds clamp cells), not n. This causes bisection to redistribute to the wrong total mass, silently violating the sum(w) = n contract.

## II. Input
File: src/sinkhorn.cpp
Lines: ~195-210 (target_mass computation before bisect_capacity_fast call)
Context: IPF sweeps preserve W_total when targets sum to 1; BUT after capacity clamping X[c] = clamp(X_tilde[c], L, U), the clamped sum < n. The bisection then projects to this partial mass rather than n.

## III. Guards
- Bug ONLY applies when capacity bounds actively clamp (is_clamped == true for some c)
- When no cells are clamped, Sigma X[c] == n already — fix is a no-op
- Do NOT change unclamped path behavior
- Must verify: after fix, Sigma weights == n at solver exit

## IV. Logic
1. Read sinkhorn.cpp lines 195-215: find target_mass assignment
2. Check: is it computed as Sigma X[c] or as static_cast<double>(st.n)?
3. If Sigma X[c]: change to static_cast<double>(st.n)
4. If conditional: ensure clamped path uses st.n
5. Compile + run full sinkhorn tests

## V. Schema
{"file": "src/sinkhorn.cpp", "lines": "200-205", "fix": "pass st.n as target_mass to bisect_capacity", "affects": "clamped cells only"}

## VI. DoD
- [ ] target_mass == st.n (not Sigma X[c]) in bisect_capacity call
- [ ] Sigma weights == n at sinkhorn exit (verified in test)
- [ ] S1+S2 GREEN
- [ ] Commit: fix(sinkhorn): pass n as target_mass to bisect_capacity
close_reason: target_mass = st.n (not W_after_clamp). Commit 7e97216.

title: fix(sinkhorn): Dykstra short-circuit must not skip when a[] is non-zero
description:
## I. Objective
Fix sinkhorn.cpp ~line 189-200: the needs_projection short-circuit skips bisect_capacity when X[c] is already in [L,U], but does NOT check whether a[c] is zero. When a[] carries accumulated Dykstra corrections from prior iterations, skipping bisection leaves the correction accumulator inconsistent — breaking Dykstra's fixed-point convergence guarantee.

## II. Input
File: src/sinkhorn.cpp
Lines: ~185-205 (needs_projection check + bisect_capacity call)
Dykstra invariant: correction a[c] must be updated at EVERY capacity projection step, not just when X[c] exceeds bounds.

## III. Guards
- Fix: short-circuit ONLY when all(a[c] == 0.0) AND X in bounds
- Do NOT change kAmax, Sinkhorn sweep logic, or convergence criterion
- Test S1 (tight bounds) and S2 (KL vs raking) must pass GREEN

## IV. Logic
1. Read sinkhorn.cpp lines 180-215 to find the exact needs_projection condition
2. Find where a[c] is used in the correction update loop
3. Add check: short-circuit only when needs_projection==false AND a_is_zero (bool flag updated alongside a[])
4. OR: remove short-circuit entirely (bisect_capacity on a feasible cell is near-instant since lo/hi bracket is trivially tight)
5. Compile: R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -3
6. Run test-calibration-solvers.R S1+S2 tests

## V. Schema
{"file": "src/sinkhorn.cpp", "lines": "185-205", "fix": "guard short-circuit with a_is_zero check", "compile_gate": "R CMD INSTALL --preclean ."}

## VI. DoD
- [ ] Short-circuit conditioned on a[c]==0 for all c (or removed)
- [ ] S1 test GREEN: sinkhorn handles tight bounds without overflow
- [ ] S2 test GREEN: sinkhorn KL <= raking on synthetic
- [ ] test-ieppa-faithful.R GREEN (not affected, regression check)
- [ ] Commit: fix(sinkhorn): gate needs_projection short-circuit on a_is_zero
close_reason: a_is_zero flag added; needs_projection gated. Commit 7e97216.

title: fix(ieppa): water-fill must operate before final normalization on STALL/BUDGET
description:
## I. Objective
Fix ieppa.cpp:1856: in unit-mode, post-loop normalization (w *= n/total_w) runs BEFORE water-fill in STALL/BUDGET cases. Water-fill then uses st.max_weight as unit bound on already-rescaled weights — invariant only at full convergence. On STALL/BUDGET, rescaling distorts cell sums before water-fill enforces bounds.

## II. Input
File: src/ieppa.cpp
Lines: ~1840-1880 (post-loop normalization + water-fill block)
Variables: st.weights, total_w, st.max_weight, bounds_mode RK_BOUNDS_UNIT

## III. Guards
- Fix ONLY unit-mode path (RK_BOUNDS_UNIT)
- Cell-mode path has separate diagnostic block — do not modify
- Correct order: water-fill at cell scale FIRST, then normalize to sum=n
- Must preserve: after fix, Σ weights = n AND all weights in [min_weight, max_weight]

## IV. Logic
1. Read ieppa.cpp lines 1840-1900 (full post-loop block)
2. Trace current order: normalize → water-fill vs correct order: water-fill → normalize
3. If normalization before water-fill: reorder to water-fill first on RK_BOUNDS_UNIT path
4. Verify water-fill uses pre-normalization cell-scale bounds (not /n scaled)
5. Compile: R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -5
6. Run: Rscript -e "testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/test-ieppa-bounds-mode.R')"

## V. Schema
```json
{
  "file": "src/ieppa.cpp",
```

title: fix(sinkhorn): surface Dykstra correction clamp violations as RK_ERR_INFEAS
description:
## I. Objective
In sinkhorn.cpp:178-185, the Dykstra log-correction 'a' is clamped at ±kAmax (±30) silently — when ratios genuinely exceed exp(30) this destroys mass-preservation and returns incorrect weights without any error signal. Fix: detect clamp, set RK_ERR_INFEAS.

## II. Input
File: src/sinkhorn.cpp
Lines: ~175-190 (Dykstra correction 'a' clamp block)
Variable: a[c] log-domain correction accumulator, kAmax constant

## III. Guards
- kAmax clamp is needed to prevent fp overflow — keep it
- Must detect WHEN clamp fires: if |a[c]| hits kAmax, the mass-preservation invariant is violated
- Set res.status = RK_ERR_INFEAS (not STALL) and return immediately
- Add: int n_clamped = 0; counter; if (n_clamped > 0) set infeasible
- Do NOT change the clamp value — change what happens when it fires

## IV. Logic
1. Read src/sinkhorn.cpp lines 165-200 (full Dykstra correction block)
2. Find the clamp: a[c] = std::clamp(a[c] + delta, -kAmax, kAmax) or equivalent
3. Add counter: n_clamped += (fabs(new_a) >= kAmax) ? 1 : 0
4. After inner capacity loop: if (n_clamped > 0) { res.status = RK_ERR_INFEAS; return res; }
5. Compile: R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -5
6. Run: Rscript -e "testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/test-calibration-solvers.R')"

## V. Schema
```json
{
  "file": "src/sinkhorn.cpp",
  "variable": "a[c]",
  "clamp_const": "kAmax",
  "new_behavior": "RK_ERR_INFEAS when clamp fires",
  "counter_var": "n_clamped",
  "compile_gate": "R CMD INSTALL --preclean ."
}
```

## VI. DoD
- [ ] clamp fires → RK_ERR_INFEAS returned, not silent wrong weights
- [ ] n_clamped counter correct
- [ ] test-calibration-solvers.R GREEN
- [ ] No regression in existing sinkhorn tests
- [ ] Commit: fix(sinkhorn): RK_ERR_INFEAS on Dykstra log-correction clamp
notes: SPEC_FAILURE: any-clamp→INFEAS too aggressive (kAmax fires on feasible problems). Revised approach: declare INFEAS only if same cell clamped across N consecutive outer iters. Needs separate spec revision session.
close_reason: WONT-FIX. Original spec (any kAmax saturation → RK_ERR_INFEAS) is wrong: S1 test (test-calibration-solvers.R:188) explicitly guards against this on a tight-bounds feasible problem. kAmax=30 is a numerical overflow guard, NOT an infeasibility detector. Three independent guards already surface genuine infeasibility: bisect_capacity pre-check, bracket failure (RK_ERR_INFEAS at line 204), and errRp convergence monitor (NOCONV). STATUS=0 requires errRp convergence; wrong weights → large errRp → no silent-wrong-weight path exists. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-04-vz1s1-revised.md.

title: fix(chebyshev): Δs sign error in Mehrotra second-order correction
description:
## I. Objective
Fix wrong sign in Mehrotra predictor-corrector second-order correction in chebyshev.cpp:584. corr_lo reuses dX_A (affine step) but needs a separately tracked dS_lo_A=+dX_A. Currently dY_lo/dY_hi terms use inconsistent sign convention → wrong Newton direction → incorrect weights computed silently.

## II. Input
File: src/chebyshev.cpp
Lines: ~580-595 (corr_lo / corr_hi computation block)
Phase-A affine step variables: dX_A, dS_lo_A (missing), dS_hi_A (missing)
Phase-B corrector variables: dX_B, dY_lo, dY_hi

## III. Guards
- MUST NOT change Phase-A predictor logic
- MUST NOT change convergence check thresholds
- New dS_lo_A = +dX_A, dS_hi_A = -dX_A by LP sign convention (slack s_lo = X - L, s_hi = U - X)
- Verify: corrected Newton step satisfies KKT complementarity to O(mu^2)

## IV. Logic
1. Read src/chebyshev.cpp lines 570-600 (full corrector block)
2. Identify all uses of dX_A inside corr_lo and corr_hi expressions
3. Add: double dS_lo_A_c = dX_A[c]; double dS_hi_A_c = -dX_A[c]; before corr computation
4. Replace: corr_lo uses of dX_A -> dS_lo_A_c; corr_hi uses -> dS_hi_A_c
5. Compile: R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -5
6. Run tests: Rscript -e "testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/test-chebyshev.R')"
7. Run full test suite: Rscript -e "devtools::test()" 2>&1 | tail -20

## V. Schema
```json
{
  "file": "src/chebyshev.cpp",
  "lines_affected": "580-595",
  "new_variables": ["dS_lo_A_c", "dS_hi_A_c"],
  "sign_convention": {"s_lo": "+dX", "s_hi": "-dX"},
  "test_file": "tests/testthat/test-chebyshev.R",
  "compile_gate": "R CMD INSTALL --preclean ."
}
```

## VI. DoD

title: Epic: PYR-PARITY — Fix Python/R weight parity (greenkhorn, logit, raking) + regression test
description:
# Epic: PYR-PARITY — Python/R Weight Parity

## Goal
Python harvest() must return numerically identical calibrated weights to R harvest() for every method when invoked with identical inputs, because both bind the same shared C library.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Python greenkhorn mkl matches R greenkhorn mkl (|rel_diff| < 0.05)
- [ ] Python logit max_err matches R logit max_err (|rel_diff| < 0.05)
- [ ] Automated parity test passes: max(|w_py - w_r|) < 1e-10 for all 6 methods on synthetic data
- [ ] No regressions on ieppa, newton_kl, sinkhorn benchmarks

## Context & Background
Root cause confirmed (2026-05-04):

greenkhorn_solve() and logit_calibrate() store calibrated obs-level weights in
res.base.best_weights and do NOT write to st.weights in-place. The R bridge
(r_bridge.cpp:807-811) has an explicit copy for these two solvers; c_api.cpp
has no such copy, so Python receives the initial weights buffer (all 1.0).

Evidence: Python greenkhorn mkl=0.74561 vs R mkl=0.007706 (100× gap).
Python greenkhorn and logit show identical mkl=0.745612 = uncalibrated value.

raking discrepancy (R mkl=0.00518 vs Python mkl=0.006275) is a benchmark
measurement artifact (tapply+factor vs groupby+string), NOT a weights gap.
The actual weight vectors are identical for raking.

Files involved:
  src/c_api.cpp      — bug fix (greenkhorn + logit branches)
  benchmarks/parity_check.py — new parity test
  R/harvest.R | tests/parity/run_parity.R — R-side parity helper

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Task order: T1 (fix c_api.cpp) MUST complete and rebuild before T2 (parity test).
T2 tests T1's fix. T1 is P0; T2 is P1 and blocks shipping.
Both tasks are in src/ and tests/; no cross-task file conflicts.

title: BUG: c_api.cpp greenkhorn/logit return initial weights — missing best_weights copy
description:
## leafblower-sa3f: Fix c_api.cpp — copy best_weights for greenkhorn and logit
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Parent:** leafblower-a9xk (PYR-PARITY Epic)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In src/c_api.cpp GREENKHORN and LOGIT branches, copy res.base.best_weights into weights[] after the solver call — mirroring r_bridge.cpp:806-813 — so Python returns calibrated weights.
* **Why:** greenkhorn_solve() and logit_calibrate() store obs-level calibrated weights ONLY in res.base.best_weights; they never write st.weights in-place. R bridge copies these back (r_bridge.cpp comment: 'greenkhorn and logit do not modify st.weights in-place'). c_api.cpp lacks this copy → Python sees the initial 1.0 buffer.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/c_api.cpp at current HEAD.
* **GREENKHORN branch:** ~line 334: `} else if (alg == RK_ALG_GREENKHORN) {`
* **LOGIT branch:** ~line 343: `} else if (alg == RK_ALG_LOGIT) {`
* **R bridge pattern to mirror (r_bridge.cpp:806-813):**
  ```cpp
  // greenkhorn and logit do not modify st.weights in-place; copy calibrated
  // weights into the weights vector so raw$weights in harvest.R is correct.
  if (!res_best_weights.empty() && (int)res_best_weights.size() == n &&
      (res_alg_used == RK_ALG_GREENKHORN || res_alg_used == RK_ALG_LOGIT)) {
      std::copy(res_best_weights.begin(), res_best_weights.end(), weights.begin());
  }
  ```

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Size guard** | Only copy if static_cast<int>(res.base.best_weights.size()) == n. |
| **Empty guard** | If res.base.best_weights is empty(), skip copy (solver exited before first check — infeasible/bad_arg cases). The empty() check is sufficient for the error path: best_weights is populated at the best observed iteration; if the solver exits before any iteration runs, it stays empty. No separate status check needed. |
| **Scope — in-place writers NOT affected:** | raking.cpp:548, sinkhorn.cpp:257, greg.cpp:156, chebyshev.cpp:708 all call apply_obs_expansion or write st.weights[i] in-place — they propagate via pointer alias (st.weights = weights at c_api.cpp:235). newton_kl has explicit copy loop at c_api.cpp:370. ONLY greenkhorn + logit need this fix. |
| **No heap allocation** | std::copy only. |
| **Order** | Copy IMMEDIATELY after solver call, before pack_solver_result. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/c_api.cpp lines 330-360 to confirm exact current line numbers.
2. In GREENKHORN branch, after `auto res = lbw::greenkhorn_solve(st);`, insert:
   ```cpp
   if (!res.base.best_weights.empty() &&
       static_cast<int>(res.base.best_weights.size()) == n)
       std::copy(res.base.best_weights.begin(),
                 res.base.best_weights.end(), weights);
   ```
3. Same insertion in LOGIT branch after `auto res = lbw::logit_calibrate(st);`.
4. Rebuild (check Makefile for correct target).
5. Smoke test:
   ```python
   import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'python')
   from leafblower import harvest
   import pandas as pd, numpy as np
   df = pd.DataFrame({'a':['x','y','x','y','x'],'b':['p','p','q','q','p']})
   tgt = {'a':{'x':0.6,'y':0.4},'b':{'p':0.5,'q':0.5}}
   r = harvest(df, tgt, method='greenkhorn', max_iterations=500)
   w = r['weights']
   assert not np.allclose(w, 1.0), 'FAIL: weights still initial'
   ```
6. Run allmethod_bench.py: verify greenkhorn mkl < 0.02.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{
  "task_id": "leafblower-sa3f",
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "files_changed": ["src/c_api.cpp"],
    "lines_added": 6,
    "greenkhorn_mkl_after": "<0.02",
    "logit_max_err_after": "within 5pct of R baseline (0.1396)"
  },
  "error_log": null
}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] src/c_api.cpp: 2 hunks, ~3 lines each, in GREENKHORN and LOGIT branches
- [ ] Smoke test: greenkhorn weights NOT all 1.0 on tiny synthetic data
- [ ] allmethod_bench.py: greenkhorn mkl < 0.02 (R baseline: 0.007706)
- [ ] logit max_err within 5% relative of R baseline (0.1396)
- [ ] No regression for ieppa / sinkhorn / newton_kl / raking mkl
- [ ] Rebuild succeeds without new warnings

title: DIAG-CONV: Verify cm.kl = obs-level marginal_kl from same X_cur; diagnose SRAA convergence discrepancy
description:
## Objective
Verify that the ieppa convergence check (cm.kl from compute_cell_metrics(X_cur)) equals the obs-level marginal_kl computed from the SAME X_cur, with and without clamping. If they differ, find the bug.

## Background
B-SRAA fix (c60ac3b) correctly selects best iterate by marginal_kl. But post-hoc marginal_kl on 1.58M shows 0.0114 while cm.kl fires convergence at <1e-3. The user correctly states: for a monotone algorithm, the final iterate IS the best. Best-iterate tracking should only be needed for non-monotone methods (SRAA/AA).

## Root cause hypothesis
The discrepancy between cm.kl (<1e-3) and post-hoc marginal_kl (0.0114) has one of these causes:
(A) The clamping (X[c] = clamp(X_cur, L_cell, U_cell)) degrades marginal_kl from <1e-3 to 0.0114
(B) compute_cell_metrics uses S_lin or some other intermediate state that doesn't match X_cur
(C) The obs-level expansion of X_cur does not equal the cell-level aggregation (algebraic error)

Hypothesis (C) should be FALSE by algebra: Σ_{i in cell c} w_i = X_init[c] * (X_cur[c]/X_init[c]) = X_cur[c].

## Investigation steps

### Step 1: Add diagnostic to ieppa.cpp (temporary, behind verbose>=3)
At the kErrCheckInterval gate in the SRAA path, after computing cm:
1. Compute marginal_kl from X_cur directly (cell-level, same as cm.kl)
2. Expand X_cur to obs level: w_obs[i] = st.weights_init[i] * X_cur[c]/X_init[c]
3. Compute marginal_kl from w_obs
4. Compare: if cm.kl != obs_mkl, log the discrepancy

Also add diagnostic for the clamping step: compute marginal_kl before and after X[c] = clamp(X_cur).

### Step 2: Run on 1.58M stepstone with accelerate=TRUE, verbose=3
Run harvest() and capture the diagnostic logs:
- cm.kl at convergence check (f_eval=10)
- obs-level marginal_kl from unclamped X_cur at f_eval=10
- obs-level marginal_kl from clamped X[c] after loop exits

### Step 3: Identify which step introduces the discrepancy
- If cm.kl == obs_mkl(unclamped): the clamping IS the problem (source A)
- If cm.kl != obs_mkl(unclamped): compute_cell_metrics is wrong (source B or C)

### Step 4: Fix the identified root cause
- Source A (clamping degrades): move convergence check AFTER clamping, or remove unnecessary clamping for non-SRAA case
- Source B/C (metric computation wrong): fix compute_cell_metrics or the expansion

### Step 5: Verify monotonicity of plain ieppa
Run plain ieppa (accelerate=FALSE) and verify marginal_kl is non-increasing every kErrCheckInterval. If it increases, the IPF algorithm has a bug.

## DoD
- [ ] Diagnostic confirms exactly which step introduces the cm.kl vs obs-level marginal_kl discrepancy
- [ ] Root cause identified with file:line evidence
- [ ] Fix applied (no workaround)
- [ ] For SRAA: convergence fires when the ACTUAL returned state has marginal_kl < tol
- [ ] For plain ieppa: marginal_kl is non-increasing (monotone verified)
- [ ] R CMD check passes
close_reason: RESOLVED by B-SRAA fix (c60ac3b). The 0.0114 benchmark result was from BEFORE B-SRAA (benchmark at 18:38, B-SRAA at 18:48). After B-SRAA, ieppa+accel on 1.58M gives mkl=0.00078 < 1e-3 — algorithm correct and monotone. No discrepancy between cm.kl and obs-level marginal_kl. Clamping confirmed NOT the cause (identical results with max_weight=1e6 and max_weight=5).

title: B-BEST-WEIGHTS: harvest() returns final-clamped weights not best iterate (WU-E incomplete)
description:
## Root Cause

harvest() returns r[["weights"]] from obs-level expansion of the FINAL CLAMPED X[c] (post-SRAA clamp at ieppa.cpp:953-960), NOT from the best iterate.

WU-E added best_weights tracking (res.base.best_weights = expanded best iterate) but the MAIN obs expansion (st.weights, line ~1803) still uses current X[c], which is the last SRAA state after clamping.

This creates two conflicting weight states:
1. cm.kl convergence check: computed from UNCLAMPED X_cur → fires at 1e-3
2. r[["weights"]] (main return): from CLAMPED X[c] → post-hoc marginal_kl = 0.0114

## Consequence
Post-hoc calibration quality of returned weights is much worse than what triggered convergence. The user gets suboptimal weights even though the solver claims convergence.

## Fix
In ieppa.cpp, after SRAA loop, if best.has_best(): use best.best_weights for the mult[] computation instead of X[c]:
  - if (best.has_best()) { mult[c] = best.best_weights[c]; } // already X_cur/X_init
  - else { mult[c] = X[c]/X_init[c]; }

This ensures r[["weights"]] = best iterate weights = consistent with cm.kl at convergence.

## Why WU-E was incomplete
WU-E added res.base.best_weights (tracking + separate expansion) but did NOT redirect the main st.weights expansion to use it. The result struct carries the right weights in best_weights[] but r[["weights"]] comes from the wrong expansion.

## Applies to
ieppa.cpp (SRAA path primarily), potentially also non-SRAA when budget is hit (current X ≠ best iterate)

## DoD
- [ ] ieppa+accel on 1.58M: r[["weights"]] post-hoc marginal_kl <= 1e-3 (matches cm.kl convergence)
- [ ] ieppa+accel on 200K: marginal_kl unchanged or better
- [ ] ieppa plain (budget case): r[["weights"]] = best-iterate weights (not final iterate)
- [ ] R CMD check passes
close_reason: REVERTED. User correctly identifies: final iteration should have lowest loss by construction for monotone IPF. Best-iterate tracking is only valid for non-monotone methods (SRAA). If plain ieppa needs it, the algorithm is broken. Root cause investigation required instead of workaround.

title: B-SRAA: ieppa SRAA path selects best iterate by errRp not method loss function
description:
## I. Context & Objective
**Objective:** Fix ieppa SRAA path to select best iterate using method's natural loss function (marginal_kl), not errRp.
**Why:** r.err_result (errRp) is the fast SRAA F-eval margin error — valid for stall detection, wrong for best-iterate selection. Non-SRAA path correctly uses select_metric(st.convergence_cfg.metric, cm). Inconsistency causes ieppa+accel to return suboptimal weights.
**File:** src/ieppa.cpp only (4 locations, single commit)
**Mechanism:** Add sraa_best_errRp for stall detection; move best-iterate update from every-f_eval errRp check to kErrCheckInterval gate (where compute_cell_metrics is already called); use select_metric(sraa_cfg.metric, cm) as the selection criterion.
**Forbidden:** Do NOT touch non-SRAA path (lines ~1390-1580). Do NOT change stall window logic beyond metric fix.

## II. Input Specification
Lines in src/ieppa.cpp:
- 809: sraa_outer_stall_count declaration — add sraa_best_errRp here
- 869-882: errRp-based best update block — DELETE entirely (move to check interval)
- 886-896: stall guard uses best.best_metric — change to sraa_best_errRp
- 905-919: kErrCheckInterval gate calling compute_cell_metrics — ADD best update here
- ~1140: SRAA reset block (best.reset()) — ADD sraa_best_errRp = infinity here

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| Logic | lf_best/lf_best_snap must still be updated when new best is found (move from 869 to check-interval block) |
| Logic | sraa_best_errRp = min(sraa_best_errRp, r.err_result) every f_eval; stall guard uses this, NOT best.best_metric |
| Logic | sraa_best_errRp reset at T1.B linear→log fallback (same place as best.reset()) |
| Logic | nat_metric = select_metric(sraa_cfg.metric, cm) — uses the MARGINAL_KL→KL remap already in place |
| Boundary | Only src/ieppa.cpp — no other files |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/ieppa.cpp lines 805-935 to confirm exact line numbers
2. Change 1 (line 809): add  after sraa_outer_stall_count
3. Change 2 (lines 869-882): DELETE the errRp-based best update block entirely (but lf_best update will move to Change 4)
4. Change 3 (line ~884 before stall guard): add  and change stall guard to use sraa_best_errRp instead of best.best_metric
5. Change 4 (inside kErrCheckInterval gate, after check_convergence): add nat_metric = select_metric(sraa_cfg.metric, cm); if new best, update best + lf_best + lf_best_snap
6. Change 5 (SRAA reset ~line 1140): add

title: A1: R_UnwindProtect for RAII+longjmp UB in r_bridge.cpp
description:
## I. Context & Objective
**Objective:** Replace try/catch+Rf_error pattern with R_UnwindProtect so std::vector destructors run on exception.
**Why:** Per R-exts §5.5, Rf_error longjmps past all C++ stack frames, skipping destructors. Every std::vector (weights, S_flat, gids_storage) in solver scope leaks on exception. UB per C++ standard; heap corruption on repeated failures.
**File:** /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/src/r_bridge.cpp (lines ~9–617, all solver dispatch blocks)

## II. Input Specification
- Existing: try { auto res = lbw::xxx_solve(st); } catch (...) { Rf_error(...); }
- Target: R_UnwindProtect-based wrapper that runs destructors before longjmp propagates

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| Logic | R_UnwindProtect available since R 3.5. Check R version >= 3.5. |
| Format | All existing SEXP PROTECT/UNPROTECT counts must remain balanced. |
| Boundary | Only change the try/catch error-propagation path; no solver logic changes. |
| Tone | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read r_bridge.cpp fully to identify all try/catch blocks.
2. For each block, replace with R_UnwindProtect: body lambda runs solver; continuation lambda runs on unwind (no-op needed since RAII handles cleanup).
3. Alternatively use cpp11::unwind_protect if cpp11 is already a dependency.
4. Verify: compile with R CMD INSTALL --preclean .

title: CR-A: Memory Safety & R↔C++ Boundary
description:
# Epic: Memory Safety & R↔C++ Boundary

## Goal
Fix all UB, memory leaks, and crash-inducing boundary violations at the R↔C++ interface.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Every solver call safe from heap leaks on exception (R_UnwindProtect)
- [ ] No OOB factor index dereference possible from R
- [ ] All scalar SEXP args validated for LENGTH==1 before use
- [ ] lbfgsb thread_local alpha documented/fixed for re-entrancy

## Context & Background
r_bridge.cpp mixes C++ RAII with R's longjmp error handling. Per R-exts §5.5, longjmp skips C++ destructors — every std::vector in a try{} block leaks on exception. Factor index OOB can segfault. Scalar SEXP reads without LENGTH check read garbage on numeric(0).

## Sub-Agent Strategy
A1 (most critical — UB on every solve) → A2 (segfault risk) → A3 (input safety) → A4 (thread safety). Each task self-contained.
close_reason: All CR-A tasks complete and merged to master.

title: C2: logit_calib.cpp — Deville-Sarndal logit Newton solver (bounds by construction)
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Implement logit_calibrate(CalibState& st) in src/logit_calib.cpp: cells_per_cat, cat_offset, Newton loop (w/D_eff from logit link, residuals b, N via compute_normal_equations, LDLT solve), degenerate cell handling, check_convergence, weight reconstruction.
* **Why:** This is the core Part 2 solver. T5-T8 turn GREEN when this lands with the bridge. Bounds enforced by construction via logit link — no std::clamp needed on weights.
* **Reference Data:** Spec Part 2 algorithm section. Functions from calib_linalg.hpp: compute_normal_equations(ct, D_eff, N, cat_offset, K, nct), ldlt_factor_inplace(N, nct, 1e-10), ldlt_solve(N, nct, b). D_eff[c]=(U-L)×σ(z)×(1-σ(z)) from Deville-Sarndal 1992 eq 8. Functions from calib_dispatch.hpp: compute_cell_metrics + check_convergence.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/calib_linalg.hpp (normal equations functions), src/calib_dispatch.hpp, src/greg.cpp (template Newton pattern), src/logit_calib.hpp.
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | cat_offset[k] = sum of cat_counts[0..k-1]; nct = total categories |
| **Logic** | z_c = sum_k lambda[cat_offset[k] + g_per_cell[k][c]]; clamp z to [-700, 700] to prevent exp overflow |
| **Logic** | w[c] = L_cell[c] + (U_cell[c]-L_cell[c]) * sigma(z_c) — bounds enforced analytically |
| **Logic** | D_eff[c] = (U_cell[c]-L_cell[c]) * sigma * (1-sigma) — Hessian for Newton weight |
| **Logic** | On compute_normal_equations failure → RK_ERR_INFEAS with 'logit: singular normal equations (degenerate bounds)' |
| **Logic** | On ldlt_factor_inplace failure → RK_ERR_INFEAS with diagnostic |
| **Logic** | Convergence: compute_cell_metrics(st, ct, w, W_total, bucket_scratch) + check_convergence() — NOT hand-rolled pct_tol check |
| **Logic** | Post-loop: RK_ERR_BUDGET if best_resid < initial_resid*0.999, else RK_ERR_STALL. Never RK_ERR_NOCONV |
| **Logic** | Weight reconstruction: w[i] = st.weights[i] * w_best[cell_of[i]] / X_init[cell_of[i]] |
| **Logic** | kMaxNewtonIters = 50 (hard cap, user's max_iterations honors this) |
| **Boundary** | Never set std::clamp on w[c] — logit link guarantees bounds |
| **Boundary** | n=0 guard: if (st.n <= 0) return RK_ERR_BADARG |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/greg.cpp for Newton + LDLT pattern; read src/calib_linalg.hpp for function signatures.
2. Implement logit_calibrate:
   (a) cells_per_cat construction (same as Greenkhorn/raking pattern)
   (b) cat_offset[K] and nct computation
   (c) X_init[c] from design weights; L_cell/U_cell; lambda[nct]=0; w[M_cell]; D_eff[M_cell]; N[nct×nct]; b[nct]
   (d) initial_resid tracking for post-loop classification
   (e) Newton loop:
       - z_c = sum_k lambda[cat_offset[k]+g_per_cell[k][c]], clamped ±700
       - sigma = 1/(1+exp(-z)); w[c] = L+(U-L)*sigma; D_eff[c]=(U-L)*sigma*(1-sigma)
       - Residuals: b[cat_offset[k]+j] = tau[k][j]*n - sum_{c in bucket(k,j)} w[c]
       - compute_normal_equations; ldlt_factor_inplace; ldlt_solve → b=Δλ
       - lambda += b
       - compute_cell_metrics + check_convergence; best-iterate tracking
   (f) Post-loop status
   (g) Weight reconstruction from w_best
3. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — must compile clean.
4. devtools::test() — FAIL unchanged.
5. git add src/logit_calib.cpp && git commit -m 'feat(logit): implement logit_calibrate — Deville-Sarndal 1992 Newton solver, bounds by construction'


title: B2: greenkhorn.cpp — full Greenkhorn solver (argmax IPF + incremental bucket sums)
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Implement greenkhorn_solve(CalibState& st) in src/greenkhorn.cpp: cells_per_cat construction, W-incremental maintenance, argmax errRp selection, single-margin IPF update, incremental bucket-sum updates, best-iterate tracking, check_convergence, weight reconstruction.
* **Why:** This is the core Part 1 solver. T1-T4 turn GREEN when this lands with the bridge (Epic D).
* **Reference Data:** Spec Part 1 algorithm section. Key functions from calib_dispatch.hpp: compute_cell_metrics(st,ct,X,W,bucket), check_convergence(cfg,m,prev_metric,tol_abs). Pattern from src/raking.cpp lines 82-100 for cells_per_cat construction.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/greenkhorn.hpp (B1), src/calib_dispatch.hpp (check_convergence, compute_cell_metrics), src/cell_table.hpp (CellTable: g_per_cell, cell_of, M_cell, n_per_cell), src/types.hpp (CalibState).
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | cells_per_cat built locally: for c in M_cell: g_per_cell[k][c] → cells_per_cat[k][g].push_back(c) |
| **Logic** | W maintained incrementally: W += delta per cell update (not recomputed from scratch) |
| **Logic** | W<=0 guard before scale factor: if (W<=0.0) { RK_ERR_INFEAS; break; } |
| **Logic** | S_flat[k*S_stride+j] recomputed exactly from cells after each bucket update (clamp may cause drift) |
| **Logic** | check_convergence via compute_cell_metrics every kErrCheckInterval=10 iterations |
| **Logic** | Best-iterate: X_best snapshot when errRp < best_errRp; return X_best not X |
| **Logic** | Status: if loop exhausts iter and still no convergence: BUDGET if improving, STALL if plateau |
| **Logic** | Weight reconstruction: w[i] = st.weights[i] * X_best[cell_of[i]] / X_init[cell_of[i]] |
| **Boundary** | Never call std::clamp with L>U — validate min_weight<=max_weight before solver |
| **Boundary** | errRp recompute for ALL k after each step (O(Σ cat_counts)) |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/raking.cpp for structural pattern; read src/calib_dispatch.hpp for check_convergence/compute_cell_metrics signatures.
2. Implement greenkhorn_solve with:
   (a) cells_per_cat construction (mirrors raking.cpp lines 82-100)
   (b) X[c] init from design weights; X_init[c] saved; L_cell/U_cell per cell
   (c) W = sum(X); S_flat[K×max_cats] init; errRp[K] init
   (d) bucket_scratch[max_cats] for compute_cell_metrics
   (e) Main loop: W<=0 guard → k*=argmax → per-j update (f=W×τ/S, per-c clamp+delta+W+S updates) → S[k*][j] recompute → errRp update → best-iterate → convergence check
   (f) Post-loop: BUDGET/STALL status via prev_metric comparison
   (g) Weight reconstruction from X_best via cell_of[i]
3. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -5 — must compile clean.
4. devtools::test() 2>&1 | tail -3 — FAIL unchanged.
5. Manual RED check: harvest(df,tgt,method='greenkhorn') still errors (bridge not wired).
6. git add src/greenkhorn.cpp && git commit -m 'feat(greenkhorn): implement greenkhorn_solve — greedy coordinate-descent IPF with incremental bucket sums'

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id":"B2","success":true,"data":{"compiles":true,"key_invariants":{"W_incremental":true,"W0_guard":true,"X_best_returned":true,"cells_per_cat_local":true}},"error_log":null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] src/greenkhorn.cpp implements greenkhorn_solve
- [ ] cells_per_cat built locally (not from CellTable)
- [ ] W maintained incrementally; W<=0 guard present
- [ ] S[k*][j] recomputed exactly after each bucket update
- [ ] check_convergence + compute_cell_metrics used (no hand-rolled pct_tol check)
- [ ] X_best returned (not X)
- [ ] Status: BUDGET=4 or STALL=5 (never NOCONV=1)
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . clean
- [ ] Committed
notes:
SQUAREM IN SCOPE (user confirmed). When st.accelerate=TRUE:
F_eval = K greedy Greenkhorn steps sorted ONCE at round start (NOT re-sorted per F_eval call).
This makes F_eval stationary → SQUAREM valid. Sort order fixed at round entry:
  std::sort(order, [&](a,b){ return errRp[a] > errRp[b]; });
  for ki in 0..K-1: single_greenkhorn_step(order[ki], X, W, S, errRp)
Then SQUAREM CBB step mirrors raking.cpp lines 351-480:
  sq_X_snap = X; sq_w1 = F_eval(X); sq_w2 = F_eval(sq_w1)
  alpha = -||sq_w1-sq_X_snap||_obs / ||sq_w2-2*sq_w1+sq_X_snap||_obs
  sq_X_star = sq_X_snap - 2*alpha*r + alpha^2*v
  sq_X_star = F_eval(sq_X_star)  [stabilization]
  Accept sq_X_star or fall back to sq_w2 on violation
Key difference from raking: greedy sort allowed (and applied) inside F_eval.
Key constraint: Sort at ENTRY of F_eval, not per individual step within F_eval.

description:

| **Logic** | Hard-clamp branch: else { double xc = clamp(X_tilde_c, L, U); X[c]=xc; W[c]=xc/X_tilde_c; X_cur[c]=xc; } — UNCHANGED |

| **Logic** | Adaptive growth: 5 consecutive violations > 1% of max_weight * mean_n_per_cell → multiply capacity_mu_adaptive by 2.0, cap at 1000x base, res.alm_n_growth_events++ |
| **Logic** | eta_i_current: declared before homotopy loop, updated at each level entry |
| **Logic** | Final projection: after main loop, BEFORE returning; clamp+rescale loop max 3 iters; log sum drift if > 1e-6*n at verbose>=1 |
| **Logic** | Populate: res.alm_capacity_mu_final = capacity_mu_adaptive; res.alm_max_dual_norm = max|lambda_cell[c]|; res.alm_sum_drift = |sum(X)-n| after projection |

title: B10: sinkhorn.cpp Dykstra a[] must be zeroed when !needs_projection
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Zero a[c] for all cells when the projection step is skipped (!needs_projection) to prevent phantom KL correction accumulation in the Dykstra iteration.
* **Why:** sinkhorn.cpp:150-156: a[c] accumulates log(X[c]) - log(X_proj[c]) only when needs_projection=true. When the box constraint is inactive (needs_projection=false), a[] is left dirty from the previous active iteration. Next time the projection activates, a[] carries phantom mass from the stale correction — drifts the KL iterate away from the Dykstra fixed point.
* **Reference Data:** sinkhorn.cpp lines 148-157 (Dykstra correction block). a[] is a vector of doubles (size M_cell). needs_projection = (bisect_capacity returned meaningful X_proj). When inactive: X_proj = X; X[c] already set; a[] should track zero (no correction applied).

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/sinkhorn.cpp
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | In the `if (needs_projection) { ... } else { ... }` block: add in the else branch: `for (int c = 0; c < ct.M_cell; c++) a[c] = 0.0;` |
| **Logic** | OR: zero a[] only when transitioning from active to inactive (track prev_needs_projection) — simpler is the full zero |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT zero a[] inside the if(needs_projection) block — the accumulation there is correct |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read sinkhorn.cpp lines 140-165 to understand the correction accumulation logic.
2. Write a test: problem where the box constraint is transiently inactive for several iterations then becomes active again — verify the KL iterate is correct vs reference.
3. Add a[c]=0.0 zero-out in the else branch.
4. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — compile gate.
5. devtools::test() — calibration-solvers tests (sinkhorn) must pass.
6. Commit: fix(sinkhorn): zero Dykstra a[] when projection inactive to prevent phantom correction.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)


- [ ] Test: transient-inactive projection → correct KL iterate

title: B17: Guard PLATEAU rule in calib_dispatch against prev=0 false convergence

title: B12: compute_margin_errRp must return +inf (not 0) when W_total<=0

title: B2: lbfgsb_solver must emit RK_ERR_BUDGET(4) and RK_ERR_STALL(5) on exit
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Differentiate lbfgsb_solver exit paths: return RK_ERR_BUDGET(4) when iteration budget exhausted with gn >= tol; return RK_ERR_STALL(5) when gradient stalls without convergence.
* **Why:** lbfgsb_solver.cpp:305 sets status unconditionally as: `res.status = converged ? RK_OK : RK_ERR_NOCONV;`. NOCONV(1) is a legacy alias — no solver should emit it. harvest.R has dead code at s==4 and s==5 for lbfgsb because it never gets there. Users get no information about WHY lbfgsb failed.
* **Reference Data:** lbfgsb_solver.cpp line 305. RK_ERR_BUDGET=4 means 'still improving, increase max_iter'. RK_ERR_STALL=5 means 'at constrained optimum, weights are valid'. Loop at lines 602-659. Convergence check at lines 291-303: converged = curr_metric < cfg.pct_tol. BUDGET: iter==max_iter AND gn >= tol. STALL: successive gn changes < eps (gradient plateau).
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/lbfgsb_solver.cpp, src/leafblower.h (status code definitions)
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Track prev_gn across iterations; if abs(gn - prev_gn)/max(prev_gn,1e-15) < stall_eps (e.g. 1e-6) for N consecutive iters (e.g. 5), set status=STALL |
| **Logic** | If loop exits via iter==max_iter and !converged: status=BUDGET |
| **Logic** | RK_OK only when convergence check fires |
| **Logic** | STALL should only fire AFTER at least burnin=10 iterations |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT emit NOCONV(1) from lbfgsb — it is a legacy alias |

An input with |sum-1| in (1e-8, 1e-6) passes the first check but fails the second AFTER memory is allocated and params parsed — confusing error reporting. Unified at 1e-6 (the less strict one) to accept valid floating-point imprecision.
* **Reference Data:** validation.hpp line 84: `if (std::fabs(sum - 1.0) > 1e-8)`. calib_validate.cpp line 81: `if (std::fabs(s - 1.0) > 1e-6)`. Both check the same property.

| **Boundary** | Grep both files after change: confirm single tolerance value used everywhere |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT change any other tolerance constants |

2. Write a test: create targets with sum=1+8e-7 (between 1e-8 and 1e-6). Before fix: harvest() should error. After fix: harvest() should accept it (or error for a different reason if problem is infeasible).
3. Change validation.hpp:84 from 1e-8 to 1e-6.

title: B7: Validate start_weights vector length before copy in r_bridge
description:

* **Why:** r_bridge.cpp:178-182 copies start_weights[i] for i in [0,n) without checking the SEXP length. If the R caller passes a vector shorter than n, this is an out-of-bounds read — undefined behavior, potential crash or silent data corruption.
* **Reference Data:** r_bridge.cpp lines 175-185. The copy loop is: `const double* sw = REAL(start_weights_sexp); for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) weights[i] = sw[i];`

title: B4: Wrap solver calls in try/catch to prevent PROTECT stack corruption
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Wrap all lbw::*_solve() dispatch calls in r_bridge.cpp in try/catch so C++ exceptions never escape past PROTECT'd SEXPs.
* **Why:** C++ exceptions do not unwind R's protection stack (PROTECT/UNPROTECT). Any std::bad_alloc or other exception thrown inside a solver will corrupt the R protection stack, causing GC errors or crashes in subsequent allocations. R's own Rf_error() uses longjmp and is safe; C++ exceptions are not.
* **Reference Data:** r_bridge.cpp lines 533-618. The PROTECT count at solver entry is ~0 (SEXPs allocated post-solve) but PROTECT calls inside the dispatch block (e.g., bw_sxp at line 591) are at risk.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/r_bridge.cpp source file.
* **Format:** C++ source — read the full dispatch block from line ~366 to ~520.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Wrap the entire lbw::*_solve() call (and its result extraction) in try { ... } catch (const std::exception& e) { UNPROTECT(N); Rf_error("leafblower: solver error: %s", e.what()); } |
| **Logic** | N in UNPROTECT must be the exact count of PROTECT calls before the try block |
| **Format** | No bare catch(...) — catch std::exception only |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT wrap Rf_error, Rf_warning (they longjmp and must not be inside try) |
| **Tone** | Compile gate: R CMD INSTALL --preclean . must succeed after change |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read r_bridge.cpp in full; count PROTECT calls before each solver dispatch.
2. Write a test that calls the solver with an input designed to trigger allocation failure (not always possible; at minimum write a test confirming no regression).
3. Wrap the solver dispatch block in try { auto result = dispatch(...); } catch (const std::exception& e) { UNPROTECT(count); Rf_error("...", e.what()); }.
4. Verify PROTECT count N matches the wrapping.
5. Compile: R CMD INSTALL --preclean . in /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower.
6. Run: Rscript -e "devtools::test()" -- must have same pass/fail count as before.
7. Commit: fix(r_bridge): wrap solver dispatch in try/catch to protect R GC stack.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{
  "task_id": "B4",
  "success": true,
  "data": { "file": "src/r_bridge.cpp", "protect_count": "N", "test_result": "PASS" },
  "error_log": null
}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] try/catch wraps all solver dispatch calls in r_bridge.cpp
- [ ] PROTECT count verified correct inside catch handler
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . succeeds
- [ ] devtools::test() no new failures
- [ ] Committed with conventional commit message

title: Epic: Validation & Error Detection Gaps
description:
# Epic: Validation & Error Detection Gaps

## Goal
Close all pre-flight validation holes so invalid inputs produce RK_ERR_BADARG/RK_ERR_INFEAS immediately, not silent wrong results or post-allocation failures.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Target-sum tolerance unified to 1e-6 across validation.hpp and calib_validate.cpp
- [ ] iEPPA and raking run calib_validate_preentry (structural-zero cell detection)
- [ ] harvest.R metric/rule lookup validated before .Call; NULL crash impossible
- [ ] NA-only-category INFEAS detected at validation time
- [ ] estimate_M_cell returns correct bound for K>8 margins
- [ ] harvest.R @return docs updated with codes 4/5

## Context & Background
leafblower dispatches multiple solvers. Validation runs at different layers (validation.hpp for all algorithms, calib_validate_preentry for new solvers only). Gaps let invalid inputs reach solver internals: NA-only categories cause silent misfit; iEPPA/raking miss structural-zero INFEAS; harvest.R metric lookup returns NULL on unknown name, causing C bridge to read integer(0)[0] — undefined behavior.

## Sub-Agent Strategy
TDD throughout. Each fix paired with a test that demonstrates the bug (returns wrong result or crashes) before fix and passes after.

title: Epic: Critical Safety & Memory Safety

# Epic: Critical Safety & Memory Safety

## Goal
Eliminate all memory-safety bugs and infrastructure hazards that can cause crashes, illegal instruction faults, or R PROTECT stack corruption.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] r_bridge.cpp: C++ exceptions wrapped in try/catch; PROTECT stack never corrupted
- [ ] r_bridge.cpp: start_weights length validated before use
- [ ] src/Makevars removed from VCS; Makevars.in is sole tracked build file
- [ ] All n*sizeof() multiplications cast to size_t before use in memcpy
- [ ] All fixes covered by regression tests

## Context & Background
leafblower is an R package (C++17, -O3 -mavx2 -lmvec). The R API uses PROTECT/UNPROTECT for GC safety; C++ exceptions escaping across R API boundaries bypass the PROTECT unwind protocol, corrupting the R protection stack. The checked-in src/Makevars hard-codes -mavx2 -lmvec, defeating the configure probe on non-AVX2 hosts.

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Each task = one fix + one regression test. TDD: write failing test first (where possible), then fix. Compile gate (R CMD INSTALL --preclean .) after each file. Atomic commits per task.

title: HUMAN: homotopy hypothesis falsified on stepstone-fulldata — choose new approach
