regime (errRp increases from iter ~100 onward). Homotopy+Greenkhorn theory targets

Decision needed: (A) stronger global damping (reduce alpha) to suppress oscillation;
(B) reframe target (accept 2.223e-3 = 39% worse than autumn as deliverable);
(C) different algorithmic approach for this regime; (D) abandon P-A/P-B for this dataset.

description:
# CR-F1b: add_na_proportion margin_kl = Inf (NA bin uncounted)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In scope: make compute_quality_metrics count NA observations toward the injected "NA" target bin for add_na_proportion margins, so margin_kl is FINITE (the NA bin contributes ~0, matching target). Out of scope: the list->numeric target type fix (dtkn.1, DONE).
* **Why:** Discovered while fixing dtkn.1. After the type fix, margin_kl for an add_na_proportion=TRUE margin is +Inf, not finite. margin_kl_one (harvest.R:1042) returns Inf because the target has an "NA" level (target=na_frac>0) but the weighted marginal W_k has no "NA" level: the K-pass fallback (harvest.R:1099-1110) does valid<-!is.na(obs_k), EXCLUDING the very NA obs that add_na_proportion intends to count toward the NA bin. dtkn.1 fixed the type error (NA->Inf); this ticket fixes Inf->finite.
* **Reference Data:** harvest.R:789 compute_quality_metrics(weights,target,data) receives target WITH the "NA" bin and data WITH raw R NA (the NA->"NA" recode at 502-520 only builds solver-local group_ids_r, does NOT mutate data). Live-verified 2026-07-03: seed=7 n=400, a with 10% NA, add_na_proportion=TRUE => margin_kl=Inf, 0 warnings.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| Logic | compute_quality_metrics must learn which margins carry an "NA" bin (target has level named "NA"): for those, recode data NA->"NA" so W_k includes the NA mass. Do NOT count NA toward NA-bin for margins that did NOT inject one (a hand-built real "NA" target level already conflates per harvest.R:141 doc). Simplest signal: target level name "NA" present. |
| Boundary | R/harvest.R compute_quality_metrics (~1096-1112) + its test. Do NOT touch the dtkn.1 target construction. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. RED test: add_na_proportion=TRUE fixture => assert margin_kl is FINITE (currently Inf).
2. In the K-pass fallback, for margins where 'NA' %in% names(T_k): treat is.na(obs_k) as level "NA" (do not exclude). Re-normalize W_k over all obs.
3. Confirm margin_kl finite and the NA-bin contribution ~0 (W matches target on NA).
4. devtools::test() 0 FAIL.

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] add_na_proportion=TRUE => finite margin_kl
- [ ] devtools::test() 0 FAIL
close_reason: K-pass fallback recodes NA->'NA' when target carries 'NA' level; margin_kl finite (was Inf). Commit 8ce9b69. 826/0 R. Adversarial PASS; comment corrected + hand-built-corner filed dtkn.13.

title: CR-C5b: raking improvement-rule reports RK_OK on bounds-blocked infeasible plateau
description:
## What
raking with the improvement/criterion convergence rule reports status=RK_OK(0) on a bounds-blocked infeasible problem where margins are grossly unmet.

## Why
Discovered while executing kxna.5 (CR-C5). Fixture: set.seed(88) n=1000, skewed targets far from empirical, max_weight=1.3/min_weight=0.7. raking converges at iter 10 with convergence_reason='criterion' status=0 but max_error=0.463 kl=0.637. The improvement rule (check_convergence) fires because kl is frozen at 0.637 from iter 1 (bounds block all progress) -> 'no improvement' -> mark_converged -> RK_OK. This is scale-blindness analogous to eb79.16/eb79.22 (logit): the improvement rule cannot distinguish converged-at-0 from stuck-at-0.637. Correct classification is STALL (constrained optimum, margins unmet). NOTE: max_error itself is honest (0.463); only the STATUS is wrong. The kxna.5 wkl_flat shortcut (now removed, commit pending) was NOT the cause — it is near-unreachable (check_convergence fires first).

## How
- Mirror eb79.22 (logit): mark_converged should require ABSOLUTE feasibility (max marginal residual errRp <= feasibility tol); a metric-plateau WITHOUT feasibility stays STALL, not RK_OK.
- Decide the feasibility tolerance (errRp threshold) — design decision, verify no ripple across existing raking tests that expect RK_OK on feasible plateaus (feasible problems meet margins -> unaffected).
- RED fixture: the set.seed(88) fixture above; assert status != 0 (STALL) when max_error > 0.1.
- Full R + Python parity + stepstone gate.
close_reason: All 3 children shipped (5e347b5). The box-feasibility certificate (jy0m.1) is the SOTA realization of the parent's 'require absolute feasibility for RK_OK' — a rigorous per-margin necessary condition (zero fitted threshold) superior to the errRp-only bar. Flat + SRAA both classify bounds-blocked plateaus as STALL(5). R 975/0 Py 136/0.

# CR-A7: Close metric=l1_weight phantom-zero spurious-OK for non-populating solvers
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Eliminate the spurious-convergence hole where `convergence=list(metric="l1_weight")` causes instant/early false-OK for solvers that never populate `CellMetrics.l1`. In scope: whichever of `src/greenkhorn.cpp`, `src/chebyshev.cpp` (and any other solver that builds a convergence `CellMetrics` without setting `l1`) plus possibly `src/validation.cpp`. Out of scope: `marginal_kl` (fixed under mxcl.3, commit 4beb613); raking/sinkhorn (already populate `l1`).
* **Why:** `CellMetrics.l1` defaults to `0.0` (calib_dispatch.hpp:126) and is written ONLY by `raking.cpp:490` and `sinkhorn.cpp:205`. `compute_cell_metrics` does NOT compute `l1` (it is obs-level Σ_i|w_out−w_in|/n, not a cell-level metric). So greenkhorn/chebyshev with `metric="l1_weight"` pass `m.l1 = 0.0` (phantom) to `select_metric` → `check_convergence` IMPROVEMENT rule (`curr <= 1e-15`) / THRESHOLD (`curr < tol`) instant-fires → false RK_OK on uncalibrated weights. Same bug class as the marginal_kl hole (mxcl.3) but l1 cannot be closed the same way (it is obs-level, not derivable in cell-level `compute_cell_metrics`). Confidence 90 (l1 writers enumerated by grep; marginal_kl analog verified in mxcl.3).
* **Reference Data:** l1 writers: `raking.cpp:490`, `sinkhorn.cpp:205` (both set the real obs-level value before their convergence check → NOT affected). Non-populating solvers reaching `metric="l1_weight"`: greenkhorn, chebyshev (verify each actually consumes `select_metric`/`check_convergence` with an unpopulated `l1`). `validation.cpp:~116` accepts `metric ∈ [0,6]` for ALL algorithms unconditionally (its `alg` param is dead code — natural home for a per-solver rejection). Discovered during mxcl.3 fable review.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` (CellMetrics:126 `l1`, select_metric convenience:168), `src/raking.cpp:490` + `src/sinkhorn.cpp:205` (correct l1 population, reference), `src/greenkhorn.cpp` + `src/chebyshev.cpp` (convergence CellMetrics build — do they set l1? if not, they are affected), `src/validation.cpp` (dead `alg` param).
* **Format:** C++ source; testthat parity of RED fixture.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Choose ONE: (a) compute the real obs-level `l1` in greenkhorn/chebyshev where cheap and set it on the convergence CellMetrics (mirrors raking/sinkhorn); OR (b) reject `metric="l1_weight"` at `validate_calibrate_inputs` for solvers that do not populate it (use the dead `alg` param; update `harvest.R` roxygen in the same commit); OR (c) default `CellMetrics.l1` to +inf so an unpopulated l1 never spuriously converges (fail-safe) — but FIRST verify raking/sinkhorn always set l1 BEFORE their check (else they regress to non-convergence). Do NOT touch marginal_kl (done) or the oris remap. |
| **Format** | Match existing style; pathspec-form commits; no AI attribution. |
| **Boundary** | Solver files that omit l1 + optionally validation.cpp + harvest.R docs. Do not touch raking/sinkhorn l1 logic. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. RED test: greenkhorn (and chebyshev) with `metric="l1_weight"` on an uncalibrated fixture returns spurious early/instant RK_OK (achieved margins far from target) — mirror the mxcl.3 test (test-select-metric-struct.R). Confirm currently RED.
2. Verify each candidate solver's convergence path: does it pass an unpopulated `m.l1` to select_metric/check_convergence? (greenkhorn/chebyshev suspected; confirm.)
3. Verify raking (raking.cpp:490) and sinkhorn (sinkhorn.cpp:205) set l1 BEFORE their check (guards option (c)).
4. Apply chosen fix; if option (b), update harvest.R roxygen same commit.
5. RED test now GREEN (l1_weight either calibrates properly or is cleanly rejected). Confirm raking/sinkhorn l1_weight behavior UNCHANGED.
6. `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`, devtools::test() 0 FAIL, `cd python && pytest` green.

# CR-C8: Fix logit Armijo failure accepting untested step
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** When logit's Armijo line search exhausts all 10 halvings without an accepted trial, the solver must accept the best TESTED trial step (argmin residual over all tested trials), not an 11th, never-evaluated, further-halved step size. Out of scope: changing the halving schedule or max-halvings count (10).
* **Why:** logit_calib.cpp:343-378 halves the step 10 times; when all 10 fail Armijo, the code halves ONE MORE time past the last tested value and then does `lambda[j] += alpha*b[j]` unconditionally — accepting a step that was never evaluated for descent. The code comment claims "accepting best available" but the actually-discarded value is the best TESTED trial; the accepted step can increase the residual.
* **Reference Data:** logit_calib.cpp:343-378 — 10 failed halvings, then one more halving past the last tested value, then unconditional acceptance.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `src/logit_calib.cpp` lines 343-378 (Armijo loop and fallback-acceptance block).
* **Format:** C++17; testthat R fixture (TDD red-first).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Track argmin residual (or argmin Armijo merit value, whichever the loop already computes per trial) over the 10 TESTED trial step sizes during the halving loop — do not add an 11th untested halving. On exhaustion, accept the tracked argmin-trial `lambda`/`alpha` values directly (reuse values already computed in the loop, no re-evaluation). |
| **Global** | Absolute-feasibility OK gate stays sufficient (eb79.16/18/22/23) — this ticket does not touch the OK gate, only what gets accepted when Armijo fails. Min-norm warm-start untouched. This ticket is logically adjacent to CR-C7 (both touch logit_calib.cpp's iteration loop) but must be implemented and tested as an independent, separately-committable change — do not bundle the two fixes into one commit. greg out of scope; finalize_weights N/A; fixture changes need arithmetic proof. |
| **Format** | Match existing loop variable naming; correct/remove the misleading "accepting best available" comment to reflect actual (fixed) behavior; no AI attribution; explicit file staging. |
| **Boundary** | Touch only `src/logit_calib.cpp` lines ~343-378 (the Armijo fallback block). Do not touch CR-C7's best-iterate tracking (:289-293/:401-409/:424/:431) or CR-C9's saturation guard in this ticket. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

Assert the accepted step's residual is <= the residual of every one of the 10 tested trials (i.e. it IS one of the tested trials, not a further-halved untested one). Confirm it FAILS against current code (residual increases or doesn't match any tested trial).
2. Add trial tracking (argmin over the loop's own per-trial residual/merit value — reuse what's already computed each iteration of the halving loop) inside the existing 10-halving loop.
3. Replace the fallback block (11th halving + unconditional accept) with: on loop exhaustion, set `lambda[j]`/`alpha` from the tracked argmin trial.

5. Rebuild (`R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`), confirm the new fixture passes.
6. Run full `devtools::test()` — confirm no regressions to cases where Armijo succeeds within 10 halvings (unaffected by this change) and to CR-C7's fixture if already landed (residual tracking there should now see monotonically-behaved trial residuals).
7. Run Python parity tests for logit.

title: Fix logit_calib step-norm guard to use signed Δz
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** logit_calib.cpp:242-249 sums |Δλ| per margin (over-estimates |Δz| by triangle inequality), throttling alpha; use signed sum then fabs. IN: inner loop. OUT: identical fixed point, fewer iterations.
* **Why:** Actual cell coord is signed z=Σ_k λ[k,g] (verified :258-260). Abs-sum inflates max_delta_z whenever a cell has ≥2 active margins (every K≥2 problem) → alpha smaller than needed → slow Newton convergence.
* **Reference Data:** :246 `if (g>=0 && g<st.cat_counts[k]) dz += std::abs(b[cat_offset[k]+g]);`. Compare :260 `z += lambda_trial[cat_offset[k]+g];` (signed).
* **Philosophy:** Goldfish Memory — all here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** delta_lambda vector b after cholesky_solve.
* **Format:** C++ nested loop over cells×margins.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | dz = signed Σ_k b[cat_offset[k]+g]; max_delta_z = max(|dz|). Fixed point MUST be unchanged. |
| **Format** | Match z-accumulation pattern at :258-260. |
| **Boundary** | Only :243-248. kMaxDeltaZ cap unchanged. |
| **Collinearity (agy RISK)** | Signed-Δz drops the abs-sum's incidental per-margin-magnitude cap → risk of dual λ drift along null space on collinear margins → cancellation in z_c. MUST regression-test a collinear K≥6 logit fixture: converged weights + max|λ| unchanged vs pre-fix. Existing ridge (adaptive LDLT eps + init max_lambda≤10) is the primary guard; if the fixture shows λ blowup, ADD an auxiliary per-margin cap alongside the signed-Δz net cap rather than reverting. |
| **Tone** | Surgical. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. :243 keep `double dz = 0.0;`
2. :246 → `if (g>=0 && g<st.cat_counts[k]) dz += b[cat_offset[k]+g];` (drop std::abs)
3. :248 → `max_delta_z = std::max(max_delta_z, std::fabs(dz));`
4. R CMD INSTALL; verify converged weights identical to pre-change (fixed point invariant), iteration count ≤ before on a K≥2 logit fixture.
5. Collinear regression: run a K≥6 collinear-margin logit fixture; assert converged weights identical AND max|λ| not inflated vs pre-fix. If inflated, add auxiliary per-margin cap.
6. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)

```toon
success: bool

  converged_weights_identical: bool
  iters_before: int
  iters_after: int
  collinear_maxlambda_before: float
  collinear_maxlambda_after: float
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done

- [ ] Converged weights identical (fixed point invariant proven on a fixture)
- [ ] Iteration count not worse
- [ ] Collinear K≥6 fixture: max|λ| not inflated (agy RISK closed); else auxiliary per-margin cap added
- [ ] R+Python parity green

Mitigation already present: adaptive LDLT ridge (eps=max(1e-10,max_b/kMaxDeltaZ)) + init max_lambda<=10 (logit_calib.cpp, commit d0757d7). Guard folded into DoD below.

description:
# Rank1: unlock omega>1 (configurable omega_max, recovery past 1.0)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Allow ORIS's adaptive omega to exceed 1.0 up to a configurable `omega_max`, reaching the proven-accelerating window omega in (1,2); IN = wire existing omega_max into the recovery clamp + default selection + benchmark; OUT = spectral estimator (sibling Rank2), greenkhorn/sinkhorn, any fixed-point/bounds/enum/API change.
* **Why:** The solver named "over-relaxed" never over-relaxes — recovery is capped at 1.0; this is the single highest-impact, lowest-risk fix.
* **Eval metric:** The statistic these solvers MINIMIZE / converge on is the KL objective `marginal_kl` (configured convergence metric for oris, `R/harvest.R:349-355`). Over-relaxation changes only the iteration PATH, not the fixed point — so evaluate: (1) ITERATIONS to reach the configured `marginal_kl` convergence criterion = the speed win; (2) `marginal_kl` objective value + converged weights at the fixed point = correctness (must match baseline). `max_err`/errRp is the FEASIBILITY residual only (margins satisfied), NOT the evaluation statistic.
* **Reference Data:** `src/oris.cpp:837` `sor_omega[k]=std::min(1.0, sor_omega[k]*kSorRecoveryGrowth)` (SRAA path) and `:1564` (flat path); `omega_init=1.0` at `:396`; `sor_cfg` in `src/types.hpp`; Thibault 2021 proves global convergence for all omega in (0,2) (`docs/methods/oris.md`, refs.bib thibault2021overrelaxed).
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** stepstone benchmark fixtures; `tests/testthat` suite; Python parity harness; the two recovery-clamp sites + `sor_cfg`.
* **Format:** C++ edits to `src/oris.cpp` + `src/types.hpp`; experiment results as the TOON block in Section V.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |

title: ORIS: unlock true over-relaxation (omega>1) + spectral optimal-omega
description:
# Epic: ORIS true over-relaxation (omega>1) + spectral optimal-omega

## Goal
Make ORIS actually over-relax: lift the omega recovery cap from 1.0 into the proven-accelerating window omega in (1,2), then replace the heuristic omega nudge with the spectral optimal-omega of Lehmann et al. 2022.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Rank1 (omega>1 unlock) ships: build clean, R tests green, parity rtol=1e-6 green, documented iteration reduction on >=1 well-conditioned stepstone config, ZERO max_error regression.
- [ ] Rank2 (spectral omega_opt) ships or is documented NO-GO vs Rank1 fixed omega_max, with benchmark numbers.
- [ ] Fixed point unchanged on all fixtures (converged weights within 1e-8 AND converged marginal_kl within 1e-9 of baseline) — omega changes step length only. Evaluation statistic = marginal_kl (the KL objective these solvers minimize) + iterations-to-converge; max_err is feasibility only.
- [ ] Net step exponent alpha*eff_omega stays in (0,2) on every logged iteration (proven-safe window, Thibault 2021).
- [ ] Both child tickets closed; learnings saved via `bd remember`.

## Context & Background
Despite the name "Over-Relaxed Iterative Scaling," the code never over-relaxes: both omega-adaptation paths cap recovery at `std::min(1.0, ...)` (`src/oris.cpp:837` SRAA path, `:1564` flat path) and `omega_init=1.0`, so omega only moves in [0.3,1.0] (pure under-relaxation/oscillation damping). The proven acceleration window omega in (1,2) is unreachable — the canonical sources now cited in `docs/methods/oris.md` (Thibault et al. 2021: global convergence for all omega in (0,2); Lehmann et al. 2022: optimal omega from the residual ratio) describe a capability the implementation forfeits. Expected payoff: 2-4x fewer iterations on well-conditioned calibration at zero correctness risk. North star: ORIS stays a pure fixed-point map (Anderson-accelerable); enum values, bounds semantics, and public API are frozen.

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Two atomic child tasks, sequential: Rank1 unlocks omega>1 (configurable omega_max + recovery past 1.0); Rank2 (BLOCKED-BY Rank1) adds the spectral omega_opt estimator. Each child is hermetic (full file/line refs, guards, TOON experiment schema, gate checklist). Global guards for both: fixed point invariant, alpha*eff_omega in (0,2), omega=1 fast-path preserved, greedy-scheduler runs flagged as outside the full-sweep proof. Every child ends with the experiment gate (build + R tests + parity + stepstone no-regression) before close.
close_reason: Rank1 GO (omega_max=1.5, 1.25x speedup). Rank2 NO-GO (Lehmann spectral fails on bounded operator). omega_mode_id wired for future experiments.

title: chebyshev.cpp Mehrotra Phase-B 2nd-order proxy not standard
description: src/chebyshev.cpp:501,514,586 — Phase-B uses ad-hoc 2nd-order proxy that does not match canonical Mehrotra centering correction; on stiff fixtures yields wrong sigma. Mechanism: replace proxy with canonical Mehrotra predictor-corrector (sigma=(mu_aff/mu)^3) using affine duality measure mu_aff. Forbidden: tuning proxy constants; weakening test tolerance to mask divergence. Audit: numeric trace vs MATLAB/IPOPT reference on stepstone fixture; rtol=1e-6 on final weights for 3 stiff fixtures.
notes: 2026-05-08 investigation: line 492 sigma=(mu_aff/mu)^3 IS canonical Mehrotra. Issue is corrector terms at lines 501-502, 514-515: corr_up = y_up*dS_aff + y_up*dS_aff^2/s_up = y_up*dS_aff*(1 + dS_aff/s_up). Standard Mehrotra cross-term is dS_aff*dY_aff. Current code substitutes dY_aff with linearization but sign appears inverted (linearization dY_aff ≈ -y*dS/s gives -y*dS^2/s; code has +y*dS^2/s). Either: (a) sign error, OR (b) different convention requiring full derivation against canonical IPM implementation. Spec audit demands MATLAB/IPOPT reference trace on stepstone fixture before fix lands. Defer until reference infra available; chebyshev already has documented divergence in leafblower-8u2y which may share root cause. Risk of fix-without-reference: regression on tested fixtures.
close_reason: not-a-bug after rigorous re-derivation. Mehrotra corrector with slack-dual complementarity (s*y=mu): standard Newton linearization gives s*dY + y*dS = -s*y + sigma*mu - dS_aff*dY_aff. When dY_aff is NOT computed in Phase A (only primal direction solved, true here for chebyshev), eliminate via complementarity row: dY_aff = (-s*y - y*dS_aff)/s = -y - (y/s)*dS_aff. Then cross-term = dS_aff * dY_aff = dS*(-y - (y/s)*dS) = -y*dS - (y/s)*dS^2. Substituting into corrector RHS: rmu_B = -s*y + sigma*mu - (-y*dS - (y/s)*dS^2) = -s*y + sigma*mu + y*dS + (y/s)*dS^2. Current code at chebyshev.cpp:501-503: corr_up = y*dS_aff + y*dS_aff^2/s; rmu_B = sigma*mu - s*y + corr_up. EXACTLY matches canonical form. Original review error: assumed dY ~ -(y/s)*dS only (missing the -y constant from elimination of full row). The +y*dS^2/s sign is correct, NOT inverted. Ref: Wright Primal-Dual IPM 1997 ch.10 + Mehrotra 1992 SIAM. Note: chebyshev R-vs-Python divergence (8u2y) is unrelated to corrector form per project memory (cell-aggregation float-op-order).

title: T-X: Remediation-wave release prep — version bump 0.2.0→0.2.1 + NEWS
description:
# T-X: Remediation-wave release prep — version bump 0.2.0→0.2.1 + NEWS
**Status:** `BLOCKED_ON: T-M, T-N, T-O, T-P, T-Q, T-R, T-S, T-T, T-U, T-V, T-W` (all 11 prior remediation tickets)
**Mechanism:** Bump DESCRIPTION + python/pyproject.toml from 0.2.0 to 0.2.1 (PATCH bump — bug fixes only, no new API surface); append NEWS.md entry for remediation wave.
**Forbidden:** minor bump (no new public API); silently bundling unrelated changes; modifying code files (release metadata only).
**Audit:** versions match between DESCRIPTION and pyproject.toml; `R CMD check --as-cran` baseline preserved; pytest green.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: T-M..T-W all merged. Out: 0.2.1 release with synced versions + NEWS bullets covering algorithmic correction (T-M), tripwire extensions (T-N, T-Q), metric correction (T-O), Σw=N diagnostic (T-P), code-cleanup (T-R, T-S, T-T), Python finiteness (T-U), spec v4 + gate alignment (T-V, T-W).
* **Why:** Per CLAUDE.md "Version sync: bump DESCRIPTION AND python/pyproject.toml manually — no automation". Remediation wave touches algorithm correctness; 0.2.0 ships are silently buggy and 0.2.1 is the corrected release.
* **Reference Data:** `DESCRIPTION` Version field; `python/pyproject.toml` version; `NEWS.md` head.

## II. Input Specification
* Current versions: 0.2.0 in both files.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | PATCH bump (0.2.0 → 0.2.1) — fixes only, no new public API. Both files MUST move identical version string. |
| **Format** | NEWS.md follows existing convention. Reference issues `leafblower-6ycz.1.13` through `.1.23` and code-review pass commit. |
| **Boundary** | TOUCH ONLY: DESCRIPTION, python/pyproject.toml, NEWS.md. DO NOT modify code. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Bump DESCRIPTION Version: 0.2.0 → 0.2.1.
2. Bump python/pyproject.toml version: 0.2.0 → 0.2.1.
3. Append NEWS.md entry under new version header `# leafblower 0.2.1 (DATE)`:
   - **Bug fixes:**
     - Stage-1 hierarchical calibration now correctly fits coarse margins only (was: all margins) — affects RAKING/SINKHORN/GREENKHORN (`6ycz.1.13`).
     - Cell-aggregate Stage-1 multiplier replaces last-obs overwrite for sparse-cell inheritance (`6ycz.1.13`).
     - `outer_residual_final` now reports spec §8 `Σ|w·X − target|/N` (was: cell-balance proxy) (`6ycz.1.15`).
     - `hier_levels_used` returns 2 when hierarchical enabled (was: 1) (`6ycz.1.14`).
     - `outer_iterations_used` returns -1 in `mode="exact"` (was: 1) (`6ycz.1.17`).
     - Σw=N invariant violations now surfaced via `result$message` + `Rprintf` warning (`6ycz.1.16`).
     - Python `HierarchicalConfig` rejects non-finite `outer_tol` (`6ycz.1.21`).
   - **Internal:**
     - Drop duplicate `LBW_MAX_HIER_CELLS` define (`6ycz.1.18`).
     - Right-size `fine_gids_buf` to `max_n_per_cell` (`6ycz.1.19`).
     - `CalibState` sub-state explicit field-by-field init (`6ycz.1.20`).
   - **Test / docs:**
     - Spec §8 amendment v4 (preserves v1/v2/v3 history) (`6ycz.1.22`, `6ycz.1.23`).
     - Stepstone regression gate aligned with spec residual contract (`6ycz.1.22`).
     - Vignette Stage-1 description corrected (`6ycz.1.13`).
4. Run `bd preflight` — fix any lint/stale items unrelated to T-X-scope.
5. Run `R CMD check --as-cran .` — baseline preserved.
6. Run `pytest python/` — green.
7. Final identity check: grep both version strings.

# T-P: Surface Σw=N gate violation via result.message + Rprintf (FIX-4)

**Audit:** new test `test-sigmaw-violation-diagnostic.R` asserts message contains "Σw=N invariant violated" AND status is preserved (NOT clobbered to RK_OK if solver returned otherwise; NOT clobbered to error code).

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: `calib_dispatch.hpp:698` (RK_OK exit), `src/raking.cpp:713` (Strategy B), `src/sinkhorn.cpp:469`, `src/greenkhorn.cpp:450`. Out: violation surfaced via `res.base.message` + `Rprintf`.
* **Why:** Bool return discarded; silent invariant violation. Σw=N foundational to bounds_mode water-fill (CLAUDE.md). `res.base.message` field exists at `leafblower.h:122` (`char message[256]`).
* **Reference Data:** rk_result_t.message at leafblower.h:122; existing `Rprintf` usage in src/r_bridge.cpp.

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Add overload `inline std::pair<bool, double> enforce_sigmaw_eq_n_diag(const std::vector<double>& weights, int N) noexcept` returning `(passed, |Σw − N|)`. Format message: `"Sigmaw=N violated: |Σw - N| = %.3e (tol = N·1e-12 = %.3e)"`. snprintf into `result.message` ONLY if message currently empty (`result.message[0] == '\0'`); otherwise append after concatenation guard. STATUS NOT CHANGED — invariant violation is a diagnostic, not a status flip. |
| **Boundary** | TOUCH ONLY: `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` (one site at 698 + new overload near enforce_sigmaw_eq_n at line 567); `src/raking.cpp:713`; `src/sinkhorn.cpp:469`; `src/greenkhorn.cpp:450`; new test. |

For test, set flag, call harvest, verify `attr(res, "result")$message` regex-matches "Σw=N violated"; AND verify status is preserved (e.g., RK_OK or whatever solver returned).

2. Add overload `enforce_sigmaw_eq_n_diag` near line 567 in `src/calib_dispatch.hpp`.
3. At each of 4 sites:

   ```cpp
       std::snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "Sigmaw=N violated: |Σw - N| = %.3e (tol = N·1e-12 = %.3e)", dev, static_cast<double>(N) * 1e-12);
   ```

title: T-O: outer_residual_final = spec §8 coarse-margin residual (FIX-5)
description:
# T-O: outer_residual_final = spec §8 coarse-margin residual (FIX-5)
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** Pass coarse `targets[]` + `group_ids[][]` + `cat_counts[]` into `outer_iterate_strategy_a`; replace `max |Σw_cell[c]/N − 1/K_cells|` cell-balance proxy with `Σ|w·X_coarse − target_coarse|/N`.
**Forbidden:** computing on fine margins; max-norm (spec is L1); changing `outer_tol` semantics.
**Audit:** new test `test-outer-residual-metric.R` matches hand-computed metric to 1e-14 across ≥3 seeds.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: `outer_iterate_strategy_a` template at `src/calib_dispatch.hpp:627-712` (lines 660-672 are the metric compute) + 3 caller sites. Out: `out.residual_final` = spec-defined `(Σ_{k ∈ coarse} Σ_{j ∈ cats(k)} |Σ_i w_i·1[X_ki=j] − target_kj|) / N`.
* **Why:** Code computes cell-balance proxy `max_c |Σw_cell[c]/N − 1/K_cells|`. Spec §8 measures L1-over-margins. Returned via `res$outer_residual_final` and tested against `outer_tol=1e-4`. Misleading.
* **Reference Data:** spec §8 paragraph 190; existing per-solver `compute_l1_residual` style — locate via grep before implementation. Confirm `targets[k][j]` is proportion (per existing solver convention) vs count.
* **Philosophy:** Atomic metric correction. Independent of T-M.

## II. Input Specification
* `outer_iterate_strategy_a` signature extends with: `const double* const* coarse_targets`, `const int32_t* const* coarse_gids`, `const int* coarse_cats_counts`, `int K_coarse`.
* Callers (raking/sinkhorn/greenkhorn `_hierarchical`) build these from `st.targets`, `st.group_ids`, `st.cat_counts`, `coarse_idx`.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | `residual = (1/N) · Σ_{k ∈ coarse} Σ_{j=0..cat_counts[k]-1} |achieved_kj − target_kj|`. Achievement: `achieved_kj = Σ_i weights[i] · 1[group_ids[k][i] == j]`. Target convention: read existing solver code to confirm proportion-scaled (`targets[k][j] * N`) vs count-scaled. |
| **Boundary** | TOUCH ONLY: `src/calib_dispatch.hpp:627-712` (metric region 660-672 + signature); `src/raking.cpp` outer-call site (~688-693); `src/sinkhorn.cpp` (~444-449); `src/greenkhorn.cpp` (~412-417); new `tests/testthat/test-outer-residual-metric.R`. |
| **Lambda [&]** | New coarse arrays in callers must be declared BEFORE any `[&]` lambda. |
| **Performance** | `O(N · K_coarse + Σ cat_counts[coarse])` per iter; bounded by full-data sweep cost. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. **Test FIRST**: `test-outer-residual-metric.R` — small DGP × 3 seeds; manually compute `Σ|w·X_coarse − target_coarse|/N` from output weights; expect equals `attr(res, "result")$outer_residual_final` within 1e-12. Verify FAIL on current code (proxy metric differs by orders of magnitude).
2. Grep convention: `grep -n "compute_l1_residual\|target_count\|target_prop" src/raking.cpp` to confirm `targets[k][j]` semantics.
3. Extend template signature with 4 new params at `outer_iterate_strategy_a` definition.
4. Replace lines 660-672 with spec metric:
   ```cpp
   double residual = 0.0;
   for (int k = 0; k < K_coarse; k++) {
       const int C = coarse_cats_counts[k];
       std::vector<double> ach(C, 0.0);
       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) { int32_t j = coarse_gids[k][i]; if (j >= 0 && j < C) ach[j] += weights[i]; }
       for (int j = 0; j < C; j++) residual += std::fabs(ach[j] - coarse_targets[k][j] * static_cast<double>(N));
   }
   residual /= static_cast<double>(N);
   ```
5. Build coarse arrays in each caller before invoking `outer_iterate_strategy_a` (function-scope storage, declared before any [&] lambda).
6. Verify: build + tests RED→GREEN.
7. Re-baseline stepstone gate (informs T-V).

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id":"T-O","success":true,"data":{"files_modified":["src/calib_dispatch.hpp","src/raking.cpp","src/sinkhorn.cpp","src/greenkhorn.cpp"],"tests_added":["tests/testthat/test-outer-residual-metric.R"],"metric_change":{"old":"max_c |Σw_cell[c]/N - 1/K_cells|","new":"Σ|w·X_coarse - target_coarse|/N"},"blocks":"leafblower-6ycz.1.22 (T-V)"},"error_log":null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Spec metric test added BEFORE fix; RED across ≥3 seeds.
- [ ] Template signature extended at definition + all 3 call sites.
- [ ] Lambda [&] rule preserved.
- [ ] Build + tests + Python parity all pass.
- [ ] Stepstone regression gate value re-baselined (data feeds T-V).
- [ ] No hallucination.

title: fix(ieppa): revisit SOR default — hurts in 4/9 design conditions including 2.92x regression at loose bounds
description:
## Evidence (from leafblower-p46l sweep, 2026-05-06)
SOR default (auto=TRUE, omega_min=0.3) measured across 3×3 grid:

HURTS (4/9 = 44%):
- tight(2)×low(3):   SOR 430 iters vs off 40 iters (+975%), time 1.43x
- loose(10)×low(3):  SOR 60 iters = off, time 1.33x (overhead only)
- loose(10)×medium(6): SOR 500 vs off 340 iters (+47%), time 1.14x
- loose(10)×high(9): SOR 470 vs off 50 iters (+840%), time 2.92x SEVERE

HELPS (1/9):
- tight(2)×medium(6): SOR 160 vs off 390 iters (-59%), time 0.93x

NEUTRAL (4/9): medium bounds or high-K tight (marginal).

## Root cause hypothesis
SOR omega estimator misreads oscillation signal when max_weight is loose — no actual
weight clamping occurs so the 'oscillation' SOR detects is numerical noise. SOR then
amplifies instead of dampens.

## Options
A. Change default to sor=NULL (off) — safe, predictable, user opt-in
B. Add activation gate: only enable SOR auto when n_clamped > 0 (actual boundary pressure)
C. Reduce default omega_min from 0.3 to 0.1 to limit damage when incorrectly activated
D. Keep default but fix the omega estimator to detect false-positive oscillation

## DoD
- [ ] Option chosen and implemented (not just decided)
- [ ] sor_sweep.R re-run confirms no hurts conditions (or acceptable trade-off documented)
- [ ] devtools::test() passes
- [ ] BREAKING CHANGE: document default change in NEWS.md if sor=NULL becomes default
close_reason: SOR default changed to NULL. 557 tests pass. 5 files changed. Commit b12d07e on master.

title: fix(R): compute_sparseness_diag O(n×levels) — apply table() per variable (R parity with q795)
description:
## I. Objective
R/harvest.R::compute_sparseness_diag() calls sum(data[[v]] == lv, na.rm=TRUE) per level —
O(n × total_levels). Python got value_counts() hoist in q795 but R was never updated.
IN: R/harvest.R function compute_sparseness_diag  OUT: same function, O(n×K) via table().

## II. Input
File: R/harvest.R, function compute_sparseness_diag (~lines 701-715)
Context: stepstone fulldata has 688+ (variable, level) pairs → 688 O(n) comparisons per harvest().
Python q795 fix: value_counts() once per variable, then O(1) dict lookup per level.
R equivalent: table(data[[v]]) once per variable, then named-integer lookup per level.

## III. Guards
- Return type unchanged: named list of lists with level, T_kj, n_kj fields
- table() omits NA by default — consistent with na.rm=TRUE behavior in original sum()
- Level names may be non-character in targets (numeric, factor) — must coerce via as.character(lv)
- Missing levels (in target but not in data) → n_kj = 0L (same as original)
- Must not change function signature

## IV. Logic
Old (WRONG — O(n × total_levels)):
  for (lv in names(target[[v]])) {
    T_kj <- target[[v]][[lv]]
    n_kj <- sum(data[[v]] == lv, na.rm = TRUE)

New (CORRECT — O(n × K)):
  for (v in names(target)) {
    if (!v %in% names(data)) next
    counts <- table(data[[v]])                        # ONE pass per variable
    for (lv in names(target[[v]])) {
      T_kj <- target[[v]][[lv]]
      n_kj  <- as.integer(counts[as.character(lv)])
      n_kj  <- if (is.na(n_kj)) 0L else n_kj

## V. Schema
No schema change. Return type: list of lists, each entry list(level=lv, T_kj=T_kj, n_kj=n_kj).

## VI. DoD
- [ ] No sum(data[[v]] == lv) inside inner loop
- [ ] table() called once per variable, outside inner level loop
- [ ] Devtools::test() passes (all testthat tests)
- [ ] allmethod_bench.R re-run: R ieppa time drops by 300-1000ms vs pre-fix baseline
close_reason: table() hoisted outside inner loop at R/harvest.R:705. Tests: FAIL 1 (pre-existing) | PASS 556. Commit on fix/r-bench-parity.

IN: python/leafblower/_harvest.py  OUT: same file, per-method metric applied when no explicit metric given.

## II. Input
File: python/leafblower/_harvest.py
R reference: R/harvest.R lines 308-331 (per-method conv$metric switch after parse_convergence and method assignment)
Order in R: map_method() at line 303 → parse_convergence() at line 304 → switch at lines 314-331.
Order in Python: _parse_convergence() at line 271 → method_lc at line 290 → params dict at line 401.
Insert window: lines 290-401 (after method_lc, before params dict).

## III. Guards
- Only override when NO explicit metric key: check convergence dict for 'metric', 'improvement', 'pct', 'absolute'
- User-explicit metric ALWAYS wins
- Insert AFTER line 290 (method_lc = method.lower()), BEFORE line 401 (params dict)
- chebyshev and logit intentionally NOT in _METHOD_DEFAULT_METRIC — no entry means no override, keeps
  max_err default from _parse_convergence. This is correct: chebyshev minimizes L-inf = max_err; logit
  has no natural KL. Matches R harvest.R:329 fallback (conv$metric = keep default).
- _METRIC_MAP already maps all strings to ints (line 20-23). metric is already int post-parse. Reassignment fine.

## IV. Logic
After line 290 (method_lc assignment), insert:

    _conv = convergence or {}
    _no_explicit_metric = not any(
        k in _conv for k in ('metric', 'improvement', 'pct', 'absolute')
    )
    if _no_explicit_metric:
        _METHOD_DEFAULT_METRIC = {
            'ieppa': 'marginal_kl', 'ieppa_soft': 'marginal_kl',
            'raking': 'kl', 'greenkhorn': 'kl',
            'sinkhorn': 'kl', 'newton_kl': 'kl',
            'greg': 'chi2',
            # chebyshev: omitted — keeps max_err (L-inf is its natural objective)
            # logit: omitted — keeps max_err (no natural KL objective)
        }
        _m = _METHOD_DEFAULT_METRIC.get(method_lc)
        if _m is not None:
            metric = _METRIC_MAP[_m]

## V. Schema
No schema change. metric (int) already in params['metric'].

## VI. DoD
- [ ] harvest(df, tgt, method='ieppa', convergence={'tol':1e-4}) — verify params['metric'] == 6 (marginal_kl)
- [ ] harvest(df, tgt, method='raking', convergence={'tol':1e-4}) — verify params['metric'] == 2 (kl)

title: perf(python): fix _compute_sparseness_diag O(n×total_levels) astype(str) regression
description:
## I. Objective
Fix Python _harvest.py::_compute_sparseness_diag() which calls df[v].astype(str) inside the inner
per-level loop, allocating a fresh 1.58M-row string Series per (variable, level) pair.
IN: python/leafblower/_harvest.py  OUT: same file, function fixed, Python benchmark 20-50% faster than R.

## II. Input
File: python/leafblower/_harvest.py
Function: _compute_sparseness_diag (lines ~34-46)
Context: Called once per harvest() invocation before C solver. stepstone fulldata (9 margins, 688+
sparse (var,level) pairs) — benchmark shows ALL Python methods cluster at 47-72s vs R 5-16s:
constant per-method overhead = sparseness diagnostic cost (688 astype(str) calls x ~50ms = ~34s).

Secondary overhead (smaller): group_ids encoding at lines ~370-372 also calls col.astype(str) per
variable (9 calls total for 9 margins). Not the primary bottleneck but document if found.

## III. Guards
- MUST NOT change the function signature or return type
- Return value must be identical dict structure: {varname: [{level, T_kj, n_kj}, ...]}
- Must handle missing columns (v not in df.columns) -> skip
- Must use value_counts(dropna=True) for NA-safe counting (mirrors R na.rm=TRUE)
- level keys in targets may be non-string (int, etc.) — must str() before lookup
- astype(str) on any dtype (object, category, int) must produce same counts as R data[[v]] == lv

## IV. Logic
OLD (WRONG — O(n x total_levels)):
    for v, tgt in targets.items():
        for level, T_kj in tgt.items():
            n_kj = int((df[v].astype(str) == str(level)).sum())

NEW (CORRECT — O(n x K) where K = number of variables):
    for v, tgt in targets.items():
        if v not in df.columns:
            continue
        counts = df[v].astype(str).value_counts(dropna=True)  # once per variable
        for level, T_kj in tgt.items():
            n_kj = int(counts.get(str(level), 0))
            if T_kj < cat_threshold or n_kj < obs_threshold:
                sparse_cats.setdefault(v, []).append(
                    {'level': level, 'T_kj': T_kj, 'n_kj': n_kj}
                )

## V. Schema
No schema changes. Function return type unchanged:
{varname: [{level: any, T_kj: float, n_kj: int}, ...]}

## VI. DoD
- [ ] _compute_sparseness_diag has value_counts() call OUTSIDE inner level loop
- [ ] No astype(str) inside inner level loop
- [ ] Python allmethod_bench.R-equivalent: all converged methods <= 15s wall time (removes ~34s diagnostic overhead)
- [ ] Warning count unchanged for stepstone fulldata (688 sparse categories detected)
- [ ] cd python && pytest passes
notes: DoD timing corrected: ≤25s (not ≤15s). After removing ~34s diagnostic overhead, iterative-method Python wall time ~15-20s (still 2x slower than R due to bridge overhead investigated in leafblower-x2b3). Bulk-compute methods (newton_kl, chebyshev) already Python-faster and unaffected.
close_reason: Fixed: value_counts() hoisted outside inner level loop. Commit on fix/python-harvest-parity.

title: bug(python): sor=None disables SOR by default, violating R parity contract (NEWS.md:107)
description:
## Root cause
_harvest.py:116 default is sor: Optional[Dict] = None. _parse_sor(None) returns (0, 0, ...) = SOR disabled. But R/harvest.R:216 defaults to sor=list(auto=TRUE, omega_min=0.3) = SOR enabled. NEWS.md:101 documents 'default: auto-enabled' and NEWS.md:107 documents 'Python harvest() updated with matching sor arguments.' Both parity claims are broken.

## Impact
Python ieppa gets different convergence path than R ieppa on identical inputs. Confirmed: at tol=1e-3 both give ~50 iters (SOR doesn't engage), at tol=1e-4 R=550 iters, Python=120 iters — different solver behaviour, different iterate selection.

## Fix
Change Python harvest() signature so sor=None means 'use R-matching defaults' (auto=True, omega_min=0.3). Preserve explicit sor=False or sor={} for opt-out. Matches R: sor=NULL disables, omitting sor uses the auto-enabled default.

## Files
- python/leafblower/_harvest.py:116 (signature default)
- python/leafblower/_harvest.py:91-101 (_parse_sor — body is correct, call-site is wrong)
notes: Plan APPROVED: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-06-fix-python-sor-default.md. _resolve_sor adapter at call site. sor=None→R default. sor=False→disabled.

title: lrk6-P2-H2b: Move group_ids encoding to C++ — eliminate R-side O(n) allocations
description:
## I. Objective
Eliminate K×3 O(n) R vector allocations (as.integer, lvl_map subscript, NA scan) per harvest() call by moving encoding to C++. Expected: ~675ms reduction at n=1.58M.

## II. Input
R/harvest.R (change what's passed per margin in group_ids list)
src/r_bridge.cpp (add C++ decode path for new format)

## III. Guards
- arity stays at 36 (no new SEXP params to C_rk_calibrate)
- backward compatible: r_bridge detects old (INTSXP pre-encoded) vs new (VECSXP {codes, lvl_map}) format
- DO NOT change C++ solver interface beyond r_bridge.cpp
- tests must pass before commit

## IV. Logic
Approach: change group_ids_sexp[[k]] from pre-encoded INTSXP to VECSXP of {raw_codes, lvl_map}:
1. harvest.R: replace lvl_map[codes]+NA-scan with list(unclass(col), lvl_map_int) per margin
   - unclass(col): R factor's integer codes (1-indexed, 0=NA_INTEGER), no encoding allocation
   - lvl_map_int: match(levels(col), names(target[[v]])) - 1L, O(L) tiny allocation
2. r_bridge.cpp: detect TYPEOF(gid_vec)==VECSXP in encoding block:
   - If VECSXP: raw=INTEGER(VECTOR_ELT(gid_vec,0)); lvl=INTEGER(VECTOR_ELT(gid_vec,1)); L=LENGTH(VECTOR_ELT(gid_vec,1))
   - C++ loop: gids_storage[k][i] = (raw[i]==0||raw[i]==NA_INTEGER) ? -1 : lvl[raw[i]-1]
   - Single C++ loop: O(n) with no allocation
3. Keep old INTSXP path for backward compat (callers passing pre-encoded arrays)
4. Benchmark: compare lrk6_profile.csv baseline

## V. Schema
{"files": ["R/harvest.R", "src/r_bridge.cpp"], "technique": "pass raw factor + lvl_map as VECSXP; decode in C++", "eliminations": ["as.integer(col) copy", "lvl_map[codes] subscript", "is.na scan+assign"]}

## VI. DoD
- [ ] harvest.R passes VECSXP per margin instead of pre-encoded INTSXP
- [ ] r_bridge.cpp detects VECSXP and decodes in C++ with 0 R allocations
- [ ] Behavioral equivalence: identical group_ids on stepstone_small
- [ ] Full test suite PASS
- [ ] Benchmark shows >= 10% wall-time improvement at n=stepstone_small
- [ ] lrk6_profile.csv updated
close_reason: 0% improvement at n=200K. C++ encoding change doesn't help — solver dominates at scale. The Rprof 5.86% FUN at n=10K was misleading; at large n encoding is negligible vs solver. Escalate to H4 (inherent FFI floor).

title: fix(ieppa): weight lf_correction by per-margin stress instead of uniform /K
description:
## I. Objective
Fix ieppa.cpp:1086-1119: T1.B log-factor correction uses lf_correction = -shift/K, distributing shift uniformly across all K margins. Under non-uniform ill-conditioning (some margins heavily stressed, others relaxed), uniform distribution can cause cycling. Fix: weight correction by per-margin max-log-f.

## II. Input
File: src/ieppa.cpp
Lines: ~1086-1119 (T1.B lf_correction computation)
Variables: lf vector, lf_correction, K, shift

## III. Guards
- Math: sum of weighted corrections must equal shift (normalize weights)
- Weight per margin k = max_j |lf[cat_offset[k]+j]| (per-margin stress proxy)
- If all weights zero (uniform lf): fall back to uniform /K (no cycling risk)
- Must not change convergence behavior on well-conditioned problems

## IV. Logic
1. Read ieppa.cpp lines 1080-1130
2. Compute per-margin stress: w_k = max_j(|lf[cat_offset[k]+j]|) for k=0..K-1
3. Normalize: W_total = sum(w_k); if W_total < eps → uniform (w_k = 1/K)
4. Replace lf_correction = -shift/K with: lf_correction_k = -shift * w_k / W_total per margin
5. Apply per-margin correction: lf[cat_offset[k]+j] += lf_correction_k
6. Compile + test

## V. Schema
```json
{
  "file": "src/ieppa.cpp",
  "lines": "1086-1119",
  "old": "uniform lf_correction = -shift/K",
  "new": "per-margin weighted lf_correction_k = -shift * w_k / W_total",
  "fallback": "uniform when W_total < eps",
  "compile_gate": "R CMD INSTALL --preclean ."
}
```

## VI. DoD
- [ ] Per-margin correction computed and applied
- [ ] Uniform fallback when all margins zero stress
- [ ] Sum of corrections = shift (conservation verified)
- [ ] test-ieppa-faithful.R GREEN
- [ ] test-convergence-trajectory.R GREEN

title: fix(newton_kl): shrink trust radius on LDLT fallback bad step
description:
## I. Objective
Fix newton_calib.cpp:556-565: trust radius (delta_radius) shrinks only when trust_step_taken flag is set (D3 path). When dsyevd degenerates and falls to LDLT, a bad step produced there leaves delta_radius unchanged. Steihaug trust-region contract violated.

## II. Input
File: src/newton_calib.cpp
Lines: ~550-570 (trust radius update block)
Variables: delta_radius, trust_step_taken, rho (gain ratio), step_norm

## III. Guards
- Shrink rule: if rho < 0.25, delta_radius *= 0.25 — must apply regardless of which path produced the step
- Do NOT shrink on successful steps (rho >= 0.25)
- trust_step_taken flag can remain for other purposes; just remove its guard on the shrink

## IV. Logic
1. Read newton_calib.cpp lines 545-575
2. Find: if (trust_step_taken && rho < 0.25) { delta_radius *= 0.25; }
3. Change to: if (rho < 0.25) { delta_radius *= 0.25; } (remove trust_step_taken guard)
4. Verify expand rule (rho > 0.75 → delta_radius *= 2) unchanged
5. Compile + test

## V. Schema
```json
{
  "file": "src/newton_calib.cpp",
  "lines": "~556-565",
  "fix": "remove trust_step_taken guard from shrink rule",
  "shrink_condition": "rho < 0.25 (unconditional)",
  "compile_gate": "R CMD INSTALL --preclean ."
}
```

## VI. DoD
- [ ] delta_radius shrinks on rho < 0.25 regardless of step path
- [ ] Expand rule (rho > 0.75) unchanged

title: perf(newton_kl): cache dsyevd eigenvectors between Newton iters
description:
## I. Objective
Fix newton_calib.cpp:381-393: dsyevd full eigendecomposition (O(n_lam³)) called every Newton iter. Cache eigenvectors when delta_lam is small relative to ||lam|| and lm_mu unchanged. Skip recompute; use cached eigenvectors for projection.

## II. Input
File: src/newton_calib.cpp
Lines: ~375-400 (dsyevd call + eigenvector usage)
Variables: H (Hessian), eigenvalues, eigenvectors, lm_mu, lam, delta_lam

## III. Guards
- Cache invalidation: recompute when ||delta_lam||/||lam|| > cache_tol (suggest 1e-2) OR lm_mu changed
- Cache_tol must be conservative enough that cached eigenvectors remain useful
- Never skip first iter (no cache yet)
- Cache = {eigenvectors, eigenvalues, lm_mu_at_cache, lam_at_cache}

## IV. Logic
1. Read newton_calib.cpp lines 370-415
2. Add cache struct: EigCache {MatrixXd V; VectorXd d; double lm_mu; VectorXd lam;}
3. Check before dsyevd: if cache valid (delta_lam_rel < 1e-2 AND lm_mu same) → skip dsyevd
4. After dsyevd: update cache
5. Compile + verify results unchanged on stepstone fixture
6. Benchmark: bench::mark(cached vs uncached, iterations=50)

## V. Schema
```json
{
  "file": "src/newton_calib.cpp",
  "cache_struct": "EigCache",
  "invalidation_condition": "||delta_lam||/||lam|| > 1e-2 OR lm_mu changed",

```

title: fix(sinkhorn): bisection bracket expansion broken for negative lo
description:
## I. Objective
Fix sinkhorn.cpp:36-44 bisection bracket expansion. Current: lo *= 2.0 doubles a negative number (lo=-50 → -100 → ... → -800 < -500, STOP) — bracket span truncated before reaching severe mass ratios, causing spurious infeasibility. Fix: derive bracket from data (log(W_total/L_min)) or use absolute subtraction.

## II. Input
File: src/sinkhorn.cpp
Lines: ~30-50 (KL box-projection bisection bracket setup)
Variables: lo (log-domain lower bound), hi (log-domain upper bound), W_total, L_min (cell lower bounds)

## III. Guards
- Bracket [lo, hi] must bracket the bisection root μ s.t. Σ clamp(X*exp(a+μ), L, U) = target_mass
- lo must be negative enough that Σ clamp(X*exp(a+lo), L, U) <= target_mass
- Correct expansion: lo -= abs_step (subtract positive constant), NOT lo *= 2
- Alternative: lo = -log(W_total / min(L_c)) as data-derived lower bound

## IV. Logic
1. Read sinkhorn.cpp lines 25-60 (full bisection bracket + loop)
2. Identify current bracket expansion (lo *= 2.0 or equivalent)
3. Compute data-derived bound: lo_init = -(log(W_total) - log(min_L)) where min_L = min positive L_c
4. Replace bracket expansion with: lo = lo_init (single assignment, no loop needed)
5. Verify hi bracket (positive side) is similarly bounded from data
6. Compile + test: Rscript -e "testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/test-calibration-solvers.R')"

## V. Schema
```json
{
  "file": "src/sinkhorn.cpp",
  "fix_type": "data-derived bracket",
  "lo_formula": "-(log(W_total) - log(min_positive_L_c))",
  "hi_formula": "log(W_total / max_positive_L_c) [or symmetric]",
  "compile_gate": "R CMD INSTALL --preclean ."
}
```

## VI. DoD
- [ ] lo *= 2.0 (or equivalent doubling) removed
- [ ] lo derived from data bounds, not iterative expansion
- [ ] Bracket guaranteed to contain root for any feasible problem
- [ ] test-calibration-solvers.R GREEN
- [ ] Commit: fix(sinkhorn): data-derived bisection bracket for KL box projection
close_reason: Data-derived bisection bracket replaces lo*=2. Both bisect_capacity variants fixed. isfinite guard added. Commit 2b9796f.

title: perf(newton_kl): eliminate redundant per-obs compute_u and group_id in Hessian build
description:
## I. Objective
Fix newton_calib.cpp:280-303: Hessian build is O(n·K²) with compute_u(lam,i) and group_ids[k][i] computed redundantly per obs per margin pair. At n=1e6, K=20 → 4e8 ops/iter. Hoist f_i and u-vector; exploit margin-block sparsity.

## II. Input
File: src/newton_calib.cpp
Lines: ~275-310 (Hessian build double-loop)
Variables: H matrix (n_lam × n_lam), compute_u(lam, i), group_ids, f_i

## III. Guards
- Correctness: H_{k1,k2}[j1,j2] = Σ_i f_i · 1(g_{k1}[i]==j1) · 1(g_{k2}[i]==j2)
- Off-diagonal block H_{k1,k2}[j1,j2] is zero when NO obs i belongs to both bins → exploit this
- Hoist: compute f_i once per obs; compute group indices once
- Numerical result must be bitwise-identical to current implementation

## IV. Logic
1. Read newton_calib.cpp lines 270-320
2. Identify: (a) redundant compute_u(lam,i) inside inner loops, (b) group_ids[k][i] repeated lookup
3. Hoist f_i = compute_f(lam, i) outer loop (per obs, not per margin pair)
4. Cache u_i = compute_u(lam, i) same loop
5. For Hessian: iterate obs outer, margins inner → accumulate H[k1*max_cats+j1, k2*max_cats+j2] += f_i * ...
6. Optional: build CSR sparsity pattern once (i→{k,j} membership) for O(n·K) instead of O(n·K²)
7. Compile + correctness test (compare H to brute force)
8. Benchmark: bench::mark(old, new, iterations=20)

## V. Schema
```json
{
  "file": "src/newton_calib.cpp",
  "lines": "275-310",
  "optimizations": ["hoist f_i per obs", "cache group indices", "exploit block sparsity"],
  "correctness_gate": "max(|H_new - H_old|) < 1e-12",
  "compile_gate": "R CMD INSTALL --preclean ."
}
```

## VI. DoD
- [ ] f_i hoisted outside margin-pair loops
- [ ] group_ids lookup not repeated in inner loop
- [ ] Hessian numerically identical to old (max diff < 1e-12)
- [ ] Benchmark shows >= 2x speedup at n=1e5, K=9
- [ ] test-newton-kl.R GREEN
close_reason: Per-obs f_i and active_a hoisted out of k1*k2 loop. No CSR infrastructure. 13% speedup at n=1e5, K=20. Commit 5520757.

title: Epic: REMOVE-LBFGSB — eliminate L-BFGS-B method from package
description:
# Epic: REMOVE-LBFGSB

## Goal
Remove lbfgsb completely from leafblower: delete implementation, strip from all APIs, replace AUTO fallback with newton_kl, clean tests and docs.

## Rationale
lbfgsb is strictly dominated by newton_kl: same KL objective, newton_kl converges in 7 iters (~10s on 1.58M×9) while lbfgsb never converges (~965ms/iter, ~48min at 3000-iter budget). The AUTO fallback to lbfgsb is a user-invisible landmine that silently hangs for hours on large data. No production use case where lbfgsb wins.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] src/lbfgsb_solver.{hpp,cpp} deleted
- [ ] All dispatch code removed from c_api.cpp and r_bridge.cpp
- [ ] AUTO fallback replaced with newton_calibrate in both bridges
- [ ] Python harvest() no longer accepts method='lbfgsb'
- [ ] R harvest() no longer accepts method='lbfgsb'
- [ ] R CMD check passes, pytest passes
- [ ] Benchmarks updated

## Files involved (exhaustive)
DELETE: src/lbfgsb_solver.hpp, src/lbfgsb_solver.cpp, tests/testthat/test-lbfgsb.R
MODIFY C++: src/leafblower.h, src/types.hpp, src/c_api.cpp, src/r_bridge.cpp, src/Makevars
MODIFY Python: python/leafblower/_harvest.py, python/leafblower/_bindings.cpp
MODIFY R: R/harvest.R, man/harvest.Rd, man/anesrake.Rd
MODIFY tests: 11 test files (remove individual lbfgsb cases)
MODIFY benchmarks: 3 benchmark files

## Key technical decisions
- RK_ALG_LBFGSB = 2: keep in enum as sentinel, dispatch returns RK_ERR_BADARG (ABI safety, no renumbering)
- lbfgs_m: remove from rk_params_t and CalibState. EXPECTED_RK_PARAMS_BYTES: 248 → 244 (int removal)
- AUTO fallback: lbfgsb_solve → newton_calibrate (same KL objective, O(M_cell) not O(n×K))

## Sub-Agent Strategy
T1 (C++ core) must complete first — headers change. T2+T3 (Python/R layers) parallel after T1. T4 (tests) after T2+T3. T5 (benchmarks) independent.

title: DOCS: Document factor label/level behavior in harvest.R encoding block
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add a comment at the match() encoding block in R/harvest.R explaining the string-matching semantics and the behavior change vs. the old C++ encoder.
* **Why:** `as.character(data[[v]])` coerces factor values via level LABELS. Old C++ path used Rf_getAttrib(col, R_LevelsSymbol) + level_to_idx string map — same string matching. BUT if a user has a factor with level LABELS that differ from names(target[[v]]) by case or spacing, both paths silently encode to -1 (OOV). The behavior is identical in practice, but the old C++ also emitted a corrupt-factor error for integer-code-out-of-range; the new R path does not. This needs documentation.
* **Reference Data:**
  Current code (harvest.R ~line 370):
  ```R
  group_ids_r <- lapply(margins, function(v) {
    idx <- match(as.character(data[[v]]), names(target[[v]]))
    as.integer(ifelse(is.na(idx), -1L, idx - 1L))
  })
  ```
  Add comment ABOVE the lapply:
  ```R
  # Encode each margin column to 0-indexed integer (NA/-1 for OOV).
  # as.character() handles both factor and character columns; for factors it
  # coerces via level labels. Levels not present in names(target[[v]]) → -1.
  # This matches the old C++ encoder (level_to_idx string lookup); case/spacing
  # differences in level names vs target names still produce silent -1 OOV.
  ```

title: TEST: Cross-language weight parity — R and Python must return identical weights
description:
## leafblower-a9xk.1: Cross-language weight parity test
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION` (depends on leafblower-sa3f being merged first)
**Parent:** leafblower-a9xk (PYR-PARITY Epic)
**Blocked by:** leafblower-sa3f

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Create two files — tests/parity/run_parity_r.R (R subprocess helper) and tests/test_parity_weights.py (pytest) — that assert max(|w_py - w_r|) < 1e-10 for 6 methods on identical synthetic data. This test locks the invariant: shared C library must produce bit-identical weights regardless of binding layer.
* **Why:** The greenkhorn/logit discrepancy was a silent regression — no test caught it. Raking's claimed parity must also be confirmed at byte level (not just metric-level similarity). The test must fail before leafblower-sa3f lands, pass after.
* **Note on test location:** tests/test_parity_weights.py goes under tests/ (not python/) — it is a cross-language integration test that calls both bindings and belongs at the repo top level, not inside the Python package.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Synthetic dataset generated in-script (no file dependency).
* **Data design:** n=2000, seed=42, 4 margins: age(4 levels), gender(2), region(3), edu(3). targets slightly off marginals. start_weights=1.0, min_weight=0, max_weight=5, max_iterations=1000, convergence=improvement/tol=1e-3.
* **Two files only:**
  - tests/parity/run_parity_r.R: standalone Rscript, takes args [data_csv] [targets_json] [method] [output_weights_csv]
  - tests/test_parity_weights.py: pytest file, generates data, calls both bindings, asserts parity

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |

title: IMPR-BUDGET-WARN: use last-interval (asymptotic) rate for spectral estimate
description:
## Objective
Replace the first-to-last average rate estimate in the budget warning with the asymptotic rate from the last kErrCheckInterval (10 iters). The asymptotic rate is r=(e_last/e_prev)^(1/10), which better reflects the true spectral radius at the current iterate.

## Why
Current estimate uses (e_final/e_first)^(1/(best_iter-10)) — the average rate over ALL iterations. Early IPF iterations converge fast; late iterations converge at the true spectral radius. The average underestimates the required budget. Asymptotic rate gives the correct estimate.

## Mechanism
1. Track metric_prev_check (second-to-last kErrCheckInterval metric) via a rolling 2-slot window in ieppa.cpp using a local variable (separate per path: SRAA and non-SRAA).
2. Pack metric_prev_check in r_bridge.cpp (N_RESULT_FIELDS 38→39, slot 38).
3. In harvest.R budget warning: ONLY use asymptotic rate (e_final/e_prev)^(1/10). If e_prev is inf (< 2 check intervals elapsed), emit simple warning without rate estimate.

## Files
- src/types.hpp: add metric_prev_check field to CalibResult
- src/ieppa.cpp: rolling update in SRAA path (nat_metric_prev_sraa local) + non-SRAA path (nat_metric_prev_nonavec local)
- src/r_bridge.cpp: declare/init res_metric_prev_check, add to pack_solver_result, SET at slot 38, N_RESULT_FIELDS 38→39
- R/harvest.R: use e_prev for asymptotic rate; no fallback to average

## kErrCheckInterval
ieppa.cpp line 128: constexpr int kErrCheckInterval = 10. Rate uses this as denominator.

## DoD
- [ ] ieppa plain (1.58M, 3000 iters budget): warning shows r≈0.9985, ~4200 total iters
- [ ] ieppa+accel (1.58M, forced budget): warning shows asymptotic rate from last SRAA interval
- [ ] < 2 intervals elapsed: simple warning without estimate (no NA or garbage)
- [ ] R CMD check passes
notes:
CRITICAL REVISION (scientific-critical-thinking):

EMPIRICAL FINDING: plain ieppa on 1.58M stalls at structural fixed point mkl=0.005 after best_iter=60 regardless of max_iterations (verified: same result at 50, 100, 500, 3000 iters). Spectral radius assumption INVALIDATED.

TWO DISTINCT BUDGET CASES:
1. STALL (best_iter << max_iterations): solver hit structural fixed point. More iterations won't help. Rate estimate is MISLEADING. Correct warning: 'fixed point detected, try ieppa+accel or newton_kl'
2. TRUE BUDGET (best_iter ≈ max_iterations): solver still improving. Rate estimate is valid and useful.

DETECTION: if best_iter / max_iterations < STALL_THRESHOLD (e.g., 0.5), it's a stall, not budget.

REVISED PLAN:
- Primary: detect stall vs true-budget FIRST (best_iter/max_iterations ratio)
- Secondary: asymptotic rate estimate ONLY for true-budget case
- Stall message: 'Fixed point at mkl=X (best_iter=Y << max_iter=N). More iterations will not help. Try: accelerate=TRUE or method=newton_kl.'

Sub-tickets skmo.1-13 need revision to reflect this two-case design.
close_reason: All 4 active tickets complete: BWARN-A(10583ec)+BWARN-B(aece723)+BWARN-1(4d0032a)+BWARN-2(635d8f5).

title: FEAT-BUDGET-WARN: emit spectral budget warning when max_iterations < estimated requirement
description:
## Objective
When a solver hits RK_ERR_BUDGET and the final marginal_kl is above tol, emit a warning estimating how many iterations are actually required based on observed convergence rate.

## Why
Plain ieppa (non-SRAA) on 1.58M stepstone hits budget at 3000 iters with mkl=0.005 (5× above tol=1e-3). The spectral radius of the 9-margin system is r≈0.9985, requiring ~4200+ iters. The current warning is generic; it should quantify the gap.

## Mechanism
Requires:
1. Track marginal_kl at first kErrCheckInterval check (iter 1 or 10) as extra result field: mkl_at_first_check
2. In harvest.R, when status=RK_ERR_BUDGET and best_error > tol:
   - Estimate r = (mkl_final / mkl_first_check)^(1/(final_iter - first_check_iter))
   - Additional iters needed = log(tol / mkl_final) / log(r)
   - Emit: warning(sprintf('ieppa: budget exhausted at mkl=%.2e (%.0fx above tol). Spectral budget requires ~%d total iterations.', mkl, mkl/tol, estimated_total))

## Files
- src/ieppa.cpp: add mkl_first_check capture at first kErrCheckInterval
- src/calib_dispatch.hpp or types.hpp: add mkl_first_check field to CalibResult
- src/r_bridge.cpp: pack mkl_first_check
- R/harvest.R: use mkl_first_check + best_error to compute estimate and emit warning

## Applies to
All methods that can hit budget. Each method should use its natural metric for the estimate.
notes:
Gate rev 1: Rate formula fix: use ri$best_iter (iteration at which best error was achieved) not ri$iterations (total budget). Correct formula:
  r_est = (e_final / e_first)^(1 / max(1, b_iter - 10))
  n_more = ceil(log(tol / e_final) / log(r_est))
  n_total = b_iter + n_more

Clarification 1: R warning block must use calib_result$convergence_used$metric for the metric name string (bare 'metric_name' is out of scope at line 471).

Clarification 2: Non-SRAA MARGINAL_KL capture point: use res.marginal_kl_at_iter (not select_metric(metric, cm)) to match what best.update() uses on that path.
close_reason: Implemented at af0e0a9. Warning fires correctly: 'leafblower: budget exhausted — marginal_kl=4.97e-03 at 100 iters (5× above tol=1e-03). Spectral rate r≈0.9773 requires ~130 total iterations.' Note: rate estimate is optimistic (early iterations converge faster than late ones) — lower bound on required iterations, not exact.

title: G1: calib_linalg LDLT replace scalar loop with LAPACK dpotrf/dsytrf
description:
# G1: calib_linalg LDLT to BLAS dpotrf/dsytrf
**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace scalar O(n^3) LDLT triple-nested loop in `ldlt_factor_inplace` with LAPACK `dpotrf` (Cholesky, PD inputs) or `dsytrf` (symmetric indefinite with partial pivoting).
* **Why:** Single biggest bottleneck for chebyshev — called ~500x per solve for n=2048; 500 x 512^3 = 67 B scalar ops. Row-major cache-hostile access. BLAS gives 5-20x speedup for n>=256.
* **File:** `/home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/src/calib_linalg.cpp` lines ~67-108 (function `ldlt_factor_inplace`).

## II. Mechanism (Required)
- **Mechanism:** LAPACK `dsytrf` (Bunch-Kaufman partial pivoting) OR `dpotrf` (Cholesky on PD input).
- **Forbidden:** Custom scalar loops, hand-written pivoting, blocked algorithms not from LAPACK.
- **Audit:** Compare numerical output element-wise against current implementation on test fixtures; benchmark wall-time for n in {128,256,512,1024}.

## III. Reference Code
Use R-bundled LAPACK headers via `R_ext/BLAS.h` and `R_ext/Lapack.h`.

Option A — `dsytrf` (symmetric indefinite, robust):
```cpp
char uplo = 'L';
int lwork = -1, info = 0;
double wkopt;
F77_CALL(dsytrf)(&uplo, &n, A, &n, ipiv.data(), &wkopt, &lwork, &info);
lwork = (int)wkopt;
std::vector<double> work(lwork);
F77_CALL(dsytrf)(&uplo, &n, A, &n, ipiv.data(), work.data(), &lwork, &info);
if (info != 0) return RK_ERR_BADARG;  // singular
```

Option B — `dpotrf` (Cholesky, faster, requires PD):
```cpp
F77_CALL(dpotrf)(&uplo, &n, A, &n, &info);
if (info > 0) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) A[i*n+i] += eps_perturb;
    F77_CALL(dpotrf)(&uplo, &n, A, &n, &info);
}
```

Note: `dsytrf` partial pivoting supersedes Gill-Murray approach; `dpotrf` requires C1 (Gill-Murray PD enforcement) merged first.

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read current `ldlt_factor_inplace` and identify call sites in chebyshev.cpp, greg.cpp.
2. Decide: `dsytrf` (no C1 dependency) or `dpotrf` (requires C1 merged).
3. Replace scalar loop with LAPACK call; preserve existing return-code semantics.
4. Update call sites if pivot vector (ipiv) is now needed for solve step.
5. Add benchmark in `benchmarks/` measuring n=512 factor time before/after.
6. Run `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` to verify per-file compilation.
7. Run all calib_linalg + chebyshev + greg tests.

## V. Definition of Done
- [ ] LDLT uses LAPACK call, not scalar loop
- [ ] Benchmark: time for n=512 factorization before/after committed under `benchmarks/results/`
- [ ] All calib_linalg + chebyshev + greg tests pass
- [ ] Implement C1 (Gill-Murray fix) first OR use `dsytrf` (path-independent)
- [ ] Confidence >=85 with exact code citations

description:
# D4: Guarantee descent direction before Armijo check in newton_calib.cpp
**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Before performing the Armijo line-search check, assert that g_dot_d > 0 (descent). If Steihaug-CG returned a non-descent direction (can occur when TSVD trust-region projection lands far from unconstrained minimizer), fall back to steepest descent.
* **Why:** Armijo `g_trial <= g_curr - c1*alpha*g_dot_d` requires g_dot_d > 0 to be meaningful. With g_dot_d <= 0, Armijo can accept an ascent step.
* **File:** /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/src/newton_calib.cpp line ~537

## II. Input Specification
* Existing variables: G (gradient), delta (search direction from Steihaug-CG), g_norm, d_norm.
* The Armijo line search and its g_dot_d computation.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| Logic | If g_dot_d <= 1e-12 * |g_norm| * |d_norm|, fall back to steepest descent (delta = -G), and recompute g_dot_d = g_norm * g_norm. |
| Format | Surgical insertion immediately before the Armijo check. |
| Boundary | Only edit src/newton_calib.cpp around line 537. |
| Tone | Match existing variable names; no new helpers unless used 3+ times. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

   ```cpp
   double g_dot_d = /* existing inner product */;

       scale_by(-1.0, delta);  // delta = -grad
       g_dot_d = g_norm * g_norm;  // guaranteed positive
   ```

title: D3: Negative delta_H_delta clamped to 0 wrong trust-region
description:
# D3: Treat negative delta_H_delta as model failure, not zero-clamp
**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** When delta_H_delta = delta^T H delta is meaningfully negative (true ascent prediction), reject the step and shrink the trust region instead of clamping to 0 and computing rho = actual / 0.
* **Why:** Current code at line ~521:
  ```cpp
  if (delta_H_delta < 0.0) delta_H_delta = 0.0;
  ```
  After Schur subtraction, TSVD truncation can produce negative quadratic forms. Clamping to 0 makes the model_decrease zero, so rho becomes +/-inf, triggering aggressive mu tightening when the real signal is "model failure: bad direction."
* **File:** /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/src/newton_calib.cpp line ~521

## II. Input Specification
* Existing variables in scope: delta_H_delta, g_dot_delta, actual_decrease, delta_radius (or equivalent trust-region radius variable).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| Logic | If delta_H_delta < -1e-10 * |g_dot_delta|, treat as model failure: force rho<0 and shrink trust region. Else clamp small negatives to 0 (rounding noise). |
| Format | Surgical replacement of the single clamp line. |
| Boundary | Only edit src/newton_calib.cpp around line 521. |
| Tone | First-principles tolerance: scale by |g_dot_delta|, do not hard-code absolute. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Replace clamp:
   ```cpp
   if (delta_H_delta < -1e-10 * std::fabs(g_dot_delta)) {
       // model predicts ascent: treat as model failure, reject step
       actual_decrease = -1.0;  // force rho < 0 -> reject
       delta_radius *= 0.25;    // shrink trust region
   } else {
       delta_H_delta = std::max(delta_H_delta, 0.0);  // only clamp near-zero noise
   }
   ```
2. Verify variable names match newton_calib.cpp (delta_radius may be named differently; locate via Read).
3. Build with R CMD INSTALL --preclean ..
4. Construct a test (R or C++ unit) that produces a non-descent direction (e.g., adversarial Hessian eigenstructure under TSVD truncation); verify trust region shrinks and step is rejected.

```json
  "data": { "files_changed": ["src/newton_calib.cpp"], "test_added": true, "trust_region_var_name": "<verified>" },
  "error_log": null
}
```

## VI. Definition of Done

- [ ] Tolerance scales by |g_dot_delta|, not absolute.

description:
# F4: Make patch_*.py Idempotent and Atomic
**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Convert /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/patch_raking.py and /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/patch_wolfe.py to fail loudly on re-run and write atomically.
* **Why:** Scripts mutate C++ source files in-place. patch_raking.py uses `match is None → exit(1)` (safe-ish). patch_wolfe.py does NOT check substitution count → silent no-op on re-run. Neither writes to temp file + atomic rename → partial writes corrupt source if interrupted.
* **Reference Data:**
  - /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/patch_raking.py
  - /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/patch_wolfe.py
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Two patch scripts.
* **Format:** Python source files.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Use `re.subn`. n_subs == 0 → exit(1) ("already patched or source changed"). n_subs > 1 → exit(1) ("ambiguous"). n_subs == 1 → atomic write. |
| **Format** | tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile in same dir as target → shutil.move. No partial writes. |
| **Boundary** | Both scripts; preserve existing pattern strings exactly. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse, no fluff. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read both patch_raking.py and patch_wolfe.py to extract OLD_PATTERN and NEW_CONTENT for each.
2. Refactor each to template:
   ```python
   import re, sys, os, tempfile, shutil
   with open(target_file, 'r') as f:
       content = f.read()
   new_content, n_subs = re.subn(OLD_PATTERN, NEW_CONTENT, content)
   if n_subs == 0:
       print(f"ERROR: pattern not found in {target_file} — already patched or source changed", file=sys.stderr)
       sys.exit(1)
   if n_subs > 1:
       print(f"ERROR: pattern matched {n_subs} times — ambiguous", file=sys.stderr)
       sys.exit(1)
   with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', dir=os.path.dirname(target_file), delete=False) as tmp:
       tmp.write(new_content)
       tmp_path = tmp.name
   shutil.move(tmp_path, target_file)
   print(f"Patched {target_file} (1 substitution)")
   ```
3. Verify both scripts still produce identical output on first run.
4. Run each twice; second run must exit 1 with clear message.
5. Verify configure/Makevars/build invokes them in correct order; if patches needed by build, document idempotence in build script.
6. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{
  "task_id": "F4",
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "files_modified": ["patch_raking.py", "patch_wolfe.py"],
    "idempotent": true,
    "atomic_write": true,
    "build_test": "configure && make passes"
  },
  "error_log": null
}
```

## VI. Definition of Done

- [ ] Writes are atomic (temp file + rename)
- [ ] Build system test: verify configure/Makevars runs patches in correct order
- [ ] First-run output byte-identical to pre-refactor

description:
# F1: Fix harvest.R Integer-Radix Key Overflow
**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Eliminate silent floating-point key collisions in `compute_quality_metrics` when product of margin levels exceeds 2^53.
* **Why:** R `numeric` (double) has 53-bit mantissa; with K=10 margins x 50 levels, multiplier = 50^10 ≈ 9.77e16 > 2^53 = 9.007e15. Two distinct cell combinations produce identical floating-point keys → silent KL corruption.
* **Reference Data:** /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/R/harvest.R lines ~730-741.
* **Buggy code:**
  ```r
  multiplier <- multiplier * nlevels(df[[k]])
  key <- key + (as.integer(df[[k]]) - 1L) * multiplier
  ```
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** harvest.R source; target_list (named list of margin proportions); df (data.frame of factors).
* **Format:** R source file; named list; data.frame.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | If max_cells > 2^53, fall back to character/paste key OR integer64 (bit64). Never silently overflow. |
| **Format** | Pure R; no new package deps unless bit64 is added to Imports + DESCRIPTION. |
| **Boundary** | Touch only `compute_quality_metrics` and its callers in harvest.R. No refactor of unrelated code. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse, no fluff. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read /home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/R/harvest.R lines 700-780 to confirm exact structure of `compute_quality_metrics`.
2. Compute `max_cells <- prod(sapply(target_list, length))` at start of function.
3. Branch:
   - If `max_cells <= 2^53`: keep radix encoding (safe path).
   - Else: build paste-based character key:
     ```r
     key <- do.call(paste, c(lapply(names(target_list), function(v) as.integer(df[[v]])), sep=","))
     ```
4. Verify margin_kl downstream consumes either numeric or character key (tapply/split work on both).
5. Add unit test in tests/testthat/test-harvest.R: K=10 x 50-level margins, verify `length(unique(key)) == nrow(df_distinct_cells)`.

# C6: Implement KKT-based release in GREG monotone active-set

**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add KKT-multiplier release condition to GREG active-set; cells with sign-violated implied dual are unclamped and re-optimized.
* **Why:** Current algorithm is monotone-add: once `fixed_lo[c] = true`, it stays true forever. If the optimal solution requires releasing an early-clamped cell, GREG converges to a non-KKT-optimal point. Misleading "active set still cycling" message also has to be fixed (algorithm cannot cycle — it's monotone-add).
* **Reference Data:**
  * File: `/home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/src/greg.cpp` lines ~111-130 (active-set update block).
  * Current bug: only adds, never releases.
  * Fix sketch:
    ```cpp
    // After Newton direction is computed, evaluate implied lambda for each clamped cell.
    // For fixed_lo[c]: lambda_c = -(gradient contribution from cell c).
    // Release if lambda_c sign violates KKT dual feasibility.
    for (int c = 0; c < M_cell; ++c) {
        if (fixed_lo[c] && lambda_implied[c] < -1e-8) {
            fixed_lo[c] = false; need_refactor = true;
        }
        if (fixed_hi[c] && lambda_implied[c] > 1e-8) {
    ```

# C5: Replace 1e300 D_eff sentinel with explicit locked[] cell flags

**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** When `inv_D <= 1e-300`, mark cell as locked (`dX[c] = 0`) instead of setting `D_eff[c] = 1e300`.
* **Why:** Current sentinel produces astronomical primal step `dX_A[c] = 1e300 * (sum_dlam + dnu)`. The step-length safeguard then computes `alpha_aff` from `dX_A`, with `dX_A[c] = 1e300` collapsing `alpha_aff -> 0` and stalling the IPM. Explicit lock semantics is correct: a cell whose barrier weight has vanished is at its bound and should not move.
* **Reference Data:**
  * File: `/home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/src/chebyshev.cpp` lines ~296-298 (D_eff assignment) and step computation site (~line ~440-460 where dX_A is computed).
  * Current bug: `D_eff[c] = (inv_D > 1e-300) ? 1.0/inv_D : 1e300;`
  * Fix:
    ```cpp
    if (inv_D < 1e-300) {
        D_eff[c] = 0.0;
        locked[c] = true;
    } else {
        D_eff[c] = 1.0 / inv_D;
    }
    // At step computation:
    dX_A[c] = locked[c] ? 0.0 : D_eff[c] * (sum_dlam + dnu_A);
    ```
