title: C1: Gill-Murray LDLT proper column-norm bound
description:
# C1: Implement proper Gill-Murray-Wright column-norm bound in LDLT

**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace naive `d_j = max(d_j, eps_perturb)` clamp with proper Gill-Murray-Wright modified LDLT bounding L by `beta`.
* **Why:** Current clamp lets `L[i,j] = s/eps = 1e10` when normal equations are near-singular, silently corrupting all back-solves with no error indicator. This breaks both chebyshev IPM and greg solvers downstream.
* **Reference Data:**
  * File: `/home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/src/calib_linalg.cpp` lines ~67-89 (LDLT factorization inner loop)
  * Current bug: `d_j = std::max(d_j, eps_perturb);  // eps_perturb = 1e-10`
  * Proper algorithm (Gill-Murray-Wright 1981 / Schnabel-Eskow 1990):
    `d_j = max(|d_j|, max(|s_ij|^2 / beta^2, eps))`
    where `theta_j = max_{i>j} |s_ij|` and `beta^2 = max(eps, max_diagonal, theta/sqrt(n-1))`.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Symmetric (possibly indefinite) n x n matrix A passed as flat double array.
* **Format:** Row-major double*, dimension n.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Must guarantee `|L[i,j]| <= beta/sqrt(d_j)` for all i,j. No silent NaN/Inf. |
| **Format** | C++ inside existing `ldlt_factor` function; no new public API. |
| **Boundary** | Touch ONLY `/home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/src/calib_linalg.cpp`. Do not modify chebyshev.cpp or greg.cpp call sites. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse, no fluff. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read current `ldlt_factor` in `/home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/src/calib_linalg.cpp` lines ~67-89.
2. Before factorization loop: compute `max_diag = max_i |A[i,i]|`, `max_off = max_{i>j} |A[i,j]|`, set `beta2 = max(eps_perturb, max_diag, max_off / sqrt(n))`.
3. Inside inner loop: track `theta_j = max_{i>j} |s[i]|` (the column being processed).
4. Replace `d_j = max(d_j, eps_perturb)` with `d_j = max(|d_j|, max(theta_j*theta_j / beta2, eps_perturb))`.
5. Recompile (`R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`) and run all calib_linalg tests.
6. Add a regression test: feed near-singular N (one nearly-zero diagonal); assert `max(|L|) < some_finite_bound` and solve recovers reasonable direction.
7. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
Sub-agent MUST return:
```json
{
  "task_id": "C1",
  "success": bool,
  "data": {
    "files_modified": ["src/calib_linalg.cpp"],
    "tests_added": ["test path"],
    "max_L_before": "numeric",
    "max_L_after": "numeric"
  },
  "error_log": "null | msg"
}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] LDLT produces bounded L (`|L[i,j]| <= beta/sqrt(d_j)`)
- [ ] Test with near-singular N (nearly-zero diagonal): solve recovers reasonable direction
- [ ] All existing calib_linalg tests pass
- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` succeeds
- [ ] No hallucination — all line numbers verified against actual file
notes: Gate finding: C1 spec must explicitly define β formula: β² = max(γ, ξ/sqrt(n²-1), DBL_EPSILON) where γ = max diagonal element, ξ = max absolute off-diagonal element. This is Gill-Murray-Wright 1981. Do not leave β as implementation-defined.
close_reason: Gill-Murray-Wright β²+θ_j column-norm bound implemented. Commit b510089 on fix/cr-epics. New test added.

title: Add Tier-1/2 calibration quality metrics to harvest() result struct
description:
# Add Tier-1/2 calibration quality metrics to harvest() result struct

## Background

During Epic-K/ylsy analysis (2026-05-03) the metric hierarchy was established:
- Tier 1 (most important): margin_kl, wall_time
- Tier 2: weight_kl, design_effect, effective_observations
- Tier 3: max_err, mean_err, chi2, grake_norm, l1_weight_change (currently exposed)

The existing result struct (attr(result, "result")) exposes only Tier-3 metrics.
The entire Epic-J/K research was conducted on Tier-3 metrics; this led to:
- ylsy research question being the wrong question (kk1204 is infeasible, not convergent-to-bad-fixed-point)
- Epic-K headline "CP beats ieppa+sraa by 2.2x" being a Tier-3 artifact (on Tier-1, ieppa+sraa wins 4.6x)

## Goal

Add to attr(result, "result"):
- margin_kl: KL divergence between calibrated marginals and target marginals
  Σ_k Σ_j T_{kj} log(T_{kj} / Ŵ_{kj}) where Ŵ_{kj} = Σ_i 1[g_k(i)=j] w_i / Σ_i w_i
- weight_kl: KL divergence of normalized weights from uniform (Shannon divergence)
  Σ_i (w_i/Z) log(n w_i / Z) where Z = Σ w_i, n = length(w)
- design_effect: DEFF = n Σ w_i^2 / (Σ w_i)^2
- effective_observations: n_eff = (Σ w_i)^2 / Σ w_i^2 = n / DEFF

## Technical notes

- Compute at O(nK) cost after solver completes — no per-iter overhead
- Compute in C++ alongside existing quality metrics (rk_result_t in leafblower.h)
- Surface via r_bridge.cpp SEXP-pack (new named slots in result list)
- Python bridge update in lockstep
- All solvers (ieppa, raking, newton_kl, greenkhorn, lbfgsb, etc.) should populate these

## Implementation sketch

In C++ (rk_result_t extension):
```cpp
double margin_kl;           // Σ_k Σ_j T_kj log(T_kj / W_kj_hat)
double weight_kl;           // KL(w_norm || uniform)  
double design_effect;       // DEFF = n * sum(w^2) / sum(w)^2
double effective_obs;       // n_eff = sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2)
```

Note: rk_params_t EXPECTED_RK_PARAMS_BYTES static_assert tripwire must be updated
if adding to rk_params_t — but these are RESULT fields (rk_result_t), not parameter
fields, so no ABI break.

## Acceptance criteria

- attr(r, "result")$margin_kl, $weight_kl, $design_effect, $effective_observations
  all return finite non-NA doubles for all methods on all fixtures
- stepstone_K9 ieppa+sraa margin_kl ≈ 8.58e-05 (verified 2026-05-03)
- kk1204 ieppa+sraa DEFF ≈ 8485, n_eff ≈ 118 (verified 2026-05-03)
- R CMD INSTALL clean; all existing tests pass
- No slowdown on existing benchmarks (O(nK) post-solver cost is negligible)

## Priority

P1 — foundational. Without these metrics, future solver research risks repeating
the Tier-3 metric trap (ylsy/Epic-J/K pattern).
close_reason: DONE at cfbdae4. margin_kl, weight_kl, design_effect, effective_observations added to attr(r,'result') for all solvers via R/harvest.R post-solve O(nK) computation. Verified: stepstone margin_kl=8.58e-05, DEFF=1.064, n_eff=187891; kk1204 DEFF=8485, n_eff=118. Full regression FAIL=2 pre-existing T2 stepstone basin floor (Epic-Dβ documented).

title: Epic-Dβ: Truncated-SVD + Steihaug-CG trust-region Newton (LAPACK-backed)

# Epic-Dβ: Truncated-SVD + Steihaug-CG trust-region Newton

## Triggered by
- Epic-B (target homotopy): BLOCKED.
- Epic-C (IEPPA warm-start): BLOCKED.
- Epic-Dα (cheap-first lm_mu/pivot sweep): ESCALATE per CSV `benchmarks/results/lm_pivot_sweep.csv` — plateau at 2.79e-04 across {1e-12, 1e-10, 1e-8}; bottleneck is structural, not conditioning.

## Goal
Composed pipeline: (1) eigendecomposition of H_pre via LAPACK, (2) truncated-SVD projection (drop small-eigval directions) for rank-deficient stepstone Hessian, (3) Steihaug-CG trust-region step in projected subspace for robust step magnitudes. User explicitly approved LAPACK linkage (no need for in-house cyclic Jacobi).

## Success Criteria
- [ ] T2 stepstone K=9 max_err < 1e-4 (closes 13% gap from current 2.79e-4 master baseline).
- [ ] T1, T4, T5 PASS unchanged.
- [ ] Full regression FAIL=0.
- [ ] No public API change (projection + trust-region internal to LM-Newton inner).
- [ ] kk1204 K=20 severe-skew: at least PARTIAL (max_err < 1e-3, no wall requirement).

## Mechanism

### Step 1 — Truncated-SVD projection
- LAPACK `dsyevr` (or `dsyevd`) computes eigendecomp `H_pre = V Λ V^T`. Symmetric PSD → real eigvals.
- Threshold-truncate: `λ_i < ratio × λ_max` dropped (`ratio = 1e-8` initial; tuned by WL-5 if needed).
- Retained subspace `V_keep ∈ R^{n_λ × n_keep}`, `Λ_keep` diagonal.

### Step 2 — Steihaug-CG inside retained subspace
- Project gradient: `g_keep = V_keep^T G`.
- Project Hessian: `H_keep = Λ_keep` (diagonal, by construction).
- Trust-region radius `Δ` (adaptive per Marquardt-style ρ ratio, separately from `lm_mu`).
- Steihaug-CG: build conjugate steps incrementally; exit when (a) ||cumulative step||₂ ≥ Δ, (b) negative curvature direction encountered, (c) residual ||r||₂ < CG tol.
- Step in original basis: `δ = V_keep · δ_keep`. Null-space components untouched.

### Step 3 — Compose with LM
- LM `μ·diag(H)` damping operates on the FULL H_damped = H_pre + μ·diag(H_pre) BEFORE eigendecomp.
- Or apply LM in the projected subspace: `Λ_keep_damped = Λ_keep · (1 + μ) + μ · d_floor_retained`.
- WL-1 design ticket picks one and justifies (likely the latter — preserves scale-invariance).

### Trust-region radius adaptation
- Standard Marquardt-style: ρ = (g_curr - g_trial) / predicted_decrease.
- ρ > 0.75 ⇒ Δ ← min(2Δ, Δ_max).
- ρ < 0.25 ⇒ Δ ← Δ/4.
- Else ρ ∈ [0.25, 0.75] ⇒ Δ unchanged.
- Init `Δ = 1.0`, `Δ_max = 100.0`, `Δ_min = 1e-8`.

## LAPACK linkage
- Edit `src/Makevars` (or `src/Makevars.in`): add `$(LAPACK_LIBS) $(BLAS_LIBS) $(FLIBS)` to `PKG_LIBS`.
- R provides these via `R CMD config LAPACK_LIBS BLAS_LIBS FLIBS` (standard R-package idiom).
- LAPACK `dsyevr` selected for symmetric eigendecomp (numerically stable, can request only top-k eigvals if perf matters; cheaper than dsyev for n_λ < 100 — actually all eigvals needed, dsyevd may be faster).

## Forbidden
- DO NOT layer warm-start on top (Epic-B / Epic-C BLOCKED).
- DO NOT remove LM damping (orthogonal concern).
- DO NOT modify R/harvest.R API.
- DO NOT loosen test gates.
- DO NOT cyclic-Jacobi (LAPACK encouraged per user).
- DO NOT skip pre-commit hooks.

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Atomic tickets (~7-8):
- WL-0: Spec amendment (truncated-SVD + Steihaug-CG subsection).
- WL-1: Makevars LAPACK linkage + dsyevr wrapper helper in calib_linalg.{hpp,cpp}.
- WL-2: Truncated-SVD projection helper in calib_linalg or newton_calib.
- WL-3: Steihaug-CG trust-region solver helper.
- WL-4: Wire pipeline in run_newton_inner (replaces LDLT solve path; LM damping still applies).
- WL-5: Tests (T2 < 1e-4, T7 K=4 over-projection regression, T8 K=20 severe-skew unit).
- WL-6: Verify suite + bench + verdict + commit.

Plan rev 1 to be drafted with Opus + plan-review-gate.

## References
- Plan rev 2 (Epic 5k08 LM): `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-01-newton-kl-lm-plan.md`
- Investigation 5k08: `docs/investigations/2026-05-01-newton-kl-lm-result.md`

- Nocedal & Wright "Numerical Optimization" §4.3 (Steihaug-CG), §10.3 (truncated-SVD Newton).

title: Epic-D: Newton-KL rank-deficient direction projection (basin-floor attack)
description:
# Epic-D: Newton-KL rank-deficient direction projection

## Triggered by
Epic-B (target homotopy, BLOCKED) and Epic-C (IEPPA warm-start, BLOCKED) both falsified empirically. Basin-floor at gap≈1.4e-4 on stepstone K=9 is intrinsic to overlapping-margin Hessian rank-deficiency. ANY non-cold-start λ* (homotopy-converged or IEPPA fixed-point) sits OUTSIDE Newton's quadratic basin → drifts → best-iterate freezes the start. Both warm-start strategies are dead ends.

## Goal
Direct attack on the basin-floor mechanism: project Newton step onto the well-conditioned subspace of H_pre. Drop directions with eigenvalues below `λ_min_ratio × λ_max(H_pre)` from the step computation. Newton converges within the projected subspace to the true optimum-in-subspace; rank-deficient directions stay at λ=0 (their natural fixed point under coordinate descent).

## Success Criteria
- [ ] T2 (stepstone K=9) max_err < 1e-4 (closes 13% gap from current 2.79e-4 master baseline).
- [ ] T1, T4, T5 still PASS.
- [ ] Full regression FAIL=0.
- [ ] No public API change (projection is internal to LM-Newton inner).
- [ ] kk1204 K=20 severe-skew: at least PARTIAL (max_err < 1e-3, no requirement on wall).

## Context & Background
- **Master HEAD:** `7dca47d` (Epic-C verdict commit). Newton-KL solver state: TH-1a refactor + LM/LSE/best-iterate + harmless `lf_capture` shim from Epic-C WI-1.
- **Investigation:** `docs/investigations/2026-05-02-newton-kl-ieppa-warmstart-result.md` documents WHY warm-start failed.
- **Investigation (older):** `docs/investigations/2026-05-01-newton-kl-homotopy-result.md` documents Epic-B target-homotopy failure.
- **Key empirical fact:** cold-start Newton on stepstone reaches gap≈1.4e-4 then drifts. Best-iterate restores. Result: max_err=2.79e-4. With LM scale-invariant damping and Marquardt gain ratio, μ ratchets down toward zero — adapting to the local conditioning. But adapting μ does NOT address rank-deficient DIRECTIONS — only magnitudes.

## Mechanism
Standard textbook fix for rank-deficient Newton: SVD or eigendecomposition of `H_pre`, threshold-truncate small eigenvalues, project the Newton step onto the column space spanned by retained eigenvectors. Newton-style algorithms call this "truncated SVD pseudoinverse" or "rank-deficient Newton".

Per-iter cost: full eigendecomposition of n_λ×n_λ matrix. n_λ for stepstone K=9 ≈ 30. Eigendecomp O(n_λ³) ≈ 27000 flops. Trivial vs accumulation O(n·K²) = 200M.

The damping (LM `μ·diag(H)`) is orthogonal to projection — they address different failure modes (LM addresses scaling, projection addresses rank). Keep LM. Add projection as an additional inner-loop step in `run_newton_inner` between the Hessian accumulation and the LDLT solve.

## Forbidden
- DO NOT layer this on top of warm-start (Epic-B and Epic-C already failed).
- DO NOT remove LM damping (orthogonal concern; both stay).
- DO NOT modify `R/harvest.R` API.
- DO NOT loosen test gates.

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Atomic tickets:
- WJ-0: spec amendment (rank-deficient projection subsection)
- WJ-1: implement projected Newton step in `run_newton_inner` (eigendecomp / threshold / project / solve via pseudoinverse OR LDLT-after-projection)
- WJ-2: T11 unit test — synthetic rank-deficient fixture asserts projection drops degenerate direction (λ stays 0 in null space)
- WJ-3: verify full testthat suite (T1-T5 PASS, T2 < 1e-4, T11 PASS)
- WJ-4: bench kk1204 + stepstone (CSV with masters baseline + projection)
- WJ-5: verdict + investigation doc + epic close

Plan to be drafted with Opus + plan-review-gate.

- Plan rev 3 (homotopy): `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-01-newton-kl-homotopy-plan.md`

- `src/newton_calib.cpp` — understand `CalibState`, `lam_off` (size sum(cat_counts-1), no NA), `cat_counts`, `lam` vector layout

Grep ALL call sites of `ieppa_solve` before touching the signature:
```
grep -rn "ieppa_solve" src/ R/ tests/
```

---

## III. Constraints & Guards

- **Fix A — lf indexing rigour:** Explicitly distinguish:
  - IEPPA `cat_offset_ieppa`: size sum(cat_counts)+K. `cat_offset_ieppa[k+1] = cat_offset_ieppa[k] + cat_counts[k] + 1`. NA bucket at index `cat_counts[k]` per margin — NEVER access in conversion.
  - Newton `lam_off`: size sum(cat_counts-1), no NA slot. `lam_off[k+1] = lam_off[k] + cat_counts[k]-1`.
  - Conversion reads `lf[cat_offset_ieppa[k] + j]` for `j in [0, cat_counts[k]-1]` only. Loop bound: `j < cat_counts[k]`.
- **Fix B — capture lf_best:** The lf-capture writes `lf_best` (IEPPA's best-iterate, mirroring `ieppa.cpp:386` `W_best`), NOT the raw `lf` at exit. Ensures converted lambda reflects quality-checked best point, not an SRAA overstep.
- **Fix C — RAII guard, not exit-path enumeration:** Implement lf-capture via a RAII guard struct that writes `*lf_capture = lf_best` on destruction. Fires at ALL exits without manual enumeration:
  ```cpp
  struct LfCaptureGuard {
      std::vector<double>* out;
      const std::vector<double>& lf_best;
      ~LfCaptureGuard() { if (out) *out = lf_best; }
  } lf_guard{lf_capture, lf_best};
  ```
- `ieppa_solve` signature change MUST default-nullptr the new parameter — all existing callers compile unchanged.
- **DO NOT touch** the IEPPA coordinate-descent loop body (~line 637).
- **DO NOT wire** the shim into Newton's call path (that is WI-2).
- Build clean: `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` — zero new warnings.
- All existing tests pass bit-identically.
- Files in scope: `src/ieppa.hpp`, `src/ieppa.cpp`, `src/newton_calib.cpp`, `src/newton_calib.hpp`.
- Files forbidden: `src/r_bridge.cpp`, `src/c_api.cpp`, `R/*.R`, `NEWS.md`, `tests/`.
- Conventional commit: `feat(newton_kl,ieppa): add IEPPA lf-capture shim for Newton-KL warm-start (no wiring yet)`

---

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

1. **Grep call sites:** `grep -rn "ieppa_solve" src/ R/ tests/`

2. **Edit `src/ieppa.hpp`:** Change declaration to:
   `IEPPAResult ieppa_solve(CalibState& state, std::vector<double>* lf_capture = nullptr);`

3. **Edit `src/ieppa.cpp`:** Add the `lf_capture` parameter. Add RAII guard (Fix C) that captures `lf_best` (Fix B) on destruction. No exit-path enumeration needed.

4. **Edit `src/newton_calib.cpp`:** Add `WarmstartResult` struct and `newton_kl_ieppa_warmstart` function (file-static):
   - `WarmstartResult { std::vector<double> lam; int n_iters; double max_err; int status; };`
   - Copy `st` -> `st_warm`, set `st_warm.outer_max_iter = K_warm`, `st_warm.accelerate = true`.
   - Declare `std::vector<double> lf_out;`, call `ieppa_solve(st_warm, &lf_out)`.
   - SRAA fallback (plan §Q5): if status != RK_OK, retry with `accelerate = false`. If still fails, return `WarmstartResult{{}, 0, 0.0, status}`.
   - **lf -> lambda conversion (Fix A):**
     ```cpp
     for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) {
         const double lf0 = lf_out[cat_offset_ieppa[k] + 0];
         for (int j = 1; j < cat_counts[k]; ++j)  // STOP before cat_counts[k] (NA bucket)
             lam_out[lam_off[k] + j - 1] = lf_out[cat_offset_ieppa[k] + j] - lf0;
     }
     // INVARIANT: lf_out[cat_offset_ieppa[k] + cat_counts[k]] (NA slot) never read
     ```
   - Finite check: if any `lam_out[a]` is non-finite, return `WarmstartResult{{}, 0, 0.0, RK_ERR_DIVERGED}`.
   - Return `WarmstartResult{lam_out, n_iters, max_err, RK_OK}`.

5. **Build:** `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` — 0 errors, 0 new warnings.

6. **Run existing tests:** `Rscript -e "testthat::test_local('.')"` — FAIL=0.

7. **Fix G — Empirical K_warm=8 validation (ABORT criterion):** After shim builds, run one-shot scratch script on stepstone:

# Epic-C: Newton-KL IEPPA warm-start

## Triggered by
Epic-B (target homotopy) verdict BLOCKED. Per-margin uniform T_eps regressed
T2 stepstone K=9 from 2.8e-4 (LM baseline, TH-1a refactor on master) to 2.29e-3.
Homotopy through smoothed targets lands Newton in a worse basin than starting
from λ=0 — for stepstone's overlapping-margin sample, the intermediate ε's λ*
is structurally distinct from λ*(T_0).

## Goal
Run 5-10 IEPPA iterations FIRST to get λ near λ*(T_0), then hand off to LM-Newton
for fast polishing. IEPPA is coordinate descent (no overshoot), proven to converge
on overlapping-margin fixtures. Newton from there starts inside the basin and
converges fast.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] T2 (stepstone K=9) PASSES at max_err<1e-4.
- [ ] T8 (K=20 severe-skew unit) PASSES at max_err<1e-3.
- [ ] kk1204 severe-skew bench: max_err<1e-4 (wall ≥3s acceptable per honest gate).
- [ ] Full regression FAIL=0.
- [ ] No public API change (warm-start is internal).

## Mechanism
- Inside `newton_calibrate`: before the LM-Newton loop, run 5-10 IEPPA iters
  at the original T (no homotopy), seeding λ from the IEPPA result.
- IEPPA already implemented in `src/ieppa.cpp` — call its inner loop directly,
  or extract a callable helper.
- Hand off λ at the LM-Newton entry point.
- LM-Newton runs the existing inner from this warm start; expected to converge
  quickly given proximity to λ*.

## Forbidden
- DO NOT layer target homotopy on top of IEPPA warm-start (Epic-B already
  attempted and failed; combining two failed strategies risks compounding).
- DO NOT call `harvest()` recursively (use the C-level IEPPA helper).
- Test gate loosening forbidden.

## Out of Scope
- AUTO routing changes (ship safety guard only on ESCAPE verdict).
- SIMD / multithread optimization.

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Atomic tickets to be drafted: TH-1a's run_newton_inner refactor is reusable;
this epic's atomic tasks will (1) extract IEPPA inner helper, (2) wire IEPPA
warm-start in newton_calibrate, (3) tests, (4) bench, (5) verdict.

## Reference
Investigation: `docs/investigations/2026-05-01-newton-kl-homotopy-result.md`
(to be written as part of Epic-B closure).

     ```cpp
     // Severe target skew: newton_kl drifts even with target homotopy
     ```

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Append T7:
   ```r
   test_that("T7: target homotopy + stepstone K=9 max_err < 1e-4", {
     skip_if_not_installed("arrow"); skip_if_not_installed("jsonlite")
     data_path <- if (file.exists("benchmarks/stepstone_bench_data.parquet"))
                    "benchmarks/stepstone_bench_data.parquet"
                  else if (file.exists("../../benchmarks/stepstone_bench_data.parquet"))
                    "../../benchmarks/stepstone_bench_data.parquet"
                  else NA_character_
     tgt_path  <- if (file.exists("benchmarks/stepstone_bench_targets.json"))
                    "benchmarks/stepstone_bench_targets.json"
                  else if (file.exists("../../benchmarks/stepstone_bench_targets.json"))
                    "../../benchmarks/stepstone_bench_targets.json"
                  else NA_character_
     skip_if(is.na(data_path) || is.na(tgt_path), "stepstone bench data not available")
     df  <- arrow::read_parquet(data_path); df$uuid <- NULL
     tgt <- lapply(jsonlite::fromJSON(tgt_path), function(t) { t <- unlist(t); t/sum(t) })
     for (nm in names(tgt)) df[[nm]] <- factor(df[[nm]])
     r <- suppressWarnings(harvest(df, tgt, method="newton_kl",
       max_weight=5, min_weight=0, max_iterations=200L,
       attach_weights=FALSE, verbose=0L))
     res <- attr(r, "result")
     expect_true(!is.null(res$n_homotopy_levels_used),
       label="T7: n_homotopy_levels_used must surface in R")
     expect_gte(res$n_homotopy_levels_used, 1L,
       label=sprintf("T7: at least 1 ε level must run; got %d", res$n_homotopy_levels_used))
     expect_equal(res$status, 0L,
       label=sprintf("T7: status=%d max_err=%.2e", res$status, res$max_error))
     expect_lt(res$max_error, 1e-4,
       label=sprintf("T7: max_err=%.2e must be < 1e-4 with homotopy", res$max_error))
   })
   ```
2. Append T8 (K=20 severe-skew unit fixture):
   ```r
   test_that("T8: K=20 severe-skew homotopy converges (no rank-deficient drift)", {
     set.seed(1L); n <- 10000L; K <- 20L; nj <- 5L
     df <- as.data.frame(lapply(seq_len(K), function(k)
       factor(sample(letters[seq_len(nj)], n, TRUE))))
     names(df) <- paste0("m", seq_len(K))
     tgt <- lapply(df, function(f) {
       p <- c(0.6, 0.2, 0.1, 0.07, 0.03); p <- p/sum(p); setNames(p, levels(f))
     })
     r <- suppressWarnings(harvest(df, tgt, method="newton_kl",
       max_weight=3, min_weight=0, max_iterations=300L,
       attach_weights=FALSE, verbose=0L))

     expect_lt(res$lm_mu_final, 1e6,
       label=sprintf("T8: lm_mu_final must NOT saturate (got %.2e); saturation indicates drift", res$lm_mu_final))
     expect_lt(res$max_error, 1e-3,
       label=sprintf("T8: max_err=%.2e must be < 1e-3 (severe-skew K=20 regime)", res$max_error))
   })
   ```

# TH-1b: Homotopy regression test

**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION
**Parent:** leafblower-91u7

* **Why:** Without a regression test, a future refactor could silently break the homotopy schedule (e.g., off-by-one on ε count, dropping the final ε=0 step).

## II. Input Specification
* **File:** `tests/testthat/test-newton-kl.R`.
* **Format:** R / testthat 3.

## III. Constraints & Guards

- DO NOT skip tests via `skip_if_not(...)` based on `n_homotopy_levels_used` being NULL — if the field is missing, the test must FAIL (signals LM-1c is incomplete).
- Test must use the same stepstone fixture as T2 (path-resolution helper from T2).

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Append T7 to test file:
```r
# T7: Target homotopy fires all ε levels and breaks stepstone basin floor.
test_that("T7: target homotopy 4 ε levels + stepstone K=9 max_err < 1e-4", {
  skip_if_not_installed("arrow")
  skip_if_not_installed("jsonlite")
  data_path <- if (file.exists("benchmarks/stepstone_bench_data.parquet"))
                 "benchmarks/stepstone_bench_data.parquet"
               else if (file.exists("../../benchmarks/stepstone_bench_data.parquet"))
                 "../../benchmarks/stepstone_bench_data.parquet"
               else NA_character_
  tgt_path  <- if (file.exists("benchmarks/stepstone_bench_targets.json"))
                 "benchmarks/stepstone_bench_targets.json"
               else if (file.exists("../../benchmarks/stepstone_bench_targets.json"))
                 "../../benchmarks/stepstone_bench_targets.json"
               else NA_character_
  skip_if(is.na(data_path) || is.na(tgt_path), "stepstone bench data not available")

  df  <- arrow::read_parquet(data_path); df$uuid <- NULL
  tgt <- lapply(jsonlite::fromJSON(tgt_path), function(t) { t <- unlist(t); t / sum(t) })
  for (nm in names(tgt)) df[[nm]] <- factor(df[[nm]])

  r <- suppressWarnings(harvest(df, tgt, method="newton_kl",
    max_weight=5, min_weight=0, max_iterations=100L, attach_weights=FALSE, verbose=0L))
  res <- attr(r, "result")
  expect_true(!is.null(res$n_homotopy_levels_used),
    label="T7: n_homotopy_levels_used must surface in R result")
  expect_equal(res$n_homotopy_levels_used, 4L,
    label=sprintf("T7: all 4 ε levels must fire; got %d", res$n_homotopy_levels_used))
  expect_equal(res$status, 0L,
    label=sprintf("T7: status=%d max_err=%.2e", res$status, res$max_error))
  expect_lt(res$max_error, 1e-4,
    label=sprintf("T7: max_err=%.2e must be < 1e-4 after homotopy", res$max_error))
})
```
2. Run `Rscript -e "testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/test-newton-kl.R')"` and confirm T1-T7 PASS (T2 will also pass since same fixture is now homotopy-solved).

**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION

## I. Context & Objective

- ≤40 added lines.

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Open spec. Locate end of "Levenberg-Marquardt damping" subsection.
2. Append:
```markdown
### Target homotopy

LM damping stabilizes Newton inside its convergence basin but cannot deform the basin itself. Severe-skew K=20 problems and stepstone-style overlapping margins have rank-deficient Hessians whose dual landscape has a finite-gap plateau — Newton converges to that plateau but no further. To break it, smooth the targets with a uniform-prior blend and anneal the blend to zero.

**Schedule:** ε ∈ {0.5, 0.1, 0.01, 0.0}.

**Per-ε targets:** `T_eps[k][j] = (1-ε)·T[k][j] + ε·(1/cat_counts[k])` (per-margin uniform; NOT joint uniform — joint would explode cell count).

**Inner solve:** existing LM-damped Newton iter loop, max 20 iters per ε. Reset `lm_mu = 1e-3` at start of each ε (don't carry stale damping across ε boundaries; standard interior-point practice). Convergence per ε: `||∇g_eps||_∞ < tol_abs`. λ carries across ε boundaries (warm start).

**Final ε=0:** runs the same inner with original targets; expected to converge in 3-5 Newton iters from a near-optimal warm start.

**Recovery:** weights computed from final ε=0's converged λ. No homotopy bias in returned weights.

**New diagnostic:** `n_homotopy_levels_used` field on `NewtonCalibResult` records actual ε steps that fired.

**AUTO routing impact:** none (homotopy is internal to `newton_calibrate`; signature unchanged).

See plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-01-newton-kl-homotopy-plan.md`.
```
3. Commit: `docs(spec): Newton-KL — add target homotopy section`.

# Epic-B: Newton-KL target homotopy

## Triggered by
LM-2 verdict NEEDS_HOMOTOPY on epic leafblower-5k08.

## Goal
Wrap Newton-KL in a target-homotopy outer loop: `T_τ = (1-ε)·T + ε·uniform` with ε schedule {0.5, 0.1, 0.01, 0}; warm-start λ from previous ε; reset `lm_mu` to init at each ε step. Push max_err below 1e-4 on stepstone K=9 (T2 currently 2.8e-4) and break the K=20 severe-skew rank-deficiency drift.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] T2 (stepstone K=9) PASS at max_err<1e-4 AND ≤ greenkhorn baseline.
- [ ] T6 / T6b (μ-schedule tests, deferred from LM-1b) authored + PASS.
- [ ] kk1204 severe-skew benchmark: max_err<1e-4 on at least one ε-level (likely intermediate ε~0.1-0.01); document final wall vs honest <3s gate.
- [ ] No public API change (homotopy is internal to newton_calibrate).
- [ ] Full regression FAIL=0.

## Mechanism
- Outer loop over ε ∈ {0.5, 0.1, 0.01, 0}.
- At each ε: build smoothed targets `T_eps[k] = (1-ε)·T[k] + ε·uniform_k`, run Newton-KL inner with warm-start λ from prior ε. Reset lm_mu=1e-3 at start of each ε.
- Final ε=0: standard Newton-KL converges quickly from a near-optimal warm start.
- Cost: 4× single Newton-KL solve per ε × ~5 iters each = ~20 inner Newton iters total (similar wall to current ~33-iter drift).

## Forbidden
- Targets are NOT modified at the API boundary; smoothing is internal.
- DO NOT replace with IEPPA warm-start (separate Epic-C path; orthogonal).
- DO NOT loosen test gates.

## Out of Scope
- AUTO routing changes (= follow-up after Epic-B verdict).
- IEPPA warm-start (= Epic-C alternative).
- r_bridge.cpp surfacing of `lm_mu_final` (= LM-1c, simple follow-up; can land before or after Epic-B).

## Sub-Agent Strategy
1 ticket: target-homotopy implementation in `src/newton_calib.cpp`. Then verify tests + benchmark.

# LM-1b: μ-schedule regression test

**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION
**Parent:** leafblower-5k08
**Depends on:** leafblower-5k08.5 (LM-1 must land first to expose `lm_mu_final` field)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add T6 to `tests/testthat/test-newton-kl.R` that exercises the lm_mu adaptation schedule on a synthetic problem; amend T1 to assert convergence exited via gradient criterion (not step_norm fallback).
* **Why:** Completeness-reviewer C1: T1-T5 cannot localize a μ-update bug from a Hessian or LSE bug. C7: μ-trajectory observability is required for LM-3 verdict diagnosis. Without T6, a swapped /3 vs ×10 sign error would not be caught.
* **Reference Data:**
  - Test file: `tests/testthat/test-newton-kl.R` (T1-T5 currently present).
  - LM-1 added `lm_mu_final` to `NewtonCalibResult`; surfaced to R via `attr(r, "result")$lm_mu_final` (verify after LM-1).

## II. Input Specification
* **File:** `tests/testthat/test-newton-kl.R` (single edit).
* **Format:** R / testthat 3.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | T6 must use a fixture where μ-decrease is the EXPECTED outcome (well-conditioned uniform K=3) — assert `lm_mu_final < 1e-3` (decreased from init 1.0 across multiple Newton successes). |
| **Logic** | T6b (sub-test): use a stress fixture where rho<0.25 fires (severely-skewed K=20 small-n) — assert `lm_mu_final >= 1.0` (did NOT decrease, indicating gain-ratio gating worked). |
| **Logic** | T1 amendment: assert `attr(r, "result")$convergence_used$convergence_reason == "criterion"` (not "step_norm"). |
| **Logic** | DO NOT skip via `skip_if_not(...)` based on lm_mu_final being NULL — if the field is missing, the test must FAIL (signals LM-1 is incomplete). |
| **Format** | testthat 3 conventions; match existing T1-T5 style. |
| **Boundary** | DO NOT touch any C++ file. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse, exact. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read `tests/testthat/test-newton-kl.R` and locate T1.
2. Amend T1 by adding (after existing assertions):
   ```r
   reason <- attr(r, "result")$convergence_used$convergence_reason
   expect_equal(reason, "criterion",
     label=sprintf("T1 must exit via gradient criterion, not step_norm; got %s", reason))
   ```
3. Append T6 + T6b at end of file:
   ```r
   # T6: μ-schedule decreases on well-conditioned problem (recovers Newton).
   test_that("T6: lm_mu decreases toward 0 on well-conditioned K=3 problem", {
     set.seed(1L); n <- 1000L
     df <- data.frame(
       a = factor(sample(c("x","y","z"), n, TRUE)),
       b = factor(sample(c("M","F"),     n, TRUE)),
       c = factor(sample(c("Y","O","S"), n, TRUE))
     )
     tgt <- list(
       a = c(x=0.4, y=0.35, z=0.25),
       b = c(M=0.50, F=0.50),
       c = c(Y=0.45, O=0.40, S=0.15)
     )
     r <- harvest(df, tgt, method="newton_kl",
                  convergence=list(absolute=1e-7), max_iterations=50L,
                  attach_weights=FALSE)
     res <- attr(r, "result")
     expect_true(!is.null(res$lm_mu_final),
       label="T6: lm_mu_final must be exposed in result struct")
     expect_lt(res$lm_mu_final, 1e-2,
       label=sprintf("T6: lm_mu must decrease from init 1.0 on well-conditioned problem; got %.2e", res$lm_mu_final))
   })

   # T6b: μ-schedule increases on stress fixture (gain ratio gates correctly).
   test_that("T6b: lm_mu increases under stress (severe skew small-n K=20)", {
     set.seed(1L); n <- 500L; K <- 20L; nj <- 5L
     df <- as.data.frame(lapply(seq_len(K), function(k)
       factor(sample(letters[seq_len(nj)], n, TRUE))))
     names(df) <- paste0("m", seq_len(K))
     tgt <- lapply(df, function(f) {
       p <- c(0.6,0.2,0.1,0.07,0.03); p <- p/sum(p); setNames(p, levels(f))
     })
     r <- suppressWarnings(harvest(df, tgt, method="newton_kl",
                                    max_weight=3, max_iterations=20L,
                                    attach_weights=FALSE, verbose=0L))
     res <- attr(r, "result")
     expect_true(!is.null(res$lm_mu_final),
       label="T6b: lm_mu_final must be exposed")
     # On hard problem: lm_mu should NOT decrease to negligible (rho<0.25 fires).
     expect_gt(res$lm_mu_final, 1e-4,
       label=sprintf("T6b: lm_mu must NOT collapse to ~0 on stress fixture; got %.2e", res$lm_mu_final))
   })
   ```
4. Run `Rscript -e "testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/test-newton-kl.R')" 2>&1 | tail -10`.
5. Confirm 8 tests PASS (T1, T2, T4, T5, T6, T6b plus internal T3 already-skipped) — all green.

Update line 76 ("Newton step: δ = H⁻¹ ∇g, λ ← λ + α δ (Armijo line search for α)") to reference damped form: "Newton step: H_damped δ = ∇g where H_damped[a,a] = max(H[a,a]·(1+lm_mu), lm_mu·d_floor); λ -= α δ (Armijo line search; gain-ratio adaptive lm_mu)". Cross-reference plan rev2 for mechanism details. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read current spec section starting at line 56 ("Math") through line 112 ("LDLT solve").
2. Edit line 76 to reference damped form (one-line update).
3. Append new subsection after line 112:
   ```markdown
   ### Levenberg-Marquardt damping
   Sample H rank-collapses dynamically as λ drifts (severe-skew K=20 case).
   Plain Newton overshoots, gradient stalls. Solution: scale-invariant damping
   with additive floor:
   - `H_damped[a,a] = max(H[a,a]·(1+lm_mu), lm_mu·d_floor)` where `d_floor = mean(diag(H))`.
   - `(1+lm_mu)` preserves scale where H is well-conditioned.
   - `max(..., lm_mu·d_floor)` provides damping where H[a,a]→0 (rank collapse).
   - Adaptive `lm_mu` via Marquardt gain ratio `ρ = (g_curr - g_trial) / (α·G·δ - 0.5·α²·δᵀHδ)`:
     * `ρ > 0.75 ∧ Armijo full accept` ⇒ `lm_mu /= 3` (recover Newton).
     * `ρ < 0.25 ∨ Armijo failed` ⇒ `lm_mu *= 10` (back off).
     * else: keep.
   - Init: `lm_mu = 1.0`. Bounds: [1e-12, 1e12]. Failed line search → retry with larger lm_mu (max 3 retries) before giving up.
   ```
4. Commit: `docs(spec): Newton-KL — add LM scale-invariant damping section`.

# Epic: Newton-KL LM-damping convergence fix (A1 + A2)

## Goal
Fix Newton-KL convergence on stepstone K=9 (regression: max_err=3.85e-4, T2 fails) and probe kk1204 severe-skew K=20 by replacing trust-region+pivot-bump bandaids with Levenberg-Marquardt scale-invariant damping `(H + μ·diag(H))·δ = G`.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] T1-T5 all PASS in test-newton-kl.R (currently 6 PASS, 3 FAIL on T2)
- [ ] Stepstone K=9 max_err < 1e-4, status=0 (was 3.85e-4 with bandaids)
- [ ] kk1204 severe-skew benchmark produces decision-grade report: GATE_MET (<2s, max_err<1e-4) | NEEDS_HOMOTOPY (≥2s or max_err≥1e-4 but converging) | ESCAPE (diverges; route AUTO away)
- [ ] Full regression: FAIL 0 across testthat suite
- [ ] No public API change (newton_calib internal only)

## Context & Background
**Diagnosis (verified 2026-05-01):**
- Original Newton-KL: NaN weights on K=20 severe-skew via exp(u_i) overflow + false convergence (gap=0 from NaN compares).
- Already shipped: LSE stabilization (A1) — fixes NaN by computing exp(u_i - u_max). kk1204 now produces finite weights but Newton drifts on severe skew (sample H rank-collapses as λ moves into low-density regions).
- Bandaids in place: trust_radius=1.0, pivot=1e-8/1e-4. Together degraded stepstone (T2 max_err 3.85e-4 vs target 1e-4) — over-regularized well-conditioned problems.

**Root cause:** Sample Hessian rank-collapses dynamically when exp(u_i - u_max) is meaningfully nonzero only on a shrinking subset. Trust-region clipping cripples Newton in those directions; small pivot floor doesn't repair direction.

**LM scale-invariant fix:** `(H + μ·diag(H))·δ = G` with adaptive μ. μ↘/3 on Armijo full-accept (recover Newton near optimum); μ↗×10 on Armijo failure (back off toward gradient descent in collapsed-rank directions). diag(H) preserves per-coordinate scale (each diag is p_a(1-p_a) ≈ 0.16 for uniform).

**Spec:** docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-01-newton-kl-calibration-design.md

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Single-file C++ change (newton_calib.cpp lines ~110-260). One coder agent (Tier 2) implements LM-1; one runner verifies LM-2 and LM-3 sequentially. No parallel WUs (LM-2 and LM-3 read state produced by LM-1).

**Global Guards:**
- DO NOT touch other solvers (ieppa, lbfgsb, raking, chebyshev).
- DO NOT change R/harvest.R signature or .Call arity.
- DO NOT skip pre-commit hooks.
- Honest reporting on LM-3: if kk1204 severe doesn't pass <2s gate, REPORT and propose Epic-B (target homotopy) — do not silently fudge fixture.
close_reason: LM-2 verdict NEEDS_HOMOTOPY. Final state: LM scale-invariant damping + Marquardt gain ratio + LSE + best-iterate = stable convergence to natural Newton basin floor (T2 stepstone max_err = 2.8e-4 vs <1e-4 gate). Investigation: docs/investigations/2026-05-01-newton-kl-lm-result.md. Follow-up: leafblower-91u7 (Epic-B target homotopy).

title: N2: Newton-KL implementation (newton_calib.hpp/.cpp full algorithm)
description:
# N2: Newton-KL Implementation
**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION
**Spec:** docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-01-newton-kl-calibration-design.md (sections "Math", "Single-Pass Per-Step Algorithm", "Cost Analysis", "Result Struct", "Convergence Criterion", "Bounds Handling and Fallback")
**Blocks:** N3 (r_bridge wiring needs the function symbol)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace the N1 stub with the full Newton solver — obs-level Hessian/gradient single-pass, LDLT solve, Armijo line search, bounds-fallback.
* **Why:** Core algorithm. < 2s on kk1204 target.
* **Reference Data:** Spec algorithm pseudocode (lines 82-111).

## II. Input Specification
* **Files:** `src/newton_calib.hpp` (extend stub), `src/newton_calib.cpp` (full implementation).
* **Reused infrastructure:**
  - `lbw::ldlt_factor_inplace(double* A, size_t n, double eps_perturb)` — calib_linalg.hpp:43
  - `lbw::ldlt_solve(const double* A, size_t n, double* b)` — calib_linalg.hpp:50
  - `lbw::solver_setup_ct(...)` — calib_dispatch.hpp:279 (cell-table+validation preamble)
  - `lbw::mark_converged(res, cfg, iter)` — calib_dispatch.hpp:267
  - `CalibState::group_ids[k][i]` — obs-level category lookup (NOT g_per_cell)

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Obs-level loop; iterate `i = 0..n-1` using `st.group_ids[k][i]`. NEVER use `cell_lf` or `g_per_cell`. Reference-eliminate `lam_{k,0} = 0`. |
| **Format** | C++17. namespace lbw. |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT modify r_bridge.cpp, harvest.R, c_api.cpp dispatch (already wired in N1). |
| **Tone** | Numeric correctness > clever vectorization. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. **Header (`newton_calib.hpp`):** finalize struct exactly:
   ```cpp
   struct NewtonCalibResult {
       CalibResult base;
       int    n_lambda  = 0;
       double dual_gap  = 0.0;
       double step_norm = 0.0;
       double line_alpha = 1.0;
   };
   NewtonCalibResult newton_calibrate(CalibState& st);
   ```
2. **Setup (`newton_calib.cpp`):** call `solver_setup_ct(...)` for the cell-table validation preamble (st validation + bounds resolution); but NEVER use the cell table for the Newton loop. Compute `lam_off[k] = sum_{k'<k}(cat_counts[k']-1)`, n_lam = lam_off[K]. Validate `n_lam <= 256` (LDLT upper bound from kNCatsTotalMax).
3. **State allocation:** `vector<double> lam(n_lam, 0.0)`, `H(n_lam*n_lam, 0.0)`, `G(n_lam, 0.0)`, `delta(n_lam, 0.0)`, `T(n_lam, 0.0)`. Pack `T[lam_off[k]+j-1] = targets[k][j]` for j=1..cat_counts[k]-1. (Reference cat j=0 omitted.)
4. **Newton loop** (`for iter in 0..min(max_iter,50)`):
   a. Zero G, H, Z=0.
   b. Single obs-level pass `for i in 0..n-1`:
      - `u_i = sum_k (st.group_ids[k][i] > 0 ? lam[lam_off[k] + st.group_ids[k][i] - 1] : 0)`
      - `f_i = st.weights[i] * exp(u_i)`
      - `Z += f_i`
      - For k in 0..K-1: if `j = st.group_ids[k][i]; j > 0` → `G[lam_off[k]+j-1] += f_i`
      - For k1 in 0..K-1, k2 in k1..K-1: if `j1>0 && j2>0` → `H[(lam_off[k1]+j1-1)*n_lam + lam_off[k2]+j2-1] += f_i` (upper triangle storage; symmetrize at end)
   c. Normalize: `for a: G[a] /= Z`; `for a,b: H[a*n_lam+b] /= Z`.
   d. Subtract outer product: `H[a*n_lam+b] -= G[a]*G[b]`.
   e. Mirror upper to lower triangle (symmetrize for ldlt_factor_inplace which expects symmetric matrix).
   f. Subtract targets: `G[a] -= T[a]`.
   g. Convergence check (BEFORE solve): `dual_gap = max|G[a]|`; if `dual_gap < tol_abs` → `mark_converged(res, st.conv_cfg, iter)`; break.
   h. Newton solve: `delta = G;` `ldlt_factor_inplace(H.data(), n_lam, 1e-12);` `ldlt_solve(H.data(), n_lam, delta.data());`
   i. Armijo line search: alpha = 1; for ls in 0..20: evaluate `g(lam - alpha*delta)` (re-pass over obs to compute Z_trial - sum(T*lam_trial)); accept if `g(lam_trial) > g(lam) + 1e-4 * alpha * (-delta dot G)` (Wolfe-1 / sufficient-decrease, here gradient-ascent so flipped); else alpha *= 0.5.
   j. Update lam: `lam[a] -= alpha * delta[a]` (sign: ascending dual).
   k. step_norm = norm(alpha*delta); if `step_norm < 1e-12` → break (Newton step collapsed; mark_converged with convergence_iter=iter).
5. **Post-solve bounds fallback:** Compute `w_i = (st.weights[i] * exp(u_i)) / Z * n` for all i; count `n_violated = #{i : w_i > st.max_weight || w_i < st.min_weight}`. If `n_violated / n > 0.05` → `res.base.status = RK_ERR_NOCONV`, set message "bounds violated >5%; Newton solution may be inadmissible". Otherwise leave status as set by mark_converged (or RK_ERR_BUDGET if loop exhausted).
6. **Return weights:** Always write Newton weights `w_i = f_i/Z * n` into `st.weights[i]`. Populate `res.n_lambda = n_lam`, `res.dual_gap`, `res.step_norm`, `res.line_alpha`. Pack `res.base.iterations = iter+1`, `res.base.max_error` as max_k max_j |achieved_kj - target_kj|.
7. **Compile gate:** `R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -2` must report DONE.

```json

}
```

- [ ] newton_calib.cpp implements obs-level loop using group_ids[k][i].
- [ ] LDLT factor + solve via lbw::ldlt_factor_inplace / lbw::ldlt_solve.

title: fix(greenkhorn): force round-robin sweep when accelerate=TRUE
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Disable greenkhorn's internal per-step argmax selection when accelerate=TRUE, replacing with round-robin so SRAA's fixed-point map is stationary.
* **Why:** Greenkhorn IS the greedy coordinate-descent Sinkhorn: each step picks argmax-violation margin. This non-stationarity (F(X) depends on X's residuals, not just X) breaks SRAA's convergence theory. Benchmark shows greenkhorn+sraa DEFF=2.031 > plain 1.963, wmed=0.439 vs 0.581, wt_kl<0 — SRAA steering to a different, worse attractor.
* **Reference:** Same issue as ieppa's greedy downgrade (B5: 'use_greedy_sraa=false when accelerate=TRUE'). src/greenkhorn.cpp needs the same fix.
* **Note:** In greenkhorn the greedy IS the algorithm (not a scheduler option). With accelerate=TRUE, the full-round-robin sweep inside f_eval_lf already calls apply_single_margin_log/linear for all K margins. Greenkhorn's own F_eval should use round-robin too.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/greenkhorn.cpp — the greenkhorn_solve function
* **Format:** C++17

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | When st.accelerate=TRUE: run all K margins in round-robin order (not argmax). When st.accelerate=FALSE: keep existing greedy argmax behavior. |
| **Format** | Single conditional at solve entry, no duplicate logic |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/greenkhorn.cpp to find the per-step argmax selection loop
2. Add: if (st.accelerate) { log message; use round-robin } else { existing greedy }
3. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . && Rscript -e 'testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat")'
4. Verify greenkhorn+sraa benchmark shows DEFF closer to plain greenkhorn

## V. Output Schema
```json
{"task_id": "LBW-XXX", "success": true, "data": {"greenkhorn_sraa_deff_improved": true}, "error_log": null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] greenkhorn+sraa uses round-robin when accelerate=TRUE
- [ ] log message '[greenkhorn] greedy disabled under SRAA-m; using round_robin' at verbose>=1
- [ ] all tests pass
- [ ] benchmark shows greenkhorn+sraa DEFF ≈ plain greenkhorn (1.963±0.05)
close_reason: Wrong analysis: greenkhorn's greedy F(X) IS deterministic (same X→same errRp→same argmax). SRAA is valid. No code change needed. wt_kl<0 is a different-attractor issue, not a theory violation.

title: B3: SRAA outer loop with lf_best tracking (replaces for-loop)
description:
## Objective
Replace iter_in_lvl for-loop with SRAA while-loop when accelerate=TRUE && use_linear. Manage lf_best for stall revert, W_best for output, SRAAState lifecycle.

## Input & Guards
- File: src/ieppa.cpp (homotopy level, after linear phase init)
- Guards: Must compile; if/else branch (not alongside old for-loop); F_cur seeded once before loop

## Logic
1. if (st.accelerate && use_linear): SRAA path
2. Init: SRAAState, lf_flat, lf_best, pack lf → lf_flat, seed F_cur
3. while-loop: f_evals_used < budget_lvl && !converged
   - sraa_step(f_eval_lf, lf_flat, {}, {}, ieppa_sraa, apply_clamp=false)
   - Update res.base.iterations = f_evals_used
   - Track best: save W_best (X/X_init) + lf_best if err < best_metric_seen
   - Outer stall guard: if err > best*(1+kSRAAOuterSlack), revert lf_best + reseed F_cur
   - Check convergence
4. else: existing for-loop unchanged

## DoD
- [ ] Compile; correct state threading
- [ ] lf_best used only for SRAA revert, not for output
- [ ] W_best (normalized ratios) remains output source

title: B2: f_eval_lf lambda (captures sweep state, handles overflow)

   - pack_lf(lf, flat)
   - if (overflow) return inf; else compute errRp and return

title: B1: pack_lf/unpack_lf helpers in ieppa.cpp
description:
## Objective
Implement pack_lf() and unpack_lf() helpers in ieppa.cpp to convert between lf-space (log-factor iterate) and cell-space (X_cur, etc.).

## Input & Guards
- File: src/ieppa.cpp
- Guards: Must compile; no changes to existing non-SRAA code paths; preserve alpha damping in sweep

## Logic
1. pack_lf(lf, dst): O(n_cats_total_with_na) copy lf → dst for SRAA state seeding
2. unpack_lf(src, lf, f_lin, cell_lf, X_cur, ct, X_init, st.K, cat_offset):
   - Copy src → lf
   - Derive f_lin[i] = exp(lf[i]) for all i
   - Rebuild cell_lf[c] = Σ_k lf[cat_offset[k] + g_per_cell[k][c]]
   - X_cur[c] = X_init[c] * exp(cell_lf[c])

## DoD
- [ ] Compile: R CMD INSTALL --preclean .
- [ ] No change to non-SRAA paths (verify with diff)

title: T5: Mehrotra predictor-corrector + Jacobi preconditioning in chebyshev.cpp
description:
# T5: Mehrotra + Jacobi
**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION (after T4)

## I. Objective
Replace the existing single-step barrier loop in chebyshev_ipm with Mehrotra predictor-corrector + Jacobi diagonal preconditioning. T_cheby_warm and T_cheby_K9 must go GREEN.

## II. Input
src/chebyshev.cpp — the main IPM iteration loop (find via grep kMaxIpm or schur_nu)
Spec §Change 3+4: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-29-chebyshev-greg-fix.md

## III. Guards
CRITICAL INVARIANTS:
- m > 0 guard: if (m == 0) { mu *= 0.1; continue; }
- N rebuilt fresh EACH iteration (A·D·A^T) — never cached between iterations
- Jacobi scaling applied ONCE before LDLT factorization
- Phase A: LDLT-factor scaled N; solve Phase A RHS (pre-scaled, post-unscale)
- Phase B: REUSE same LDLT (no refactor); solve Phase B RHS (pre-scaled, post-unscale)
- σ = clamp((μ_aff/μ)³, 1e-8, 1.0)
- μ_aff = clamp(dot(x+α*Δx, s+α*Δs)/(2m), 0, μ*100)
- 0.99 damping on step lengths
- Tikhonov fallback if LDLT fails
FORBIDDEN: changing kMaxIpm or existing convergence check; touching r_bridge.cpp/harvest.R

## IV. Logic
1. Read the existing IPM iteration loop in chebyshev.cpp (grep kMaxIpm, schur_nu)
2. Extract the complementarity vectors (x, s) and normal equations build (N = A·D·A^T)
3. Before the loop: understand the existing Schur complement formulation
4. Replace single-step loop body with:
   a. m>0 guard
   b. Rebuild N = A·D·A^T fresh
   c. Jacobi preconditioning: D_jac[j]=1/sqrt(max(N[j*nct+j],1e-12)); scale N in-place
   d. LDLT-factor scaled N once
   e. Phase A: scale rhs_A, solve, unscale Δλ_A
   f. Compute α_aff, μ_aff (with clamp), σ (with clamp)
   g. Phase B: rhs_B = rhs_A + σ*μ - Δx_aff·Δs_aff; scale rhs_B, solve SAME LDLT, unscale Δλ_B
   h. Line search α_p, α_d with 0.99 damping
   i. Update x, λ, s; recompute μ = dot(x,s)/(2m)
5. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -3 → '* DONE (leafblower)'
6. Rscript -e 'devtools::test(filter="chebyshev")' → T_cheby_warm GREEN
7. devtools::test() FAIL=3
8. Commit: 'feat(chebyshev): Mehrotra predictor-corrector + Jacobi preconditioning'

## V. Schema
{"task_id":"T5","success":true,"data":{"T_cheby_warm":"PASS","fail_count":3},"error_log":null}

## VI. DoD
- [ ] Mehrotra loop replaces existing single-step loop
- [ ] Jacobi preconditioning on Phase A and Phase B
- [ ] m>0 guard present; σ/μ_aff clamped
- [ ] Phase B reuses Phase A LDLT (confirmed by n_factorizations==iterations)
- [ ] T_cheby_warm GREEN (status=0, finite, ≤ raking)
- [ ] T_cheby_K9 GREEN or SKIP (parquet-dependent)
- [ ] devtools::test() FAIL=3
- [ ] Committed
close_reason: Mehrotra+Jacobi implemented. T_cheby_warm PASS (4.12e-14 < 1e-3). FAIL=3. n_factorizations increments once. Phase B reuses Phase A LDLT.

title: T3: Armijo line search with step-norm guard and pre-allocated buffers
description:
# T3: Armijo Line Search for logit_calib.cpp
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add Armijo backtracking line search to logit_calibrate() Newton loop: pre-allocate trial buffers, cap step via max_delta_z norm guard, backtrack until sufficient decrease, log warning if all halvings exhausted.
* **Why:** Without line search, Newton steps can be arbitrarily large, saturating cells even from a good initialization. Armijo guarantees progress toward the calibration fixed point.
* **Reference Data:** Spec §Layer 1 + Security Fix 1 (norm guard) + Security Fix 2 (pre-alloc) + Designer Fix 1 (stall warning). See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-29-sv89-logit-newton-fix.md.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/logit_calib.cpp after T1+T2 applied. Target: the Newton for-loop.
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | kMaxHalvings=10, kArmijoC=0.01, kMaxDeltaZ=2.0 — constexpr at function top |
| **Logic** | ORDERING: norm guard runs AFTER ldlt_solve (when b = delta_lambda, not residuals) |
| **Logic** | Pre-alloc: w_trial(M_cell), b_trial(nct), lambda_trial(nct) declared BEFORE Newton loop |
| **Logic** | Armijo condition: resid_sq_trial < resid_sq_0 * (1.0 - kArmijoC * alpha) |
| **Logic** | If all halvings exhausted with no improvement: accept alpha anyway (last alpha); emit st.log() warning if verbose>=1 |
| **Logic** | Recompute w_trial from lambda_trial (logit link); recompute b_trial residuals |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT change Newton loop iteration count (kMaxNewtonIters=50) |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT change check_convergence call — it remains at end of each iteration |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/logit_calib.cpp — understand current Newton loop structure.
2. Add constexpr: kMaxHalvings=10, kArmijoC=0.01, kMaxDeltaZ=2.0
3. BEFORE Newton loop: declare w_trial(ct.M_cell, 0.0), b_trial(nct, 0.0), lambda_trial(nct, 0.0)
4. INSIDE Newton loop, AFTER ldlt_solve (b = delta_lambda):
   a. Norm guard: compute max_delta_z over all cells (sum |b[cat_offset[k]+g]| per cell); alpha_max = min(1.0, kMaxDeltaZ / max_delta_z) if max_delta_z>0
   b. double alpha = alpha_max; resid_sq_0 = sum(b_current^2) [b_current = current residuals, NOT delta_lambda]
   c. Armijo loop: for halv in 0..kMaxHalvings: fill lambda_trial, recompute w_trial from logit link, compute b_trial; if resid_sq_trial < resid_sq_0*(1-kArmijoC*alpha): break; alpha *= 0.5
   d. If !armijo_improved && verbose>=1: st.log('[logit] Armijo exhausted (alpha=%.2e)', alpha)
   e. lambda += alpha * b [where b = delta_lambda from ldlt_solve]
5. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -3 → '* DONE'
6. Rscript -e 'devtools::test()' 2>&1 | tail -3 → FAIL == 3
7. Quick test: run harvest on 2-margin K=2 problem → must converge
8. git commit: 'fix(logit): Armijo line search with step-norm guard prevents Newton divergence'

## V. Output Schema (Strict)

```json
{"task_id": "T3", "success": true, "data": {"file": "src/logit_calib.cpp", "change": "Armijo+norm guard added"}, "error_log": null}
```

- [ ] Armijo condition checks calibration residuals (not step size)

description:
# T2: Design-weight initialization for logit_calib.cpp
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace the lambda=0 cold-start in logit_calibrate() with lambda_0 computed from a LS solve that places the starting point where sigma(z_c) ≈ normalized design weight — preventing the cold-start saturation cascade.
* **Why:** lambda=0 gives w[c]=2.5*n_per_cell (midpoint), far from calibrated solution. First Newton step overshoots. Design-weight initialization places lambda_0 such that the starting weights approximate the design weights, keeping sigma away from 0 and 1 on the first iteration.
* **Reference Data:** Spec §Layer 2 — Design-Weight Initialization. Uses calib_linalg.hpp: compute_normal_equations(ct, D_ones, N, cat_offset, K, nct), ldlt_factor_inplace(N, nct, 1e-10), ldlt_solve(N, nct, b). All already included.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/logit_calib.cpp — find where lambda is initialized (currently near line 79: std::vector<double> lambda(nct, 0.0)).
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | kInitSigmaEps = 1e-4 — clips sigma_target to [1e-4, 1-1e-4] to bound z_target |
| **Logic** | Degenerate: if (U_cell[c] <= L_cell[c] + 1e-12) set z_target[c] = 0.0 |
| **Logic** | Clip X_init outside [L, U]: sigma_target = clamp((X_init-L)/(U-L), 1e-4, 1-1e-4) |
| **Logic** | AA^T initialization uses compute_normal_equations with D_eff=1 (all-ones D vector) |
| **Logic** | lambda = ldlt result (b_init after solve), NOT accumulated with 0-init lambda |
| **Format** | Insert initialization block BEFORE the Newton for-loop, AFTER lambda is declared |
| **Boundary** | Do NOT change the Newton loop itself in this task (that is T3) |
| **Boundary** | scratch vectors: z_target(M_cell), D_ones(M_cell, 1.0), b_init(nct, 0.0), N_init(nct*nct, 0.0) |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read src/logit_calib.cpp — find lambda declaration (~line 79) and Newton loop start.
2. Add constexpr: `constexpr double kInitSigmaEps = 1e-4;`
3. After lambda declaration, insert initialization block:
   a. Allocate z_target(M_cell), D_ones(M_cell, 1.0), b_init(nct, 0.0), N_init(nct*nct, 0.0)
   b. For each cell c: compute sigma_target, z_target[c] = logit(sigma_target)
   c. For each (k,j) bucket: b_init[cat_offset[k]+j] = sum of z_target[c] over bucket
   d. compute_normal_equations(ct, D_ones.data(), N_init.data(), cat_offset.data(), K, (size_t)nct)
   e. ldlt_factor_inplace(N_init.data(), (size_t)nct, 1e-10) — check return value; if not RK_OK, leave lambda=0 (fall back silently)
   f. ldlt_solve(N_init.data(), (size_t)nct, b_init.data()) — b_init is now lambda_0
   g. lambda = b_init (assign, not accumulate)
4. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . 2>&1 | tail -3 → '* DONE'
5. devtools::test() 2>&1 | tail -3 → FAIL == 3
6. Quick sanity: verify that running harvest(df,tgt,method='logit') still works and gives finite weights

title: T1: D_eff floor — prevent sigma saturation singularity
description:
# T1: Add D_eff floor to logit_calib.cpp
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Change the D_eff[c] assignment in logit_calib.cpp from raw (U-L)*sigma*(1-sigma) to std::max(1e-6*(U-L), (U-L)*sigma*(1-sigma)), preventing the normal equations matrix N from becoming exactly singular when sigma→0 or 1.
* **Why:** D_eff[c]→0 collapses the normal equations matrix N. Tikhonov regularization (kEps=1e-10) is insufficient — the LDLT solve returns Δλ≈0 and convergence fires on a degenerate fixed point. The floor (1e-6) biases the solution by O(1e-6) when active, negligible for survey calibration.

# Epic: sv89 — Logit Newton Stabilization

## Goal
Fix logit_calibrate() divergence on large-K problems via three surgical changes to src/logit_calib.cpp: D_eff floor, design-weight initialization, and Armijo line search with step-norm guard.

## Success Criteria

## Context & Background

Root cause: lambda=0 cold-start gives midpoint weights (w=2.5*n_per_cell, far from calibrated solution). First Newton step is enormous, saturates cells (sigma→0 or 1), D_eff[c]→0, N nearly singular, LDLT regularization dominates, convergence fires on wrong fixed point. Execute T1→T2→T3→T4 sequentially (same file, cannot parallelize). Each task commits atomically. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . compile gate after every task. No bundling.

title: bug: logit diverges on large-K problems (lambda=0 warmstart + Newton overshoot)
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Fix logit_calibrate to converge on the stepstone benchmark (K=9, n=1.58M, max_weight=5). Currently: max_err=1.0, DEFF=527k, ESS=3 — completely diverged.
* **Why:** lambda=0 warmstart → sigma(0)=0.5 → w[c]=2.5×n_per_cell. First Newton step on K=9 conflicting margins produces large Δλ, pushing some lambda to extreme values → sigma→0 or 1 → D_eff[c]=(U-L)×sigma×(1-sigma)≈0 for those cells → column of N is near-zero → LDLT solve produces unbounded Δλ → next step worse → divergence spiral. Stepstone has large sparse cell tables where this degeneracy is likely.
* **Evidence:** Benchmark: logit status=0 (reports converged!), iters=9 Newton steps, max_err=1.0, DEFF=527,577, ESS=3. Pearson r with ieppa = 0.006 (near-zero correlation — essentially random weights).
* **Root cause hypotheses:**
  1. No Newton step damping — Δλ can be unbounded
  2. lambda=0 gives poor warmstart for large-K problems (sigma=0.5 is far from solution)
  3. check_convergence fires on a false convergence metric before weights are meaningful
  4. kEps=1e-10 Tikhonov regularization insufficient for near-zero D_eff cells
* **Fix options (evaluate in order):**
  A. Add line search / damping: alpha = argmin ||b(lambda + alpha*delta_lambda)|| (bisection, max 5 halvings). Simplest fix.
  B. Increase Tikhonov regularization for near-degenerate D_eff: if min(D_eff) < threshold, increase kEps.
  C. Warmstart from raking solution: run a few raking steps to get a better lambda_0 before Newton.
  D. Cap |Δλ[j]| per step to prevent runaway updates.
* **Recommended:** Option A (damped Newton / line search). Standard practice for logit calibration (survey::calib with method='logit' uses step-halving by default).

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/logit_calib.cpp — Newton loop lines ~50-120.
* **Format:** C++17 source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Damped Newton: after computing delta_lambda, find alpha in (0,1] via bisection on ||b||; accept step if ||b(lambda+alpha*Δλ)|| < ||b(lambda)|| * (1-0.01*alpha) (Armijo condition) |
| **Logic** | Max halvings = 10; if no improvement found, take smallest step (alpha=2^-10) |
| **Logic** | Recompute w[c], D_eff[c] at trial lambda before evaluating Armijo |
| **Boundary** | Damping adds O(M_cell × halvings) cost per Newton step — acceptable |
| **Boundary** | T5-T8 tests must still pass after fix |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. After ldlt_solve gives delta_lambda in b[], add Armijo line search:
   - alpha = 1.0; halving_count = 0
   - while halving_count < kMaxHalvings:
     - trial_lambda = lambda + alpha * delta_lambda
     - recompute w_trial[c] from trial_lambda
     - recompute residuals b_trial[]
     - if ||b_trial|| < ||b_current|| * (1 - 0.01*alpha): break
     - alpha *= 0.5; halving_count++
   - lambda += alpha * delta_lambda
2. Run stepstone benchmark: logit should converge within 50 Newton steps.
3. Verify T5-T8 still pass.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "logit_damping", "success": true, "data": {"stepstone_max_err": "<0.01", "t5_t8_pass": true}, "error_log": null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Stepstone logit: max_err < 0.01 (comparable to raking 1.60e-3)
- [ ] Stepstone logit: DEFF in reasonable range (1.5-2.5)
- [ ] T5-T8 tests GREEN
- [ ] devtools::test() FAIL unchanged
close_reason: sv89 fully fixed: all 3 layers implemented, T_logit_armijo+T_logit_init GREEN

title: bug: greenkhorn accelerate=TRUE silently ignores SQUAREM (harvest.R only enables for raking)
description:
## I. Context & Objective

* **Why:** harvest.R lines 94-99 document accelerate as 'Only supported for method=raking; ignored for all other methods.' The R8 fix hardcoded this guard. Greenkhorn has its own SQUAREM implementation (F_eval = K greedy steps, sorted once at round entry — stationary operator) but st.accelerate is never set to TRUE in the bridge.
* **Evidence:** Benchmark: greenkhorn=1030 iters, max_err=1.5714e-3; greenkhorn+squarem=1030 iters, max_err=1.5714e-3 (bit-identical). SQUAREM super-steps count iterations as K*3 per super-step — if SQUAREM fired, iteration count would be very different.

* **Fix:** Extend the accelerate-allowed methods list to include 'greenkhorn'. Remove the warning suppression for greenkhorn. Verify SQUAREM actually fires (greenkhorn+squarem should have fewer total margin operations than plain on stepstone K=9).

title: bug: ieppa_soft ADMM produces identical weights to ieppa hard clamp (T3 fails)
description:
## I. Context & Objective

* **Why:** Spec acceptance criterion 6: 'ieppa_soft better: max_err strictly lower than ieppa on tight-bounds (T3 test)'. T3 is failing: weights are bit-identical. ADMM is not providing the intended smoother convergence path.
* **Reference Data:** Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-27-sinkhorn-a1-fix-ieppa-admm-method.md §T3. T3 result: ieppa=0.02735, ieppa_soft=0.02735, identical=TRUE. ADMM u[] reset sites: ieppa.cpp:692, 708 (fill u with 0 on overflow/fallback). ADMM z-update: ieppa.cpp:804-809.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Root cause hypothesis 1: u[c] resets at lines 692+708 (overflow fallback) kill accumulated dual → ADMM degenerates to hard clamp on any problem that hits overflow even once |
| **Logic** | Root cause hypothesis 2: On tight-bounds problems, the fixed point of ADMM z-update coincides with the hard-clamp fixed point (same attractor basin) |
| **Logic** | Root cause hypothesis 3: The convergence check triggers before u[c] has accumulated meaningful signal (50 iters default) |
| **Boundary** | Fix must make T3 pass: me_soft < me_hard on set.seed(3), n=5000, max_weight=1.8, 5-category problem |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

2. Trace: does the T3 problem hit the overflow/fallback path? Add verbose output.
3. If resets are the cause: only reset u[] when strictly necessary (not on every fallback).
4. If fixed-point coincidence: investigate whether ADMM needs a non-zero alm_mu penalty to break the symmetry.
5. Verify T3 passes after fix.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "ieppa_soft_t3", "success": true, "data": {"me_soft_less_than_me_hard": true, "root_cause": "..."}, "error_log": null}
```

- [ ] stepstone benchmark: ieppa_soft max_err < ieppa max_err (or documented why they're equal)
- [ ] u[] not reset unnecessarily
notes: Root cause confirmed: ieppa_soft uses ADMM z-update which still contains a hard clamp inside (z=clamp(X_tilde+u,L,U)). This is NOT what was intended. User explicitly wanted ALM (Augmented Lagrangian Method) to REPLACE the hard cap. ALM: dual variable per cell accumulates violation; penalty term in BCD objective drives X toward feasible set without clamping. The per-cell u[] vector allocated for ADMM is the correct structure for ALM duals. alm_mu in CalibState exists for this purpose but is not wired to the capacity BCD.

title: R7: chebyshev negative slack must warn and promote to INFEAS
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In chebyshev.cpp, when s_up[m] or s_dn[m] would be negative (before std::max(..., kEps) clamping), log a warning and promote status to RK_ERR_INFEAS.
* **Why:** chebyshev.cpp:443-449: `s_up[m] = std::max(T_flat[m]*W_upd + w_kj[m]*delta - S[m], kEps);`. When the bracket is negative, the slack is set to kEps silently — the LP interior invariant s*y ≈ mu is broken for those margins. This is a latent convergence stall source. The correct action is to flag potential infeasibility.
* **Reference Data:** chebyshev.cpp lines 443-449. kEps is a small positive constant. Negative slack means T_flat[m]*W + w_kj[m]*delta < S[m] — infeasibility indicator.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/chebyshev.cpp
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Before the std::max clamp: if (T_flat[m]*W_upd + w_kj[m]*delta - S[m] < 0) { st.log("[chebyshev] slack violation at margin m"); res.status = RK_ERR_INFEAS; } |
| **Logic** | Only promote to INFEAS if this occurs more than kInfeasPersistence consecutive iterations (to avoid transient false positives) |
| **Logic** | Still apply the std::max clamp after the check (don't change clamp behavior) |
| **Boundary** | Log warning at verbose >= 1; INFEAS only after persistent violation |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read chebyshev.cpp lines 440-455 — identify all slack update sites.
2. Add a slack_violations counter; increment when any s_up/s_dn would be negative.
3. If counter > kInfeasPersistence: res.status = RK_ERR_INFEAS; break.
4. Reset counter when no violations.
5. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — compile gate.
6. devtools::test() — no regressions on non-infeasible inputs.
7. Commit: fix(chebyshev): flag INFEAS on persistent negative slack; log warning.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)


- [ ] Transient violations tolerated (not immediate INFEAS)

title: R1: Cache greg.cpp Newton factorization; only recompute on active-set change
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Cache the LDLT factorization of N = A*diag(X_init)*A^T in greg.cpp; only recompute it when the active set (fixed_lo[], fixed_hi[]) changes between Newton iterations.
* **Why:** greg.cpp computes N and its LDLT factorization from scratch at every Newton step. N = A*diag(X_init)*A^T where X_init is CONSTANT — the normal equations do not change unless the active set changes. For kMaxNewtonIters=10 steps with unchanged active set, the factorization is recomputed 10× identically. Each factorization is O(nct^3) where nct = total categories.
* **Reference Data:** greg.cpp lines ~75-95 (compute_normal_equations call + ldlt_factor_inplace). fixed_lo[], fixed_hi[] arrays track which cells are at bounds. active set changes when any cell transitions to/from bounds.

## II. Input Specification

* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Track active set hash (or compare fixed_lo/fixed_hi between iterations). If unchanged: skip recomputation; reuse cached L matrix. |
| **Logic** | On first iteration: always compute. |
| **Logic** | When any cell transitions: invalidate cache and recompute |
| **Format** | Use a bool active_set_changed flag: compare old vs new fixed_lo/fixed_hi arrays |
| **Boundary** | N is nct x nct where nct = Σ cat_counts[k] — typically 10-100 |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read greg.cpp fully — find factorization call site and active-set tracking.
2. Add: std::vector<bool> prev_fixed_lo, prev_fixed_hi; bool need_refactor = true;
3. At start of each Newton iter: compare current fixed_lo/hi with prev; set need_refactor accordingly. Update prev arrays.
4. Only call compute_normal_equations + ldlt_factor_inplace when need_refactor.

title: B15: chebyshev alpha_p/alpha_d floor 1e-10 can violate IPM interior invariant
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace the alpha_p = max(alpha_p, 1e-10) floor in chebyshev.cpp with a proper handling that either accepts degeneration or uses a safe fraction-to-boundary formula.
* **Why:** chebyshev.cpp:424: `alpha_p = std::max(alpha_p, 1e-10);` forces forward progress when the Newton direction would drive a slack to zero. When the natural alpha_p is near-zero (degenerate direction), forcing 1e-10 can produce s_lo[c] < 0 or s_up[c] < 0 — violating the interior-point invariant. Non-monotone behaviour results.
* **Reference Data:** chebyshev.cpp line 424 (alpha_p floor). The standard IPM safe step is: alpha = min over i where ds[i]<0: -0.99*s[i]/ds[i]. Forcing 1e-10 violates this. Same issue at alpha_d line.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/chebyshev.cpp
* **Format:** C++ source.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Remove the 1e-10 floor. If alpha_p == 0 (exact degeneracy), accept the zero step and iterate again — OR use the fraction-to-boundary formula with factor 0.995 |
| **Logic** | Option A: alpha_p = max(alpha_p, 0.0) (no floor). If alpha_p==0 → skip step, count as degenerate iter |
| **Logic** | Option B (preferred): use standard 0.995*fraction-to-boundary for alpha_p and alpha_d |
| **Boundary** | Both alpha_p AND alpha_d floors must be fixed |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read chebyshev.cpp line-search section (lines ~418-435 for alpha_p and equivalent for alpha_d).
2. Understand the current fraction-to-boundary computation.
3. Replace floor with proper fraction-to-boundary: alpha_p = min over c: (ds[c]<0 ? -0.995*s[c]/ds[c] : 1.0); then clamp to [0,1].
4. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . — compile gate.
5. devtools::test() — chebyshev tests pass; verify no new convergence failures.
6. Commit: fix(chebyshev): replace alpha floor 1e-10 with proper fraction-to-boundary formula.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id": "B15", "success": true, "data": {"file": "src/chebyshev.cpp", "formula": "fraction-to-boundary"}, "error_log": null}
```

- [ ] alpha_p and alpha_d use fraction-to-boundary (no 1e-10 floor)
- [ ] Interior invariant s > 0 maintained after step
- [ ] devtools::test() chebyshev tests pass
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . succeeds; no regressions

title: R8: Assert greedy scheduler and SQUAREM accelerate are mutually exclusive in raking.cpp
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Add a C++ assertion (or forced override) in raking.cpp that disables the greedy scheduler when accelerate=true (SQUAREM mode).
* **Why:** raking.cpp:159 + 354: greedy scheduler and SQUAREM are mutually exclusive but not enforced. Under SQUAREM, F_eval is invoked on different iterates (X, w1, X*); greedy sorts margins by errRp_k before each F call making F non-stationary — SQUAREM requires identical F for F(X) and F(F(X)). If a user sets both accelerate=true and scheduler=GREEDY, behavior is silently wrong. The comment '(void)errRp_w1' acknowledges the problem but doesn't fix it.
* **Reference Data:** raking.cpp lines 159 (use_greedy declaration), 256 (greedy sort inside F_eval), 277 (errRp_k update). CalibState.accelerate field. harvest.R:222 has the guard in R but not in C++.

| **Logic** | Warning: '[raking] SQUAREM and greedy scheduler are mutually exclusive; forcing round-robin' |

title: R5: lbfgsb convergence_rule must reflect user config or warn when overridden
description:

title: R4: Fix estimate_M_cell to return correct bound for K>8 margins
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace the `if (K > 8) return n;` shortcut in estimate_M_cell with min(product_of_cat_counts, n) to avoid misrouting small-cell problems to iEPPA.
* **Why:** estimate_M_cell currently returns n for any K>8, making AUTO route everything to iEPPA regardless of actual cell count. For K=9 with 2 categories each, M_cell <= 512 << n — raking is the correct choice. Wrong routing wastes time on the heavier iEPPA algorithm.
* **Reference Data:** src/cell_table.cpp lines 146-155 (estimate_M_cell function). The bit-packing path (K<=8) computes exact M_cell. For K>8 it falls back to n.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** src/cell_table.cpp
* **Format:** C++ source.

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Compute M_cell_bound = min over all k: product(cat_counts[k]); cap at n |
| **Logic** | Use int64_t for the product to avoid overflow (K=20, 100 cats each = 100^20 overflows int) |
| **Logic** | If product overflows int64_t or exceeds n, return n (safe upper bound) |
| **Format** | Keep the existing fast path for K<=8 unchanged |

title: Epic: Chebyshev, Sinkhorn, Greg Correctness
description:
# Epic: Chebyshev, Sinkhorn, Greg Correctness

## Goal
Fix seven correctness bugs across the three newer solvers (chebyshev IPM, sinkhorn Dykstra, greg Newton QP) that produce wrong results on edge cases or under numerical stress.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] chebyshev: guard convergence check AFTER W<=1e-300 infeasibility check
- [ ] sinkhorn: Dykstra a[] zeroed when !needs_projection (no phantom mass)
- [ ] chebyshev: dual explosion guard uses mu_new (not stale mu)
- [ ] chebyshev: alpha_p/alpha_d floor replaced with safe step clamping that preserves interior invariant
- [ ] greg: N factorization cached; only recomputed when active set changes
- [ ] chebyshev: s_up/s_dn negative slack warns and promotes to INFEAS
- [ ] greg: kMaxNewtonIters=50 or parameterised; NOCONV message populated

## Context & Background
chebyshev is a Mehrotra-style IPM. sinkhorn uses Dykstra KL projections with bisection capacity. greg is a Newton QP solver for chi-square calibration. Each has distinct correctness issues: chebyshev evaluates convergence before infeasibility guard; sinkhorn accumulates phantom KL corrections; greg re-factors the same matrix 10 times needlessly.

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Each solver is independent — tasks can run in parallel. TDD throughout. Compile after each file change.

**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Pre-allocate 5 SQUAREM scratch buffers; remove up to 17 wasted O(M_cell) copies per super-step; fix alpha formula clarity.
* **Why:** R1: X_star=X_snap copies immediately overwritten — 272MB/step wasted on stepstone-scale. R2: 5 malloc/free per super-step = 135 heap ops per solve.
* **Reference Data:** raking.cpp:319-480 (SQUAREM block). Buffers: sq_w1/sq_w2/sq_X_snap/sq_X_star/sq_X_star_pre. Rename ALL w1/w2/X_star/X_snap/X_star_pre refs to sq_* prefix.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Current raking.cpp (independent of ieppa tasks).
* **Format:** C++17 source edit. 8 edit steps per plan Task 4.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Completeness** | After edits: grep -n 'auto w1\|auto w2\|auto X_star\|auto X_snap\|auto X_star_pre' src/raking.cpp must show 0 matches inside while loop. |
| **Compile** | R CMD INSTALL --preclean after ALL 8 steps. Do NOT build mid-way. |
| **Scope** | Only SQUAREM while loop (line 330-480). Flat loop (else branch) untouched. |
| **S6** | alpha formula: (alpha - 1.0) / 2.0 — one character change at line ~405. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Add 5 pre-allocated buffers before while loop (after X_prev_sq declaration).
2. Replace auto w1=X; auto w2=w1; with sq_w1=X; sq_w2=sq_w1 assignments.

4. Fix fixed-point guard X=w2 → X=sq_w2.
5. Replace X_snap=w2 and initial X_star fill loop with sq_* vars (remove wasted copy).
6. Replace X_star_pre=X_star and first F_eval(X_star) with sq_* vars.

8. Update best-iterate block fell_back ref. Fix S6 alpha formula.
9. R CMD INSTALL. grep check. devtools::test().
10. Commit.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)

* **Objective:** Replace compute_errRp_ct inside F_eval with compute_cell_metrics storing into last_F_metrics; use last_F_metrics in SQUAREM convergence check; precompute inv_n_per_cell vector.
* **Why:** R3: F_eval + separate compute_cell_metrics = 2× O(K×M_cell) per super-step. S1: 1/n_per_cell[c] division in hot loop = unnecessary per-cell division.
* **Reference Data:** raking.cpp:317 (end of F_eval). raking.cpp:115 (declare before accelerate block). raking.cpp:451 (convergence block). W_total inside F_eval post-hyperplane = st.n exactly.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here. MUST run after Task 4 (sq_* vars in place).

## II. Input Specification

* **Format:** C++17 source edit.

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Scope** | last_F_metrics declared before while loop (inside if(st.accelerate) block). inv_n_per_cell declared before if(st.accelerate). |
| **F_eval change** | Replace return compute_errRp_ct(...) with compute_cell_metrics call storing to last_F_metrics. Return last_F_metrics.errRp. |
| **Convergence block** | Remove W_sq loop + compute_cell_metrics call. Replace with: lbw::CellMetrics m_conv = last_F_metrics; m_conv.errRp = errRp_new; m_conv.l1 = wchange; |
| **Compile** | R CMD INSTALL after edits. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Add inv_n_per_cell vector declaration+fill before if(st.accelerate) block.
2. Add last_F_metrics declaration before while loop.
3. Replace return compute_errRp_ct(...) in F_eval with compute_cell_metrics + store + return errRp.
4. Replace norm loop divisions 1.0/n_per_cell[c] with inv_n_per_cell[c] (2 loops).
5. Replace wchange loop division with inv_n_per_cell[c].
6. Replace convergence block (W_sq+compute_cell_metrics call) with last_F_metrics reuse.
7. R CMD INSTALL --preclean.
8. squarem-c2 test PASS (kl convergence now correct).
9. devtools::test() FAIL ≤ 3.
10. Commit.

- [ ] Build succeeds
- [ ] devtools::test() FAIL ≤ 3
