title: WU-D: raking.cpp + lbfgsb_solver.cpp — mirror ieppa metric+rule dispatch
description:
WU-D: raking.cpp + lbfgsb_solver.cpp — mirror ieppa metric/rule dispatch

PLAN REF: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-25-convergence-redesign-impl.md §WU-D (Steps D0-D9)

FAILING TEST FIRST (TDD):
Append to tests/testthat/test-convergence-criteria.R:
  test A3: list(pct=0.001) on raking (seed=43 n=2000 K=2 max_weight=10 500 iter) → status=0, l1_weight_change < 0.001
  test "improvement rule fires on raking": list(improvement=0.001) on raking → status=0, convergence_used$rule=="improvement"
Run: should FAIL before implementation.

FILES: src/raking.cpp, src/raking.hpp, src/lbfgsb_solver.cpp, src/lbfgsb_solver.hpp

RAKING.CPP:
Same pattern as ieppa WU-C. raking uses obs-level weights.
1. l1_weight = Σ|w[i]-w_prev[i]| / st.n  (existing w_prev vector already tracks prev weights)
2. grake_norm: same cells_by_margin_cat-style loop OR use margin accumulation already in raking errRp loop (reuse per-margin S_kj sums)
3. prev_metric_for_rule declared before main loop (no homotopy in raking)
4. Same dispatch switch as ieppa WU-C
5. At exit: res.convergence_metric/rule/tol/iter populated

UPDATE raking.hpp (RakingResult): grake_norm field already added in WU-B, but verify it's initialized to 0.0 in raking.cpp.

LBFGSB_SOLVER.CPP:
lbfgsb is a BATCH solver — single pass. Convergence measured start→final.

1. Save pre-solve weights and compute pre-metrics BEFORE the solve:
   std::vector<double> pre_weights(st.weights, st.weights + st.n);
   LBFGSResult pre_res = compute_final_weights_and_error(st, fn, bounds);
   // compute pre_metric (same type as active metric):
   double pre_metric = 0.0;
   switch (cfg.metric) {
     case lbw::CalibMetric::MAX_ERR:    pre_metric = pre_res.max_error;  break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::MEAN_ERR:   pre_metric = pre_res.mean_error; break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::KL:         pre_metric = pre_res.kl;         break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::CHI2:       pre_metric = pre_res.chi2;       break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::GRAKE_NORM: pre_metric = pre_res.grake_norm; break;
     case lbw::CalibMetric::L1_WEIGHT:  pre_metric = 0.0; break; // starts at 0
   }
   // Restore weights (compute_final modifies them):
   std::copy(pre_weights.begin(), pre_weights.end(), st.weights);

2. Actual solve (existing code)

3. After solve: compute final metrics (compute_final_weights_and_error again for finals)
   Also compute l1_weight_change = Σ|w_final[i] - pre_weights[i]| / st.n

4. Convergence dispatch (same switch as ieppa but using pre_metric as "previous"):
   double curr_metric = ...(from final result)...
   IMPROVEMENT: rel = |curr - pre_metric| / pre_metric; converged = rel < pct_tol
   PLATEAU: converged = !(curr < pre_metric * (1 - pct_tol))
   THRESHOLD: converged = curr < pct_tol

5. res.convergence_metric/rule/tol/iter populated

- cells.empty() + target>0: STATIC condition. Bucket topology fixed. Latch structural_infeas_pairs once (pre-loop scan).
- log_S_kj<threshold: TRANSIENT. Can recover. Used only for infeas_streak (drives WU-3 damping).

Exit status:
- Pre-split: persistent_infeas_pairs non-empty → RK_ERR_INFEAS (fires on stepstone false-positive)
- Post-split: structural_infeas_pairs non-empty → RK_ERR_INFEAS (fires only on genuine no-observations-for-target)
design: Pre-loop scan populates structural_infeas_pairs from cells.empty() AND target>0. infeas_streak[] still tracks transient empties for damping. Fallback blocks do NOT clear structural_infeas_pairs (topology static). Exit sites replaced: persistent_infeas_pairs → structural_infeas_pairs.

title: CR-D11a: unit-mode water-fill can exit out-of-bounds on iter exhaustion
description:
## What
finalize_weights_buf unit-mode water-fill (calib_dispatch.hpp ~L377-400) can return weights outside [min_weight,max_weight] when kWaterFillMaxIter is exhausted: the final loop iteration applies the redistribution multiply (w[i]*=factor) with no trailing clamp, so a free weight can be pushed past a bound.

## Why
Pre-existing (governs oris/chebyshev/logit/greenkhorn already). Newly relevant after CR-D11 (j7x8.11) routed raking/greg/sinkhorn through this path. test-calibration-solvers.R unit-mode assertion asserts strict bounds; a slow-converging fixture could exceed the cap. Surfaced by adversarial review of j7x8.11.

## How
Add a clamp-only pass after the water-fill loop (or 'if (it == last) { clamp; break; }') so unit-mode bounds hold unconditionally. Add a regression fixture that forces exhaustion. Verify Sw-drift accounting still correct.

title: CR-B4b: SRAA overflow fallback misses plain-overflow + finite-AA-accept case
description:
# CR-B4b: plain-overflow-with-finite-AA-accept escapes the y2ks.4 fallback

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In scope: make the SRAA linear→log overflow fallback (y2ks.4) also fire when the PLAIN F-step overflows but the AA trial happens to land finite and is accepted. Out of scope: the fallback reset mechanism itself (y2ks.4, DONE).
* **Why:** Found by adversarial review of y2ks.4. Detection is 'use_linear && !r.aa_accepted && !isfinite(r.err_rp)'. If the plain F-step overflows (err_plain=+inf) but the AA extrapolation lands finite, the safeguard 'err_AA <= err_plain' is vacuously true (finite <= +inf) so the AA is ACCEPTED: r.aa_accepted=true, r.err_rp=finite err_AA. The '!r.aa_accepted' clause then skips the fallback, and the solver stays on the linear path with the safeguard defeated (any finite AA beats a +inf baseline → bad AA steps accepted). Fallback fires only once a later overflow hits a reject/guard path.
* **Reference Data:** src/oris.cpp SRAA detection (~L932, post-y2ks.4 @ 8ca948d); sraa.hpp:220-228 accept path 'if (err_AA <= err_plain)'. Reviewer confidence 80.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| Logic | Clean fix: expose plain-baseline overflow from sraa_step. Add 'bool plain_overflow' to SRAAStepResult (sraa.hpp), set '= !std::isfinite(err_plain)' where err_plain is computed, then OR it into the oris.cpp detection: 'use_linear && (r.plain_overflow || (!r.aa_accepted && !isfinite(r.err_rp))) && !linear_fallback_used'. Alternatively refuse to accept an AA step whose baseline is +inf (sraa.hpp: 'err_AA <= err_plain && isfinite(err_plain)'). Do NOT touch the ALM Newton step or metric selection. |
| Boundary | src/sraa.hpp (SRAAStepResult + accept guard) + src/oris.cpp detection. Crosses the y2ks.4 oris.cpp-only boundary — that is why it is a separate ticket. |

## IV. Step-by-Step
1. RED: construct/trace a plain-overflow + finite-AA case (may need a unit-level sraa_step test since API-level overflow is hard to trigger).
2. Expose plain_overflow OR guard the accept on finite baseline.
3. Wire into the oris.cpp detection.
4. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . ; devtools::test() 0 FAIL.

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Plain-overflow-with-finite-AA no longer stays on the linear path with a +inf safeguard baseline
- [ ] devtools::test() 0 FAIL
close_reason: Committed; R 823 PASS/0 FAIL; finite-baseline accept guard makes y2ks.4 fallback fire on plain-overflow; adversarial review 4/5 PASS + DoD5 orchestrator-verified

title: CR-C7b: logit does not enforce Σw=n on BUDGET/STALL exit; obs-expanded best_weights residual diverges from internal best_error
description:
## What
On BUDGET/STALL exit, logit returns weights with Σw != n (measured sum=802-819 for n=800 at max_iter=2-3), and the obs-expanded best_weights realize a residual (e.g. 3.9 abs-count) that differs from the reported internal cell best_error (6e-3). At convergence Σw=n holds.

## Why
Found during kxna.7. logit's w_best is the internal cell-mass iterate; unlike greenkhorn (kxna.1) it is not routed through finalize_weights on non-OK exits, and the obs expansion does not preserve the internal absolute-count residual. Analogous to greenkhorn kxna.1 (Σw=n enforcement) but for logit + a returned≡reported gap (mxcl.5-class) on unconverged exits. Not caused by kxna.7/8 (verified vs baseline: baseline mi=2 sum=818.97, my-change 802.67 — kxna.7 improved it).

## How
- Route logit's returned best_weights through finalize_weights_buf on all exit paths (mirror greenkhorn kxna.1 / oris_finalize) so Σw=n.
- Verify the obs expansion preserves margins so returned residual == reported best_error (mxcl.5 invariant) on BUDGET too.
- RED: set.seed(7) n=800 a(3,.5/.3/.2) b(2,.6/.4) tg a=.34/.33/.33 b=.5/.5, max_iter=2 -> assert sum(w)==n and recomputed max margin resid == best_error.

title: CR-C14: Stabilize newton_calib Steihaug trust-boundary root
description:
# CR-C14: Stabilize newton_calib Steihaug trust-boundary root
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace the cancellation-prone quadratic-formula evaluation `tau = (-bq + sqrt(disc))/(2*aq)` at newton_calib.cpp:224 with the numerically stable equivalent form `tau = 2*(Delta^2 - xx)/(bq + sqrt(disc))`, per project mandate on zero cancellations. Out of scope: changing the Steihaug-CG algorithm structure itself.
* **Why:** The direct form cancels catastrophically when `xp>0` and `cq -> 0^-` (cq = xx - Delta^2 < 0, since x is strictly interior to the trust region at this point) — subtracting two nearly-equal floating point quantities loses precision. The alternate form avoids the subtraction of near-equal quantities, is mathematically equivalent (same root of the same quadratic), and is standard numerically-stable practice for this exact root-selection pattern (cf. numerical recipes' quadratic formula stabilization).
* **Reference Data:** newton_calib.cpp:224: `tau = (-bq + sqrt(disc))/(2*aq)`; `cq = xx - Delta^2 < 0` since x is strictly interior (given). Alternate stable form: `tau = 2*(Delta^2 - xx)/(bq + sqrt(disc))`.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `src/newton_calib.cpp` line 224 (Steihaug trust-boundary root), surrounding context defining `aq`, `bq`, `cq`, `disc`, `xx`, `Delta`, `xp` (needed to verify sign assumptions hold at this call site before applying the algebraic identity).
* **Format:** C++17. Single-line change + a derivation comment (mandatory — "no hand-waving" project rule; the comment must show the algebra, not just assert equivalence).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Verify algebraically (in the ticket's own derivation, then again as a code comment) that `2*(Delta^2 - xx)/(bq + sqrt(disc))` is the SAME root as `(-bq + sqrt(disc))/(2*aq)` for THIS specific quadratic `aq*tau^2 + bq*tau + cq = 0` (standard identity: multiply numerator and denominator of the `+sqrt` root by `(-bq - sqrt(disc))`, using `cq = aq*tau1*tau2` i.e. `product-of-roots = cq/aq`). Confirm `bq + sqrt(disc) != 0` cannot occur in this branch (or add a guard if it can) before dividing. Do NOT alter which root is selected (still the `+sqrt` root) — only the numerically stable formula for computing that same root. |
| **Global** | Do NOT touch the chebyshev Mehrotra corrector or the oris ALM Newton step — those are separate, already-verified-correct formulas per project convention; this ticket is exclusively about newton_calib's Steihaug root. logit eb79.16/18/22/23 preserved (N/A); min-norm dsyevd warm-start untouched (this IS a different numerical routine — Steihaug-CG trust region, not the min-norm warm-start; do not conflate); greg out of scope; finalize_weights N/A; fixture changes need arithmetic proof — if any fixture's numeric output shifts at the ULP level due to this rewrite, that is EXPECTED (improved precision) and must be documented, not treated as a regression, but any shift beyond expected floating-point-level noise must be investigated. |
| **Format** | One-line change; mandatory derivation comment at the site (not just "numerically stable form" — show the algebra or cite the standard identity by name); no AI attribution; explicit file staging. |
| **Boundary** | Touch only `src/newton_calib.cpp` line ~224 and its immediate comment. Do not touch CR-C12 (:781) or CR-C13 (:72-77) despite same file. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read the surrounding context at newton_calib.cpp:224 to confirm `aq`, `bq`, `cq`, `disc`, `xx`, `Delta`, `xp` definitions and confirm the stated sign assumption (`cq = xx - Delta^2 < 0`, x strictly interior) holds at this exact call site (not just in general).
2. Derive the stable form algebraically: for `aq*tau^2 + bq*tau + cq = 0`, roots are `tau = (-bq +/- sqrt(disc)) / (2*aq)`. Using product-of-roots `tau1*tau2 = cq/aq`, the `+sqrt` root can be rewritten as `tau = 2*cq / (-bq - sqrt(disc))` — verify this reduces to the manifest's stated form `2*(Delta^2 - xx)/(bq + sqrt(disc))` given `cq = xx - Delta^2` (sign flip absorbed correctly — check this explicitly, do not copy the manifest's form without re-deriving).
3. Write a numeric test (R fixture or standalone C++ unit check) constructing an `xp>0`, `cq->0^-` near-cancellation case; compare old-formula vs new-formula tau against a high-precision (e.g. long double or Kahan-summed) reference — confirm the new formula is measurably more accurate (fewer ULPs of error) in this regime, and confirm both formulas agree away from the cancellation regime (sanity check equivalence).
4. Apply the one-line change plus the derivation comment.
5. Rebuild (`R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`).
6. Run full `devtools::test()` — confirm 0 FAIL; any fixture-level numeric shift must be at floating-point noise level (document the magnitude) and framed as improved precision, not investigated as a regression unless the shift exceeds expected floating-point tolerance.
7. Run Python parity tests for newton_calib.

# CR-H9: Chebyshev — dead machinery + constant-vector cleanup
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Five sub-fixes in chebyshev.cpp: (a) remove orphaned `converged_pct`/`prev_metric_for_rule` dead state while preserving the documented IPM-vs-CalibRule design comment; (b) remove six dead per-iteration locals; (c) fold constant-`n_d`-sized vectors (`w_kj`/`w_kj_sq`/`u_red`) to scalars; (d) hoist the redundant `compute_S(X,S)` call out of the loop since `X` is unchanged after iteration 0; (e) decide (implement or remove) the unused `delta_warm` parameter. In scope: all five as one coordinated ticket since they touch overlapping loop regions. Out of scope: the IPM-vs-CalibRule algorithmic choice itself (keep as designed).
* **Why:** (a) `converged_pct` (line 265) is never read — `apply_rule` survives only for its `prev_metric_for_rule` side effect, and `prev_metric_for_rule` (line 223) has no other consumer, meaning `select_metric`/`apply_rule` run every iteration purely to feed dead state. (b) six locals per iteration (errRp/mean_err/kl_max/chi2_total/grake_norm/l1_weight) are computed and discarded. (c) `w_kj`/`w_kj_sq`/`u_red` are vectors sized `n_d` but always hold the same constant value — no need for vector storage or per-element access. (d) `compute_S(X,S)` at the loop top (line 229) recomputes from `X`, but `X` hasn't changed since line 639 — only the duals update per iteration, so recomputing `S` every iteration is redundant after the first. (e) `delta_warm` (hpp:24) promises warm-start-delta behavior in its doc comment, but cpp:117-119 ignores it — callers currently compute `oris_max_err*1.5` for a parameter that does nothing.
* **Reference Data:** (a) chebyshev.cpp:265 (converged_pct dead), :223 (prev_metric_for_rule single dead consumer) — keep the documented IPM-vs-CalibRule choice comment, remove only the orphaned bool+state. (b) chebyshev.cpp:255-257 (six dead locals). (c) chebyshev.cpp:59-64,199,203-204 (w_kj/w_kj_sq/u_red as constant-n_d vectors → fold to scalar, ~15 LOC + per-iter mults saved). (d) chebyshev.cpp:229 (compute_S(X,S) redundant after iter 0; X unchanged since :639, only duals update) — hoist pre-loop. (e) chebyshev.hpp:24 delta_warm param, cpp:117-119 ignores it, callers compute oris_max_err*1.5 for nothing — DECIDE with measurement; coordinate with CR-G9(h) comment fix (a separate, already-known ticket in another epic — do not duplicate its comment fix here, just avoid conflicting with it).
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification

Chebyshev fixture battery (R + Python parity).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | (a)-(d) must be byte-identical (pure dead-code/redundancy removal + algebraic scalar-fold, no numeric change). (e) is NOT byte-identical by default — deciding to "implement" delta_warm changes numeric behavior; deciding to "remove" it changes caller code but not numeric behavior (since it was already a no-op) — the decision must be measurement-backed (bench/accuracy comparison with vs. without an implemented delta_warm), not a coin flip. Keep the IPM-vs-CalibRule design comment when removing (a)'s dead state — the comment documents a deliberate choice, only the orphaned bool+state that no longer serves that choice gets removed. NO-LTO: this is hot per-iteration loop code — all fixes here are in-TU edits, not TU splits, so no LTO risk, but do not accidentally move any of this into calib_dispatch.hpp as "shared" since it's chebyshev-specific. |

title: CR-H5: sraa.hpp — incremental Gram update
description:
# CR-H5: sraa.hpp — incremental Gram update
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace the full Gram-matrix recompute in `sraa.hpp` (lines 154-172) with an incremental update, since only one (ΔX, ΔR) pair changes per SRAA step. In scope: the Gram update mechanism only. Out of scope: the AA acceleration algorithm's acceptance/rejection logic.
* **Why:** The current code recomputes the full Gram matrix every step — m²/2 dot products of length M — though only one (ΔX, ΔR) pair actually changed since the last step. An incremental update needs only m new dot products plus the RHS update, which is up to ~60% of SRAA's linalg cost at m=5.
* **Reference Data:** sraa.hpp:154-172 (full Gram recompute). m²/2 dots of length M per step currently; incremental needs m new dots + rhs. M = M_cell for greenkhorn/raking callers, M = total_cats for oris lf-space callers — the incremental update must be correct for BOTH caller contexts. Up to ~60% of SRAA linalg cost at m=5 per finding.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `src/sraa.hpp` (Gram matrix construction/update, AA solve step), callers in `greenkhorn.cpp`/`raking.cpp` (M=M_cell context) and `oris.cpp` (M=total_cats lf-space context). Accelerate/SRAA-specific benchmark fixture (check `benchmarks/`/`bench/` for an existing SRAA or accelerate fixture before creating a new one).
* **Format:** C++17, `lbw` namespace, hot per-iteration linear algebra code.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | NO-LTO guard applies directly here: this is hot per-iteration code (runs every SRAA step) — it must stay co-located in its current TU (sraa.hpp), not split into a new .cpp. Incremental update must be numerically identical to full recompute OR, if floating-point associativity causes drift, that drift must be explicitly measured and gated on fixture parity (do not silently accept a "close enough" result — either prove bit-identical or quantify+document the delta and get it approved via the fixture gate). Must work correctly for both M=M_cell (greenkhorn/raking) and M=total_cats (oris lf-space) callers — do not hardcode assumptions from one caller context. |
| **Format** | Match existing sraa.hpp style. Conventional commit, no AI attribution. |
| **Boundary** | `src/sraa.hpp` only. Do not touch caller sites in greenkhorn.cpp/raking.cpp/oris.cpp beyond what's needed to feed the incremental update the single changed (ΔX,ΔR) pair (if they don't already expose it cleanly, that plumbing is in-scope). |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read sraa.hpp lines 100-200 to understand the current Gram matrix construction: what's stored (full m×m Gram + rhs), how it's rebuilt each step, and where the (ΔX,ΔR) history buffer lives.
2. Identify exactly which single (ΔX,ΔR) pair changes per step (newest entry replacing oldest in the m-window, or appended) and confirm the incremental math: new row/column of the Gram matrix = m new dot products against the existing (ΔX,ΔR) history, not m² recompute.
3. Implement the incremental update, maintaining the full Gram matrix as persistent state across steps instead of rebuilding from scratch.
4. Verify against both caller contexts: greenkhorn/raking (M=M_cell) and oris lf-space (M=total_cats) — read each caller's SRAA invocation to confirm the incremental state threads correctly through both.
5. Numerical validation: run the SRAA/accelerate fixture battery comparing incremental vs. full-recompute Gram matrices at every step for exact match; if any fp-associativity drift appears, quantify it (max abs/rel error) and document rather than dismiss.
6. Interleaved bench::mark before (full recompute) vs. after (incremental) on the accelerate fixture at m=5, single bench::mark() call, not sequential runs.
7. Run `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` then `devtools::test()`; run Python parity tests; run stepstone benchmark for regression check.

```toon
success: bool

error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . + devtools::test() 0 FAIL (+ pytest)
- [ ] Dead-code removals: N/A (this is an algorithmic change, not dead-code removal)
- [ ] Perf: interleaved before/after in single bench::mark() call on accelerate fixture at m=5 (target: up to ~60% SRAA linalg cost reduction); stepstone no regression
- [ ] Numerically identical (or documented+gated fp-drift) AA solutions across greenkhorn/raking (M_cell) AND oris lf-space (total_cats) caller contexts

Provably bit-identical (FP-commutative dots, immutable columns, count-gated reads). Byte-identical dump on SRAA branches; R 904/0, Python 93/0; fresh opus review confirmed (wrap invariant, 4 clear sites, warmup, off-by-one, M-independence). ~67% fewer Gram dots at m=5.

# CR-H1: Dedupe result-packing in both bridges
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective

Out of scope: changing which fields get packed (that is CR-D5/D6, a separate epic — this ticket only removes duplication, it does not add missing fields).
* **Why:** The four/five duplicated blocks are the root cause of the field-omission drift class documented in CR-D5/D6 — every time a new ORIS field was added, some copy sites got updated and others didn't. A single helper makes omission structurally impossible for future fields.
* **Reference Data:** r_bridge.cpp has FOUR near-identical ~25-line ORIS field-copy blocks (lines 566-592, 618-647, 770-803, 804-833: n_xcur_writes…sraa_demoted, best_weights) across the severe-skew-auto, compressed-auto, oris_soft, and oris dispatch branches. c_api.cpp has TWO ~38-line ORIS/ORIS_SOFT copy blocks (lines 421-460, 468-507) plus THREE hand-rolled partial base-field copies (raking lines 306-324, newton lines 363-383, AUTO-fallback lines 525-544). Cross-epic note: CR-D5/D6 (field-omission bug instances) depend on this ticket landing first or together — flag the dependency in a comment on this ticket when CR-D5/D6 IDs are known; do not block on it.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here — do not assume prior context about r_bridge.cpp or c_api.cpp internals beyond what is stated.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `src/r_bridge.cpp` (dispatch branches: severe-skew-auto, compressed-auto, oris_soft, oris), `src/c_api.cpp` (ORIS/ORIS_SOFT blocks + raking/newton/AUTO-fallback base-field copies), existing `pack_solver_result` helper (location TBD by grep) as the pattern to follow, `RakingResult` struct (lacks a `message` field — `pack_base_fields` must skip `message` when called from the raking path), R test fixture battery under `tests/testthat/fixtures/`, Python parity fixtures under `python/leafblower/ (test_*_parity.py files — NOTE: python/parity/ is an empty stale dir; the real parity-test pattern home is python/leafblower/test_solver_parity.py et al.)`.

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Helpers must be pure copy/pack — zero behavior change to packed values. `pack_base_fields` must handle the `RakingResult`-lacks-`message` case (skip, do not stub with empty string that later gets misread as "no message" vs "field absent"). No-LTO: this is COLD once-per-solve packing code, not a hot per-iteration loop — safe to factor into a shared helper in a new or existing cold TU without perf risk. Do not delete `_reserved_lbfgs_m` ABI padding or reuse algorithm enum slot 2 (unrelated but global guard). |

2. Read the four r_bridge.cpp ORIS blocks (566-592, 618-647, 770-803, 804-833) and diff them field-by-field to confirm they are truly identical in content (not just similar) before extracting — if any field differs across branches, that is a pre-existing drift bug; document it, do not silently unify without flagging.

Design `pack_base_fields(dest, res.base)` signature to cover the union of fields used across raking/newton/AUTO-fallback, with `message` handling conditional on the result type having that field (template or overload, whichever matches existing codebase idiom — check for existing overload patterns before choosing).

6. Replace all 4 r_bridge.cpp call sites and 2 c_api.cpp ORIS call sites with `pack_oris_result` calls.
7. Replace the 3 c_api.cpp partial base-field copies with `pack_base_fields` calls.
8. Run `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` then `devtools::test()`; run `cd python && pip install -e . && pytest`.

description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Audit greg.cpp (and confirm the other non-finalize solvers) for the scale-blind-metric / silent-infeasible-success class of bug found in logit (eb79.16). IN: read + diagnostic run. OUT: fix or document per finding.
* **Why:** Scope reviewer flagged greg.cpp shares logit's shape (Newton/active-set, boundary convergence, no Σ-rescale in exit path). Must verify whether greg (a) targets absolute counts, (b) reports a scale-invariant proportion metric, (c) can certify an infeasible/wrong-scale stall as status=0 — the exact defect fixed in logit.
* **Reference Data:** greg.cpp exit path (fixed_lo/fixed_hi active-set, apply_obs_expansion). Compare its convergence metric to the constraint it solves. Run the collinear fixture (seed 23, n=200, mw=0.1) through greg and check Sum(w) vs n + reported status/max_error vs actual absolute residual.

| Type | Guard |

| **Logic** | Determine: absolute vs ratio constraint; metric scale-aware?; can status=0 co-occur with a violated absolute constraint? If yes -> same bug -> fix analogous to eb79.16 (own ticket if non-trivial). If greg is safe (structural Σ=n or scale-aware metric), document evidence + close. |
| **Boundary** | Audit only; any fix is a follow-up ticket. |

2. Run collinear fixture through greg: Sum(w), status, max_error vs true absolute residual.

```toon
success: bool

  file: src/greg.cpp
  verdict: same-bug|safe
  collinear_sum_w: float
```

- [ ] If same-bug: fix ticket filed. If safe: documented + closed.
close_reason: NOT-A-BUG (audit clean). greg lacks the eb79.16 scale-blind false-certification. (1) Convergence gate is active-set-based (greg.cpp:132 !any_clamped), not a scale-blind metric threshold. (2) Newton residual is absolute-count-driven (greg.cpp:87 b=T_kj*n-sumX), unlike logit's scale-invariant sigmoid — greg cannot rest at a proportion-correct/scale-wrong point. (3) Interior convergence forces every margin met in absolute space => Sigma w=n implied (each margin partitions all cells, targets sum to 1), so at every status=0 W=n and shared proportion-space compute_cell_metrics is honest. (4) On infeasible/tight/collinear inputs greg exhausts budget => NOCONV(status=1), never silent status=0. Empirically verified: feasible=>status=0/Sw=400.000000/max_err=1.85e-3; tight-skew mw1.5/1.2 + collinear mw1.5/1.2 (logit's exact failure modes) all => status=1 NOCONV. title: logit Newton stalls at infeasible boundary on rank-deficient (collinear/redundant) margins instead of the feasible optimum
description:
# leafblower-eb79.18: logit min-norm warm-start — reach the feasible optimum on rank-deficient (collinear) margins
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** Min-norm (pseudo-inverse via symmetric eigendecomposition, dsyevd) warm-start solve for lambda_0.
**Forbidden:** ridge-Cholesky for the rank-deficient init; the adaptive-eps Tikhonov shortcut (approximation — no feasible-start guarantee, see Alternatives); raising kLambdaInitRejectAbs as a band-aid; rewriting the main Newton loop (LM port is a CONTINGENT follow-up, not this ticket); touching verified solver math (oris/ieppa/chebyshev).
**Audit:** iter-0 stderr trace (max|lambda_0|, reject y/n, initial w range, max_b) on the stalling fixture; Σw=n on the now-feasible result; independent in-code (not prototype-only) convergence verification.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: consistent rank-deficient/collinear logit margin problem that currently STALLs (all obs at min_weight). Out: logit reaches the feasible optimum (Σw=n, all margins met) via a min-norm warm-start, matching raking/oris. INCONSISTENT redundant targets remain honest STALL/INFEAS (unchanged).
* **Why:** E2 of the eb79 logit arc. E1 (eb79.16) made the collinear failure HONEST (STALL, not silent status=0). E2 makes the *consistent* collinear case SUCCEED — the feasible optimum exists (design w=1 satisfies all margins, Σw=n) and raking/oris find it; logit does not.
* **Reference Data (verified root cause, 2026-07-02):**
  - Warm-start (logit_calib.cpp:104-127) solves `(AA^T)λ0 = A·z_target` with D_eff=1 via `cholesky_factor_inplace(...,ε=1e-10)` (Tikhonov ridge — NOT a true modified-Cholesky; single uniform diagonal bump then dpotrf, per calib_linalg.cpp). For the stalling fixture (test-logit.R:141-151: n=200, v1=v2=v3=base(A/B), v4=v5=v6=base2(P/Q), all targets 0.5) `AA^T` is 12×12 **rank-3** (basis {1_A,1_B,1_P,1_Q}, one dependency 1_A+1_B=1_P+1_Q=𝟙) → near-zero eigenvalues bumped to ~1e-7 → RHS components along them amplified by 1/bump → λ0 blows up.
  - Sanity check (logit_calib.cpp:131-133): `max|λ0| > kLambdaInitRejectAbs(=10)` ⇒ REJECT ⇒ `lambda=0` COLD start ⇒ z=0 ⇒ w=midpoint, residual ~405. (A second sub-case — λ0 ACCEPTED but biased so z_c≠z_target — is also covered by the fix: eigen-clip removes the ridge-bump distortion entirely.)
  - First Newton step overshoots ⇒ cells saturate at L (sig→0) ⇒ `D_eff=max(kDeffFloor·range, range·sig·(1−sig))` floors at `kDeffFloor=1e-6·range` ⇒ built `N=A·diag(D_eff)·A^T` ≠ true `∂(Aw)/∂λ` ⇒ Newton direction non-descent ⇒ Armijo exhausts EVERY iter (α floors 1.63e-4 = min(1, kMaxDeltaZ/max_δz)·2^−kMaxHalvings) ⇒ STALL at min.
  - EVIDENCE: `verbose=1` prints "Armijo exhausted (alpha=1.63e-04)" every iteration; real result status=5, Sw=20 (=n·min_weight), w range [0.1,0.1], max_error=0.45. Exact GN step is provably descent (`⟨N⁻¹b,Nb⟩=‖b‖²>0`); non-descent ⇒ N inconsistent with Jacobian (D_eff floor) OR never near feasible (λ0 reject).
  - **Correctness scope (agy Q4):** min-norm λ0 = (AA^T)⁺A·z_target gives `A^T λ0 = P_range(A^T)·z_target`. Exact reproduction (iter-0 residual=0) holds IFF `z_target ∈ range(A^T)`. TRUE for this fixture: X_init, L, U identical across cells ⇒ z_target = const·𝟙 ∈ range(A^T). For HETEROGENEOUS X_init (non-constant z_target) min-norm gives the best L2 projection — still ≫ better than λ0=0 cold-start, but not necessarily 1-iter. The fix is provably exact only under `z_target ∈ range(A^T)`; broader inputs get a well-conditioned (bounded) start, not an exact one.
  - Prototype `scratchpad/logit_minnorm_proto.R`: feasible/min-norm warm-start ⇒ converge in 1 iter; 6-margin min-norm λ0 = z_target/6 per dual = −0.384 < 10 (never rejected). NOTE: prototype is corroborative ONLY — DoD requires in-code verification.
* **Alternatives Considered (CLAUDE.md mandate):**
  - **(A) Min-norm eigen (dsyevd) warm-start — CHOSEN.** Exact pseudo-inverse: eigenvalues>tol kept unmodified, null space dropped ⇒ bounded λ0 that reproduces z_target when in-range ⇒ feasible start. dsyevd already linked+used (newton_calib.cpp) ⇒ no new dependency. Surgical (warm-start block only), lowest regression risk to working logit paths.
  - **(B) Adaptive-eps Tikhonov in warm-start (reuse main-loop `max(1e-10,max_b_mag/kMaxDeltaZ)`) — REJECTED.** 1-line, no LAPACK, but Tikhonov ≠ pseudo-inverse: biases λ0 toward 0, does NOT guarantee `A^T λ0 = P_range·z_target`, so no feasible-start guarantee on non-constant z_target. Fails the "absolute correctness / proven" bar.
  - **(C) Levenberg-Marquardt + gain-ratio in the MAIN loop (port newton_calib.cpp machinery) — DEFERRED to contingent follow-up.** Strictly more general (handles mid-solve saturation, agy Q2), matches codebase precedent, BUT rewrites logit's core Newton step ⇒ behavior-change risk to ALL logit uses + full stepstone regression. title: logit certifies infeasible rank-deficient stall as success: scale-blind convergence metric (fix to absolute-count residual)
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Make logit's convergence + reported error measure the ABSOLUTE-count residual it actually minimizes (max_k,j |target_kj*n - S_kj|), not the scale-invariant proportion metric — so a grossly-infeasible stall reports STALL/INFEAS with a large error, never status=0/max_error=0. IN: logit_calib.cpp convergence block (:313-317) + reported max_error. OUT: the Newton step/objective/init (that is E2, eb79.18).
* **Why:** logit_calib.cpp:193/276 targets absolute counts (S_kj -> target*n; total Σw=n implied). But the reported/convergence metric is compute_cell_metrics.errRp = PROPORTION (S_kj/W_total), scale-invariant -> reads 0 whenever proportions match, even when the absolute constraint is violated by 90 (collinear all-min: Sum_A=10 vs target*n=100). The solver SILENTLY CERTIFIES an infeasible result as success (status=0, max_error=0). Correctness-critical: a solver must not report error=0 on a constraint violated by 90.
* **Verified (orchestrator prototype):** adding a scale-aware gate -> collinear reports status=5 STALL (honest); normal fixture status=0 Sum=200 (no regression; also fixes a pre-existing status=4-with-max_error=0 decoupling). Prototype reverted.
* **Reference Data:** logit_calib.cpp:189-196 already computes b=target*n - S_kj each iter; :313-317 convergence uses compute_cell_metrics (proportion). cells_per_cat[k][j] in scope (used :277). st.tol_abs is the absolute fallback tol.
* **Philosophy:** SOTA + absolute correctness (proven) + fastest. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** post-step w, targets (proportions), st.n.
* **Format:** C++.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Convergence requires BOTH the existing metric AND max_abs_resid <= tol_abs * n. Reported res.base.max_error must reflect the absolute residual (scale-aware) so status and error are CONSISTENT (no status=5 with max_error=0). |
| **Format** | logit-LOCAL: do NOT modify shared compute_cell_metrics (affects all solvers). Reuse the b/S_kj computation pattern. |
| **Boundary** | Convergence + reporting only. Do NOT touch the Newton step, sigmoid link, init, ridge, or step-norm guard (eb79.3) — solver convergence to the feasible optimum is E2 (eb79.18). |
| **Tone** | Provable, cheap (residual already available), fastest. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. At :313-317 compute max_abs_resid = max_k,j |targets[k][j]*n - sum_{c in cells_per_cat[k][j]} w[c]|.
2. converged = check_convergence(...) && (max_abs_resid <= st.tol_abs * st.n).
3. Set the reported scale-aware error (e.g. res.base.max_error incorporates max_abs_resid/n) so a STALL is not reported with max_error=0. Decide: keep proportion max_error as-is + add a field, OR report the absolute-normalized residual as max_error. Match how oris reports infeasibility.
4. If not converged and residual large at budget/stall exit, ensure status reflects STALL/INFEAS (existing post-loop logic at :326-329 already does BUDGET/STALL; verify it now fires correctly).
5. Verify (formalize the prototype): collinear -> status != RK_OK + reported error large; normal -> status=0 Sum=n byte-identical weights; a tight-but-feasible fixture -> still converges status=0.
6. R CMD INSTALL; pybind rebuild; full R suite + pytest parity.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: eb79.16-scale-aware-metric
success: bool
data:
  file: src/logit_calib.cpp
  collinear_status: int
  collinear_reported_error: float
  normal_status: int
  normal_sum_w: float
  normal_weights_identical: bool
  tests: pass|fail
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Convergence + reported error use the absolute-count residual (logit-local; compute_cell_metrics untouched)
- [ ] Collinear fixture: status != RK_OK (STALL/INFEAS), reported error reflects the ~0.45 violation (NOT 0)
- [ ] Normal fixture: status=0, Sum=n, weights byte-identical to pre-fix (no regression)
- [ ] R suite + Python parity green

## ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED
- (A) finalize/normalize Σw=n at exit: REJECTED — rescale hits the feasible point only by luck (feasible set happens to contain a uniform rescale here); unprovable in general; masks a lying solver.
- (D) add Σw=n constraint to the objective: REJECTED — the total is ALREADY implied by the absolute-count constraints; adding it is redundant -> worsens rank deficiency; does not address the metric bug.
- (E1, chosen) scale-aware metric: the residual the solver optimizes IS the correct convergence criterion (provable); already computed (fastest); makes the solver honest; no regression. Splits the harder rank-deficient-Newton convergence to E2.
close_reason: 4-phase PASS. Scale-aware convergence gate + absolute-count recompute of 4 residual metrics (max/best/mean/grake), kl/chi2 left proportional. Collinear now status=5/max_err=0.45 (was silent status=0/err=0); normal unchanged (status=0/Sw=n/~5e-16). Exposes+defers logit tight-problem convergence quality to E2/eb79.18. agy SOUND (recompute not floor); plan-review-gate iter-4 3/3 PASS; opus adversarial PASS (metric aggregation faithful, tests honest). R 365/0, pytest 46/0. Superseded finalize(A)/add-total(D) misdiagnoses.

title: Fail-fast on skipped greenkhorn/logit weight copy in c_api
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** c_api.cpp:339-347,354-362 silently no-ops the best_weights copy if empty/mis-sized, leaving caller weights stale while status reads success; force error status when copy skipped. IN: 2 copy blocks + distinguishing test. OUT: no change when copy succeeds.
* **Why:** Violates Σw=n contract silently — caller may read res.base.status as OK with unmodified weights buffer.
* **Reference Data:** :339 `if (!res.base.best_weights.empty() && size==n) std::copy(...)`. GREENKHORN + LOGIT only (others write st.weights in-place). RK_ERR_INFEAS exists (leafblower.h:35) as candidate status.
* **Philosophy:** Goldfish Memory — all here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** CalibResult after solve (incl. an engineered skip case).
* **Format:** C++.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | ANTI-PIVOT: FIRST verify the skip is truly an error path (solver errored before BestIterTracker::update). If best_weights legitimately empty on a valid exit, do NOT force error — document + close not-a-bug. |
| **Format** | Match existing status-set convention. |
| **Boundary** | Only the 2 copy blocks + one test. |
| **Tone** | Investigate before fix. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Trace greenkhorn/logit: does a successful solve ALWAYS populate best_weights with size==n? Read solver exit paths.
2. If yes and skip ⇒ error: add `else { status=RK_ERR_INFEAS; }` when copy skipped.
3. If skip can be benign, STOP; document + reclassify not-a-bug (no code change).
4. DISTINGUISHING TEST (only if classified bug): engineer the skip condition (e.g. a fixture/harness where greenkhorn or logit exits before best_weights is populated, or a unit harness forcing empty best_weights on a nominal-success status) and assert the returned status is an error code, NOT OK, and the caller weight buffer is flagged. Existing suite does not exercise this branch (that is WHY the no-op went unnoticed) → "existing tests green" is insufficient. Prove RED on pre-fix (status OK + stale weights), GREEN on fix.
5. R CMD INSTALL; tests; parity.
6. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: T6-weight-copy-guard
success: bool
data:
  file: src/c_api.cpp
  verdict: bug|not-a-bug
  fix_applied: bool
  distinguishing_test: added|na-not-a-bug
  red_on_prefix: bool
  tests: pass|fail
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Skip-path classified (bug vs benign) with evidence
- [ ] If bug: error status forced + distinguishing test proven RED-on-prefix→GREEN-on-fix
- [ ] If benign: documented, closed not-a-bug (no code change)
- [ ] Tests green
close_reason: NOT-A-BUG (orchestrator-verified direct read). RK_OK set only by mark_converged (calib_dispatch.hpp:429), which in both greenkhorn (267->301) and logit (319->348) always falls through to unconditional best_weights.resize(st.n); all early returns are error status. c_api.cpp:345/:360 assign status=res.base.status UNCONDITIONALLY (outside the copy if), so a skipped copy only co-occurs with an error status — caller never sees OK+stale weights. size==n half is dead (st.n immutable). No code change.

## Context & Background
Single C++17 core (src/), R bridge (r_bridge.cpp), Python via pybind11 (_bindings.cpp). Parity contract: Python matches R to rtol=1e-6. Σw=n enforced via finalize_weights[_buf] (normalize→bounds order sacred). CalibResult fields at res.base.*.

title: Wire omega_mode_id through the Python binding (R/Python parity)
description:
# T10: Wire omega_mode_id through the Python binding (R/Python parity)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** IN = wire the EXISTING C field `sor_omega_mode_id` through the Python binding so Python `harvest(..., sor={...,"omega_mode_id":N})` selects the SOR omega mode exactly like R, closing the cross-language asymmetry. OUT = the ship-gate decision (e18t.9), the default-value flip (e18t.9), any oris.cpp algorithm change.
* **Why:** plan-review-gate iter-1 found Python `_parse_sor` returns a 6-tuple that DROPS omega_mode_id and `_bindings.cpp` never forwards it, so Python silently always runs the C default (mode-2) regardless of the dict — R can select the mode, Python cannot. This blocks deterministic cross-language parity (e18t.9 may flip the C default to mode-1 on NO-SHIP, after which only explicit selection can exercise mode-2 in Python). This is NOT new ABI: `sor_omega_mode_id` already exists in `rk_params_t` and r_bridge.cpp already forwards it; this wires the same existing field through the Python layer.
* **Reference Data:** Design spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-oris-iterate-change-omega-design.md` §3.7. Sites: `python/leafblower/_harvest.py` `_parse_sor` (~:135, docstring ':136 returns (enabled,auto,omega_init,omega_min,omega_fixed,burnin)' — 6-tuple, add omega_mode_id -> 7-tuple), its call site that unpacks the tuple, and the dict passthrough; `python/leafblower/_bindings.cpp` (the params-building block that sets sor fields — add `p.sor_omega_mode_id = <parsed>`); C field `src/types.hpp:74` (int omega_mode_id, default 2), `src/c_api.cpp:114` (p->sor_omega_mode_id=2) + :278 (st.sor_cfg.omega_mode_id = p->sor_omega_mode_id). R reference: `R/harvest.R` parse_sor returns omega_mode_id and r_bridge.cpp forwards it — mirror that contract. Default when key absent: use the C default (do NOT hardcode 2; read from a single source or pass-through-None so the C init default governs) — so e18t.9's later default flip in c_api.cpp governs Python too.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** installed leafblower; the Python binding source.
* **Format:** edits to `python/leafblower/_harvest.py` + `python/leafblower/_bindings.cpp` + a Python test.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | `_parse_sor` 6-tuple -> 7-tuple adding omega_mode_id; read `sor.get("omega_mode_id", DEFAULT)` where DEFAULT preserves the C-init default (pass the C default through, do NOT hardcode a literal that will drift from e18t.9's flip — e.g. sentinel/None -> let c_api rk_params_init default govern, OR read it but document the single-source default). Update the unpack call site. `_bindings.cpp` forwards parsed omega_mode_id to `p.sor_omega_mode_id` BEFORE the calibrate call, AFTER rk_params_init. Disabled-SOR path (sor=NULL/{}) unchanged. |
| **Format** | No new ABI: `sor_omega_mode_id` already in rk_params_t. No oris.cpp change. No change to the DEFAULT VALUE (that is e18t.9). Mirror R's omega_mode_id contract exactly (same int semantics 0/1/2). |
| **Boundary** | `_harvest.py` + `_bindings.cpp` + one Python test only. No oris.cpp, no R, no types.hpp/c_api.cpp default-value edit. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse, no fluff. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read R parse_sor + r_bridge.cpp omega_mode_id forwarding to mirror the contract. Read `_parse_sor`, its unpack call site, and the `_bindings.cpp` sor-field block.
2. `_parse_sor`: add omega_mode_id to the returned tuple (7-tuple); update the docstring; read `sor.get("omega_mode_id", <C-default sentinel>)`. Update every unpack site of `_parse_sor`'s return.

# T4: Implement free-subspace theta2 estimator in ORIS flat path

## I. Context & Objective

* **Why:** Replace the mj1p.2 global-residual θ₂ (which → 1 near bounds → ω→1.99 → oscillation) with the free-coordinate estimate that tracks ρ(M_II)².
* **Reference Data:** Design spec §2 (VERIFIED code map `docs/superpowers/derivations/oris_structure_map.md` — authoritative), §3.1–§3.6. Edit sites (advisory line numbers, confirm against map): flat capacity clamp `oris.cpp:1362`(lin)/`1444`(log) → set `is_pinned`; convergence sweep `1512–1516` → accumulate `S_lin_free`; flat omega-adapt block `1588–1642` → estimator+guards. θ₂ machinery: `estimate_theta2`(:415), `omega_from_theta2`(:425), `sor_theta2_ema`(:435). Use the T1-derived formula (NOT a blind reuse of `estimate_theta2`, which is lag-1 squared). Constants: kPinTol=1e-9, kResidFloor=1e-12, kMinSafeTotalWeight=1e-100, kSorProdCeiling=1.8, kSorCooldown=5, kSorLatchTrips=3.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

* **Format:** C++ edits to `src/oris.cpp` only (solve-local state; no CalibSorCfg/ABI input field).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Implement the FULL ordered guard envelope (design §3.4 gates 1–10): scope(ALM excluded)→free-set(n_free=0→ω=1)→warmup→finiteness/mass-floor→converged-denom→**ratio≥1 HARD-resets sor_theta2_ema=0 AND ω=1**→EMA decay on every fallback(gates 2–6)→formula min(·, **1.8**)→oscillation damp reads errF→monotone fallback(3 consec errF increase→ω=1 cooldown=5; latch after 3 trips→ω=1 permanent for margin). NEVER clamp to 1.99. |
| **Format** | omega=1 fast path preserved. `is_pinned` = `std::vector<char>(M_cell)`; `S_lin_free`/`n_free_k`/lag-2 buffers solve-local. Two distinct loops: is_pinned in clamp loop, S_lin_free in (kErrCheckInterval-gated) sweep. |

description:
# Epic: ORIS free-subspace optimal-omega (box-constrained Lehmann)

## Goal
Derive the box-constrained analog of the Lehmann optimal over-relaxation factor (free-subspace spectral radius ρ(M_II)) and conditionally implement it in the ORIS solver, fixing the mj1p.2 NO-GO where the global-residual spectral estimator was slower than fixed ω=1.5 on bounded problems.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Phase 1 (PRIMARY): SageMath artifact DERIVES ρ(M_II) + the free-subspace residual functional + θ₂ estimator formula from first principles, and numerically verifies free-ratio→ρ(M_II)², global-ratio→1, ω_opt(I) beats fixed on a synthetic. Committed with result table. GO/NO-GO recorded.
- [ ] Phase 2 (CONDITIONAL on Phase-1 GO + ship gate): ORIS flat-path implementation of the derived estimator with the full guard envelope; ships as mode-2 default ONLY if the pre-registered ship gate passes (spectral < fixed on the slow-unconstrained fixture, mw=5 no-regression, no converged fixture → NOCONV, wall-clock not regressed). Else revert, default → mode 1 (fixed), commit documented negative.
- [ ] R `devtools::test()` 0 failures + Python parity rtol=1e-6 (mode-2 exercised) on every code-touching ticket.
- [ ] No re-introduction of the mj1p.2 ω→1.99 oscillation (production ceiling 1.8; gate-6 EMA hard-reset; gate-10 permanent latch).

## Context & Background
North star: the design spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-31-oris-free-subspace-omega-design.md` (rev 4, design-review-gate PASSED 5/5). Verified code map: `docs/superpowers/derivations/oris_structure_map.md` (byte-exact — the authoritative anchor; line numbers in tickets are advisory, symbol names + map are load-bearing). Predecessor: leafblower-mj1p.2 closed NO-GO (Lehmann global θ₂ → ω→1.99 → oscillation on bounded ORIS). Literature (NotebookLM notebook 1e3036a1, 191 sources): no closed-form box-constrained ω_opt; correct optimum uses ρ(M_II) on the free coordinate block. SOR is off-by-default (`sor=NULL`); this is research/optionality, the derivation is the primary value.

Global constraints: ω changes only the iteration path, NEVER the fixed point (converged weights 1e-8, marginal_kl 1e-9 vs baseline). Build gate: `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` (not devtools::install). Python parity: `cd python && uv run pytest ../tests/test_parity_weights.py -x -q`. Commits: explicit file lists, NEVER `git add -A`; `.beads/issues.jsonl` must not leak into code commits. Scope: `method="oris"` flat (non-SRAA) path only; SRAA path and oris_soft/ALM mode OUT (deferred — relates to leafblower-e65t.1).

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Two phases, hard-gated. Phase 1 (T1) is a standalone SageMath derivation — its GO/NO-GO blocks ALL of Phase 2. Phase 2 tickets: fixture+pre-registration (T2), fixed-ω baseline snapshot (T3), estimator implementation (T4), observability + output-ABI (T5), ship-gate evaluation + finalize/docs (T6). Each sub-agent gets the design spec §-references + the verified code map; sub-agent = goldfish memory, every ticket is hermetic. Orchestrator INDEPENDENTLY re-runs all benchmark numbers (subagent numbers not trusted — prior fabrication incidents). Per-file explicit staging mandatory. NO-SHIP is an acceptable, expected outcome (third negative); the derivation stands regardless.

title: Rank2: ORIS spectral optimal-omega (Lehmann residual ratio)
description:
# Rank2: spectral optimal-omega from residual ratio (Lehmann)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Replace ORIS's heuristic multiplicative omega nudge (0.7 damp / 1.05 grow) with the spectral optimal-omega of Lehmann et al. 2022: estimate theta2 from the successive-residual ratio, set omega_opt=2/(1+sqrt(1-theta2)); IN = estimator + omega_opt formula + mode switch + benchmark; OUT = the omega>1 unlock (sibling Rank1, DEPENDS on it), greenkhorn/sinkhorn, fixed-point/bounds/enum/API change.
* **Why:** Replaces a blind heuristic with the provably optimal parameter using residual history the code already keeps.
* **Eval metric:** Evaluate on ITERATIONS to the configured `marginal_kl` convergence criterion (speed) + converged `marginal_kl` objective and weights (correctness, must match baseline). `max_err`/errRp is a feasibility guard only — NOT what these solvers minimize.
* **Reference Data:** `src/oris.cpp` adapt blocks `:823-843` (SRAA) and `:1556-1568` (flat); `kSorRecoveryGrowth`/`kSorOscillationDamp` `:104-105`; `sor_prev_errRp` history; Lehmann formula in `docs/methods/oris.md` Canonical-sources section (refs.bib lehmann2022overrelaxation).
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** per-margin errRp history in `sor_prev_errRp`; stepstone fixtures; parity harness; merged Rank1 (omega_max>1 available).
* **Format:** C++ estimator in `src/oris.cpp` + `sor_cfg.omega_mode` switch; results as Section V TOON.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | theta2 in [0,1); if residual ratio non-informative (NaN, >=1, or pre-burn-in) FALL BACK to Rank1 fixed omega_max — never emit omega>=2. omega_opt clamped to [omega_min, omega_max]. |
| **Format** | Estimator zero-extra-cost in common case (reuse stored residuals, no new full pass). omega=1 fast path preserved when mode disabled. |
| **Boundary** | Per-margin theta2 may differ — estimate per-margin (matches existing per-k omega array) or global; justify. Greedy path stays outside the proof. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse, no fluff. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Confirm Rank1 merged (omega_max>1). Read Lehmann formula block in `docs/methods/oris.md` and both adapt sites.
2. Implement `estimate_theta2(prev_resid, curr_resid, history)` from successive-residual-norm ratio; guard non-informative ratios.
3. Compute omega_opt=2/(1+sqrt(1-theta2)); clamp to [omega_min, omega_max]; apply after burn-in else fixed-omega_max fallback.
4. Add `sor_cfg.omega_mode` in {fixed, heuristic, spectral} so all three are A/B-testable; default decided by experiment.
5. EXPERIMENT: benchmark spectral vs Rank1 fixed vs legacy heuristic across stepstone configs x >=3 seeds; record ITERATIONS to the marginal_kl criterion, converged `marginal_kl`, converged-weight maxdiff vs baseline, feasibility max_err, and the realized omega trajectory; verify omega_opt tracks the empirically best fixed omega.
6. Set winning default; update `docs/methods/oris.md` guarantees table (spectral row) citing lehmann2022overrelaxation; `bd remember` whether spectral beat fixed and by how much.
7. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: rank2-spectral-omega
success: bool
data:
  modes: [string]
  per_config: [{config_id: string, iters_fixed: int, iters_heuristic: int, iters_spectral: int, marginal_kl_spectral: float, weight_maxdiff_vs_baseline: float, feasibility_max_err: float, theta2_estimated: float, omega_opt_mean: float}]
  chosen_mode: string        # fixed | heuristic | spectral (fixed = spectral did not win -> NO-GO for spectral)
  no_go_reason: null | string
  regressions: int    # MUST be 0
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` builds clean.
- [ ] `Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'` green.
- [ ] Python parity rtol=1e-6 green.
- [ ] GO/NO-GO recorded: GO = spectral iteration reduction >= Rank1 fixed mode on >=1 config with zero max_error regression -> ship spectral as default. NO-GO = spectral does not beat Rank1 fixed on iterations-to-marginal_kl on any config -> keep Rank1 fixed omega_max as default, set chosen_mode=fixed + no_go_reason, document benchmark numbers, close as NO-GO (a documented negative result is a valid close).
- [ ] theta2 estimator never yields omega>=2; fallback path unit-tested.
- [ ] Fixed point unchanged: converged weights within 1e-8 AND converged marginal_kl within 1e-9 of baseline.
- [ ] `docs/methods/oris.md` updated; `bd remember` saved.
close_reason: FINAL NO-GO: Lehmann spectral theta2 (point + EMA alpha=0.1-0.5) all give 40 iters vs fixed-1.5 at 30 iters on stepstone. theta2→1 near bounds → omega_opt→1.9 → oscillation damp at iter-30 → 10 extra iters. Structural: box-constraint operator spectral gap differs from unconstrained Sinkhorn. EMA commit 6b7753f. 686 R + 8 Python pass.

title: OT-family over-relaxation transfer (Greenkhorn/Sinkhorn/Anderson)
description:
# Epic: OT-family over-relaxation transfer (Greenkhorn / Sinkhorn / Anderson)

## Goal
Investigate, with benchmark-gated GO/NO-GO verdicts, whether over-relaxation transfers to the solvers where the full-sweep proof does NOT directly apply: Anderson-co-run in ORIS, greedy Greenkhorn, and stateful-Dykstra Sinkhorn.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Each child reaches a documented GO/NO-GO verdict backed by benchmark numbers — iterations to the configured `marginal_kl` convergence criterion + converged marginal_kl across >=3 seeds (max_err reported as feasibility only, NOT the ranking statistic) — recorded via `bd remember` and ticket comments.
- [ ] No solver's existing guarantee is weakened: any shipped change keeps build + R tests + parity rtol=1e-6 + stepstone no-regression green.
- [ ] NO-GO outcomes are explicitly acceptable and closed with the negative result documented (a proven dead-end is a valid deliverable).
- [ ] Zero default behavior change lands without a GO verdict.

## Context & Background
Sinkhorn, Greenkhorn, and ORIS are three update schemes for one computation (alternating KL/Bregman projection onto marginals = coordinate dual ascent on the entropic-OT dual). The over-relaxation theory cited in `docs/methods/oris.md` (Thibault 2021, Lehmann 2022, Soma-Uschmajew 2024) is proven only for full-sweep alternation. Three open questions: (Rank3) ORIS currently DISABLES SOR adaptation on Anderson-accepted steps (`src/oris.cpp:822` `sor_auto_v = sor_base && !r.aa_accepted`) — do they compose? (Rank4) does omega>1 help greedy single-coordinate Greenkhorn — no published analysis exists. (Rank5) the Sinkhorn solver is stateful (Dykstra correction vectors) so it is not a clean fixed-point map and Thibault's Lyapunov proof does not transfer directly. These are research bets, gated on empirical evidence, NOT speculative ships.

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Three independent child tasks (Rank3 Anderson-interplay, Rank4 over-relaxed Greenkhorn, Rank5 over-relaxed Dykstra-Sinkhorn). Each is hermetic with a flag-guarded prototype, a multi-arm benchmark, and a mandatory GO/NO-GO decision step. Global guard: NO default change without a GO verdict; keep best-iterate / outer-stall reverts as safety nets; a NO-GO with a documented mechanism is success. Rank5 has an early theory-assessment gate that may stop before any code.
close_reason: All 3 children done with documented verdicts: e65t.1 NO-GO (Anderson+SOR no benefit), e65t.2 NO-GO (Greenkhorn omega no benefit), e65t.3 GO (fixed omega easy-regime only, retracted at scale per leafblower-778a), e65t.4 NO-SHIP (adaptive omega Dykstra interference). Epic success criterion met: each child has documented verdict.

This is a real NON-edge bug, not just the literal-"NA" edge case. Verified by execution: tabulate(match(c("X","X","X",NA,NA), c("X","NA")))["NA"] == 0.
* **Reference:** solver harvest.R:475; Python ALREADY passes na_injected=_na_vars to _compute_sparseness_diag (_harvest.py:376); R compute_sparseness_diag has NO injection param — that asymmetry is the fix. Plan: .beads/plans/2026-05-30-4ihf5-diag-solver-na-consistency-plan.md (this ticket = Family S: WUs D, E, G-ii, G-iii).

title: chebyshev.cpp:514-520 — Mehrotra corrector includes spurious linear-in-ΔS_aff term
description:
Phase-B corrector RHS computes:
  corr_up = y_up[m]*dS_up_A[m] + y_up[m]*dS_up_A[m]^2 / s_up[m]
  (same pattern at L515-516 corr_dn, L592-598 corr_lo/hi, L502-505 RHS_B build, L583-587 dual step)

Standard Mehrotra (Nocedal-Wright 19.55, Mehrotra 1992 §4):
  corrector RHS = sigma_mu*e - S*Y*e - ΔS_aff·ΔY_aff
  Substituting ΔY_aff ≈ -y·ΔS_aff/s from predictor → -ΔS·ΔY ≈ +y·ΔS²/s

The y·ΔS² term IS the standard cross-term. But the linear y·ΔS term has no Mehrotra justification — it is the predictor's own residual, not the corrector's. Hypothesized cause of documented K≥9 non-convergence (file header L19-21).

Fix: drop linear-in-dS piece. corr_up = y_up[m]*dS_up_A[m]*dS_up_A[m]/s_up[m]. Same for corr_dn/lo/hi/delta. Validate via 2-margin LP convergence count vs CVXPY reference.
notes: Verified L510-520. Math derivation by Opus reviewer. Confidence 60. Requires unit test against external IPM reference (e.g. CVXPY) before fix lands. May explain Chebyshev K≥9 stall.
close_reason: NOT A BUG. Linear term y*ds_aff is the correct -y part of the Mehrotra cross-term -ds_aff*dy_aff (dy_aff=-y-y*ds_aff/s). Ticket derivation dropped the -y. Verified vs CLARABEL LP: solver hits optimum ~1e-11 on converged cases; dropping term does not fix K>=9 stall (separate conditioning issue). Guard comment added (commit).

title: chebyshev.cpp Mehrotra Phase-B corrector uses y_up instead of dY_up_A [T16]
description:
T16 from cr52 NUM plan. Not yet fixed.

## I. Objective

In: src/chebyshev.cpp Phase-B corrector loops (~lines 501, 514, 583) use y_up[m] (current dual variable Y) where standard Mehrotra (1992) predictor-corrector requires dY_up_A[m] (Phase-A dual step ΔY_A).

Out: dY_up_A[nct] declared alongside dS_up_A, filled during Phase-A dual solve; Phase-B corrector uses dY_up_A[m]*dS_up_A[m] at all 3 sites.

## II. Input

- src/chebyshev.cpp lines ~213-680 (Mehrotra predictor-corrector block)
- Reference: Mehrotra 1992 'On the Implementation of a Primal-Dual Interior Point Method', SIAM J. Optim. 2(4):575-601. Phase-B complementarity RHS: rhs_c_B = -Y*s + sigma*mu*e - dY_A.*dS_A

## III. Guards

| Type | Guard |
|------|-------|
| Logic | dY_up_A must be computed INSIDE Phase-A loop (lines ~456-492). Identify where y_up direction is solved (Schur/dlambda path) and extract ΔY component. Do NOT guess; read the solve path. |
| Logic | Phase-B corrector becomes: corr_up = sigma*mu - dY_up_A[m]*dS_up_A[m] - s_up[m]*y_up[m]. Centering term (sigma*mu) and current complementarity term (-s*y) unchanged; only the second-order term changes. |
| Forbidden | Touching Phase-A primal solve, dS_up_A logic, any other solver file, git add -A, --no-verify. |
| Boundary | Touch ONLY src/chebyshev.cpp. If ΔY_A is not explicitly computed (implicit in Schur solve), file DONE_WITH_CONCERNS and describe what was found. |
| Tone | Commit body MUST contain: (1) Mehrotra 1992 eq reference for Phase-B complementarity RHS, (2) before snippet showing y_up[m]*dS_up_A[m], (3) after snippet showing dY_up_A[m]*dS_up_A[m], (4) one-line derivation 'second-order correction removes O(Delta^2) cross term from Taylor expansion of complementarity'. |

## IV. Logic

1. Grep src/chebyshev.cpp for the Phase-A dual update loop to locate where y_up direction is set.
2. Declare std::vector<double> dY_up_A(nct) at line ~216 alongside dS_up_A(nct).
3. In Phase-A dual loop: assign dY_up_A[m] = <Phase-A ΔY direction for y_up[m]>.
4. In Phase-B corrector at lines ~501, ~514, ~583: replace y_up[m]*dS_up_A[m] with dY_up_A[m]*dS_up_A[m].
5. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . (build gate — must compile clean).
6. Rscript -e 'devtools::test(reporter=summary)' — 0 FAIL required.
7. cd python && pip install -e . -q && pytest python/leafblower/ -q — must pass.

## V. Schema (TOON)

{
  file: 'src/chebyshev.cpp',
  changed_lines: [
    '~216: add dY_up_A(nct) declaration',
    '~Phase-A dual loop: dY_up_A[m] assignment',
    '~501: corr_up uses dY_up_A[m]*dS_up_A[m]',
    '~514: corr_up uses dY_up_A[m]*dS_up_A[m]',
    '~583: corr_up uses dY_up_A[m]*dS_up_A[m]'
  ],
  gate: 'R CMD INSTALL --preclean . && devtools::test() 0 FAIL',
  commit_body: 'Mehrotra 1992 eq + before/after + one-line derivation'
}

## VI. DoD

- [ ] dY_up_A declared (line ~216) and filled in Phase-A loop
- [ ] Phase-B corrector uses dY_up_A[m]*dS_up_A[m] at all 3 sites (lines ~501, ~514, ~583)
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . clean compile
- [ ] devtools::test() 0 FAIL
- [ ] python/leafblower/ pytest passes
- [ ] Commit body contains Mehrotra 1992 citation + algebraic derivation
- [ ] bd close leafblower-<this-id> with linked commit hash
close_reason: False positive: code algebraically correct. corr_up = y*dS + y*dS^2/s = -dY_A*dS_A via diagonal complementarity step dY_A = -y*(1+dS/s). Verified at lines 501,514,583 (up-margin), 592 (hi-bound sign-flip consistent). Mehrotra 1992 Eq 4.5 satisfied. No change needed.

title: calib_dispatch.hpp apply_rule unconditional prev=curr leaks past stop_when=ANY
description:
## I. Context & Objective

`src/calib_dispatch.hpp` `apply_rule(...)` (find via `grep -n "apply_rule" src/calib_dispatch.hpp`) writes `prev = curr` unconditionally at function exit. Outer driver uses `stop_when=ANY` short-circuit semantics: when any rule fires, the driver halts and never re-enters `apply_rule`. The unconditional `prev = curr` mutates state in a way that leaks past the halt — subsequent reads of `prev` (e.g. by diagnostic code or a re-entry path) see post-halt curr, not the value at convergence.

**Objective:** Gate the `prev = curr` write on whether the rule body actually completed its work AND the caller intends to continue iterating (i.e. NOT a stop_when=ANY short-circuit that halts the driver). Either move the assignment into the iteration-continue branch only, OR restructure so `prev` is only consulted at iteration entry, never post-halt.

## II. Input Specification

- File: `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` (function `apply_rule` and its caller `outer_iterate_strategy_*` or similar).
- Related context: bd memory `gotcha-iterative-outer-loop-algorithms-with-correction-tail` — outer-loop algorithms with correction-tail step have a known bug class where residual references different weight state than caller-visible. Same flavor.
- `stop_when=ANY` semantics: defined in `rk_stop_when_t` enum in `src/leafblower.h` or local; first matching rule fires, driver returns.

## III. Constraints & Guards

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | After this fix, `prev` reflects the value at last completed iteration (not post-halt mutated). Verify by adding/extending a unit test that drives `stop_when=ANY` with a fixture whose `prev` value matters at exit. |

```
deff_H ≈ deff_K(w) · σ̂²_u / σ̂²_y         (Eq 3.5, zero-correlation approximation)
deff_K(w) = n · Σwᵢ² / [Σwᵢ]²              (Eq 2.4, Kish 1965 weighting deff)
û_i = y_i - x_i^T·β̂                          (GREG residuals; intercept absorbed into A separately)
β̂ = (X^T·W·X)^{-1}·X^T·W·y                  (survey-weighted least-squares slope)
σ̂²_u = Σwᵢ·(ûᵢ - ū_w)² / Σwᵢ                (Eq 2.7)
σ̂²_y = Σwᵢ·(yᵢ - ȳ_w)² / Σwᵢ                (Eq 2.7)
```

```c
typedef struct {
    double deff_K;        /* Kish (1965) Eq 2.4 */
    double deff_H;        /* Henry & Valliant (2015) Eq 3.5; NaN if outcome=NULL */

/*

int rk_design_effect(
```

# 🚨 SPEC REVISION v2 (2026-05-08) — Henry & Valliant 2015 corrected scope

The v1 spec below cited "Cochran 1977 §4.5 unbiased weighted variance" as the target formula. **This was wrong.** The 4-arg form of `design_effect` is documented as the Henry & Valliant 2015 calibration design effect; v1 patched the denominator to a generic Cochran reliability-weight variance ratio that diverges from H&V 2015 Eq 3.4/3.5 in three ways:

1. **Numerator uses y instead of GREG residuals û_i** — H&V Eq 3.4 requires `û_i = y_i - x_i^T·β̂` where β̂ = (X^T·W·X)^{-1}·X^T·W·y is the survey-weighted least-squares slope. v1 uses y_i directly with no calibration-covariate adjustment.
2. **Denominator is Bessel n-1 unweighted, not weighted** — H&V uses `σ̂²_y = Σwᵢ·(yᵢ - ȳ_w)² / Σwᵢ` (survey-weighted population unit variance, paper §2.3 Eq 2.7 / §3 Step 5). v1 uses `var(outcome)` (Bessel unweighted).
3. **`data` and `target` arguments are ignored** — H&V Eq 3.4 requires the calibration covariate matrix X (built from the categorical margin variables in `target` keyed against columns in `data`). v1 accepts these args but never uses them.

Commits 13bbe77 (v1 fix landed under wrong cite) and 38f7d20 (roxygen attribution patch) must be reverted; the correct fix is a feature-sized reimplementation, not a 1-line denom swap.

## Authoritative formula (paste-verbatim from H&V 2015 PDF, Survey Methodology vol 41 no 2)

**Eq 3.4 (sample-based exact estimator):**

```
deff_H ≈ deff_K(w) · (σ̂²_u / σ̂²_y)
       + (n · σ̂_w / (N · σ̂²_y)) · (ρ̂_{u²w} · σ̂_{a²} - 2·â · ρ̂_uw · σ̂_u)
```

**Eq 3.5 (zero-correlation approximation; first-pass implementation target):**

```
deff_H ≈ deff_K(w) · σ̂²_u / σ̂²_y
```

where:

- `deff_K(w) = 1 + [CV(w)]² = n·Σwᵢ² / [Σwᵢ]²` — Kish design effect (paper Eq 2.4)
- `û_i = y_i - x_i^T·β̂` — GREG residuals (no intercept; intercept absorbed into A)
- `β̂ = (X_s^T·W·X_s)^{-1}·X_s^T·W·y_s` — survey-weighted least-squares slope
- `W = diag(w_1, ..., w_n)` — weight matrix
- `X_s` — n×p matrix of calibration covariates from sample, built from `data` + `target`
- `σ̂²_u = Σwᵢ·(ûᵢ - ū_w)² / Σwᵢ` — survey-weighted variance of GREG residuals (population unit variance per §2.3)
- `σ̂²_y = Σwᵢ·(yᵢ - ȳ_w)² / Σwᵢ` — survey-weighted variance of y (population unit variance)
- `ū_w = Σwᵢ·ûᵢ / Σwᵢ`, `ȳ_w = Σwᵢ·yᵢ / Σwᵢ`
- (Eq 3.4 only) `â`, `ρ̂_{u²w}`, `σ̂_{a²}`, `ρ̂_uw`, `σ̂_w` — additional terms per §3 Step 5

PracTools `deffH` (Valliant et al., R package on CRAN; reference impl) implements Eq 3.4 with all correlation terms. First-pass leafblower scope MAY land Eq 3.5 (zero-correlation) and document the gap; full Eq 3.4 deferred to follow-up if simulation evidence shows correlation terms matter for our typical fixtures.

## Building the calibration covariate matrix X from `data` + `target`

`target` is a named list where each entry is a named vector of margin proportions (one entry per categorical calibration variable). `data` is a data frame containing the corresponding columns. To build X:

```r
build_X <- function(data, target) {
  cols <- list()
  for (var in names(target)) {
    levs <- names(target[[var]])
    f <- factor(data[[var]], levels = levs)
    # Drop one level for full rank (intercept absorbs); follow PracTools convention for which to drop
    M <- model.matrix(~ f)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
    cols[[var]] <- M
  }
  X <- do.call(cbind, cols)
  X  # n × p, no leading intercept column (intercept tracked separately as A)
}
```

Edge cases:
- Empty `target` → degenerate; return Kish-only deff_K(w) with documented note
- `data[[var]]` levels not subset of `names(target[[var]])` → error with clear message
- Singular X^T·W·X (collinear margins) → return NA with cause OR fall back to Eq 3.5 with σ̂²_u = σ̂²_y (deff_H = deff_K)

   - Build X via `build_X(data, target)` helper above

   - Compute û = y - X·β̂
   - Compute weighted means/variances: `ū_w = sum(w*û)/sum(w)`, `ȳ_w = sum(w*y)/sum(w)`, `σ̂²_u = sum(w*(û-ū_w)²)/sum(w)`, `σ̂²_y = sum(w*(y-ȳ_w)²)/sum(w)`

title: harvest.R convergence_reason from accelerate_bool not stall
description:
## I. Context & Objective

`R/harvest.R:537` populates `convergence_reason` for solver status==5 (stall) by branching on user input flag `accelerate_bool`: `if (isTRUE(accelerate_bool)) "stall_wchange" else "stall_kl"`. Reason should derive from the actual stall mechanism the solver hit, not the user's request flag. If `accelerate=TRUE` was honored but the solver fell back to plain IPF and stalled on KL plateau, harvest reports `"stall_wchange"` (wrong).

**Objective:** Source `convergence_reason` for status==5 from a solver-emitted truth. Either (a) introduce a new C++ `CalibResult` field carrying the stall-kind enum and propagate it through `r_bridge.cpp` to harvest, OR (b) prove via solver-code audit that `accelerate_bool` is bijective with the actual stall path (no fallback), document, and label the heuristic correct. Subagent must investigate then implement.

## II. Input Specification

- File: `R/harvest.R` (line 537 in switch over `calib_result$status`)
- Solver code under `src/`: `src/sraa.hpp` (Anderson-acceleration stall path), `src/raking.cpp` (plain IPF KL stall path), `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` (status emission), `src/leafblower.h` (`rk_result_t` enum + struct), `src/r_bridge.cpp` (struct→list bridge).
- Existing reasons grepped: only two strings `"stall_wchange"`, `"stall_kl"` — no other emitter.
- Documentation in `R/harvest.R:153-154` describes the two reasons.

## III. Constraints & Guards

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | If audit finds `accelerate=TRUE` ↔ wchange path is bijective: keep heuristic, document. If NOT bijective (any fallback or interleaved path): add solver-emitted field. NO guessing. |
| **Format** | If field added: extend `CalibResult` (or `rk_result_t`) with `stall_kind: int` + named-enum mapping; bridge through `r_bridge.cpp` as `convergence_stall_kind`; harvest reads it. If heuristic kept: add roxygen note + commit body proof. |
| **Boundary** | Touch `R/harvest.R` (always); touch `src/leafblower.h` + `src/r_bridge.cpp` + emitting solver(s) ONLY if route (a). Do NOT touch unrelated solvers. |
| **Tone** | Commit body MUST cite the audit evidence (file:line where stall path is set under each acceleration setting). No "should be safe" language. |
| **Forbidden** | Using `accelerate_bool` as proxy without audit-justified bijectivity proof. Adding a new R-side flag to mirror `accelerate`. `git add -A`. `--no-verify`. Touching `rk_algorithm_t` slot 2 (LBFGSB reserved). |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

1. Audit: read `src/sraa.hpp`, `src/raking.cpp`, `src/ieppa.cpp` for every code path that returns status==5. For each, identify whether its emission depends on `state.accelerate` or on solver-internal stall detection.

title: harvest.R compute_sparseness_diag string lookup x K
description:
## I. Context & Objective

`R/harvest.R` `compute_sparseness_diag` (def near line 707) iterates over K margins. title: r_bridge.cpp UNPROTECT(5) after 108 lines unprotected allocations
description:
## I. Context & Objective

`src/r_bridge.cpp:791-905` holds 5 SEXPs PROTECTed across a 114-line span:
- L791 `wts`, L795 `res_list`, L796 `res_names`, L898 `out`, L899 `out_names`
- L905 `UNPROTECT(5)` + return.

Plan epic RWRAP mechanism: "scope-correct UNPROTECT immediately after each PROTECT". Long span risks GC-survival bugs if any intermediate `Rf_error` fires; balanced UNPROTECT on the error unwind is correct in R but the wide scope obscures local reasoning.

**Objective:** Tighten PROTECT scope. Move each `PROTECT` adjacent to first use; insert `UNPROTECT_PTR` or scope-paired `UNPROTECT(N)` so no protected SEXP outlives its written-into-parent step. `out` / `out_names` (the final return list) PROTECT can stay near the end since the construction sites for them are local.

## II. Input Specification

- File: `src/r_bridge.cpp` (single function span 791-905; `rk_calibrate_single` or its caller — confirm function via grep `^SEXP\|^extern "C"` immediately above 791).
- Surrounding pattern (already balanced at L846-850 for `bw_sxp`): `PROTECT → SET_VECTOR_ELT(res_list, ...) → UNPROTECT(1)` (since adopted by parent).
- N_RESULT_FIELDS macro defines result-list field count; do not change.

## III. Constraints & Guards

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Once SEXP is `SET_VECTOR_ELT`'d into a parent that is itself PROTECTed, the child can be UNPROTECTed (parent retains it). Apply same idiom as L846-850. End-of-function `UNPROTECT(N)` should match number of currently live PROTECTs at that point — typically only the return list. |
| **Format** | C++17. Use `UNPROTECT(1)` after each child adoption; final `UNPROTECT(K)` matches remaining live PROTECTs only. Add a one-line `// adopted by <parent>` comment per adoption (only WHY-clarifying, not WHAT). |
| **Boundary** | Touch only `src/r_bridge.cpp` lines in the affected function. Do NOT modify N_RESULT_FIELDS or struct field order. Do NOT change which SEXPs go into the result list. |
| **Tone** | Commit body explains adoption invariant; no narrating WHAT each PROTECT does. |
| **Forbidden** | Removing PROTECT entirely from any allocation path. Replacing PROTECT/UNPROTECT with `R_PreserveObject`/`R_ReleaseObject`. `git add -A`. `--no-verify`. Touching unrelated functions in `r_bridge.cpp`. |

1. Read `src/r_bridge.cpp` 770-910 to confirm function boundary and all PROTECT sites in scope.
2. For each of `wts`, `res_list`, `res_names`: identify the line where it is `SET_VECTOR_ELT`'d into its parent (or where its parent is finalized). Insert `UNPROTECT(1)` after adoption, with `// adopted by <parent>` comment.

9. Commit. Body cites adoption invariant + before/after PROTECT scope spans.

title: newton_calib.cpp bound-violation writes weights before status downgrade
description:
## I. Context & Objective

`src/newton_calib.cpp` bound-violation handler writes weights INTO the result struct BEFORE downgrading status to `RK_ERR_BOUND` (or equivalent). Caller observes weights that violate the user-specified `[min_weight, max_weight]` clamp under the wrong status code: `RK_OK` weights look valid even though they aren't.

**Objective:** Reorder write-then-downgrade so caller never sees violated weights with non-error status. Either (a) downgrade status FIRST, then write only the pre-violation safe weights; OR (b) keep current write but flip the write site so violated weights are written ONLY when status reflects the violation. (a) is preferred.

## II. Input Specification

- File: `src/newton_calib.cpp` — bound-violation path (search `min_weight\|max_weight\|RK_ERR_BOUND\|bound_violation`).
- Related: `src/leafblower.h` `rk_result_t` status codes — confirm exact bound-violation code name.
- `CalibState` struct: weights live in `st.weights`; result struct field via `res.base.best_weights` per project convention (CLAUDE.md note: "`res.base.*` not `res.*` since ztid.4").
- Test surface: `tests/testthat/test-bounds*.R` or similar — verify by adding a fixture that violates bounds and asserts `result$status == RK_ERR_BOUND` AND `result$weights` does NOT exceed `max_weight`.

## III. Constraints & Guards

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | After fix: status==BOUND ⇒ caller-visible weights are pre-violation (last good iterate or zero-vec sentinel, NOT the violating iterate). status==OK ⇒ all weights ∈ [min_weight, max_weight]. Verify with new test. |
| **Format** | C++17. Single function-body reorder. No new state. Comment any non-obvious WHY (e.g. why pre-violation weights are tracked). |
| **Boundary** | Touch only `src/newton_calib.cpp` and the new test file. Do NOT modify `rk_result_t` enum or `CalibResult` struct layout. Do NOT touch other solvers (`raking.cpp`, `ieppa.cpp`, etc.) even if they have similar pattern — separate ticket per memory rule. |
| **Tone** | Commit body shows status-machine before/after as ASCII state diagram. Cites `res.base.*` invariant from CLAUDE.md. |
| **Forbidden** | Post-clamping the violating iterate to satisfy the bound (silent fix masking the convergence-failure signal). Tweaking `min_weight`/`max_weight` defaults to avoid the violation in tests. `git add -A`. `--no-verify`. |

1. Read `src/newton_calib.cpp` end-of-iter / cleanup section. Identify the line that writes `weights` to result struct AND the line that sets status. Confirm current order is write→downgrade.

3. Identify what "last good iterate" means in this solver: typically the previous-accepted iterate cached in `st.prev_weights` or `res.base.best_weights`. Use whichever is already maintained.
4. Add unit test in `tests/testthat/test-newton-bounds.R`: fixture forces bound violation; assert `result$status == <bound-violation code>` AND `all(result$weights >= min_weight - 1e-12)` AND `all(result$weights <= max_weight + 1e-12)`.

9. Stage explicitly: `git add src/newton_calib.cpp tests/testthat/test-newton-bounds.R`.
10. Commit. Body: ASCII state-machine before/after + algebraic note that pre-violation iterate is the safe fallback.
