title: calib_dispatch.hpp kChi2Floor=1.0 distorts Pearson chi2 for W>>n
description:
## I. Context & Objective

`src/calib_dispatch.hpp` defines `kChi2Floor = 1.0` and applies it as a floor on the Pearson chi-square denominator (or numerator depending on form). For calibrations where total weight `W = Σwᵢ ≫ n` (e.g. weights on the order of population scaling factors, common in survey calibration), the floor distorts the chi-square value: clamping to 1.0 swallows the natural scale and reports a misleadingly small chi2.

**Objective:** Replace the constant 1.0 floor with either (a) a derivation-justified scale-relative floor (e.g. `kChi2Floor * max(1.0, n / W)` or similar), OR (b) remove the floor entirely and add a caller-side guard that handles the W→0 degenerate case explicitly. Decision driven by first-principles algebraic derivation; subagent picks route based on Pearson chi2 spec.

## II. Input Specification

- File: `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` — search `kChi2Floor`; identify decl + every use site.
- Pearson chi2 form: `χ² = Σ (wᵢ - 1)² / 1` (basic) OR `Σ (wᵢ - dᵢ)² / dᵢ` (calibration-design); confirm which by reading the use site.
- Related: `src/raking.cpp` last_F_metrics.chi2 path (bd ticket leafblower-ny2b/leafblower-a605 closed; chi2 computation already audited there — read those close_reasons in `.beads/issues.jsonl` for context).
- Tests likely sensitive: `tests/testthat/test-quality-metrics.R`, `test-design.R`. Verify by grep.

## III. Constraints & Guards

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | First-principles derivation: Pearson chi2 has a natural lower-bound at 0 (perfect uniform); a hard 1.0 floor only makes sense if downstream divides by chi2 (verify). If no division: floor is dead code; remove it. If division: floor must scale with `W` to remain meaningful. |
| **Format** | C++17. Either replace constant with constexpr derivation OR delete the floor + add caller-side guard. No magic numbers. |
| **Boundary** | Touch only `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` (declaration + use sites in same file). If the floor is referenced from other solvers, scope expands to those — confirm by grep first; if scope grows beyond 2 files, halt and report DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. |
| **Tone** | Commit body MUST contain algebraic derivation block: starting from Pearson chi2 definition, derive correct lower-bound behavior under `W ≫ n`. Cite chi2 form used. |
| **Forbidden** | Tweaking the constant value (1.0 → 0.1 etc.) without algebraic derivation — that's "tweak constants to make tests pass" forbidden by CLAUDE.md and plan. Weakening test assertions. `git add -A`. `--no-verify`. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

1. Read `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` `kChi2Floor` declaration + every use site (grep within file).
2. For each use site, classify: (i) division-by-floor (floor prevents div-by-zero), (ii) clamp-up of computed chi2 (floor sets minimum reported value), (iii) other.
3. Derive correct behavior from Pearson chi2 spec for each use site under `W ≫ n` regime. Document derivation in commit body.
4. Pick fix route per use site: route (a) scale-relative floor with derivation, OR route (b) delete floor + caller guard for degenerate.
5. Implement fix.
6. Verify chi2 numerical output on `W ≫ n` fixture: construct test where `W = 1e6 * n`, compute chi2 before-fix vs after-fix, document delta in commit body. Add as new test.
7. Build: `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`.
8. Test: `testthat::test_local()` ≥562 PASS / 0 FAIL / 11 SKIP.
9. Parity: `cd python && pytest python/parity` rtol=1e-6.
10. Stepstone smoke: chi2-related fixture not regressed (or regression is the spec correction — explain in commit).
11. Stage explicitly: `git add src/calib_dispatch.hpp tests/testthat/<new-test>.R`.
12. Commit. Body: algebraic derivation + before/after chi2 on W≫n fixture.
13. `bd close leafblower-p0iy --reason="<route>; chi2 spec-correct under W≫n"`.
14. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)

Sub-agent MUST return:

```toon

success: bool
data:
  files_changed: [path, ...]
  commit_sha: <40-hex>
  fix_route: a_scale_relative | b_remove_with_guard
  use_site_count: int
  algebraic_derivation_in_commit: bool
  w_gg_n_chi2_before: float
  w_gg_n_chi2_after: float
  test_pass: int
  test_fail: int
  test_skip: int
  parity_check: passed | failed | skipped
  stepstone_smoke: passed | failed | skipped
error_log: null | string
```

## VI. Definition of Done

- [ ] First-principles algebraic derivation appears in commit body (Pearson chi2 spec → correct lower-bound behavior).
- [ ] Floor replaced or removed per derivation; no magic-number tweaks.
- [ ] New test on `W ≫ n` fixture documents before/after chi2 delta.
- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` clean.
- [ ] `testthat::test_local()` ≥562 PASS / 0 FAIL / 11 SKIP.
- [ ] Parity rtol=1e-6 (or skipped with cause).
- [ ] Stepstone fixture not regressed (or spec-driven regression explained).
- [ ] `bd close leafblower-p0iy` succeeded.
- [ ] Output matches V. Output Schema.

* **Objective:** Apply minimal patch from T3.fix_target with STRICT EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION GATE — chebyshev parity_bench max_abs_diff drop from 2.047e-3 to <1e-4 BEFORE commit. If escalate_irreducible=true (cause = libstdc++/compiler ABI not fixable from leafblower codebase): doc-only NEWS commit acknowledging known epsilon-divergence.
* **Cycle bound (REV 2 fix)**: max 2 retry cycles total (initial + 2 reopens). On 3rd reopen attempt, FORCE branch=escalate_irreducible regardless of T3.fix_target. Prevents unbounded T2-T3-T5 loop.
* **Why:** Anti-2apm-relapse — empirical verification load-bearing. 8u2y precedent: T4 capacity_mu fix had 0 effect; gate caught it.
* **Reference:** T3 winner.toon; T4 multi-DGP winner.toon (if applicable).

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Approved T3 (and optionally T4) attribution.
* **Format:** Diff against HEAD; build pass log; **EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION LOG**.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **T5 cycle counter** | bd ticket field `t5_attempt_n` initialized 1; on each reopen-T2 increment. If t5_attempt_n > 2 (i.e., this is the 3rd entry), set branch=escalate_irreducible automatically (no further code-patch attempts). User can override but default stops the loop. |
| **Caller-audit gate** | grep -rn the patched param/op across R/, python/, tests/, src/, vignettes/. Save to benchmarks/8u2y.7/caller_audit.txt. |
| **Allowed file set** | r_bridge.cpp, c_api.cpp, _bindings.cpp, R/harvest.R, _harvest.py, NEWS.md, man/*.Rd, src/parity_dump.hpp, src/ieppa.cpp (DIAGNOSTIC INSTRUMENTATION OK + LOGIC IF GATE PASSES), src/chebyshev.cpp (same). calib_dispatch.hpp + cell_table.hpp/cpp logic forbidden. |
| **Build-test-stage ordering (strict)** | (1) caller-audit. (2) Edit code. (3) NEWS.md + roxygen/docstring + spec amendment if needed. (4) devtools::document() if roxygen touched. (5) R CMD INSTALL --preclean . (6) pip install -e . --no-build-isolation. (7) Rscript -e "devtools::test()" must pass. (8) cd python && pytest must pass. (9) **EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION GATE**: parity_bench R+Py + parity_compare.R; chebyshev max_abs_diff MUST be <1e-4. If gate FAILS AND t5_attempt_n <= 2: HALT — `git checkout HEAD -- <files>`; back out; comment ticket BLOCKED + reopen T2; do NOT commit. If gate FAILS AND t5_attempt_n == 3: force escalate_irreducible. (10) ONLY THEN stage explicit + commit. |
| **escalate_irreducible branch** | NEWS.md doc-only commit + explicit recommendation. Skip empirical gate. testthat + pytest must pass on doc-only commit. |
| **Spec amendment** | If T3.spec_amendment_needed: APPEND per memory feedback_spec_amendment_append. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read T3 winner.toon (and T4 if exists). Read t5_attempt_n from ticket.
2. If t5_attempt_n > 2: force escalate_irreducible.
3. Branch:
   - Code patch: caller-audit + edit + builds + suites + EMPIRICAL GATE.
   - escalate_irreducible: NEWS.md doc + suites pass + commit.
4. Both: explicit file staging + atomic commit.

## V. Output Schema (Strict TOON, valid YAML)
```yaml

success: bool
data:

  staged_files: [...]
  commit_status: COMMITTED | BLOCKED_BACKED_OUT_REOPEN_T2 | DOC_ONLY_COMMITTED

```

## VI. Definition of Done
- caller_audit.txt committed (if commit_status=COMMITTED).
- Files modified ⊆ allowed set.
- Both builds pass (or skipped for doc-only).
- testthat + pytest pass.
- **EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION GATE PASSED** (code_patch branch) OR doc-only commit (escalate_irreducible).
- NEWS.md entry committed in same commit.
- Atomic commit, explicit file list.
- IF gate FAILED: status=BLOCKED, T2 reopened, attempt_n incremented; OR if attempt_n>2: forced escalate.

title: T3 8u2y.7: code-line attribution (ULTRATHINK on operator/op-order; FPU/ABI/linker hypotheses)
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** From T2 first-divergent iter + category, identify the EXACT operator (file:line + statement) producing the float divergence. Branch on category:
  - Cat D (ieppa diverges first): trace ieppa_outer_iter logic at first-divergent iter; identify operator (margin loop, accumulator, BLAS call) responsible.
  - Cat E (chebyshev_ipm diverges first): trace IPM Newton step at first-divergent iter; identify operator.
  - Cat F (FPU state differs): identify which side has the offending FPU mode + WHY (R startup sets it? Py default different?).
* **Why:** Concrete fix_target enables T5 patch + empirical-verification gate.
* **Reference:**
  - T2 outputs: benchmarks/8u2y.7/diff_summary.toon + per-fixture trace diffs.
  - src/ieppa.cpp + src/chebyshev.cpp inspection (read-only at this stage).
  - Memory `gotcha-iterative-outer-loop-algorithms-with-correction-tail`: residual-vs-correction subtleties.
  - Memory `chebyshev-ref-cat-convention-change-is-behavioral-not`: ref-cat j=0 driver.
  - Memory `ghosal-nutz-2022`: theoretical backing for Sinkhorn-class operators.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** T2 outputs.
* **Format:** TOON with verbatim code quotes both sides + operator-level attribution.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **ULTRATHINK** | Use opus model for this task. Float-internal divergences require deep reasoning about op-order, ABI, FPU semantics. |
| **Empirical preview MANDATORY** | Before T3 closes: run candidate fix in working tree; rebuild; rerun parity_bench chebyshev; capture max_abs_diff drop. If drop confirmed → T5 fix_target validated. If no drop → hypothesis wrong; refine OR escalate. REVERT preview before T3 closes. |
| **No code commits** | Only winner.toon. |
| **Cat F branch** | If FPU state differs: investigate (a) R startup sets FPU mode (Rinternals.h, R_init function), (b) Py / numpy default. Fix by aligning either side's startup. Tag separately as cause-F-FPU. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read T2 first_divergent_iter + category per fixture.
2. Read solver source at the operator producing divergence at the first-divergent iter.
3. Cat D branch: trace ieppa_outer_iter; identify divergent op (margin loop accum order? BLAS call? log/exp?).
4. Cat E branch: trace chebyshev_ipm Newton step; identify divergent op (Cholesky? linear solve? lambda update?).
5. Cat F branch: investigate FPU control word setup at R/Py startup; identify mismatch + impact on chebyshev.
6. Empirical preview: pick candidate fix, edit working tree, rebuild, rerun parity_bench. Capture max_abs_diff drop. REVERT.
7. Write benchmarks/8u2y.7/winner.toon.

title: DEEP: chebyshev R-Py solver-internal trace (post-8u2y escalation)
description:
# Epic: chebyshev R-Py solver-internal divergence trace (REV 2)

## Goal
Identify the SOLVER-INTERNAL operator/op-order producing chebyshev parity_bench max_abs_diff = 2.047e-3 between R and Py paths on stepstone fulldata, OR confirm cause is toolchain-ABI/process-state and document irreducibility. 8u2y proved cause is BEYOND wrapper-layer dump-able state.

## Worktree base (REV 2 fix)
**Worktree base: 8u2y-investigate branch (NOT master).** parity_dump.hpp + benchmarks/8u2y/ artifacts (12 trace files, diff_summary.toon, T2-redux full-vector hash methodology) live ONLY on 8u2y-investigate. T0 + T1+ build on top. Worktree command: `git worktree add .worktrees/8u2y-7-deep -b 8u2y.7-deep 8u2y-investigate`.

## Prior-investigation lessons (FROM 8u2y)
- Wrapper-layer instrumentation (parity_dump.hpp at chebyshev_ipm entry) is INSUFFICIENT — captures struct state only, not solver-internal state.
- Empirical-verification gate (8u2y T4) IS load-bearing — caught wrong attribution. Carry forward unchanged.
- T2-redux full-vector hashes detected real divergence (w_warm differs on small/fulldata Cat D) AND identified Cat E (chebyshev_ipm internal divergence on bitwise-identical inputs medium fixture).

## Hypothesis space
1. **Cat D — ieppa warm-start internal float-op order**: r_bridge calls ieppa with subtle config diff; ieppa internal accumulator order differs.
2. **Cat E — chebyshev_ipm internal**: chebyshev_ipm produces different output from BITWISE-IDENTICAL inputs. Implies process-state / ABI:
   - FPU control word (rounding mode, denormals flush, mxcsr) differs.
   - libstdc++ / glibc / BLAS ABI differs between R-package and Py-package builds.
   - Compiler-version mismatch producing different optimization decisions.
3. **Cross-cut**: BLAS routine internal nondet at single-thread.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] T0 toolchain-identity pre-flight evidence captured (FPU state + compiler info both langs; optionally: rebuild with identical toolchain).
- [ ] Locate cause OR confirm irreducible.
- [ ] Apply minimal patch with EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION GATE pass OR doc-only NEWS commit if cause irreducible.
- [ ] testthat + pytest pass.
- [ ] 15/15 identical OR documented exception with NEWS guidance.

## Forbidden list (RELAXED vs 8u2y; FURTHER GATED vs prior rev)
- Solver-core LOGIC edits forbidden (ieppa.cpp/chebyshev.cpp algorithm changes).
- Solver-core DIAGNOSTIC instrumentation ALLOWED, but ONLY AFTER T0 evidence justifies it. T0 (cheap wrapper-only FPU probe + optional toolchain rebuild) MUST precede T1 (expensive solver-core printf).
- API widening / tol-bump / single-DGP winner forbidden.
- **EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION GATE at fix-commit time MANDATORY.**

## Authority
Empirical: parity_bench chebyshev max_abs_diff drop to <1e-4 IS the gate. Code attribution + multi-DGP + FPU-state evidence confirm winner side.

## Audit Strategy
- T0 wrapper-only FPU probe + optional toolchain identity check; gate decision for T1+.
- T1 solver-core diagnostic instrumentation (only if T0 evidence justifies).
- T2 per-iter trajectory diff.
- T3 ULTRATHINK code-line attribution.
- T4 multi-DGP if ambiguous.
- T5 minimal patch + STRICT EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION GATE.
- T6 regression test + 15/15 verify.

## Tasks (children)
T0 wrapper-only FPU probe + toolchain identity check (NEW; cheap pre-flight gate)
T1 solver-core instrumentation (CONDITIONAL on T0 outcome; gated by T0 result)
T2 per-iter trajectory diff
T3 ULTRATHINK code-line attribution
T4 multi-DGP winner if ambiguous (CONDITIONAL)
T5 minimal patch + STRICT EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION GATE OR doc-only escalate
T6 regression test + verify 15/15

NEWS.md + test docstring document the unsolved state. Master parity: 14/15 (chebyshev at 2.047e-3 no_conv exception). title: Locate residual chebyshev R-Py divergence (post-2apm) via state-dump diff
description:
# Epic: Locate residual chebyshev R-Python divergence post-2apm

## Goal
Identify the wrapper-layer code-path divergence that produces max|w_R - w_Py| = 2.047e-3 for chebyshev on stepstone fulldata, with identical Tier-1 metrics R/Py at iter cap. 2apm's floor-typo fix did NOT close the gap (mirror restored but no observable behavioral effect — chebyshev IPM is weight-invariant to warm-start floor). The cause is elsewhere in the r_bridge bypass vs c_api path setup. Apply a minimal patch and bring chebyshev to identical_1e4=YES on stepstone.

## Prior-investigation lessons (FROM 2apm)
- Code-comment authority alone is INSUFFICIENT. 2apm T3 latched onto `c_api.cpp:352` mirror invariant ("mirrors r_bridge.cpp:628-657"); the floor-literal mismatch was real but had NO observable effect on chebyshev output because IPM Newton overwrites warm-start state within few iterations.
- **Empirical verification gate is MANDATORY**: any proposed fix MUST be empirically demonstrated to reduce the observed parity_bench chebyshev max_abs_diff (2.047e-3 baseline) BEFORE the patch commits. T4 of this Epic enforces this strictly.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Locate the FIRST-divergent field in `st` state at the moment of `lbw::chebyshev_ipm(st, w, delta)` invocation, comparing R bypass path (r_bridge.cpp) vs Py c_api path (c_api.cpp:rk_calibrate).
- [ ] Empirical winner determined per Tier-1 metric across ≥3 DGPs OR (if `st` state PARITIES post-investigation but output STILL diverges) escalate to chebyshev-internal Epic.
- [ ] Minimal patch applied to wrapper-layer (allowed: r_bridge.cpp, c_api.cpp, _bindings.cpp, harvest.R, _harvest.py).
- [ ] **Empirical verification at T4 commit gate**: parity_bench chebyshev max_abs_diff < 1e-4 post-fix on stepstone fulldata.
- [ ] benchmarks/parity_compare.R reports identical_1e4=YES for chebyshev (15/15 total).
- [ ] tests/test_parity_weights.py extended with stepstone-style chebyshev parity test at rtol=1e-6.
- [ ] testthat + pytest pass.

## Context & Background

Post-yh0l + post-2apm baseline (master c7c628a):
- chebyshev parity_bench (stepstone fulldata, n=1.58M, K=9, max_weight=5, max_iterations=3000): max_abs_diff=2.047e-3, mean 5.1e-6.
- Both langs hit no_conv at iter cap=500 (chebyshev's effective inner cap).
- Identical Tier-1 metrics: mkl=0.7456, max_err=0.1394, chi2=6.615e4.
- Cause (a) param packing RULED OUT (2apm T1: 0/37 mismatches).
- Cause (b) C-binding default fallback RULED OUT (same as a).
- Cause (c) shared-code drift CONFIRMED (2apm T2: d_st=d_mt=2.047e-3 → BLAS thread count irrelevant).
- Cause (d) BLAS thread nondet ELIMINATED.
- 2apm T4 fix (c_api.cpp:359 floor 50→5) is real but unrelated to observed divergence.

Architecture:
- R: harvest.R → .Call C_rk_calibrate → r_bridge.cpp:177-360 (manual rk_state init via build_cell_table; manual ieppa warm-start at r_bridge.cpp:628-657; lbw::chebyshev_ipm).
- Py: harvest() → pybind11 calibrate → _bindings.cpp → c_api.cpp:rk_calibrate (manual rk_state init via estimate_M_cell or build_cell_table; manual ieppa warm-start at c_api.cpp:351-367; lbw::chebyshev_ipm).
- Both eventually call SAME `lbw::chebyshev_ipm(st, w, delta)` C++ entry point.
- The DIVERGENCE must be in the `st`/`w`/`delta` state INPUT to chebyshev_ipm.

Likely-candidate `st` fields differing at IPM entry (per memory + code structure):
- `st.alm.capacity_mu` (yh0l harmonized for ieppa_soft; chebyshev may have separate path).
- `st.lambda_A` / `st.lambda_B` initial values (ref-cat j=0 driver per memory chebyshev-ref-cat-convention).
- Cell aggregation (cells, n_per_cell, sum_per_cell) — order may differ if R-factor and Py-Categorical encode levels differently.
- `delta` initial vector — computed from initial `w` against targets; depends on cell aggregation.
- Warm-start output `w_warm`/`delta_warm` from ieppa pre-IPM step.

## Mechanism
1. T1 instrument both wrappers with one-shot `st` state dump immediately before `lbw::chebyshev_ipm` call. Wrapper-only (allowed). Run on small + medium + stepstone fulldata; compare dumps.
2. T2 field-by-field diff: locate first-divergent field at IPM entry. Categorize: setup divergence (cell agg / lambda / capacity_mu) OR warm-start output divergence OR `st` parities (cause-internal-IPM).
3. T3 trace which wrapper-layer code produces the differentiated field. Multi-DGP empirical winner-determination IF ambiguous; otherwise direct attribution from dump comparison + code reading.
4. T4 apply minimal harmonization patch with **STRICT EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION GATE**: rerun parity_bench chebyshev BEFORE committing; max_abs_diff MUST drop from 2.047e-3 to <1e-4. If not, escalate (this fix is wrong; back out, refine T2/T3).
5. T5 stepstone-style chebyshev parity test at rtol=1e-6 with red-green proof.
6. T6 verify 15/15 identical via parity_compare.R + testthat + pytest.

## Forbidden
- Changing C++ solver core (chebyshev.cpp IPM Newton logic; calib_dispatch.hpp; cell_table.hpp; cell_table.cpp logic edits — read-only inspection OK).
- Permanent verbose-trace instrumentation in solver core. T1 dump goes in r_bridge.cpp + c_api.cpp ONLY (wrapper layer; allowed). Dump may be left as a `verbose >= 3` block for future use OR removed; either is acceptable.
- API widening.
- Tol-bump.
- Refactoring around the bug.
- **Crucially: declaring victory via code-comment authority WITHOUT empirical parity_bench verification.** 2apm's lesson.

## Authority
Empirical: parity_bench chebyshev max_abs_diff drop from 2.047e-3 to <1e-4 IS the gate. Tier-1 metrics + multi-DGP confirm winner side. Code-comment authority is supportive evidence, NOT a substitute for empirical verification.

## Audit Strategy
- One-shot `st` state dump pre-IPM in BOTH wrappers (T1).
- Dump-diff identifies first-divergent field (T2).
- Code-line attribution via wrapper-layer reading (T3).
- Empirical parity_bench rerun pre-commit (T4 gate).
- rtol=1e-6 regression test (T5) on STEPSTONE-ANALOG fixture (not the 2apm correlated K=9 fixture which is weight-invariant to warm-start floor; need a fixture that triggers the residual cause).
- testthat + pytest + parity_compare (T6).

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Single-thread per memory feedback_subagent_explicit_file_staging. Each task atomic; output schema strict TOON valid YAML.

## Tasks (children)
T1 instrument & dump `st` state pre-IPM (r_bridge.cpp + c_api.cpp wrapper instrumentation)
T2 dump-diff: locate first-divergent field at IPM entry
T3 code-line attribution + multi-DGP winner-determination if needed
T4 minimal harmonization patch + STRICT EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION GATE (parity_bench rerun pre-commit)
T5 stepstone-analog regression test rtol=1e-6 (red-green confirmed)
T6 verify 15/15 identical via parity_compare.R + testthat + pytest
close_reason: Epic ESCALATED. Empirical-verification gate worked. capacity_mu fix attempt produced 0 drop. T2-redux revealed w_warm hash mismatch (small/fulldata Cat D) + medium bitwise-match (Cat E). Cause beyond 8u2y wrapper-only scope. Open child leafblower-8u2y.7 filed for solver-internal trace with relaxed forbidden list. T1 parity_dump.hpp + T2-redux full-vector-hash methodology committed as reusable diagnostic infra. parity_bench chebyshev unchanged at 2.047e-3 baseline. 4 commits on branch 8u2y-investigate.

title: T2 chebyshev parity: single-thread reproduction + IPM trajectory diff
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Determine whether chebyshev R-Py divergence is cause (d) BLAS thread nondeterminism, cause (c) shared-code numerical drift, or cause (e) AMBIGUOUS (intermediate residual), by re-running parity bench at OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 AND capturing per-iter IPM Newton trajectory at verbose=2.
* **Why:** Most likely cause is BLAS thread nondeterminism (chebyshev uses BLAS-3 dpotrf via calib_linalg). Single-thread test discriminates. If divergence vanishes → cause (d) → no code fix; doc-only. If fully persists → cause (c) → continue T3 forensic. If partially shrinks → cause (e) AMBIGUOUS → controlled thread-sweep + HALT to user with evidence.
* **Reference Data:**
  - src/chebyshev.cpp verbose>=2 emission: ONE diagnostic at iter==0 only (line ~419: schur_nu/dnu/r_nu Phase A). NO per-IPM-iter residual emission.
  - src/calib_linalg.cpp:150 F77_CALL(dpotrf) — chebyshev's BLAS-3 hot path.
  - benchmarks/parity_bench.{R,py} + parity_compare.R existing.
  - Memory gotcha-openblas-thread-oversubscription.
  - Memory chebyshev-ipm-homotopy: chebyshev_ipm called ONCE per harvest().
* **Philosophy:** Single-thread test gates whole investigation. Three explicit branches, no grey zone.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** T1 short_circuit (likely false). Repo HEAD post-yh0l. Existing parity_bench scripts.
* **Format:** Single-thread parity rerun + (if cause c only) attempted IPM trajectory parse with documented HALT if logs insufficient.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Skip-condition** | If T1.short_circuit==true: T2 SKIPPED. (Unlikely.) |
| **Single-thread enforcement** | Sys.setenv at top of any new R script; os.environ.setdefault BEFORE numpy import in any new Py script. Set OMP+OPENBLAS+MKL trio. |
| **Three-way cause attribution (explicit thresholds, no gap)** | Compute single-thread chebyshev max_abs_diff (`d_st`) and default-thread max_abs_diff (`d_mt`, baseline 2.05e-3). Branch: (d) if `d_st < 1e-9` AND `d_mt > 1e-3` (full BLAS attribution); (c) if `d_st > 1e-3` (single-thread cannot reduce → shared-code drift); (e) AMBIGUOUS otherwise (1e-9 <= d_st <= 1e-3 — partial reduction). |
| **Ambiguous-cause (e) gate** | Run NREPS=5 single-thread reruns AND NREPS=5 default-thread reruns. Compute per-rep variance. If single-thread d_st STABLE across reps (variance < 1e-12) AND non-zero (>1e-9) → cause (e1) deterministic-residual cause-c attributable; treat as cause c with reduced-magnitude divergence. If single-thread d_st unstable across reps (variance > 1e-9) → cause (e2) BLAS lingering nondet; treat as cause d with stricter NEWS note (env vars insufficient on this machine; recommend BLAS_THREAD_AFFINITY pinning). |
| **No instrumentation** | verbose>=2 in src/chebyshev.cpp emits only iter-0 diagnostic. Per-IPM-iter trajectory IS NOT AVAILABLE. T2 cause-c branch SKIPS the trajectory-parse step (no log to parse) and instead writes benchmarks/2apm/trajectory_unavailable.toon documenting the gap, transferring forensic to T3 code-attribution by static reading of chebyshev.cpp + calib_linalg.cpp invocation order. |
| **Boundary** | All new files under benchmarks/2apm/. NO src/ edits. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Inspect src/chebyshev.cpp: confirm verbose>=2 emits only iter==0 diagnostic. Document.
2. Re-run parity_bench at single-thread:
   - `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 Rscript benchmarks/parity_bench.R` (sequential).
   - `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 python benchmarks/parity_bench.py`.
   - `Rscript benchmarks/parity_compare.R`.
   - Save combined CSV to benchmarks/2apm/parity_singlethread.csv.
3. Compute d_st (chebyshev row, single-thread) and d_mt (default-thread, from existing parity_bench_combined.csv or rerun).
4. Three-way branch:
   - cause (d): d_st < 1e-9 AND d_mt > 1e-3. Write benchmarks/2apm/cause.toon with cause=d.
   - cause (c): d_st > 1e-3. Trajectory unavailable per chebyshev verbose=2 limitation. Write benchmarks/2apm/cause.toon with cause=c + benchmarks/2apm/trajectory_unavailable.toon documenting forensic must proceed via static code reading in T3.
   - cause (e) AMBIGUOUS: 1e-9 <= d_st <= 1e-3. Run NREPS=5 single-thread reruns. Compute d_st_variance.
5. Cause-(e) sub-attribution:
   - (e1) variance < 1e-12 AND d_st > 1e-9: stable residual → treat as cause c (proceed T3 cause-c branch with reduced-magnitude divergence noted).
   - (e2) variance > 1e-9: BLAS nondet lingering despite OMP=1 → treat as cause d (proceed T3 cause-d branch with stricter NEWS note).
6. Write benchmarks/2apm/cause.toon documenting the resolved cause + evidence.

## V. Output Schema (Strict TOON, valid YAML)
```yaml
task_id: T2_2apm
success: bool
data:
  status: SKIPPED | DONE_CAUSE_C | DONE_CAUSE_D | DONE_CAUSE_E1_RESOLVED_C | DONE_CAUSE_E2_RESOLVED_D | HALTED_INSUFFICIENT_LOGS
  d_st: float                      # single-thread chebyshev max_abs_diff
  d_mt: float                      # default-thread chebyshev max_abs_diff
  d_st_variance: float | null      # cause (e) only, NREPS=5
  cause_resolved: c | d            # final attribution after sub-resolution
  singlethread_csv: benchmarks/2apm/parity_singlethread.csv
  trajectory_csv: <path|null>      # null because chebyshev verbose=2 lacks per-iter trajectory
  trajectory_unavailable_note: <path|null>
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- Single-thread parity rerun completed; chebyshev d_st recorded.
- Cause attributed to (c) or (d) WITH NO grey zone (e1/e2 sub-resolution applied if needed).
- cause.toon valid YAML.
- No solver edits.
- If verbose=2 trajectory unavailable: documented in trajectory_unavailable_note path.
close_reason: T2 single-thread cause attribution complete. d_st = d_mt = 2.047e-3 (BLAS thread count IRRELEVANT). Cause = (c) shared-code numerical drift; both R and Py reach DIFFERENT deterministic fixed points within iter cap regardless of thread count. cause (d) BLAS nondet ELIMINATED. trajectory_unavailable.toon documents src/chebyshev.cpp:419 verbose>=2 emits only at iter==0 (no per-IPM-iter trajectory available without forbidden src/ instrumentation). Forensic transferred to T3 static code reading. Commit bdd5d8a.

title: Harmonize chebyshev R-Python weight parity (better algo wins)
description:
# Epic: Harmonize chebyshev R-Python weight parity

## Goal
Identify root cause of chebyshev R/Python weight divergence (max|w_R-w_Py|=2.05e-3, mean 5.1e-6) at iter cap=500, identical Tier-1 metrics (mkl=0.7456, max_err=0.1394, chi2=6.615e4). Apply minimal fix to bring 15/15 parity to identical_1e4=YES.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Root cause identified — one of (a) param mismatch, (b) C++ binding default-fallback, (c) shared-code numerical drift, (d) BLAS thread nondeterminism.
- [ ] Multi-DGP empirical winner determined OR cause (d) confirmed (test single-thread; if divergence vanishes → cause d → no code fix; doc-only).
- [ ] If cause (a)(b)(c): minimal patch on loser side; testthat + pytest pass.
- [ ] If cause (d): NEWS.md guidance only, no code change. Document thread-pinning recommendation.
- [ ] benchmarks/parity_compare.R reports identical_1e4=YES for chebyshev (post-fix) — OR documented exception with justification.
- [ ] tests/test_parity_weights.py extended with chebyshev case at rtol matching cause severity.

## Context & Background
Parity bench 2026-05-08 (post-yh0l) on stepstone fulldata, n=1.58M, max_weight=5, tol=1e-4:
  R:  chebyshev iter=500, mkl=0.7456, max_err=0.1394, status=no_conv (iter cap)
  Py: chebyshev iter=500, mkl=0.7456, max_err=0.1394, status=no_conv (iter cap)
  max|w_R - w_Py| = 2.047e-3, mean|w_R - w_Py| = 5.1e-6.

Same algorithm, same data, same convergence path (both hit iter cap). All loss metrics tie to 4 sig figs. Only weight VECTORS differ — distinct numerically near-equivalent fixed points within max_iter.

Both languages call src/chebyshev.cpp (IPM Newton + LP) via .Call C_rk_calibrate (R) / pybind11 calibrate (Py). Per memory `chebyshev-ipm-homotopy-chebyshev-ipm-never-uses-homotopy`: chebyshev_ipm is called ONCE per harvest(). Per memory `chebyshev-ref-cat-convention-change-is-behavioral-not`: ref-cat j=0 (matches newton_kl) drives full_to_red, dlambda_A_red, dlambda_B_red, dX_A, dX_B per IPM iter.

Suspected causes:
- (d) BLAS thread nondeterminism — chebyshev uses BLAS-3 (dpotrf, dsyevd). Per memory `gotcha-openblas-thread-oversubscription`: thread variance can produce 2-9× timing diff AND (relevant here) numerical drift in BLAS-3 reductions.
- (c) Shared-code numerical drift — same C++, same params, but different float-op order from R vs Py invocation context.
- (b) C++ binding default-fallback — params dict missing key on Py side defaulting to a value differing from R's -1.0 sentinel.

Cause (d) most plausible. Single-thread test is the discriminating diagnostic.

## Mechanism
1. T1 boundary-param audit (chebyshev-specific 37-arg dump; identify any mismatched defaults).
2. T2 single-thread reproduction + IPM trajectory diff at verbose=2; if single-thread reproduces divergence → cause (c). If not → cause (d).
3. T3 multi-DGP winner-determination + code-line attribution (if cause (c)) OR document BLAS recommendation (if cause (d)).
4. T4 harmonize loser→winner OR doc-only patch.
5. T5 parity test (chebyshev rtol calibrated by cause severity).
6. T6 verify via parity_compare.R + testthat + pytest.

## Forbidden
- Changing C++ solver core (src/chebyshev.cpp IPM Newton logic, src/calib_dispatch.hpp, src/cell_table.hpp).
- API widening.
- Refactoring around the bug.
- Skipping NEWS.md / docstring updates when behavior or guidance changes.
- Choosing winner from single DGP (multi-DGP required if cause c).

## Authority
Empirical winner on Tier-1 metrics across ≥3 DGPs IS the spec. Tier-1 ties → use weight_kl + max_abs_diff stability across reps as tiebreaker. If cause (d): authority is documented BLAS-thread-pinning recommendation (no winner; both sides correct).

## Audit Strategy
- Param dump via diagnostic Rscript / Python script (T1, reuse benchmarks/yh0l/dump_params_*.R/.py templates with method='chebyshev').
- Verbose=2 IPM Newton trajectory parse (T2; check src/chebyshev.cpp for verbose>=2 emission lines).
- Single-thread vs multi-thread parity_bench rerun (T2 disambiguates cause c vs d).
- Multi-DGP if cause c (T3); doc-only if cause d.
- Both builds + both test suites + benchmark re-run (T4 + T6).

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Single-thread; numerical-claim verification by orchestrator (memory feedback_subagent_explicit_file_staging). Each task atomic; output schema strict TOON valid YAML.

## Tasks (children)
T1 boundary-param audit (chebyshev)
T2 single-thread + trajectory diff (cause c vs d disambiguation)
T3 multi-DGP winner + code-line attribution OR BLAS doc-only recommendation
T4 harmonize port OR doc-only patch + tests
T5 parity test
T6 verify via parity_compare.R + testthat + pytest

T5 reframed as mirror-invariant CONTRACT test (asserts R/Py share floor literal at HEAD; not a behavioral red-green). Preliminary boundary scan:
  - R sends 37 positional .Call args; capacity_penalty/alm_penalty as -1.0 sentinel when NULL.
  - Python OMITS capacity_penalty/alm_penalty keys when None — defers to C++ binding default-fallback.
  - inner/outer_max_iter equal in both for ieppa_soft (not the cause).

## Mechanism
1. T1 boundary-param audit (where do the args / defaults differ?).
2. T2 trajectory bisect (at which iter does the metric diverge? confirms divergence is real, not FP-noise).
3. T3 multi-DGP winner-determination + code-path identification (which side runs the better algorithm and what is the exact code-level differentiator?).
4. T4 harmonize: port winner-side algorithm/default to loser side. May touch wrappers (R/harvest.R, _harvest.py) and/or param-unpack bindings (r_bridge.cpp, _bindings.cpp) — NEVER C++ solver core.
5. T5 parity test (rtol=1e-6, red-green confirmed).
6. T6 re-run parity_compare + testthat + pytest, verify 15/15 identical, multi-DGP winner unchanged after harmonization.

## Forbidden
- Changing C++ solver core (ieppa.cpp, calib_dispatch.hpp solver logic).
- Adding verbose-trace instrumentation to C++ (verbose=2 already emits).
- Bumping tol to mask divergence.
- Widening user-facing API.
- Refactoring around the bug.
- Skipping NEWS.md / docstring updates when behavior changes.
- Choosing winner from single DGP — multi-DGP required (≥3 DGPs).

## Authority
Empirical winner on Tier-1 metrics across ≥3 DGPs IS the spec for harmonization. Existing spec docs (docs/superpowers/specs/*) and roxygen/docstring docs are secondary; if winner conflicts with documented behavior, AMEND the spec doc per memory feedback_spec_amendment_append (APPEND v_next; preserve prior versions verbatim).

## Audit Strategy
- Param dump via diagnostic Rscript / Python script (T1).
- Verbose=2 stdout trajectory parse (T2; conditional skip if T1 short-circuits).
- Multi-DGP winner-determination harness (T3): stepstone fulldata + 2 small synthetic DGPs (e.g. existing benchmarks/stepstone_bench_data.parquet + new small fixture sized to ≥20 outer iters).
- Both builds + both test suites + benchmark re-run (T4 + T6).
- rtol=1e-6 parity test (T5).

## Sub-Agent Strategy
Single-thread; numerical-claim verification by orchestrator (memory feedback_subagent_explicit_file_staging — no parallel implementation, explicit file lists, no `git add -A`). Each task atomic; output schema strict TOON.

## Tasks (children)
T1 boundary-param audit (with short-circuit)
T2 trajectory bisect (skip-able)
T3 multi-DGP winner-determination + code-path identification
T4 harmonize: port winner→loser + docs + tests
T5 parity test (rtol=1e-6)
T6 verify via parity_compare.R + testthat + pytest
notes: Epic complete. T1-T6 closed. ieppa_soft R-Python harmonized: max_abs_diff dropped from 0.58 to 2.1e-13 (machine epsilon); R iter count dropped from 220 to 90 matching Py-winner. Root cause: capacity_mu computed via build_cell_table.capacity_mu_auto (R bypass path) ≈ 0.073 vs c_api estimate_M_cell-based 1.0 (Py path) for K>8 fulldata. Fix: r_bridge.cpp now uses estimate_M_cell matching c_api. Branch: yh0l-harmonize. 9 commits.

Single-file fix (src/r_bridge.cpp use estimate_M_cell matching c_api path). ieppa_soft byte-identical R-Python at tol=1e-4 (max_abs_diff 0.58 → 2.1e-13, R 220 iter → 90 iter matching Py). 14/15 parity methods identical (chebyshev = leafblower-2apm). testthat 557/557 + pytest 10/10 pass. T-M (leafblower-6ycz.1.13) rescue-rate handoff observations under T-M-fixed algorithm:

Tested raking 2-stage post T-M fix (Stage-1 coarse-only + cell-aggregate multiplier) on §8 v0/v1/v2/v3 DGPs:

| DGP                                            | n_seeds | ok @1e-3 | dominant failure mode |
|------------------------------------------------|---------|----------|------------------------|
| §8 v3 (make_rescue_dgp, N=80 K=6)             | 30      | 0/30 (0%) | INFEAS (30/30)         |
| §8 v1 approx (K=9 skew 0.95 max_weight=2)     | 20      | 0/20 (0%) | BUDGET (20/20)         |
| §8 v2 approx (make_stress_dgp, N=80 K=6)      | 30      | 0/30 (0%) | INFEAS (30/30)         |

Conclusion: T-M algorithmic correctness fix does NOT auto-rescue these DGPs. The pre-fix bug (Stage-1 secretly fitting all margins) was masking algorithmic correctness but did not produce passing rescue-rates either. T-W's seed-sweep gate remains DGP-bound (consistent with prior deferral in leafblower-6ycz.1.12). The §8 DGPs need re-search of (K, N, cardinality, joint, target) parameter space, not algorithmic changes.

Multiplier-aggregate test (test-stage1-multiplier-aggregate.R) AND coarse-only test (test-stage1-coarse-only.R) demonstrate the algorithm now correctly implements spec §6 Strategy A. Method tested: raking only (other 2 solvers expected similar pattern; INFEAS dominates on N=80 chain-correlated DGPs because Stage-2 within-cell on near-empty fine cells cannot satisfy 50/50 targets). All other R + Python tests PASS post-fix.

# T-F: Wire RAKING through 2-stage with rescue + parity tests + roxygen docs
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** Pass `lbw::raking_within_cell` callable into `outer_iterate_strategy_a()` (T-C) for `mode="refine"`; for `mode="exact"`, call within-cell direct after Strategy B validator (T-D) passes. **Forbidden:** copy-pasting partition / inheritance / outer-loop logic into raking.cpp. **Audit:** rescue test + parity + 9 adversarial fixtures + roxygen.

## I. Context & Objective

* **Why:** RAKING = highest-priority P1 target (most-used method in survey practice; 0/0 NaN failure mode is the canonical pain point).
* **Reference Data:** Spec §8 P1 sparse-cell rescue test (DGP fully specified); spec §6 disturbance strategies; `src/raking.cpp` (lambda `[&]` capture rule per CLAUDE.md — declare bool guards BEFORE `auto F_eval = [&]`); `R/harvest.R` (44.7K) for roxygen pattern.
* **Philosophy:** Raking is cyclic ratio updates; within-cell raking is just a sub-problem with cell-restricted observations. ~50 lines of glue at most.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Read `src/raking.cpp` for the existing inner sweep (find `F_eval` lambda or per-margin sweep). Read `R/harvest.R` for existing list-arg roxygen pattern (`@param convergence`, `@param sor`).
* **Format:** C++ glue + R roxygen + tests.

## III. Constraints & Guards

| **Logic** | Glue only — no new raking math. Within-cell call = existing `raking_inner_sweep(...)` with `obs_indices = partition.obs_indices_by_cell[cell_id]` slice. Lambda `[&]` capture rule: declare any new bool guards BEFORE the `[&]` lambda definition (CLAUDE.md, bug re-introduced). |

| **Boundary** | TOUCH: `src/raking.cpp` (~50 lines glue), `R/harvest.R` (roxygen + arg passthrough), `tests/testthat/test-2stage-raking.R`. DO NOT touch sinkhorn / greenkhorn / logit / greg files. |
| **Tone** | Roxygen comments terse, one-line `@param` description; one example, one `@seealso` cross-link. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. In `src/raking.cpp` solver entry: dispatch on `params.hierarchical_enabled`:
   - `enabled == 0`: existing single-stage path (unchanged) — branch-coverage assertion in test confirms early-out.
   - `enabled == 1 && mode == 0 (refine)`: build partition (T-B), define within-cell lambda `[&](weights, partition, cell_id) { raking_inner_sweep(weights, obs_indices_by_cell[cell_id], ...); }`, call `outer_iterate_strategy_a(lambda, ...)` from T-C. Apply `apply_sparse_inheritance` for sparse cells (already handled inside outer loop). Final Σw=n gate.
   - `enabled == 1 && mode == 1 (exact)`: validator (T-D) already passed at entry. Stage 1 raking on coarse margins, then per-cell raking on fine margins. NO outer loop. Final Σw=n gate.
2. Lambda capture rule (CLAUDE.md): if any new bool guards are introduced for the within-cell case, declare BEFORE the `[&]` lambda definition. (`[&]` captures by reference at definition site, not call site.)
3. In `R/harvest.R`: add `hierarchical = NULL` param. Pass through to `.Call` site (T-A wired the slot). Add roxygen `@param hierarchical` describing the list and 5 sub-args. Add an `@examples` block with a tiny K=4 sparse case.

title: T-E: Add hierarchical input-validation table
description:
# T-E: Add hierarchical input-validation table to validate_calibrate_inputs
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** Extend `lbw::validate_calibrate_inputs` (`r_bridge.cpp:311`) with all 9 hierarchical-arg checks per spec §9. Enforce BEFORE partition build / cell allocation. **Forbidden:** validation in solver dispatch (must be pre-allocation). **Audit:** unit test for each row of §9 table returns expected error code.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: T-A merged. Out: validator extension at `r_bridge.cpp:311` covering all 9 rows of spec §9, plus `hierarchical_coarse_mask` length check (per Security iter-2 suggestion).
* **Why:** Heap-DoS prevention, footgun reduction. Catches all hierarchical-arg misuse before any allocation.
* **Reference Data:** Spec §9 Input Validation Contract (table). `r_bridge.cpp:311` `lbw::validate_calibrate_inputs`. `validation.hpp`, `calib_validate.cpp` for existing pattern.
* **Philosophy:** Validate ALL hierarchical args before any partition build, before any cell allocation, before solver dispatch. Each check returns BADARG with named-arg diagnostic.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** `rk_params_t.hierarchical_*` fields (post-T-A), original SEXPs at validate-entry.
* **Format:** C++ function body extension; no new entry point.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Order matters: (1) `hierarchical_enabled` short-circuit, (2) coarse_mask length, (3) coarse_mask non-empty + proper subset, (4) min_cell_n bounds, (5) mode enum, (6) outer_tol finite + positive + ≥ machine_eps × N, (7) outer_iterations 1..1e4, (8) algorithm × mode constraint (P2 forces exact; P1 accepts both), (9) bounds_mode unit × hierarchical → BADARG, (10) cell-count cap (preliminary partition), (11) Strategy B orthogonality (delegated to T-D validator). |
| **Format** | Each BADARG returns `result.message` ≤ 256 chars naming the arg(s) and computed bounds. |
| **Boundary** | TOUCH ONLY: `src/r_bridge.cpp` validate function body. DO NOT touch solver dispatch or .cpp solvers. |
| **Tone** | Terse. Messages actionable, e.g., `"min_cell_n=0 invalid; must satisfy 1 <= min_cell_n <= N=10000"`. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Add early-out: if `params.hierarchical_enabled == 0`: skip all hierarchical checks.
2. Validate `hierarchical_coarse_mask` length == K: if not, BADARG `"hierarchical_coarse_mask length=<got> != K=<expected>"`.
3. Validate `popcount(coarse_mask) > 0` (non-empty): BADARG `"hierarchical: coarse_margins is empty"`.
4. Validate `popcount(coarse_mask) < K` (proper subset): BADARG `"hierarchical: coarse_margins == margins; nothing to refine — disable hierarchical"`.
5. Validate `1 <= min_cell_n <= N`: BADARG with computed bounds.
6. Special case `min_cell_n > N`: emit warning (not BADARG); will degenerate to single-stage; do NOT silently fall through (warning is user-visible).
7. Validate `mode ∈ {0, 1}`: BADARG enum.
8. Validate `outer_tol`: `isfinite && > 0 && >= machine_eps * N`.
9. Validate `outer_iterations`: `1 <= n <= 10000`.
10. Validate algorithm × mode: if `algorithm ∈ {LOGIT, GREG} && mode == 0 (refine)`: BADARG `"algorithm '<name>' cannot use mode='refine' (Newton re-factor cost prohibitive); pass mode='exact' and ensure orthogonal coarse/fine split"`.
11. Validate `bounds_mode == RK_BOUNDS_UNIT && hierarchical_enabled`: BADARG `"bounds_mode='unit' incompatible with hierarchical calibration; use bounds_mode='cell' or disable hierarchical"`.
12. Cell-count preliminary check: cells_estimated = product of (cat_counts[k] for k in coarse_mask). If `cells_estimated > min(N / min_cell_n, 100000)`: BADARG with cells_estimated + suggested action ("increase min_cell_n or reduce coarse_margins cardinality").
13. Strategy B orthogonality: if `mode == 1`, delegate to `validate_orthogonal_split` from T-D. Propagate diagnostic.
14. Add `tests/testthat/test-2stage-validation.R`: one assert per §9 row + the new coarse_mask length row.
15. `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`; existing tests pass.
16. Check guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{
  "task_id": "T-E",
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "files_modified": ["src/r_bridge.cpp"],
    "checks_added": 12,
    "tests_added": ["test-2stage-validation.R"],
    "cell_count_cap": 100000,
    "outer_iterations_cap": 10000
  },
  "error_log": null
}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] All 12 checks fire BEFORE partition build / cell allocation (audit: read code, no allocation calls before validator return)
- [ ] Each diagnostic names the failing arg and computed bounds
- [ ] Cell-count cap is the LAST check before allocation; partition build short-circuits if cap exceeded (no hash-table grows past 100000)
- [ ] `bounds_mode='unit' × hierarchical` BADARG fires at validate entry, not in solver
- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` succeeds; existing tests pass
- [ ] No hallucination

Verify by grep for 'Rf_warning' in src/r_bridge.cpp for existing usage. (2) Cell-count cap constant — reference LBW_MAX_HIER_CELLS from T-B's #define, do NOT inline literal 100000.

title: T-D: Implement Strategy B orthogonality validator
description:
# T-D: Implement Strategy B orthogonality validator
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** O(N · K_fine) hash-based detector validates that every fine-margin level lies wholly within exactly one coarse cell. **Forbidden:** heuristic equality on margin names; rank-based check. **Audit:** unit test on contrived non-orthogonal split returns BADARG with offending margin/cells named.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: T-A merged, partition helpers from T-B. Out: `lbw::validate_orthogonal_split()` returning `OK | BADARG_WITH_DIAG`, called from `lbw::validate_calibrate_inputs` at `r_bridge.cpp:311` (extension lives there per spec §6).
* **Why:** P2 methods (LOGIT, GREG) cannot afford Strategy A outer iteration. P2 default = `"exact"` mode requires orthogonal coarse/fine split for correctness — disturbance-free by construction. P1 also accepts `mode="exact"` as opt-in.
* **Reference Data:** Spec §6 "Strategy B — Orthogonality contract", spec §9 validation table row "Strategy B orthogonality". `r_bridge.cpp:311` (`lbw::validate_calibrate_inputs`).
* **Philosophy:** Deterministic — no ε-tolerance, no rank-deficiency proxy. Pass iff the set of coarse-cell IDs spanned by each (fine_margin, level) pair has cardinality ≤ 1.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Coarse-margin mask (length K), fine-margin set (complement of coarse), full design data (group_ids, cat_counts).
* **Format:** C++ function returning `int status` plus `std::string diagnostic` message.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Hash key: `(fine_margin_idx, fine_level_value)`. Hash value: `unordered_set<int>` of coarse cell IDs touched. Pass: every value-set has size ≤ 1. Fail: emit diagnostic naming first offending fine-margin name + first offending fine-level value + the coarse cell IDs spanned. |
| **Format** | Diagnostic message ≤ 256 chars (matches `rk_result_t.message` length). |
| **Boundary** | TOUCH ONLY: `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` (or `src/hierarchical.hpp`) for the validator function; `src/r_bridge.cpp:311` to call it from `validate_calibrate_inputs`. DO NOT modify solver files. |
| **Tone** | Terse. Diagnostic message must be actionable — name the margin and the cells. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Implement `lbw::validate_orthogonal_split(group_ids, cat_counts, coarse_mask, K, N) -> std::pair<int, std::string>`:
   - Build coarse cell IDs per obs using `build_cell_partition` from T-B (or inline if dependency cycle)
   - For each fine margin `f` (where `coarse_mask[f] == 0`):
     - For each obs `i ∈ [0, N)`: insert `coarse_cell_id[i]` into `level_to_cells[(f, group_ids[i, f])]`
   - For each `(f, ℓ)` key: if `level_to_cells[(f, ℓ)].size() > 1`: return `(RK_ERR_BADARG, "Fine margin '<name>' level '<value>' spans coarse cells {<cell_ids>}; require orthogonal split")`
   - Else return `(RK_OK, "")`
2. Call from `lbw::validate_calibrate_inputs` (`r_bridge.cpp:311`): when `params.hierarchical_enabled && params.hierarchical_mode == 1` (exact), invoke validator. On BADARG, propagate diagnostic via `result.message`.
3. Cost: O(N · K_fine) — verify by counting outer iterations in test (no nested N loops).
4. Add `tests/testthat/test-2stage-strategy-b.R`: (a) orthogonal split passes (e.g., coarse=age_bracket, fine=age_year nested); (b) non-orthogonal split fails with diagnostic naming offender (e.g., coarse=region, fine=urbanicity which spans regions); (c) mode="exact" with orthogonal split AND P1 method works.
5. `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`; existing tests pass.
6. Check guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)

description:
# T-B: Add shared 2-stage infrastructure to calib_dispatch.hpp
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** Pure helpers — partition build + sparse mask + inheritance + Σw=n gate — in `calib_dispatch.hpp`. **Forbidden:** per-solver fragmentation; touching solver `.cpp` files. **Audit:** unit tests on each helper at `tests/testthat/test-2stage-shared.R` (or C++ equivalent if existing pattern uses it).

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: T-A merged. Out: 4 helper functions in `lbw` namespace exported from `calib_dispatch.hpp`, each unit-tested in isolation.
* **Why:** All 5 P1+P2 methods share this infrastructure. Per-method duplication would re-trigger the WU-B dedup that `calib_dispatch.hpp` was built to eliminate.
* **Reference Data:** Spec §5 "Architectural Placement (mandatory)", §6 "Stage-2 Disturbance Strategy", §6 "Σw=n composition invariant", §6 "Sparse-cell inheritance semantics". Existing `solver_setup_ct`, `build_cell_table`, `aggregate_to_margin` in `cell_table.hpp` / `calib_dispatch.hpp` for style reference.
* **Philosophy:** Helpers must be pure (no global state); all inputs explicit; Σw=n gate is mandatory and uniform across methods.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Read `src/calib_dispatch.hpp`, `src/cell_table.hpp` for existing helper patterns. Spec §6.
* **Format:** C++17 header (`lbw` namespace).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | All helpers `inline` or `static` per existing convention. No heap allocation in tight inner loops — use stack or pre-sized vectors. Σw=n tolerance: `\|Σw − N\| < N · 1e-12`. |
| **Format** | C++ snake_case match existing helpers (`build_cell_table`, `resolve_hi`). Templated where existing helpers are. |
| **Boundary** | TOUCH ONLY: `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` (or split into `src/hierarchical.hpp` if total adds >300 lines). New helpers stay in `lbw` namespace. DO NOT touch solver `.cpp`. |
| **Tone** | C++ terse. No comment narration except WHY for non-obvious math. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. `lbw::build_cell_partition(group_ids, cat_counts, coarse_mask, K) -> CellPartition`: groups observations by joint coarse-margin profile. Returns `CellPartition { cell_id_per_obs (size N), n_per_cell (size K_cells), obs_indices_by_cell (CSR-like) }`. O(N) hash-based.
2. `lbw::build_sparse_mask(partition, min_cell_n) -> SparseMask`: returns `vector<bool> is_sparse_cell` (size K_cells). Cells with `n_per_cell < min_cell_n` flagged.
3. `lbw::apply_sparse_inheritance(weights, partition, sparse_mask, stage1_multipliers)`: in-place — for obs in sparse cells, set `weights[i] = w_init[i] * stage1_multipliers[cell_id_per_obs[i]]`. Per spec §6 "unscaled Stage-1 multiplier inherit" (NOT cell-total preservation).
4. `lbw::enforce_sigmaw_eq_n(weights, N) -> bool`: assert `\|Σw − N\| < N · 1e-12`; return false on violation. CALLED BY SOLVER AT EXIT, NOT BY OUTER LOOP. Outer loop may temporarily violate.
5. Add `EnableExactInherit` template flag if needed for future cell-total-preservation variant (NO behavior change in this WU — flag default false).
6. Cell-count cap check: `if (K_cells > min(N / min_cell_n, 100000)) return RK_ERR_BADARG`. Located inside `build_cell_partition` BEFORE allocating `obs_indices_by_cell` (heap-DoS guard per spec §9 + Security review).
7. Add `tests/testthat/test-2stage-shared.R` (or C++ unit tests if existing convention) covering: empty partition, single-cell partition, all-sparse partition, dense partition, cap-overflow (BADARG), Σw=n gate accept/reject.
8. `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`; verify no regression.
9. Check guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{
  "task_id": "T-B",
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "header_modified": "src/calib_dispatch.hpp | src/hierarchical.hpp",
    "loc_added": "<int>",
    "helpers_added": ["build_cell_partition", "build_sparse_mask", "apply_sparse_inheritance", "enforce_sigmaw_eq_n"],
    "unit_tests_added": "<int>",
    "cell_cap_constant": 100000
  },
  "error_log": null
}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] All 4 helpers compile under `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`
- [ ] Per-helper unit tests pass; cell-count cap triggers BADARG with diagnostic
- [ ] No solver `.cpp` files touched (audit: `git diff --stat src/*.cpp` shows zero changes)
- [ ] Σw=n gate is the ONLY post-solver normalization (audit: grep solver .cpp for `weights /=`, `weights *=` outside solver inner loop returns no new matches)
- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` succeeds; existing tests still pass
- [ ] No hallucination
notes: EXECUTION ITER 1 FAILED — orchestrator validation found UB crash. Subagent reported success but R aborts on test-2stage-shared.R 'cap fires when K_cells > N/min_cell_n'. ROOT CAUSE: C_hier_partition_probe (src/r_bridge.cpp:1045-1064) does NOT guard the rc != RK_OK branch. When build_cell_partition returns BADARG (cap fired), it executes 'out = {}' clearing all output fields including cell_id_per_obs. The probe then unconditionally Rf_allocVector(INTSXP, n) and memcpy's n ints from part.cell_id_per_obs.data() — but cell_id_per_obs has size 0 → memcpy reads invalid memory → crash. C_hier_inherit_probe (line 1100) handles this correctly with an early-return on rc != RK_OK. FIX: mirror the inherit-probe early-return pattern in partition-probe; on rc != RK_OK return list(rc=rc) with names=c('rc') only, skipping cio/npc allocations. Re-run test suite to confirm.

title: T-C: Implement Strategy A outer-iteration loop
description:
# T-C: Implement Strategy A outer-iteration loop in calib_dispatch.hpp
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** Outer loop alternates Stage 1 ↔ Stage 2 until margin residual < `outer_tol` or `outer_iterations` exhausted. Reuses existing `CalibConvergenceCfg`. **Forbidden:** new convergence-config struct; calling solver-specific code from outer loop. **Audit:** unit test BUDGET-exit returns last-iterate weights + `converged=false`.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: T-A + T-B merged. Out: `lbw::outer_iterate_strategy_a()` template function that takes a per-method "calibrate within cell" lambda and orchestrates the outer loop.
* **Why:** P1 default mode is `"refine"` — outer iteration is required to repair Stage-2 disturbance of Stage-1 margins. Strategy A code is method-agnostic when the within-cell solve is parameterized as a callable.
* **Reference Data:** Spec §6 "Strategy A — Outer iteration (P1 default)". `CalibConvergenceCfg` definition and `check_convergence()` in existing convergence module (grep `pct_tol`, `absolute_tol`, `metric`, `rule` — likely `convergence.hpp` or inside `calib_dispatch.hpp`). `kErrCheckInterval` in `calib_dispatch.hpp` for best-iterate selection cadence.
* **Philosophy:** Keep outer loop solver-agnostic. Per-method code passes a `WithinCellSolve` callable; outer loop never references RAKING/SINKHORN/GREENKHORN.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** Read existing convergence helpers; existing best-iterate selection (`select_metric(sraa_cfg.metric, cm)`).
* **Format:** C++ template function in `lbw` namespace.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Reuse `CalibConvergenceCfg` (metric, rule, pct_tol, absolute_tol). New params `outer_tol` shadows `absolute_tol` at outer level only; `outer_iterations` shadows `max_iterations` at outer level only. Best-iterate uses `select_metric(sraa_cfg.metric, cm)` at `kErrCheckInterval` (NOT `errRp`). |
| **Format** | Template `template<class WithinCellSolve>`; callable signature `(weights, partition, cell_id) -> rk_status_t`. Outer loop returns `OuterResult { status, iterations_used, residual_final, last_iterate_weights }`. |
| **Boundary** | `src/calib_dispatch.hpp` (or `src/hierarchical.hpp` if T-B split it). DO NOT modify solver files. |
| **Tone** | Terse. WHY-only comments where the FP/iteration semantics are non-obvious. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Define `lbw::OuterResult` struct: `int status; int iterations_used; double residual_final; vector<double> last_iterate_weights;`.
2. Implement `lbw::outer_iterate_strategy_a(WithinCellSolve fn, ...)`:
   - Stage 1: full-data calibrate to coarse margins using `fn(weights, FULL_PARTITION, NO_CELL_ID)`
   - Loop `iter ∈ [0, outer_iterations)`:
     - Stage 2: for each non-sparse cell, call `fn(weights, partition, cell_id)`
     - For sparse cells: call `apply_sparse_inheritance(weights, partition, sparse_mask, stage1_multipliers)`
     - Compute coarse-margin residual
     - At `iter % kErrCheckInterval == 0`: track best-iterate via `select_metric()`
     - If residual < outer_tol: SET status=RK_OK, break
     - Else: re-run Stage 1 to repair coarse-margin sums
3. On loop exhaustion: SET status=RK_ERR_BUDGET, populate `last_iterate_weights` (NOT best-iterate — best-iterate is for diagnostic only; user gets last actual iterate per spec §6).
4. Set `res.base.outer_iterations_used = iterations_used`, `res.base.outer_residual_final = residual_final`, `res.base.hierarchical_levels_used = 2`.
5. After successful exit (RK_OK), call `enforce_sigmaw_eq_n(weights, N)` from T-B. On gate failure: solver-internal error (NOT BUDGET). This is the ONLY mandatory final-pass normalization gate.
6. Add `tests/testthat/test-2stage-strategy-a.R`: synthetic 2-margin DGP, mock within-cell solve = identity. Verify (a) RK_OK on convergent, (b) BUDGET exit + last-iterate weights + converged=false on contrived non-convergent, (c) Σw=n preserved at exit.
7. `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`; existing tests still pass.
8. Check guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{
  "task_id": "T-C",
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "files_modified": ["src/calib_dispatch.hpp"],
    "loc_added": "<int>",
    "best_iterate_metric_helper": "select_metric",
    "k_err_check_interval_used": "<int>",
    "tests_added": ["test-2stage-strategy-a.R"]
  },
  "error_log": null
}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] BUDGET-exit returns last-iterate weights with `converged = false` flag in result
- [ ] Best-iterate diagnostic uses `select_metric(sraa_cfg.metric, cm)` at `kErrCheckInterval` (audit: grep for this exact pattern in new code)
- [ ] No solver `.cpp` modified (still just dispatch infra)
- [ ] Σw=n gate fires on RK_OK exit; outer loop intermediate states NOT gated
- [ ] `outer_tol` / `outer_iterations` shadow `absolute_tol` / `max_iterations` at outer level only — no parallel convergence-config struct introduced (audit: grep for new typedef/struct named `OuterConvergenceCfg` returns zero matches)
- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` succeeds; existing tests pass
- [ ] No hallucination
notes: PLAN-REVIEW iter 1: Clarify BUDGET-exit semantics — TWO weight vectors are tracked: (a) BEST-ITERATE (selected via select_metric(sraa_cfg.metric, cm) at kErrCheckInterval) — DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, exposed in res.base for instrumentation; (b) LAST-ITERATE (final outer-loop weights) — RETURNED to caller as the result's main weight vector. On RK_ERR_BUDGET, caller gets last-iterate weights + converged=false; spec §6 explicit. Best-iterate is for downstream debugging tools, NOT for swap-on-budget.

title: P1: 2-stage hierarchical for biproportional family (RAKING/SINKHORN/GREENKHORN)
description:
# Epic: P1 — Two-Stage Hierarchical Calibration (Biproportional Family)

## Goal
Ship 2-stage hierarchical calibration (coarse-then-fine with `min_cell_n` threshold) for RAKING / SINKHORN / GREENKHORN, eliminating 0/0 / log(0) failure mode on K≥8 sparse high-D survey designs (ESS, ANES, BLS CPS, marketing panels).

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All 5 P1+P2 methods build with `hierarchical = NULL` early-out (single-stage parity at rtol=1e-12)
- [ ] RAKING/SINKHORN/GREENKHORN 2-stage rescue test: 100% convergence on K=9 N=10000 Dirichlet(0.1) DGP, seed-sweep 1..100, with margin residual ≤ 1e-4
- [ ] Same DGP single-stage path: ≥80% NaN/INFEAS failure rate (proves rescue is real)
- [ ] Strategy A BUDGET-exit contract honored: last-iterate weights + `converged=false` on `outer_iterations` exhaustion
- [ ] Strategy B orthogonality validator: O(N·K_fine) hash-based, BADARG with offender names on non-orthogonal split
- [ ] Σw=n composition invariant: `|Σw − N| < N · 1e-12` at solver exit
- [ ] Stepstone regression gate: single-stage path matches commit `8146894` within 1e-8; new fixture `stepstone_2stage_reference.rds` for 2-stage path
- [ ] Python parity at rtol=1e-6 + integer-exact outer iter count on all R tests
- [ ] CI runtime budget: ≤ +30s testthat, ≤ +60s pytest

## Context & Background

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-2-stage-hierarchical-method-assessment-design.md` (commit `6b97310` + rev1, gate-approved iter 2 by all 5 agents: PM, Architect, Designer, Security, CTO)

**Issue:** `leafblower-6ycz`

**Project North Star:** leafblower R/Python/C++ calibration weighting library. R primary surface = `harvest()` (NOT `calibrate()`). Single C++17 core in `src/`. Algorithm enum `rk_algorithm_t` populated; slot 2 reserved (LBFGSB removed).

**Hard constraints:**
- C_rk_calibrate arity is currently 37 at `r_bridge.cpp:129`. ABI extension precedent: bump arity + bump `EXPECTED_RK_PARAMS_BYTES` (homotopy/SOR/ridge_lambda all did this). NO "reserved-flag mechanism" exists; `_reserved_lbfgs_m` is dead padding.
- `CalibResult` fields live at `res.base.*` (post-ztid.4 migration).
- `calib_dispatch.hpp` is the canonical home for shared solver helpers — DO NOT fragment 2-stage logic across solver files.
- Σw=n enforced at solver exit; NEVER post-normalize (silently invalidates `bounds_mode="unit"` water-fill clamps).
- `bounds_mode="unit"` × hierarchical → BADARG at preprocessing, before partition build / memory allocation.
- Best-iterate selection at `kErrCheckInterval` MUST use `select_metric(sraa_cfg.metric, cm)` (NOT `errRp` fast proxy — bug re-introduced twice).
- `-O3` lives in `OPT_FLAGS`, not `PKG_CXXFLAGS` (CRAN portability).
- Lambda `[&]` in raking.cpp: declare bool guards BEFORE `auto F_eval = [&]` definition.

**Out of scope (this epic):** P2 methods (LOGIT, GREG); excluded methods (CHEBYSHEV, NEWTON_KL, IEPPA, IEPPA_SOFT); auto-detection of coarse/fine split; 3+ stage; cell-total-preservation inheritance variant.

## Sub-Agent Strategy

**Mechanism:** 2-stage hierarchical raking via outer iteration (Strategy A "refine" mode) or orthogonality contract (Strategy B "exact" mode). Shared infrastructure in `calib_dispatch.hpp` (`build_cell_partition`, `apply_sparse_inheritance`, `outer_iterate`, `validate_orthogonal_split`, `enforce_sigmaw_eq_n`). Per-method code limited to within-cell solver call (~50 lines).

**Forbidden:**
- Per-solver duplication of partition / inheritance / outer-loop logic
- Adding new algorithm enum slot for 2-stage (it's a wrapper, not an algorithm)
- Post-normalizing weights to satisfy Σw=n
- Bundling tasks: each WU = own beads ticket per CLAUDE.md
- Skipping hooks via `--no-verify`
- Documentation as standalone WU (bundle docs WITH each method WU per CLAUDE.md §8)

**Audit:**
- Spy: per-method ablation tests with seed-sweep 1..100 verify rescue rate
- Spy: branch-coverage assertion confirms `hierarchical = NULL` path takes early-out
- Mock: synthetic DGP via `r-synthetic-test-data` patterns; only stepstone_2stage_reference persisted as `.rds` golden
- Adversarial fixtures: 9 in §8 (n=1, n_min-1, all-sparse, single-coarse, BUDGET-exit, zero-target, duplicate-keys, NA-key, Strategy-B violation)

**Global guard:** every WU MUST pass `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` before proceeding. Definition of Done = R tests pass + Python parity tests pass + stepstone benchmark shows no regression.

**Task handoff:** use `bd ready` after each WU close to surface unblocked successors.

**Adversarial review:** 3-reviewer `/plan-review-gate` (Feasibility, Completeness, Scope & Alignment) MUST pass before WU implementation begins. After P1 ships, run `/self-reflect` to commit learnings.
notes: Reopening for code-review remediation wave (12 tickets .1.13-.1.24). Original close at commit 03c84a5 was premature — code review found Stage-1 algorithm deviates from spec §6 (calibrates ALL margins instead of coarse-only) across all 3 P1 solvers. P1 ships CORRECTLY only after this wave.

Spec §8 amendment trail v1-v5 preserved as historical record. T-L (.1.12) closed under T-W disposition. R 753 PASS / 0 FAIL. title: fix(R): malloc_trim() before .Call in r_bridge.cpp — reduce heap fragmentation causing 63% solver cache miss excess
description:
## I. Objective
konh investigation proved R's solver generates 1.63x more LLC cache misses than Python's
for identical C code and data. Root cause: R's heap is fragmented after loading packages
(arrow, jsonlite, leafblower), causing solver's internal C++ allocations (CellTable,
CalibState, best-iterate buffers) to land in scattered memory → poor spatial locality.

## II. Test
In src/r_bridge.cpp, add before rk_calibrate() call:
  malloc_trim(0);  // compact glibc heap, return free pages to OS
Then run perf stat comparison:
  R_solver_cache_misses = R_total - R_preprocessing
  Compare to baseline: 747.9M (current) vs target: closer to 457.5M (Python)

## III. Guards
- malloc_trim(0) is glibc-specific — add #ifdef __GLIBC__ guard
- malloc_trim() pauses the program briefly (compact heap = walk free list)
- Only call ONCE per .Call, not per iteration
- Do NOT call in the solver loop itself

## IV. DoD
- [ ] malloc_trim(0) added with __GLIBC__ guard in r_bridge.cpp before rk_calibrate
- [ ] perf stat shows R solver cache misses drop by >20% (from 748M toward 458M)
- [ ] Rscript -e 'devtools::test()' passes
- [ ] Timing improvement measured and reported
close_reason: malloc_trim(0) added under __GLIBC__ guard. ieppa 9079→5374ms (-41%), chebyshev -57%, greg -54%. R/Python gap: 96%→16% slower. Tests: FAIL 0 | PASS 557.

title: investigate(R): phase-isolated cache-miss profiling — solver vs preprocessing split
description:
## I. Objective
Revised root cause from x2b3/so85/kptj investigations: R preprocessing (SEXP allocation for
factor encoding) likely generates ~75% of the 291M extra cache misses vs Python, not the solver.
Confirm by measuring cache misses ONLY during .Call(rk_calibrate) vs ONLY during preprocessing.

## II. Input
Evidence from x2b3 perf stat (whole-process):
  R: 789.4M cache misses, 36.9B cycles, 8.9s
  Py: 497.6M cache misses, 28.3B cycles, 7.0s
  
R preprocessing: as.integer(factor(col)) - 1L × 9 margins = ~170MB SEXP allocs (hot, all touched)
Python preprocessing: pd.Categorical × 9 = ~57MB numpy allocs (C-level, single pass)
Hypothesis: preprocessing churn accounts for ~200M of the 291M extra cache misses

## III. Logic
Phase-isolate using one of:
  Option A: perf_event_open ENABLE/DISABLE syscalls in r_bridge.cpp around rk_calibrate
  Option B: perf record --call-graph dwarf + perf report to attribute cache misses to functions
  Option C: Simpler — run perf stat on JUST the preprocessing step (before harvest()) and JUST
             the solver (minimal harvest() with max_iterations=1 after pre-encoding group_ids)

Option C is most tractable without C code changes.

## IV. DoD
- [ ] Cache miss count attributed to (a) preprocessing phase and (b) solver phase for both R and Python
- [ ] Ratio R_preprocessing_misses / Py_preprocessing_misses (expect ~3x)
- [ ] Ratio R_solver_misses / Py_solver_misses (expect ~1x if preprocessing is the bottleneck)
- [ ] If preprocessing IS the dominant source: file fix ticket for C-level categorical encoder
      in r_bridge.cpp to replace as.integer(factor()) - 1L chain
close_reason: Root cause: solver itself generates 1.63x more cache misses in R vs Python, NOT preprocessing (1.04x ratio). Cause: R heap fragmentation → solver internal allocations scattered → poor spatial locality. Fix: arena allocator or malloc_trim() before .Call.

comments.author: Dennis Alexis Valin Dittrich
comments.text:
## Phase-isolated perf stat results (2026-05-06)

### Preprocessing only (exit before harvest()/calibrate())
R:  41.5M cache-misses, 26.8B instr, 11.7B cycles, 3.12s
Py: 40.1M cache-misses, 22.8B instr, 10.3B cycles, 2.95s
Ratio: 1.04x cache-misses — NEARLY IDENTICAL

### Solver phase (subtraction: x2b3 total - preprocessing)
R_solver:  789.4M - 41.5M = 747.9M cache-misses, 45.0B instr, 25.2B cycles
Py_solver: 497.6M - 40.1M = 457.5M cache-misses, 42.2B instr, 18.0B cycles
Ratio: 1.63x cache-misses — THE SOLVER IS THE SOURCE

### Verdict
- Preprocessing SEXP churn hypothesis: REJECTED (1.04x ratio is noise)
- Solver itself generates 63% more cache misses in R (1.63x)
- Same C code, same data, same flags -> root cause: heap fragmentation
- R's allocator (after loading arrow/jsonlite/leafblower) is more fragmented
- Solver internal allocations (CellTable, CalibState, etc.) land in scattered memory
- Worse spatial locality -> more LLC misses accessing solver's own buffers

Contiguous arena allocator for solver-internal buffers in rk_calibrate():

- Option B: mmap(MAP_ANONYMOUS) contiguous block passed to solver as arena
- Option C: jemalloc/tcmalloc as R's allocator (requires LD_PRELOAD)

title: fix(python): release GIL around rk_calibrate() in _bindings.cpp
description:
## I. Objective

title: fix(bench): run R and Python allmethod benchmarks sequentially to avoid OpenBLAS contention
description:
## I. Objective
R and Python benchmark scripts currently run concurrently (launched independently), causing

thrash catastrophically under contention; timing variance is 2-9x.

IN: benchmarks/  OUT: benchmarks/run_allmethod.sh (sequential runner)

Files: benchmarks/allmethod_bench.R, benchmarks/allmethod_bench.py
Evidence: run1 R newton_kl=107s, run2=50s, run3=22s — same 7 iters, same results, pure load variance.
Root cause: OpenBLAS defaults to ncore threads per process; R+Py concurrent = 32 threads on 16 cores.

## III. Guards
- Do NOT restrict OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS — full thread count is correct for single-process runs
- Script must run R first, then Python (or vice versa, documented order)
- Must capture both outputs and save CSVs as before
- No changes to allmethod_bench.R or allmethod_bench.py themselves

## IV. Logic
Create benchmarks/run_allmethod.sh:
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -e
  echo '=== R benchmark ===' && Rscript benchmarks/allmethod_bench.R
  echo '=== Python benchmark ===' && python benchmarks/allmethod_bench.py

Simple. 3 lines. No threading flags.

## V. Schema

Existing CSVs: benchmarks/results/allmethod_bench_{r,py}.csv (unchanged paths)

title: perf(python): profile iterative-method bridge overhead — why Python 2x slower than R after diagnostic fix
description:
## I. Objective
After leafblower-q795 removes the sparseness diagnostic regression (~34s), Python iterative methods
will still be ~15-20s vs R 5-10s for same iter counts (ieppa 550 iters: Python ~20s, R 9.9s).

title: feat(newton_kl,greg): ridge regularization — Tikhonov penalty on dual to handle cell-level sparseness
description: P2: Add optional ridge_lambda parameter (Tikhonov regularization). Adds tau*||lambda||^2 to KL/chi2 dual objective, stabilizing near-singular X'DX (cell-level sparseness). User controls ridge_lambda (default 0 = off). Statistical basis: Bethlehem 2002, Guggemos-Tille 2010. Bias = O(tau), vanishes as tau->0. Affects: newton_kl (Hessian modification), greg (closed-form lambda update). Does NOT affect ieppa/raking (KL projection, different structure). Separate from min/max_weight — ridge handles Hessian ill-conditioning; bounds handle weight extremes.

title: perf(newton_kl): incremental u_trial in backtracking avoids O(n*K) per step
description:
## I. Objective
Replace O(n*K) eval_dual(lam_trial) call inside line-search backtracking with incremental update: u_trial = u + (lam_trial - lam) * indicator, avoiding full obs-level re-scan per backtrack step.

## II. Input
File: src/newton_calib.cpp
Lines: ~663 (eval_dual call inside backtracking/line-search loop)
Context: u_i = sum_k lambda_k * x_ik. When lam_trial = lam + alpha*delta, u_trial_i = u_i + alpha * sum_k delta_k * x_ik = u_i + alpha * (delta dot indicator_i).

## III. Guards
- Incremental update only valid for linear parameterization of u
- Must verify: u_trial[i] == u_base[i] + alpha * grad_u[i] for each obs i
- Requires pre-computing grad_u[i] = sum_k delta[k] * x_ik once before backtracking

## IV. Logic
1. Read newton_calib.cpp lines 650-680 (backtracking loop)

title: doc(ieppa): document Σ-weight drift bound after renorm+clamp in unit-mode post-loop
description: After water-fill + gbib.1 renorm + iw2a clamp, Σweights may be slightly < n in the pathological case where all weights are pinned to bounds (n_free==0) and renorm > 1. close_reason: 6-line drift-bound comment added at ieppa.cpp:380. Commit 19a2e89.
