title: logit convergence threshold tol_abs*n is bucket-size-blind (rare small-target categories may over/under-converge at large n)
description:
## What
The logit OK-convergence gate (logit_calib.cpp, eb79.22) uses `max_abs_resid <= st.tol_abs * n` where max_abs_resid is the max ABSOLUTE-count margin residual and the threshold scales with TOTAL n, not with the target count of the specific (k,j) bucket. For large n with rare small-target categories (e.g. target count ~10 at n~1.58M), an absolute slack of tol_abs*n (~1.58 at stepstone scale) is a large RELATIVE error in that rare bucket while looking negligible in aggregate; conversely for small n the threshold can demand near-machine-zero on every bucket.

## Why
Pre-existing design property of the eb79.16 absolute-residual clause, NOT introduced by eb79.22 (eb79.22 only made that clause SUFFICIENT rather than AND-ed with the plateau rule). agy flagged it during eb79.22 review (Q5, confidence 70, pattern-level not a proven failure). Correctness-relevant for large-n calibration with skewed/rare margins.

## How
- Consider a per-bucket RELATIVE tolerance: converged when for every (k,j), |target_kj*n - S_kj| <= tol_abs * max(target_kj*n, floor) (relative to the bucket's own target count), instead of a single tol_abs*n absolute bound.
- Or a hybrid abs+rel bound (max(tol_abs*n_bucket, tol_rel*target_kj*n)).
- Verify against stepstone (n~1.58M skewed margins) that rare buckets converge to the intended relative accuracy; add a large-n skewed-rare-category fixture.
- Cross-check the same threshold form in other solvers' gates (raking/oris/greg) for consistency.
close_reason: WONTFIX / not-a-demonstrated-bug (verify + agy conf 75). The gate 'max_abs_resid <= tol_abs*n' is equivalent to 'max PROPORTION residual <= tol_abs' — a self-consistent, standard survey-calibration (Deville-Särndal) tolerance. Bucket-size-blindness is inherent to any single global proportion tolerance, expected behavior of that norm, NOT a coding defect. EVIDENCE: solver converges TIGHTER than the threshold in all tested cases (n=500..1e5, rare 0.01%-2%: rel error 7e-6..1e-5, far below the ~1% rare-bucket slack the threshold algebra permits) — the coupled Newton drives all margins together (shared normal-equations solve) so it never stops one bucket loose while another is tight. No real false-OK case could be constructed. A bucket-relative tolerance is NOT low-risk: changes convergence semantics for every bucket across every solver sharing the tol_abs*n idiom (sinkhorn/oris/chebyshev) + introduces div-by-zero on zero-target buckets. Re-open only if a real config is found where the gate certifies OK with a materially-wrong rare bucket (agy B2 flagged an untested pathological near-collinear-margin-isolating-a-rare-bucket case as theoretically possible but unreached).

title: logit misclassifies genuinely-infeasible tight-bounds problems as BUDGET (status=4) instead of INFEAS/STALL
description:
# leafblower-eb79.23: logit structural-feasibility pre-check — report INFEAS (not BUDGET) when bounds cannot meet the margins
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** One-shot O(M·K) pre-loop interval-sum feasibility pre-check (Σ[L_cell,U_cell] per bucket vs target·n) → RK_ERR_INFEAS with a margin-named message, before the Newton loop.
**Forbidden:** running the Newton loop first then reclassifying (wasteful + the current best_resid→BUDGET/STALL heuristic can't distinguish structural infeasibility); flagging BORDERLINE-feasible problems as INFEAS (FP-safe strict comparison only); touching eb79.22 gate / eb79.18 warm-start / eb79.20 metrics / verified oris·ieppa·chebyshev math.
**Audit:** structurally-infeasible fixture → status=2 with the offending margin named; feasible + near-feasible-but-reachable → NOT flagged; R/Python parity (shared core).

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: a logit problem where per-cell bounds [L_cell,U_cell] cannot satisfy some SINGLE margin (target outside the achievable [Σ L_cell, Σ U_cell] interval for that bucket). Out: return RK_ERR_INFEAS (status=2) with a message naming the margin, BEFORE the Newton loop — instead of iterating to the 50-cap and mis-reporting RK_ERR_BUDGET ("increase max_iterations", which never helps on infeasible input).
* **SCOPE (necessary, not sufficient — HONEST):** the per-margin interval-sum is a NECESSARY feasibility condition per margin in isolation: violating it PROVES infeasibility (no false positives — cells are independently box-clampable, so a single margin's achievable mass is exactly [Σ L_cell, Σ U_cell]). It is NOT SUFFICIENT: a problem where every margin is individually reachable but the JOINT/coupled system (cells shared across margins) is infeasible is NOT caught here and correctly still falls through to the existing BUDGET/STALL path (unchanged). This ticket does not attempt full joint (transportation-polytope) feasibility — that would need an LP, out of scope for a P3.
* **Why:** Follow-up to eb79.22 (which fixed OK-detection). On genuinely-infeasible tight-bounds problems logit currently returns status=4 BUDGET (prescription: raise iterations — futile) instead of INFEAS (prescription: relax bounds). Verified case (n=400 seed=41, 4× collinear a targets .4/.6, mw=1.5): margin a=y has ~80 obs, max mass = 1.5·80 = 120 < target 0.6·400 = 240 ⇒ structurally infeasible; currently status=4/50/abs_resid≈97.
* **Reference Data (verified 2026-07-02):**
  - Post-loop status (logit_calib.cpp:398-405): `status = (best_resid < initial_resid*0.999) ? RK_ERR_BUDGET : RK_ERR_STALL` — no INFEAS path; structural infeasibility falls to BUDGET/STALL.
  - Variables in scope after logit_calib.cpp:75 (before the warm-start block at :116): `L_cell`, `U_cell` (per-cell mass bounds = min_weight·n_c … max_weight·n_c), `cells_per_cat[k][j]` (cell indices per bucket), `st.targets[k][j]` (proportion target), `st.n`, `K`, `st.cat_counts[k]`.
  - CONVENTION (adapt, do not reinvent): sinkhorn returns RK_ERR_INFEAS via bisect_capacity_fast (sinkhorn.cpp:164-165); oris tracks structural_infeas_pairs = buckets with cells.empty() AND target>0 (oris.cpp:265,282) and the saturated interval [Σ L_cell, Σ U_cell] (oris.cpp:1037). This pre-check is the closed-form interval version.
  - harvest.R:644-646: status==2 (RK_ERR_INFEAS) ⇒ stop("leafblower: <message>") — R surfaces the actual res.message naming the margin (correct UX).
  - **Python PRE-EXISTING BUG (must fix for parity): _harvest.py:609-613 raises a HARDCODED sinkhorn-specific string on status==2 ("...persistent empty cell with positive target (detected after 5 consecutive outer iterations)") and NEVER reads result_dict["message"] — so the margin-named message can NOT reach Python callers, and the message is misleading for ANY non-sinkhorn infeasible result. Contrast status==3 (_harvest.py:614-615) which correctly uses result_dict["message"]. Fix: make status==2 surface result_dict["message"] (matching status==3 + R harvest.R:645), falling back to the generic string only when message is empty.**
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** In-function C++ state after solver_setup_ct + build_cells_per_cat (logit_calib.cpp:~76). Reads L_cell/U_cell/cells_per_cat/st.targets/st.n. No new allocation beyond scalars.
* **Format:** C++; no new public API; no ABI change (uses the existing RK_ERR_INFEAS status + res.message).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | For each margin k∈[0,K) and category j∈[0,cat_counts[k]): min_mass = Σ_{c∈cells_per_cat[k][j]} L_cell[c]; max_mass = Σ U_cell[c]; target_count = st.targets[k][j]·st.n. Flag INFEAS iff `target_count > max_mass·(1+kFeasEps)` OR `target_count < min_mass·(1−kFeasEps)` — STRICT outside-interval with an FP margin kFeasEps (≈1e-9) so borderline-feasible problems are NOT flagged. ALSO flag a bucket with NO cells (cells_per_cat[k][j] empty) AND target_count>0 (structural, matches oris). On the FIRST flag: set res.base.status=RK_ERR_INFEAS, snprintf a message naming margin k / category j and the achievable interval, `return res`. Do NOT enter the Newton loop. |
| **Format** | Confined to a pre-loop block inserted at logit_calib.cpp:~76 (after build_cells_per_cat, before the Layer-2 warm-start at :116). No change to the loop, gate (eb79.22), warm-start (eb79.18), or metrics (eb79.20). |
| **Boundary** | src/logit_calib.cpp pre-loop block + python/leafblower/_harvest.py (status==2 message surfacing, :609-613) + tests (tests/testthat/test-logit.R, python/leafblower/test_python.py). No new TU. Do NOT change the sinkhorn/oris INFEAS behavior (only the Python message-surfacing for status==2, which applies to all solvers uniformly and is strictly more correct). |
| **Tone** | Match file style; cite eb79.23 + the sinkhorn/oris convention. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. **WU1a (IMPLEMENT — C++):** insert the O(M·K) interval-sum pre-check at logit_calib.cpp:~76 per the Guards. Message form: "logit: infeasible — margin <k> category <j>: target <target_count> outside achievable [<min_mass>, <max_mass>] (relax bounds)".
1b. **WU1b (IMPLEMENT — Python message parity):** in _harvest.py:609-613 change the status==2 branch to raise result_dict["message"] (matching status==3 at :614-615), falling back to the current generic string only when message is empty. This surfaces the C++-emitted margin-named message to Python callers and fixes the pre-existing sinkhorn-hardcoded misleading message for ALL solvers' infeasible results.
2. **WU2 (TEST):** R + Python:
   (a) structurally-infeasible (mw=1.5 4×collinear skewed, the verified case) ⇒ harvest stop/status=2 with a margin-named message (was BUDGET/50).
   (b) FEASIBLE (mw=3 or loose) ⇒ status unaffected (0), NOT flagged.
   (c) BORDERLINE / exactly-at-corner feasible (target_count == max_mass) ⇒ NOT flagged INFEAS (kFeasEps guard); still solvable/BUDGET as before. Concrete fixture: 2 obs in a category, min_weight=0.1 max_weight=2, target = 2*2/n_total chosen so target_count == 2*max_weight EXACTLY.
   (d) R/Python parity: the infeasible fixture ⇒ status=2 in BOTH, AND the Python error message now contains the logit margin-named text (NOT the sinkhorn hardcoded string) — asserts WU1b.
3. **WU3 (REGRESSION):** eb79.16/18/20/22 logit tests pass; full R suite + pytest green.
4. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: leafblower-eb79.23
success: bool
data:
  mechanism: "pre-loop interval-sum feasibility check -> RK_ERR_INFEAS"
  infeasible_mw15_status_before: 4
  infeasible_mw15_status_after: 2
  message_names_margin: bool
```

title: logit default convergence gate never fires OK on cleanly-converging (collinear) feasible problems -> spurious BUDGET at 50-iter cap
description:
# leafblower-eb79.22: logit scalar-μ Levenberg — replace the fixed residual-proportional ridge with gain-ratio adaptive damping
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** Persistent scalar Levenberg damping μ, gain-ratio adapted, REPLACING the fixed `eps_ldlt = max_b/kMaxDeltaZ` formula in the logit main Newton loop. ~30-40 LOC. NO TSVD/Steihaug, NO step-cap change, NO eigendecomposition.
**Forbidden:** full LM+TSVD+Steihaug port (over-engineering — logit's Cholesky+ridge does not need the dual-KL null-space machinery); changing the step-norm cap kMaxDeltaZ (trace shows it does NOT bind); "bit-identical" common-path claims (μ≠0 perturbs the direction); tuning μ constants to a fixture; touching eb79.18 warm-start / eb79.16 gate / eb79.20 metrics / verified oris·ieppa·chebyshev math.
**Audit:** per-iter μ/ρ trace on the repro; iter-count + weight + status comparison LM-vs-baseline on a panel INCLUDING the mw=1.5 near-infeasible case; common path no-worse; stepstone logit no regression; R/Python parity.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: ill-conditioned / tight-bounds / rank-deficient logit problems that converge but exhaust the 50-Newton-iter cap (status=4 BUDGET). Out: logit converges (status=0) in far fewer iters via a self-tuning scalar Levenberg μ, with the common well-conditioned path no-worse.
* **Why:** Deferred alt (C) from eb79.18, evidence-backed (eb79.18 WU4 + this ticket's WU1). eb79.18 fixed the iter-0 collinear STALL; this addresses the SEPARATE main-loop convergence-SPEED limit. Philosophy: SOTA + fastest + MINIMAL.
* **Reference Data (root cause CORRECTED + trace-verified 2026-07-02):**
  - Logit main step (logit_calib.cpp): build N=A·diag(D_eff)·A^T (:203-loop); ridge `eps_ldlt=max(1e-10, max_b_mag/kMaxDeltaZ)` (:283); cholesky_factor+solve → δλ; step-norm cap `alpha=min(1, kMaxDeltaZ/max_δz)`, kMaxDeltaZ=2.0 (:112); Armijo kMaxHalvings=10 (:313); Newton cap `min(50, st.inner_max_iter)` (:91).
  - ROOT CAUSE (per-iter trace, mw=3 repro, gate-demanded): the step-norm cap is NOT the throttle — after iter1 `alpha0=1` (max_δz=0.02-0.9 ≪ 2, cap never binds). The THROTTLE is the residual-proportional ridge `eps_ldlt=max_b/2` (trace 72.5→5.2→0.19: shrinks WITH the residual so it never relaxes relative to the signal, over-damping every step; Armijo then halves alpha 1→0.25 when the damped step still overshoots). Slow-but-monotone: abs_resid 10.48(it10)→1.32(it25)→0.35(it50).
  - FIX: replace the FIXED ridge formula with a PERSISTENT scalar μ updated by a gain ratio ρ = (‖b‖²−‖b_trial‖²)/predicted_reduction. ρ>0.75 ⇒ μ/=3 (relax → bigger next step); ρ<0.25 ⇒ μ*=10; else keep. eps used in cholesky_factor becomes μ (scaled to the diagonal), not max_b/2. The loop ALREADY computes resid_sq_0 (:266) and resid_sq_trial (Armijo) — reuse them.
  - GAIN-RATIO PITFALL (agy Q4, code-traceable): D_eff floors at kDeffFloor=1e-6·range (:227); near saturation the floor INFLATES assumed local sensitivity, so a Jacobian-based predicted_reduction overstates → ρ underestimated exactly in the tight-bounds regime → μ would grow (re-damp) where it should relax. MITIGATION: base predicted_reduction on the LINEAR MODEL reduction δλᵀ(2b − Nδλ) using the SAME N/b actually solved (self-consistent), OR exclude floored cells from the predicted sum. Do NOT use the true-sigmoid derivative for prediction.
  - μ-UPDATE scheme = the simple newton_calib.cpp rule (newton_calib.cpp:724-742: ρ>0.75→μ/3, ρ<0.25→μ*10), NOT the Nielsen cubic (resolve the earlier plan's contradiction — use the codebase's existing, proven scheme).
  - NO result-field surfacing of μ: the r_bridge `lm_mu_final` slot is fed from newton_calib's OWN struct (LogitCalibResult has no such field; the logit r_bridge branch never assigns it). Surfacing μ for logit would need a NEW LogitCalibResult field + wiring (NOT zero-ABI) ⇒ OUT OF SCOPE. μ stays loop-local; verified via a temporary trace (WU3), not a persisted field.
* **Alternatives Considered (CLAUDE.md mandate):**
  - **(A) Scalar-μ gain-ratio Levenberg on eps_ldlt — CHOSEN.** ~30-40 LOC; targets the trace-confirmed throttle (the ridge); reuses resid_sq already computed; simple proven μ-rule from newton_calib. No new dependency, no ABI change, no step-cap change.
  - **(B) Full LM + dsyevd TSVD + Steihaug trust-region port (the earlier plan) — REJECTED as over-engineering (agy Q3 conf 72).** The eigendecomposition/null-space machinery in newton_calib exists for the dual KL Hessian; logit's Cholesky+scalar-ridge only needs the scalar-μ swap. Disproportionate for P3 + higher regression risk.
  - **(C) Raise/configure the 50-iter Newton cap — REJECTED as the fix.** Trace shows steps are heavily DAMPED (not merely capped), so more iters would reach tol but wall-time stays poor (200+ iters); fails "fastest". May ADD a configurable cap as a cheap safety net (default unchanged), not the fix.
  - **(D) INFEAS misclassification (tight-bounds genuinely-infeasible → BUDGET, e.g. mw=1.5 abs_resid=97) — SEPARATE ticket, BUT add a cheap feasibility pre-check here to CLASSIFY the mw=1.5 case (interval-sum Σ[L_cell,U_cell] vs each margin target) so WU1 can prove whether it is infeasible (out of scope) or a damped plateau (in scope). The FIX for D stays separate; the CLASSIFICATION happens here to justify the split.**
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** logit main Newton loop, src/logit_calib.cpp:~203-345 (per-iter build-N / ridge / solve / Armijo). Loop-local μ state. No LAPACK beyond what's present.
* **Format:** C++ in-function; no new public API; result struct unchanged; μ stays loop-local (no field surfaced).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Persistent `double lm_mu` (init 1e-3, matching newton_calib.cpp:100 seed; bounds μ_min=1e-12, μ_max=1e12 from newton_calib.cpp:98-99). **N and b are destroyed in place** by `cholesky_factor_inplace(N,...)` (:284, overwrites N with LDLT) and `cholesky_solve(N,b)` (:290, overwrites b with δλ) — so BEFORE factoring, SNAPSHOT `N0 = N` and `b0 = b` (two O(nct²)+O(nct) copies). Each iter: factor `(N + lm_mu·diag(N))·δλ=b`; predicted reduction from the snapshots (floor-independent per agy Q4): `pred = δλᵀ(2·b0 − N0·δλ)`; ρ=(resid_sq_0 − resid_sq_trial)/max(ε, pred). μ-update = newton_calib.cpp:735-742 VERBATIM (do NOT paraphrase): `(alpha>=0.999 && ρ>0.75) → lm_mu=max(μ_min, lm_mu/3)` [tighten ONLY on a full unshortened step]; `(ρ<0.25) → lm_mu=min(μ_max, lm_mu*10)`; else unchanged. Keep step only if ρ>0 (else reject + grow μ*=10 + re-solve; MAX 5 retries per Newton iter, then accept best-available δλ and continue — the outer min(50,inner_max_iter) cap still bounds total work; no unbounded loop). Constants NOT fixture-tuned. Preserve the singular-N INFEAS guard (:284-288) + the >50%-saturation early-exit (:234-240). Do NOT touch the step-norm cap (trace shows it does not bind) or the Armijo structure beyond the μ accept/reject. |
| **Format** | Confined to the logit main-loop step. No change to warm-start (eb79.18), gate (eb79.16), metrics (eb79.20). |
| **Boundary** | src/logit_calib.cpp main loop + tests (tests/testthat/test-logit.R, python/leafblower/test_python.py) + bench fixture (benchmarks/stepstone_all_methods.R already runs logit). No new TU. |
| **Tone** | Match file style; cite eb79.22 + the ridge-throttle trace + agy Q4 pitfall in comments. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. **WU1 (BASELINE + CLASSIFY):** record iters/weights/status at the current code for a PANEL: (a) common well-conditioned (K=2/3, loose) — bit-neutral target; (b) eb79.18 consistent-collinear (iter-1); (c) hard collinear+skewed+tight mw=3 (BUDGET/50, monotone); (d) the mw=1.5 abs_resid=97 case + a feasibility pre-check (Σ[L,U] vs targets) classifying it infeasible-vs-damped-plateau. Record in a bd comment. Determines whether (d) is out-of-scope (infeasible) or must also improve.
2. **WU2 (IMPLEMENT scalar-μ Levenberg):** replace the fixed `eps_ldlt=max_b/kMaxDeltaZ` with the persistent gain-ratio μ per Guards; predicted-reduction from the solved linear model (floor-independent). No TSVD, no step-cap change.
3. **WU3 (VALIDATE + REGRESSION, no-worse):** (a) common path: same status, iters within a small noise band (±1), weights within rtol 1e-6 (LM reduces to GN when well-conditioned — "no-worse", NOT bit-identical); (b) hard collinear mw=3 now status=0 in ≪50 iters; (b') μ/ρ TRACE deliverable: capture per-iter lm_mu + ρ on the mw=3 repro (temporary trace, removed before commit) confirming μ RELAXES on successful steps and the gain-ratio is NOT stuck growing under partial saturation (agy Q4) — attach to bd comment; (c) mw=1.5 no WORSE than baseline (status not worse AND abs_resid ≤ 1.01× baseline); (d) eb79.18 collinear/inconsistent/heterogeneous + all existing logit tests pass; (e) full R suite + pytest green; (f) R/Python parity on the hard fixture rtol 1e-6.
4. **WU4 (STEPSTONE + wall-clock):** logit stepstone (benchmarks/stepstone_all_methods.R) — CONCRETE tolerance: status identical, iters within ±2 (or ±5%, whichever larger), and max_error/kl/weights within rtol 1e-6 vs the pre-change baseline (a well-conditioned stepstone must be no-worse). Capture wall-clock hard-case LM-vs-baseline ratio to substantiate the speed win (and C's rejection).
5. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)

```toon
success: bool

```

description:
# leafblower-eb79.20: Populate logit's l1_weight_change + convergence_solver_objective result fields
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: converged logit cell weights `w_best[]`, `X_init[]`, `L_cell[]`, `U_cell[]`, output `best_weights[]`, `st.weights[]`. Out: two currently-default CalibResult fields set to their mathematically-correct values. NO change to the solver iteration, convergence gate, or any other field.
* **Why:** `logit_calibrate` (src/logit_calib.cpp) sets max_error/best_error/mean_error/kl/chi2/grake_norm/best_weights but leaves `res.base.l1_weight_change` and `res.base.convergence_solver_objective` at struct/override defaults (`convergence_solver_objective` explicitly set to `+inf` at logit_calib.cpp:29; `l1_weight_change` stays 0). Downstream R (r_bridge.cpp:899/907 slot 17) and Python surface these as garbage/stub. greg populates both (greg.cpp:155); logit must too. Correctness-first: report the true minimized objective, not NaN/inf.
* **Reference Data:**
  - Forward map (logit_calib.cpp:300-306): `z_c = Σ_k λ[cat_offset[k]+g_k(c)]`; `w[c] = L_cell[c] + range_c·σ(z_c)`, `σ(z)=1/(1+e^{-z})`, `range_c = U_cell[c]-L_cell[c]`. NO z_target offset inside the sigmoid — z=0 ⇔ w=midpoint. `lambda_0=z_target` (line 103-113) is warm-start ONLY, not part of the objective.
  - `l1_weight_change` doc semantic (leafblower.h:133): "L1 normalized weight change Σ|Δw|/n (renamed from pct_change)". Δw = calibrated − input, obs-level.
  - Distance function the solver actually minimizes (Euler-Lagrange of the sigmoid, midpoint-referenced Fermi-Dirac entropy):
      D_L(w) = (w−L)·log((w−L)/(range/2)) + (U−w)·log((U−w)/(range/2))
      D_L'(w) = log((w−L)/(U−w)) = z   ⇒  D_L=0 and D_L'=0 at w=midpoint (z=0). Gradient equals the constraint combination z — provably the code's stationarity condition.
  - `select_solver_objective` (calib_dispatch.hpp:175) covers ONLY GREG(chi2)/CHEBYSHEV(errRp); default prints internal error + returns NaN. logit is neither ⇒ MUST compute D_L inline, NOT route through the helper.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** In-function C++ state at the logit_calib.cpp exit block (post-loop, after w_best/best_weights are finalized, ~line 352-399). Vectors: `w_best` (cell masses), `L_cell`, `U_cell` (cell bounds), `X_init` (design cell mass), `res.base.best_weights` (obs-level output), `st.weights` (obs-level input design weights, length st.n). Scalars: `M=ct.M_cell`, `st.n`.
* **Format:** C++ `std::vector<double>` + raw `double*` (st.weights). No external I/O.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |

# Epic: Remove dead over-relaxation code (sk_omega, gk_omega)

## Goal
Strip the three non-improving over-relaxation parameters (gk_omega, sk_omega, sk_omega_mode_id) from the rk_params_t ABI, the R bridge, and the two solvers that read them, restoring the params struct to 264B / r_bridge arity 40.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] sinkhorn.cpp runs plain omega=1 (no power-law, no adaptive estimator); src/sor_omega_estimator.hpp + tests/sor_omega_estimator_test.cpp deleted.
- [ ] greenkhorn.cpp runs plain omega=1 (no gk_omega read).
- [ ] gk_omega, sk_omega, sk_omega_mode_id removed from leafblower.h, types.hpp, c_api.cpp, r_bridge.cpp, R/harvest.R; EXPECTED_RK_PARAMS_BYTES 288->264; r_bridge arity 43->40; diff_params.R parity-arity harness 43->40.
- [ ] Dead e65t experiment bench DRIVERS deleted (result .txt evidence logs kept).
- [ ] R CMD INSTALL --preclean . green; devtools::test() green; Python parity green; stepstone no regression.

## Context & Background
Three over-relaxation knobs were added as experiments and all failed their ship gates:
- gk_omega (e65t.2 NO-GO): over-relaxation on greedy Greenkhorn = 0% iter improvement; no literature theorem.
- sk_omega (e65t.3 GO->RETRACTED): fixed Sinkhorn over-relaxation; toy-regime speedup only, neutral/harmful on production fixtures.
- sk_omega_mode_id (e65t.4 NO-SHIP): adaptive iterate-change estimator; Dykstra/bisection interference -> limit cycle, +267% iters on stepstone.
Docs already updated (commit 2a3bd68) to NOT reference these knobs, only the why-not note. The estimator src/sor_omega_estimator.hpp is used ONLY by sinkhorn.cpp + tests/sor_omega_estimator_test.cpp — ORIS's mode-2 default uses its OWN inline v2 block in oris.cpp:1681-1813, so the header is deletable. No Python binding sites (these params were never wired to pybind — R-only scope). All three fields are CONTIGUOUS at the params-struct tail (offsets 264/272/280, arity positions 41/42/43), so removal is a clean tail-truncation.
TWO distinct omega_mode_id concepts exist in harvest.R: `sor=list(omega_mode_id=...)` is the ORIS SOR mode (KEEP — ships as mode 2 default) vs the top-level `sk_omega_mode_id` param (REMOVE). Do NOT confuse them.
Version: changes stay within UNRELEASED 0.1.0 — ABI was bumped 280->288 this same dev cycle and never published, so shrinking back to 264 needs NO version bump. CRAN version bump is separate (leafblower-kk1.24).

## Sub-Agent Strategy
4 atomic tasks, strictly ordered. T1 (sinkhorn revert) + T2 (greenkhorn revert) remove solver reads first, leaving the struct fields dead-but-present (R CMD INSTALL green after each). T3 (ABI shrink) then removes the now-unused fields in ONE atomic cross-file change (leafblower.h + types.hpp + c_api.cpp + r_bridge.cpp + harvest.R + test-bridge-length-checks.R + diff_params.R must move together or per-file compile / arity-check breaks). T4 (bench-driver deletion) last. Each task: explicit per-file `git add <paths>` staging (NEVER `git add -A` — beads leak + cross-contamination, CLAUDE.md). Gate every task on `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` then `Rscript -e devtools::test()`. FORBIDDEN: touching ORIS oris.cpp omega code (mode-2 iterate-change ships, unrelated); touching the ORIS_SOFT ALM Newton-step or chebyshev corrector guarded formulas; bumping DESCRIPTION/pyproject version (0.1.0 unreleased).

title: Share diagnostics gate NA-conflation on has_na_bin, not the injection set (.na_margins)
description:
## What
The user-facing share diagnostics (get_current_miss, diagnose_weights, py diagnose_weights) gate NA-bin conflation on has_na_bin ('NA' %in% names(target)), while the solver + sparseness diagnostics gate on the injection set (.na_margins/na_injected). For a hand-built target with a level literally named 'NA' but NO add_na_proportion, the solver drops true-NA (maps to dropped/OOV) and matches literal-'NA' to the named level, while the share diagnostics CONFLATE true-NA into that bin -> diagnostic != solver.

## Why
Pre-existing design boundary (NOT introduced this session). The 4ihf work deliberately decided the family-P (share) contract is has_na_bin-gated because these exported funcs have signature (data, target, weights) with no access to .na_margins. title: BUG: compute_quality_metrics droplevels fails on character margin column (margin_kl)
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** compute_quality_metrics returns a FINITE margin_kl (Tier-1 primary quality metric) for CHARACTER margin columns, instead of NA via a swallowed droplevels error.
* **Why:** Tier-1 margin_kl is silently lost (NA) for any harvest() run with a character (non-factor) margin; only factor margins currently work. Weights are unaffected — diagnostic-only gap.
* **Reference Data:** R/harvest.R:1029 `W_k <- tapply(w_v, droplevels(obs_k[valid]), sum) / Z_k`. `droplevels()` has NO method for class character -> error "no applicable method for 'droplevels' applied to an object of class character" -> caught by tryCatch at :1033 -> `margin_kl = NA`. The K-pass fallback (:1019-1031) fires for character margins because `use_single_pass` requires ALL margin cols to be factors (:978-980). Surfaced during h0dg (test-eta-schedule.R emits the warning every harvest call on its character margins).
* **Philosophy:** Goldfish memory — all context inline.

## II. Input Specification
* **File:** R/harvest.R, function `compute_quality_metrics` (:946-1041). The bug is the grouping at the K-pass fallback line :1029.
* **Trigger:** any harvest() with a character (non-factor) margin column routed through the K-pass path (fires when K<3 OR anyNA in margin cols OR not-all-factor).

## III. Constraints & Guards
* **Logic:** call droplevels ONLY when the grouping vector is a factor; for character (or any non-factor) pass the raw vector to tapply directly. tapply coerces a character index to a factor over present values only — equivalent to droplevels(factor) — so W_k names remain the category-value strings and margin_kl_one() name-matching (intersect names(T_k), names(W_k)) is unchanged.
* **Boundary:** ONLY the grouping at :1029. Do NOT touch: the single-pass path (:993-1018), deff/weight_kl, the tryCatch, or use_single_pass eligibility (factor-only stays — single-pass needs as.integer(factor codes)+nlevels). Do NOT auto-convert margins to factor upstream.
* **Format:** margin_kl numerically IDENTICAL for a character margin vs the same data with that margin as a factor.
* **Tone:** surgical, minimal.

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Replace the :1029 grouping with a factor-guard:
   `obs_kv <- obs_k[valid]; grp <- if (is.factor(obs_kv)) droplevels(obs_kv) else obs_kv; W_k <- tapply(w_v, grp, sum) / Z_k`
   (For a factor: drop unused levels as before. For character/other: group as-is.)
2. Add a regression test (tests/testthat/): harvest() on a small fixture with a CHARACTER margin column -> assert `attr(r,"result")$margin_kl` is finite (NOT NA), AND no "droplevels" warning is emitted, AND it equals the margin_kl of the SAME data with the margin coerced to factor (consistency).
3. Gates: `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`; `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'` 0 fail (baseline 681 pass); confirm the "margin_kl: no applicable method for 'droplevels'..." warning no longer fires (e.g. via test-eta-schedule or the new test).
4. Check guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: mb06
success: bool
files_changed: []
margin_kl_char_finite: bool
char_equals_factor: bool
droplevels_warning_gone: bool
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Character margin -> margin_kl finite (was NA); numerically == factor-margin margin_kl.
- [ ] "droplevels" warning no longer emitted from compute_quality_metrics.
- [ ] Factor path unchanged; single-pass path + use_single_pass eligibility untouched.
- [ ] R suite 0 fail; new regression test green.
- [ ] Single atomic commit; no .beads leak (pathspec commit).
close_reason: Fixed (commit 02870e4, landed master). compute_quality_metrics K-pass margin_kl grouping (harvest.R:1029) guards droplevels to factors: grp <- if (is.factor(obs_kv)) droplevels(obs_kv) else obs_kv; W_k <- tapply(w_v, grp, sum)/Z_k. Character (or any non-factor) margin now computes a finite margin_kl (was NA via swallowed 'no droplevels method for character' error). Verified independently: char margin_kl finite + expect_identical(char,factor) (tapply coerces char index to factor over present values = droplevels(factor), bit-identical W_k); no droplevels warning; factor path byte-unchanged; single-pass/use_single_pass/tryCatch untouched. New regression test calls compute_quality_metrics directly (decoupled from solver per code-quality review). Load-bearing comment added at fix site. R 684 pass/0 fail. Spec-review PASS, code-quality APPROVE (test scoped off solver + expect_identical + comment, re-reviewed). Pure-R post-solve metric — Python/C++/solver untouched, weights unaffected. Commit clean (2 files, no beads).

title: fix(R): add_na_proportion NA-binding parity with Python + test [ya85 follow-up]
description:
# tu15: Fix R add_na_proportion NA-binding (R↔Python parity) + test + roxygen

**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`  (gate iteration 2: parity mechanism + assertion sharpened; root-cause rebuttal embedded)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Make `harvest(add_na_proportion=TRUE)` in R correctly bind NA observations to the injected `"NA"` target bin (currently dropped → "structurally infeasible" error), matching the already-correct Python behavior; add tests; fix the stale roxygen.
* **Why:** Empirically confirmed R↔Python PARITY DIVERGENCE. Python bins NA→"NA" (works); R drops NA obs (errors). User contract: feature SUPPORTED — fix for real.

## I-bis. ROOT CAUSE — REPRODUCED (do not re-litigate)
Confirmed by live R execution (twice, independently):
```
> as.character(NA)            # => NA_character_   (NOT the string "NA")
> as.character(NA) == "NA"    # => FALSE
> match(as.character(NA), c("a","NA"))   # => NA
> paste(NA)                   # => "NA"   <-- the lookalike; as.character is NOT paste
```
End-to-end: `harvest(df_with_20pct_NA, tgt, add_na_proportion=TRUE)` → ERROR "margin …: target=0.2 but 0 observations assigned (all NA); structurally infeasible". The injected `"NA"` bin (R/harvest.R:295 `list("NA"=na_frac)`) gets ZERO obs because the else-branch encoding uses `match(as.character(col), …)` and `as.character(NA)=NA_character_` never matches `"NA"` → idx=NA→0L→-1L (dropped). **The bug IS in the else-branch L451-454.** A prior reviewer claimed `as.character(NA)=="NA"` — that is FALSE (confused with `paste(NA)`); rebutted by the repro above.

## II. Input Specification
* **Files:** `R/harvest.R` (fix + roxygen), `man/harvest.Rd` (regenerated, NOT hand-edited), new `tests/testthat/test-add-na-proportion.R`, new `python/leafblower/test_harvest_na_parity.py` (R↔Python parity). Build gate `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`.
* **REFERENCE (Python, already correct — MIRROR, do NOT change):** `python/leafblower/_harvest.py:407-411` pandas path `col.astype(str).where(~pd.isna(col), other="NA")` when `varname in _na_vars`; L419-424 non-pandas `if is_na and varname in _na_vars: gid[i]=level_to_idx.get("NA",-1)`.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Mechanism** | In `R/harvest.R` else-branch (~L451-455): when `v %in% .na_margins`, replace NA with literal `"NA"` BEFORE match — `key <- as.character(col); key[is.na(key)] <- "NA"; idx <- match(key, names(target[[v]]))`. Fill GUARDED by `v %in% .na_margins` (non-NA-bin margins' NAs stay OOV/-1). Mirror Python exactly. |
| **WHY the fix is NOT a no-op (preempt recurring review confusion)** | `match()` PROPAGATES NA: `match(NA_character_, x)` returns `NA` for ANY `x`, INCLUDING when the string `"NA"` is an element of `x` — NA never equals anything under `match`. And `as.character(NA)` is `NA_character_`, NOT the string `"NA"` (that is `paste(NA)`/`format(NA)`). So the CURRENT `match(as.character(col), …)` yields NA for NA obs → `idx[is.na(idx)] <- 0L` → `idx-1L = -1L` (dropped). The fill `key[is.na(key)] <- "NA"` converts the NA to the literal STRING `"NA"`, which DOES `match` the injected bin. Verified by live R 3× (`as.character(NA)`→`NA_character_`; `match(as.character(NA), c("a","NA"))`→`NA`). The fix is load-bearing, not cosmetic. |
| **Fix covers FACTOR columns too (explicit)** | The else-branch is reached for ALL `v %in% .na_margins` columns regardless of type (the L444 fast-path guard `is.factor(col) && !v %in% .na_margins` excludes NA-bin margins → they fall here). `as.character(factor_with_NA)` ALSO yields `NA_character_` for the NA entries, so the fill is applied UNCONDITIONALLY to the `as.character(col)` output (the `key` vector) — covering factor AND non-factor NA-bin columns uniformly. Do NOT gate the fill behind `!is.factor(col)`. The test fixture (factor `g`) exercises exactly this path. |
| **Unknown-level handling unchanged (no missing -1L)** | Post-fill, a genuinely UNKNOWN level (not NA, not in `names(target[[v]])`) still → `match`→NA → existing `idx[is.na(idx)] <- 0L` → `idx-1L = -1L` (OOV, dropped). This is the char-path equivalent of the factor path's `gids[is.na(gids)] <- -1L`; it already works and is NOT changed by this fix. The RED test SHOULD include one observation with an unknown level to confirm it still maps to -1L (no regression). |
| **Forbidden** | Do NOT change Python. Do NOT touch the factor fast-path (L444-450), the na_frac==1 `stop()` (L287-290), or the renormalize math (L292-296). Bin name stays `"NA"`. |
| **Parity** | After fix, R and Python produce weights agreeing rtol=1e-6 for add_na_proportion=TRUE on identical data+targets. |
| **Behavior (non-NA)** | Non-NA-bin behavior byte-identical (fill is guarded). Full R suite + existing parity (9) + stepstone unchanged. |
| **Docs** | Fix roxygen `R/harvest.R:123` (stale "Not supported in v1; raises error if TRUE") to document actual behavior; REGENERATE `man/harvest.Rd` via `devtools::document()` in the SAME commit (do NOT hand-edit the .Rd; it currently echoes the stale text at man/harvest.Rd:184). Fix false comment L442-443 + L276 "__NA__" comment. |
| **Known limitation (document, do NOT fix)** | If a column has BOTH real NA values AND a literal level named `"NA"` (the string), the injected bin and the real level collide (indistinguishable post-fill). Note this in the roxygen as a known limitation; not in scope to resolve. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic (TDD)
1. **RED:** add `tests/testthat/test-add-na-proportion.R`: df with a factor margin ~20% NA + targets summing to 1; `harvest(..., add_na_proportion=TRUE, method="raking")`. Assert (initially FAILING): (a) no error / converges; (b) Σw=n (within 1e-8); (c) MARGINAL NA share — `sum(w[is.na(col)]) / sum(w) ≈ na_frac` within the solver's achieved tolerance (use `result$diagnostics`/max_error, or an explicit `tolerance = 1e-3` for the marginal — NOT rtol=1e-6, since calibration matches the marginal to convergence tol, not exactly; the `/sum(w)` form is the well-posed marginal, and since Σw=n the `/n` form is equivalent). (d) non-NA targets honored (renormalized by 1-na_frac), checked as marginals `sum(w[col==lvl])/sum(w) ≈ (1-na_frac)*tgt[lvl]`. Run → confirm FAIL pre-fix (structurally-infeasible error). Add a na_frac==1 case asserting the existing `stop()` fires.
2. **GREEN:** apply the Mechanism fix. Fix comment L442-443 + roxygen L123 + L276 comment; run `devtools::document()` to regen man/harvest.Rd. `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`. Test (1) passes.
3. **PARITY:** add the new test in the SAME directory as the existing parity test — confirm that dir first (`python -c "import os; print([p for p in ['leafblower/test_design_effect_parity.py'] if os.path.exists('python/'+p)])"`); the existing R↔Python parity test is `python/leafblower/test_design_effect_parity.py`, so place the new test at `python/leafblower/test_harvest_na_parity.py` and run it via `cd python && python -m pytest leafblower/test_harvest_na_parity.py -q` (the same invocation the suite uses for test_python.py). Mirror its pattern: Python builds the FIXTURE below, writes JSON to /tmp, `subprocess` runs an Rscript that `jsonlite::fromJSON`s it, calls `leafblower::harvest(..., add_na_proportion=TRUE)`, writes R weights+status to JSON; Python runs `harvest(..., add_na_proportion=True)` on identical data. **Convergence precheck (MANDATORY before comparing):** assert BOTH the R result and the Python result report converged/OK status (no error, status success) — if either did not converge, FAIL with a clear message (do NOT compare weights of a non-converged solve). Then assert `np.allclose(w_r, w_py, rtol=1e-6)`.
   * **FIXTURE (concrete, pre-validated feasible — use this exactly):** seed=1; n=500; single factor margin `g` with levels {"a","b","c"}, sampled ~equally, then ~20% set to NA (so each non-NA level and the NA bin all have ample obs); `target=list(g=c(a=0.4,b=0.35,c=0.25))`; method="raking", max_iterations=200. After inject: a/b/c scaled by 0.8, "NA"=0.2 — every bin has >0 obs ⇒ structurally feasible ⇒ both solvers converge. (This is the same shape as the empirical repro that confirmed the bug; post-fix it converges.) Identical seed/data must be used on both sides (pass the sampled column values, not just the seed, through the JSON fixture so R and Python see the EXACT same observations).
4. Regression: full R suite (baseline 598+ pass, 0 fail); existing Python parity (`python -m pytest leafblower/test_python.py` → 9 pass); stepstone (`Rscript benchmarks/stepstone_compare_current.R` → max|Δw|≈1.2e-12). All unchanged.
5. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: tu15
success: bool
data:
  red_test_failed_pre_fix: bool        # bug reproduced first (structurally-infeasible)
  files_changed: [R/harvest.R, man/harvest.Rd, tests/..., python/.../test_harvest_na_parity.py]
  na_marginal_share_correct: bool      # sum(w[NA])/sum(w) ≈ na_frac within solver tol
  sum_w_equals_n: bool
  r_py_parity_na_case: {rtol: 1e-6, pass: bool}
  r_suite: {fail: int, pass: int}
  python_parity_existing: {pass: int}
  stepstone_regression: bool           # MUST be false
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] RED test written and observed to FAIL pre-fix (structurally-infeasible reproduced).
- [ ] R encoding fix applied (NA→"NA" guarded by .na_margins, mirrors Python); Python UNCHANGED.
- [ ] R test passes: converges, Σw=n, MARGINAL `sum(w[NA])/sum(w) ≈ na_frac` (solver tol), non-NA marginals renormalized; na_frac==1 still `stop()`s.
- [ ] R↔Python parity test at `python/leafblower/test_harvest_na_parity.py` (subprocess+Rscript+JSON, the pinned feasible fixture): BOTH runtimes converge (precheck), then weights agree rtol=1e-6.
- [ ] roxygen L123 fixed + `man/harvest.Rd` REGENERATED via devtools::document() + comments (L442-443, L276) corrected — all SAME commit as code; known-limitation (real "NA" level collision) documented.
- [ ] Regression: full R suite, existing Python parity (9), stepstone all unchanged.
- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` clean; diff confined to R/harvest.R + man/harvest.Rd + the two new test files.
close_reason: Fixed R add_na_proportion NA-binding (R↔Python parity). else-branch fills NA->'NA' guarded by .na_margins (mirrors Python). RED confirmed (structurally-infeasible pre-fix), GREEN after (test 10/0). Verified independently: na-test 10 pass, R↔Py parity both-converged rtol=1e-6, full R suite 608/0, existing parity 9, stepstone 1.227e-12. roxygen+man/harvest.Rd corrected. Python unchanged. Commit 5fc010a.

description:
## Goal
Hoist repeated R predicates out of tight loops and convert SIMD-eligible hot scalar loops to lbw kernels — strictly behavior-preserving.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] R/harvest.R compound predicates (is.factor && !v %in% .na_margins) bound once per outer scope; all .Call setup hoisted (l1p3)

## Context & Background

title: ieppa.cpp:148-182 — ieppa_finalize 3-iter rescale loop does NOT guarantee cell-aggregate Σ X = n
description:
Rescale loop (L154-165) clamps X to [L_cell, U_cell] then scales by n/total then clamps. If all cells pinned at U (mass-saturated infeasible), rescale n/total < 1 pushes cells below bounds, clamp re-pins at L; iterates oscillate. After kMaxRescaleIters=3, residual alm_sum_drift = |final_total - n| recorded but Σ_c X[c] ≠ n unenforced.

Obs-level renorm at L276-281 fixes Σw=n at the OBS level, so this is a Suggestion only. Cell-aggregate Σ X may remain off by alm_sum_drift.

Fix: After rescale loop, normalize X by n/Σ X (no clamp); document that bound violations in X may remain on infeasible inputs. Or report alm_sum_drift > threshold as RK_ERR_INFEAS.
notes: Verified L148-182. Obs Σw=n unaffected. Cell-level Σ X drift only. Confidence 75.
close_reason: Fixed: unclamped final scale forces cell sum(X)=n after recording alm_sum_drift. Obs weights unchanged (obs renorm absorbs uniform X scale) — 593 R/15 py pass byte-identical. Cell invariant now holds; X may exceed bounds on infeasible inputs (documented).

title: ieppa.cpp:1591-1606 — ALM linearized Newton formula missing -ρ in numerator (SUSPECTED)
description:
ALM Newton step:
  X_alm = X_tilde * (1 - λ + μ·z) / (1 + ρ),  ρ = μ·X_tilde

Derivation from KL Bregman ALM stationarity ∂f/∂X + λ + μ(X − z) = 0 with f = Σ X log(X/X_tilde):
  expected: X_alm = X_tilde * (1 - λ + μ(z - X_tilde)) / (1 + ρ) = X_tilde * (1 - λ + μ·z - ρ) / (1 + ρ)
  code:     X_tilde * (1 - λ + μ·z) / (1 + ρ)
The -ρ term is missing in numerator.

Fixed-point check: when constraints inactive (z=X_tilde, λ=0), code gives X = X_tilde · (1+μ·X_tilde)/(1+μ·X_tilde) = X_tilde ✓. Correct fixed point. Missing -ρ affects convergence rate under tight constraints, not final answer.

Fix: Derive symbolically from KL-Bregman ALM (cite design spec); validate on 2-cell test case vs scipy.optimize. If wrong, change numerator to (1 - λ + μ·z - ρ).
notes: Verified L1591-1601 code. Math derivation incomplete — needs design-spec cross-check. Confidence 50. May be intentional simplification.
close_reason: NOT A BUG. Code is the correct linearization of iEPPA's un-normalized KL (I-divergence) Bregman generator: dD/dX=log(X/Xt), linearize -> X=Xt(1-lam+mu z)/(1+rho), matches code exactly. Ticket's -rho assumes normalized KL (log+1), wrong generator. 2-cell sim: both share fixed point clamp(Xt,L,U), rate is a wash. Guard comment added.

title: ieppa.cpp:1287-1297 — SRAA-end cell clamp reduces Σ X by over-cap excess (cell-level invariant)
description:
After SRAA while-loop exit, code clamps X[c] = clamp(src_cells[c], L_cell[c], U_cell[c]). Per-cell hard clamp reduces Σ X by cumulative over-cap excess. ieppa_finalize obs-level renorm (L276-281) fixes the obs-level Σw=n contract, but cell-aggregate Σ X may differ from n; in bounds_mode=CELL the renorm distributes evenly across obs, which can push obs above max_weight (caught by water-fill in UNIT mode, silently violates cell-aggregate ≤ U_cell in CELL mode).

Also: if next homotopy level's warm start uses this clamped X, it begins below the true SRAA fixed point.

Fix option A: After clamp, mass-preserving bisection rescale: pick scalar r such that Σ clamp(r·src_cells[c], L, U) ≈ n.
Fix option B: Skip clamp on intermediate levels; rely on next-level capacity block to renormalize.
notes: Verified L1287-1297. Obs-level Σw=n unaffected (finalize fixes). Cell-aggregate / warm-start state corrupted. Confidence 70.
close_reason: Fixed via option A: mass-preserving bisection rescale (Σ clamp(r·src,L,U)=n) replaces plain SRAA-end clamp. Restores warm-start fidelity + cell ΣX=n; best-effort if mass-saturated. 593 R/15 py pass, no parity shift.

title: ieppa.cpp:2049-2058 — convergence_iter reports final stop-iter, not convergence-firing iter
description:
Non-SRAA branch sets status=RK_OK at L2054 when converged=true but does not record the iter at which convergence first fired. ieppa_finalize at L220-227 then sets convergence_iter = (status==RK_OK) ? res.base.iterations : -1 — which is the FINAL iter from last level's last iter, off by potentially kErrCheckInterval iters from the actual convergence-firing iter. Same issue on SRAA path (mark_converged at L1284 only fires on final level).

Fix: Add res.base.convergence_iter = iter; at L2049-2058 (non-SRAA) and inside SRAA converged block (L1280). Use this in ieppa_finalize instead of res.base.iterations.
notes: Verified. Reported field accuracy issue, no math impact. Confidence 80. Source: Opus review.
close_reason: Fixed: convergence_iter pinned at firing sites (non-SRAA terminal block + SRAA mark_converged); finalize no longer clobbers with finalize-time iterations (only -1 on non-OK). Robustness fix (current values already correct). 593 R/15 py pass incl convergence_iter assertion.

title: R/harvest.R — 46KB file, hoist repeated compound predicates
description:
# l1p3: Hoist 2 loop-invariant queries in R/harvest.R (H4, H7b)

**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`  (revised post plan-review iteration 1)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Hoist 2 genuinely loop-invariant R expressions in `R/harvest.R` so each is computed once per call instead of once per margin; output byte-identical.
* **Why:** Parent ya85 (behavior-preserving). NOTE: review iteration 1 falsified the original "tight-loop compound predicate" premise — the cited `is.factor(col) && !v %in% .na_margins` (L443) is loop-VARIANT (col=data[[v]]). H7a (L929) and H8 (L473) are single evaluations with NO enclosing loop → dropped. Only H4 and H7b are real loop-invariant hoists, both O(K margins) (not hot O(n)); value is cleanliness, not measurable speed.
* **Reference Data:** harvest.R is 990 lines. Line numbers are HEAD/master — re-confirm before editing.
* **Philosophy:** Behavior MUST be identical. Parity rtol=1e-6 + stepstone zero-regression are the gate. No new behavioral tests required.

## II. Input Specification
* **File:** `/home/dd/Gemini/leafblower/R/harvest.R` (ONLY this file).
* **Format:** R source. Build gate: `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Hoist ONLY where hoisted vars are proven loop-invariant (not mutated in loop). Re-read each region to confirm before editing. |
| **Scope** | Edit ONLY the H4 site and the H7b sites. Two distinct functions. No reformatting, no adjacent refactor. |
| **DO-NOT-HOIST / DO-NOT-TOUCH** | (a) L443 `is.factor(col)&&!v%in%.na_margins` — col loop-variant. (b) L255/L270 `names(target[[v]])` — target[[v]] MUTATED between reads. (c) L256, L285, L293 — loop-variant. (d) L949 `as.integer(df[[k]])` encoding — leave intact. (e) L974 obs_k variant. (f) `data_names` at L730 in `compute_sparseness_diag` — ALREADY hoisted, different function, DO NOT touch. (g) Dropped H7a (L929 `all(vapply(... is.factor ...))`) and H8 (L473 `.Call` slot-11) — NOT loops, leave as-is. |
| **Tone** | Match existing harvest.R style. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. **H4** — in `harvest()`, the `add_na_proportion` block (L281-298; default-off feature, `add_na_proportion=FALSE` default). Loop `for (v in names(target))` (L283). `data` is NOT mutated in this loop (only `target[[v]]` and `.na_margins` are). Insert `data_names <- names(data)` once before the loop (e.g. right after `n_local <- nrow(data)` at L282), and replace `if (!v %in% names(data))` (L284) with `if (!v %in% data_names)`. Do NOT reuse/disturb the `data_names` in compute_sparseness_diag (L730) — separate scope.
2. **H7b** — in `compute_quality_metrics`, `df` and `margin_cols` are params, not mutated. Hoist `col_nlevels <- vapply(margin_cols, function(k) nlevels(df[[k]]), integer(1))` once (place it just before the `if (use_single_pass)` guard near L934, or immediately after `margin_cols` is defined). Then: replace `prod(vapply(margin_cols, function(k) nlevels(df[[k]]), integer(1)))` at L935 with `prod(col_nlevels)`; replace `nlevels(df[[k]])` at L950 (inside `for (k in margin_cols)`) with `col_nlevels[[k]]`. nlevels() on a non-factor returns 0 → safe; ordering of margin_cols preserved so indexing matches. Leave `as.integer(df[[k]])` at L949 untouched.
3. Check Guards. Confirm zero DO-NOT-TOUCH sites changed; diff limited to the H4 line-pair and the H7b hoist+2 substitutions.
4. Build gate `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`. Run full R suite, Python parity, AND stepstone (DoD).

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon

success: bool
data:

  files_changed: [R/harvest.R]
  r_tests: {fail: int, pass: int}
  parity_unchanged: bool
  stepstone_regression: bool   # MUST be false
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done

- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` clean.
- [ ] Full R suite: no new failures vs master.
- [ ] Python parity rtol=1e-6 UNCHANGED.
- [ ] Stepstone: `Rscript benchmarks/stepstone_compare_current.R` → zero regression (max|Δw| at FP-noise, r=1.0) vs reference.
- [ ] Diff touches ONLY R/harvest.R, only the H4 + H7b sites.

Verified: named-vector col_nlevels[[k]] lookup order-independent correct; diff exactly gate-approved plan; H7a/H8 correctly dropped (not loops). title: raking.cpp:161 — water-fill loop pass<=n off-by-one
description: Loop 'for (int pass = 0; pass <= n; ++pass)' runs n+1 iterations. Csiszar-Tusnady water-fill bound: ≤ n passes (one pin per pass). Inner break guards catch degenerate case so behavior safe in practice, but extra iter at pass==n can flip is_infeasible=true on otherwise-converged inputs. Fix: pass < n.
notes: Verified L155-185. Minor; defensive correctness fix.
close_reason: Confirmed bound proof: <=n allows useless (n+1)th pass that re-applies eps-infeasibility guard (free_sum<kAbsoluteZeroThreshold) spuriously vs post-loop <=0.0. Each clamping pass shrinks free pool by >=1, so n iters suffice. Changed <=n -> <n + rationale comment. raking 21 pass, infeas 4 pass, build clean. Commit 6ab04c7.

title: Stall_kind coverage tests for greenkhorn + logit_calib STALL emission
description:
## I. Context & Objective

The `stall_kind` field was added to `CalibResult` in commit cbb0313 (leafblower-8eod) and setters were wired into 4 RK_ERR_STALL emission sites: `raking.cpp:494` (kl=2), `ieppa.cpp:188` (st.accelerate?wchange=1:kl=2), `greenkhorn.cpp:230` (kl=2 — added in commit 38f7d20), `logit_calib.cpp:290` (kl=2 — added in commit 38f7d20). harvest.R:544 maps the int via switch to the user-visible `convergence_reason` string ("stall_wchange", "stall_kl", or NA).

No testthat coverage exists for the greenkhorn/logit STALL paths because forcing those solvers into RK_ERR_STALL deterministically requires constructing a fixture where the metric plateaus before max_iterations. Greenkhorn and logit-calib both prefer to converge or hit budget; STALL emission is a narrow third branch.

**Objective:** Add a testthat fixture per solver that deterministically forces RK_ERR_STALL emission and asserts `attr(r, "result")$convergence_reason == "stall_kl"` (or whatever string the post-fix switch maps stall_kind=2 to) for greenkhorn AND logit_calib.

## II. Input Specification

- Files to add: `tests/testthat/test-stall-kind-coverage.R` (new).
- Files to read: `R/harvest.R:528-540` (the convergence_reason switch), `src/greenkhorn.cpp:225-235` (STALL emission site), `src/logit_calib.cpp:285-295` (STALL emission site), `tests/testthat/test-newton-kl.R T4` (~line 80, existing forced-violation pattern for newton).
- Solver behavior to exploit:
  - greenkhorn: STALL when `final_errRp >= first_errRp * 0.999` (i.e., < 0.1% improvement over initial). A target requiring near-zero net error change is hard to construct; alternative: extreme bound clamp + budget-tight max_iterations may corner it.
  - logit_calib: STALL when `best_resid >= initial_resid * 0.999`. Same idea.

## III. Constraints & Guards

| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Each test MUST drive the solver to RK_ERR_STALL (status==5L) AND assert `convergence_reason == "stall_kl"`. If status comes back as RK_ERR_BUDGET (4L) or RK_OK (0L), fixture is wrong; tighten or recraft. |
| **Format** | testthat v3. Use `harvest()` public API. Use `set.seed()` for determinism. Use `skip_if_not_installed()` for any optional deps. |
| **Boundary** | Touch only the new test file. Do NOT modify solver C++ code. Do NOT modify harvest.R. |
| **Tone** | Test names cite ticket id (this ticket's bd id) and the solver under test. |
| **Forbidden** | Modifying solver thresholds (0.999) to make STALL trigger easier. Asserting against a stall_kind value the harvest.R switch hasn't been verified to map to. Catching exceptions to mask non-STALL outcomes. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic

1. Read `R/harvest.R:528-540` to confirm the int→string mapping under stall_kind=2 (currently "stall_kl"). Note the value the test must assert.
2. Construct a fixture for greenkhorn that forces RK_ERR_STALL: try (a) extreme target skew (90/10 + tight max_weight=1.05), (b) very small max_iterations=3, (c) high-tolerance convergence threshold so net-improvement-over-initial check fails. Iterate until one combo gives status==5L deterministically.
3. Same exercise for logit_calib.
4. Add `tests/testthat/test-stall-kind-coverage.R` with two tests:
   - "greenkhorn RK_ERR_STALL emission populates convergence_reason='stall_kl'"
   - "logit_calib RK_ERR_STALL emission populates convergence_reason='stall_kl'"
5. Each test asserts: `attr(r, "result")$status == 5L` AND `attr(r, "result")$convergence_reason == "stall_kl"`.
6. If after reasonable effort (say 30 minutes) no fixture deterministically triggers STALL for one of the solvers: mark that test with `skip("environment-fragile; STALL fixture not derivable")` and document the attempts in a header comment. Don't ship a flaky test.
7. Build: `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`.
8. Test: `Rscript -e "testthat::test_local(reporter='silent')"` ≥ current baseline + N (where N = tests actually added, max 2).
9. Stage explicitly: `git add tests/testthat/test-stall-kind-coverage.R`.
10. Commit. Body cites this ticket id + reviewer-finding origin (critical-code-reviewer pass on P2 batch, IMPORTANT-1 follow-up).

## V. Output Schema (Strict)

Sub-agent MUST return:

```toon
task_id: <this-ticket-id>
success: bool
data:
  files_changed: [tests/testthat/test-stall-kind-coverage.R]
  commit_sha: <40-hex>
  greenkhorn_stall_test: passed | skipped_env_fragile
  logit_stall_test: passed | skipped_env_fragile
  test_pass: int
  test_fail: int
  test_skip: int
  baseline_preserved: bool
error_log: null | string
```

## VI. Definition of Done

- [ ] `tests/testthat/test-stall-kind-coverage.R` exists.
- [ ] At least one of {greenkhorn, logit_calib} STALL test runs and passes (asserts status==5L AND convergence_reason=="stall_kl"); the other may be `skip()`-ed if env-fragile, with documentation of attempts.
- [ ] `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .` clean.
- [ ] `testthat::test_local()` 0 FAIL; PASS rises by 1-2; SKIP rises by 0-1.
- [ ] Commit body cites IMPORTANT-1 origin (critical-code-reviewer pass on P2 batch).
- [ ] No flaky tests introduced (no `expect_*` that depends on RNG without `set.seed()`).
- [ ] Output matches V. Output Schema.

description:
# T-T: CalibState sub explicit field-by-field init (FIX-10)
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** Convert `CalibState sub = st;` (3 sites) to explicit field-by-field init listing every field actually used by the within-cell call.
**Forbidden:** `static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<CalibState>)` — Feasibility reviewer pre-confirmed this FAILS at compile time (CalibState has in-class initializers throughout). DO NOT ATTEMPT static_assert path.
**Audit:** explicit init pattern compiles; weight-history test (second-outer-iter weights differ from first-outer-iter weights by > epsilon on non-trivial DGP) verifies sub-state isolation works.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: `src/raking.cpp:664`, `src/sinkhorn.cpp:420`, `src/greenkhorn.cpp:381`. Out: `CalibState sub` constructed via explicit field assignment of all members the solver needs.
* **Why:** `CalibState sub = st;` aliases raw pointers (`weights`, `group_ids`, `targets`, `cat_counts`). Risk: dangling pointers if CalibState owns heap. CalibState has in-class initializers (e.g., `bool ieppa_auto_selected = false`) → NOT trivially copyable per C++17 §10.9.

## II. Input Specification
* `src/types.hpp:107+` (CalibState definition; orchestrator verified non-trivially-copyable).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Replace `CalibState sub = st;` with: `CalibState sub{}; sub.n = ...; sub.K = ...; sub.weights = ...; sub.group_ids = ...; sub.targets = ...; sub.cat_counts = ...; sub.convergence_cfg = st.convergence_cfg;` and any other fields the inner solver reads. Inspect each solver's data dependencies. |
| **Boundary** | TOUCH ONLY: 3 sub-state init blocks in 3 solver files. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. **Test FIRST** (`tests/testthat/test-substate-isolation.R`): construct DGP with non-trivial fine margins; run hierarchical with `outer_iterations=2`; assert `weights_after_iter_2 ≠ weights_after_iter_1` (i.e., second outer iter actually performed work, not no-op). Verify CURRENT code passes (the `sub = st` path works with raw pointer aliasing); explicit init must also pass.
2. Read CalibState definition; enumerate fields used by `raking_solve` / `sinkhorn_solve` / `greenkhorn_solve` (typically: `n`, `K`, `weights`, `group_ids`, `targets`, `cat_counts`, `convergence_cfg`, `min_weight`, `max_weight`, possibly `bounds_mode`).
3. Replace each `CalibState sub = st;` with explicit init listing only the used fields.
4. Verify: build + tests pass.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```json
{"task_id":"T-T","success":true,"data":{"files_modified":["src/raking.cpp","src/sinkhorn.cpp","src/greenkhorn.cpp"],"tests_added":["tests/testthat/test-substate-isolation.R"],"approach":"explicit_init"},"error_log":null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Substate isolation test added FIRST and passes on un-patched (verifies test infrastructure).
- [ ] 3 sub-init blocks converted to explicit field init.
- [ ] No `static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<CalibState>)` introduced.
- [ ] Build + tests pass.
- [ ] No hallucination.

title: T-L: DGP discovery for §8 rescue test seed-sweep gate
description:
# T-L: DGP discovery for §8 rescue test seed-sweep gate
**Status:** `OPEN_FOR_RESEARCH` (P3 — research, not blocking)
**Mechanism:** Empirical search over (K, N, margin cardinality, joint distribution, target distribution, max_weight) for a DGP that simultaneously satisfies spec §8 bullets: 2-stage ≥95% / single-stage ≥80% failure on SAME DGP, both at margin-residual ≤ 1e-4.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Find a DGP that empirically demonstrates 2-stage rescue at spec §8 thresholds. Codify into spec §8 v4 + wire into tests/testthat/test-2stage-raking.R rescue test_that block (currently skip()'d).
* **Why:** T-F partial-completion deferred this. P1 ships without empirical seed-sweep gate; correctness covered by branch coverage + 9 adversarial fixtures + roxygen example. T-L re-enables the seed-sweep performance claim once a viable DGP is found.

## II. Input Specification
* **Spec amendment trail:** docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-06-2-stage-hierarchical-method-assessment-design.md §8 has rationale section listing v1/v2/v3 failed amendments. Read first to understand failure modes.
* **Empirical findings (T-F iter 1-5):**
  - v1 (N=10000 binary K=9 Dirichlet(0.1) + target_skew=0.95 + max_weight=2): geometrically infeasible (sample base ~50%, target 95%, factor 19× exceeds bound)
  - v2 (N=200 binary K=9 Dirichlet(0.1) empirical targets): trivially feasible (identity weights satisfy)
  - v3 (N=80 K=6 Bern(0.1/0.15/0.2) chain + 50/50 targets): infeasible Stage-1 (Bern(0.1) at N=80 = ~8 obs needs 5-20× upweight)

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | DGP must produce: (a) Stage-1-feasible coarse calibration (no impossible upweights), (b) single-stage failure across the FULL margin set (NaN/INFEAS/BUDGET in 80%+ seeds), (c) 2-stage success at margin residual ≤ 1e-4 in 95%+ seeds. Mechanism: cell-local target absorption + sparse-cell inheritance. |
| **Format** | DGP function in tests/testthat/helper-2stage.R returning list(df, targets, coarse_mask). Spec §8 amended to specify the construction recipe. |
| **Boundary** | tests/testthat/helper-2stage.R, tests/testthat/test-2stage-raking.R (uncomment skip()), spec §8 (amend with v4 DGP). |
| **Tone** | Exhaustive empirical evidence — table of (K, N, cardinality, joint, target) variants tried with rates per seed-sweep. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Empirical search across DGP space:
   - Vary K ∈ {6, 9}
   - Vary N ∈ {80, 200, 500, 1000, 2000}
   - Vary margin cardinality ∈ {2, 3, 4} per margin
   - Vary joint construction: Dirichlet(α=0.01, 0.1, 1.0) | chain-correlated | independent
   - Vary targets: empirical | uniform | extreme-skew
   - Vary max_weight (within solver defaults)
2. For each combo, run 100 seeds; record 2-stage success rate + single-stage failure rate
3. Identify Pareto-frontier: combos where both ≥ thresholds
4. Pick smallest viable (lowest N×K — minimize CI cost)
5. Codify winner into spec §8 v4 (DGP description + rationale paragraph)
6. Update helper-2stage.R + uncomment skip() in test-2stage-raking.R
7. Re-trigger lightweight design-review-gate iter 4 on §8 only
8. Verify: R CMD INSTALL + devtools::test() green; rescue gate fires correctly

## V. Output Schema (Strict)

```json
{
  "task_id": "T-L",
  "success": true,
  "data": {

    "viable_variants": <int>,

  }
}
```

- [ ] tests/testthat/helper-2stage.R updated; skip() removed from test-2stage-raking.R

All return 0/n rescue rate at spec §8 thresholds. v0/v1 BUDGET-exit; v2/v3 INFEAS/BADARG. Root cause: 2-stage rescue mechanism is sparseness-rescue (1-D zero-row), not bounds-infeasibility rescue. v3 DGP (N=80, K=3 binary coarse → 8 cells) also fails cell-count cap floor(80/30)=2 < 8, RK_ERR_BADARG on every seed. title: B2: Single-pass margin_kl aggregation (replace K separate tapply calls)

# B2: Single-pass margin_kl aggregation

**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION
**Mechanism:** Replace K separate `tapply(weights, data[[k]], sum)` calls inside `sapply(names(target), ...)` with a single `rowsum(weights, interaction(data[names(target)]))` or equivalent pre-aggregation using `model.matrix`-style design that accumulates all K marginals in one data pass. Fall back to existing K-pass approach if data has NAs (per B1 NA fix).
**Forbidden:** No metric value changes. Values must match existing margin_kl to within 1e-10 relative.
**Audit:** `all.equal(compute_quality_metrics_old, compute_quality_metrics_new)` on stepstone + t1_small.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Reduce margin_kl from K separate O(n) hash-builds to a single O(nK) aggregation pass.
* **Why:** With K=20 and n=200K stepstone, current impl builds 20 separate hash tables. A single cell-aggregation groups observations once.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** After B1. Master HEAD post-B1 commit. compute_quality_metrics helper exists.
* **Format:** none

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Must preserve NA handling (NA observations excluded per B1 fix). Must preserve Inf return for missing categories. Benchmark on stepstone K=9 + kk1204 K=20 to confirm speedup; if not faster for K<5, keep old approach with dispatch. |
| **Boundary** | compute_quality_metrics helper only (B1's extracted function). |
| **Tone** | Code normal. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Profile current margin_kl: `microbenchmark::microbenchmark(compute_quality_metrics(w, tgt, df), times=10)` on stepstone.
2. Implement single-pass version using: `cell_df <- data[names(target)]; cell_df[is.na(cell_df)] <- NA; agg <- tapply(weights, do.call(paste, c(cell_df, sep="\x01")), sum)` — or equivalent approach that groups ALL margin-level combinations. Compute per-margin sums via group projection.
3. Verify values identical to old impl.
4. Benchmark again; document speedup in commit body.
5. Stage R/harvest.R. Commit: `perf(harvest): single-pass margin_kl aggregation; ~Kx fewer hash-builds`.

## V. Output Schema
```json
{"task_id":"<EPICB>.2","success":true,"data":{"speedup_ratio":">1.0","values_identical":true,"commit_sha":"<sha>"},"error_log":null}
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] margin_kl uses single data-pass (verify via profiling)
- [ ] Values identical on stepstone + t1_small
- [ ] Speedup documented in commit body
- [ ] Commit: `perf(harvest): single-pass margin_kl aggregation`
notes: DoD additions (rev 3/4 plan-review-gate closures): (1) Commit benchmarks/profile_margin_kl.R + baseline profile BEFORE B2 implementation. (2) STOP RULE: if measured speedup <1.5x on stepstone, REVERT and close DEFERRED. (3) dispatch test: test_that in test-quality-metrics.R asserting single-pass NOT taken when anyNA(df[names(target)]). (4) muffleWarning test: targeted handler fires on 'missing values' text, propagates other warnings. (5) NA fixture (set.seed(42L), n=500, K=3, 3-level factors, 25 NA injections in col a) must fall back to K-pass and produce identical results. (6) projection mechanism: paste+rowsum to aggregate cells, then per-margin tapply over M_cell (not n). Full algorithm in plan rev 4 B2 step 3.

title: research: greenkhorn vs autumn quality difference — algorithm and parameter analysis
description:
## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Understand and document why greenkhorn (1.57e-3) differs from autumn (1.60e-3) on stepstone.

* **Reference Data:** Cached autumn result: 33.6s, max_err=1.5996e-3 (from stepstone_reference_autumn_only.rds). Autumn was run with accelerate=TRUE (SQUAREM+greedy). Greenkhorn benchmark: 3.3s, max_err=1.5714e-3 (single-margin steps per iteration, no SQUAREM actually active due to harvest.R bug leafblower-e0zb). Both use max_weight=5, min_weight=0.

## II. Input Specification

| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Report max_err, L1, marg_kl, DEFF, ESS for both methods |
| **Logic** | Report autumn cached params (max_weight, convergence criterion, accelerate setting) |
| **Logic** | After leafblower-e0zb fix: re-run greenkhorn+squarem and compare to greenkhorn+plain |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Read stepstone_reference_autumn_only.rds — what params was it captured with?
2. Compare greenkhorn (plain, no SQUAREM) vs autumn (SQUAREM+greedy rounds): are they the same algorithm?
3. After e0zb fix: run greenkhorn+squarem; compare to autumn+SQUAREM quality.
4. Document the algorithm differences in a beads memory entry.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)

```json
{"task_id": "grk_autumn_analysis", "success": true, "data": {"algorithm_difference": "...", "quality_comparison": "..."}, "error_log": null}
```

- [ ] Greedy-single-step vs greedy-all-K-rounds difference explained

close_reason:
Answered by benchmark results after e0zb fix:
- greenkhorn plain (1.57e-3) vs autumn (1.60e-3): different algorithms (single-margin steps vs K-step greedy rounds), different fixed points — expected.
- greenkhorn+squarem (2.12e-3): SQUAREM overshoots bounded optimum, tracked in leafblower-i0am.
- Correlation with ieppa: r=0.980 (plain), r=0.958 (squarem). Both acceptable.
Core question resolved. Documentation value minimal — closing.

The user intended ALM (Augmented Lagrangian Method) to replace the hard capacity cap in ieppa_soft. alm_lambda/alm_mu fields in CalibState were designed for this but never wired to the capacity BCD block. description: Empirical finding (2026-04-24): kk1204 (n=1M, K=20, max_weight=3) exhibits PURE SLOW-RATE Sinkhorn convergence. errRp trajectory strictly monotone-decreasing, rate ≈ iter^{-0.5} asymptotic. No oscillation. Fixed-point accelerators explored and rejected: APVA (P2.2c), Joint Anderson (P2.2b), Halpern mixing (P2.2d). UPDATE 2026-04-28: raking+SQUAREM with geometry fix (obs-level CBB norms) achieves stepstone fulldata 1.46e-3 max_err in 1.6s (19x faster than autumn 30.8s). However kk1204 is a fundamentally different problem — K=20 dense with M_cell/n=1.0 gives zero iEPPA compression; ieppa 22x slower than raking per-iter. kk1204 slow-rate is still unresolved for iEPPA-class solvers. Open research: Newton on constraint duals, Chambolle-Pock primal-dual, or mirror descent with entropic regularization (per memory fixed-point-accelerators-apva-anderson-joint-anderson-on).
acceptance_criteria: Decision: either ship P2.1-state as kk1204's practical answer OR commit to one algorithmic replacement pathway. Not an implementation ticket — research first.
notes: Epic-J spike verdict FAIL (2026-05-02): docs/investigations/2026-05-02-ylsy-cp-ipm-spike-result.md. CP kk1204=0.308, IPM kk1204=0.483, ieppa+sraa=0.0501 (best), newton_kl=0.0624. R3 RULED_OUT (max/min=9.64x). Side-finding: CP outperforms ieppa+sraa on stepstone (5.08e-5 vs 4.4e-4, 2.2x better) — Epic-K candidate scope-deferred.
close_reason: BLOCKED: kk1204 near-infeasible fixture — not an algorithm gap. DEFF=8000-14000, n_eff=71-118 on ALL solvers (ieppa/newton_kl/auto). The 'slow-rate Sinkhorn' was solver behavior on an ill-conditioned problem, not a convergence ceiling that better algorithms can break. Investigation report: docs/investigations/2026-05-02-ylsy-cp-ipm-spike-result.md. Epic-J conclusion (CP/IPM FAIL on kk1204) was correct but the root cause analysis was incomplete — kk1204 calibration itself is degenerate. title: WU-3 iEPPA adaptive damping auto-triggered on persistence stress
description:
Geometric-blend damping in src/ieppa.cpp: lf_new = alpha*(log_target - log_S_kj) + (1-alpha)*lf_old. Default alpha=1.0 via explicit if-branch (std::pow(_, 1.0) is NOT a no-op — full transcendental cost). Auto-engages alpha=0.5 when infeas_streak[idx] >= kInfeasPersistence/2; latched per-solve.

Env var LBW_IEPPA_FORCE_DAMPING={on,off,unset} for tests (mandatory for falsifiable iter_damped > iter_stable assertion per spec §7 / CTO B5). Step 3.6.5 patches WU-2 fallback blocks to also reset alpha/damped_latched (spec §5 state-clean checklist).

title: WU-R3.3-defer: log_prod_all Gauss-Seidel vs Jacobi convergence study
