title: CR-H-MV: replace global -mavx2 with function multiversioning (portability + future-CRAN-NOTE)
description:
# CR-H-MV: replace global -mavx2 with function multiversioning (target_clones) — portability + future-CRAN-NOTE
**Status:** READY_FOR_EXECUTION (investigation-first)

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In scope: investigate + (if viable) replace the global `-mavx2` build flag with GCC/Clang function multiversioning (`__attribute__((target_clones("avx2","default")))` or `target("avx2")` + runtime CPUID dispatch) on the AVX2 hot kernels only, so the shipped object is (a) portable — runs on non-AVX2 CPUs via a scalar fallback selected at runtime, and (b) does not carry a global `-m` flag in PKG_CXXFLAGS. Out of scope: changing the AVX2 kernel MATH; the glibc libmvec (`_ZGVdN4v_exp`) linkage decision; any non-AVX2 build path.
* **Why:** Two coupled concerns recorded as a deliberately-unfiled speculative forward-note on closed uj6x.5. (1) PORTABILITY (the real latent hazard): `-mavx2` is applied to the whole TU and `LBW_HAS_GLIBC_MVEC` is feature-tested at BUILD time on the build machine — so a binary compiled on an AVX2 host and run on a non-AVX2 CPU executes `_mm256_*` intrinsics and SIGILLs; there is no runtime dispatch. (2) CRAN HYGIENE: uj6x.5 hides `-mavx2` from `tools:::.check_make_vars` via the opaque `@MAVX2_FLAG@` placeholder (the check greps Makevars.in paths[1L] only); a future R that also checks the generated Makevars would NOTE it. Function multiversioning removes the global `-m` (per-function `target` attributes need no command-line `-mavx2`) AND adds the missing runtime dispatch, resolving both at once — true SOTA vs the current build-time-only gate.
* **Reference Data:** configure:67-88 (feature-tests `-mavx2`, sets MAVX2_FLAG + LBW_HAS_GLIBC_MVEC at build time); src/Makevars.in:1-15 (`@MAVX2_FLAG@` in PKG_CXXFLAGS); python/CMakeLists.txt:37-96 (same gate; `-mavx2 -lm -lmvec`, x86_64 only); AVX2 code = `bulk_scaled_exp`/`_mm256_*` in src/lbw_math.hpp, called from oris.cpp/sinkhorn.cpp/chebyshev.cpp, preprocessor-gated on LBW_HAS_GLIBC_MVEC. Confidence 70 (investigation — libmvec `_ZGVdN4v_exp` symbol availability under per-function `target` without global `-mavx2` must be empirically confirmed; the vectorized-exp call may still need the flag or an explicit ifunc). P4 backlog.
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** configure (:60-105), src/Makevars.in, python/CMakeLists.txt, src/lbw_math.hpp (bulk_scaled_exp AVX2 path), the three caller TUs.
* **Format:** Investigation writeup first (docs/investigations/), then C++/build edits only if the approach is proven portable + perf-neutral. R CMD INSTALL --preclean . + Python CMake rebuild both required if code changes land.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | Runtime dispatch MUST fall back to a correct scalar/default path on non-AVX2 CPUs — verify by building WITHOUT -mavx2 and confirming both a non-AVX2 execution path exists and the AVX2 path is still selected on capable hardware. Perf MUST stay neutral on the AVX2 hot loops (stepstone: max|dw| within existing tolerance, iteration counts unchanged) — cross-TU multiversioning can defeat inlining of bulk_scaled_exp into its per-iteration callers; measure before/after. The libmvec vectorized-exp (`_ZGVdN4v_exp`) linkage under per-function target attributes must be confirmed to still resolve, else keep the flag for that symbol only. |
| **Boundary** | Touch only the AVX2 flag delivery (configure/Makevars.in/CMakeLists.txt) and the AVX2 kernel function attributes in lbw_math.hpp. Do not change kernel math, solver logic, or the non-AVX2 fallback numerics. |
| **Tone** | Tech, terse. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. Confirm the exact portability failure: build with -mavx2 on an AVX2 host, inspect whether the shipped .so has an unconditional AVX2 codepath reachable on a non-AVX2 CPU (objdump / gate analysis). Document the SIGILL surface.
2. Prototype `target_clones("avx2","default")` (or `target("avx2")` + `__builtin_cpu_supports`) on bulk_scaled_exp; build WITHOUT global -mavx2; confirm it compiles, links (incl. libmvec exp), and produces a default path.
3. Bench stepstone (oris/sinkhorn/chebyshev) before/after: assert max|dw| within tolerance + iteration counts unchanged (guard against lost inlining).
4. If portable + perf-neutral: drop @MAVX2_FLAG@ from PKG_CXXFLAGS (configure/Makevars.in) and the -mavx2 from CMakeLists; keep only where a specific symbol still needs it. If NOT viable, write the investigation note documenting why and close as won't-fix with evidence.
5. Full R + Python gates; stepstone no-regression.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: CR-H-MV
success: bool
data:
  files_changed: [list]
  tests_run: [commands + results]
  bench: [stepstone before/after max|dw|, iters]
  verification: [proof]
  error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Investigation writeup: is per-function multiversioning portable + perf-neutral here? (yes/no + evidence)
- [ ] If YES: global -mavx2 removed from PKG_CXXFLAGS + CMake; runtime dispatch selects AVX2 on capable CPUs and a correct default path elsewhere; R+Python gates 0 FAIL; stepstone no-regression
- [ ] If NO: won't-fix with documented reason (e.g. libmvec symbol needs the flag / inlining loss); the current placeholder approach stays and the portability caveat is documented
- [ ] Closes both the future-CRAN-NOTE risk and the non-AVX2 SIGILL portability hazard, or documents why not
close_reason: Investigation complete (docs/investigations/2026-07-04-xc1s16-avx2-multiversioning.md, commit fcadcbe). Drafted target_clones-on-leaf approach is NON-VIABLE: bulk_scaled_exp/bulk_log/bulk_exp_clipped are inline hot kernels (lbw_math.hpp) called per-iteration from oris/sinkhorn/chebyshev; target_clones defeats inlining (indirect IFUNC call) = hot-path regression. Severity LOW: R source-install runs the configure -mavx2 feature-test on the target machine => no SIGILL on non-AVX2 CPUs for the standard model; CRAN-NOTE is hypothetical (placeholder already clean). Viable alternatives (outer-function FMV, dedicated dispatched TU) are architectural + warrant own bench campaign — disproportionate to P4. Recommendation: keep the build-time gate, defer. Closed won't-fix-as-drafted per ticket step 4.

comments.author: Dennis Alexis Valin Dittrich
comments.text: VERIFY: PARTIAL. CRAN-NOTE is LATENT not current (@MAVX2_FLAG@ placeholder evades tools:::.check_make_vars on Makevars.in). SIGILL only for BINARY dist (source installs feature-test on run host). SOTA GAP: target_clones on leaf kernel bulk_scaled_exp (lbw_math.hpp:17 inline, per-iter sinkhorn.cpp:218/oris.cpp:1415) breaks inlining => ifunc indirect call on hot path (violates no-cross-TU-inline rule) = REGRESSION. Better: object-scoped flag on a dedicated AVX2 TU, or FMV at the OUTER loop. Keep P4 investigation-first.

title: CR-H2b: logit post-step recompute is NOT redundant (FMA/ULP) — do not reuse w_trial
description:
# CR-H2b: logit post-step recompute — reuse rejected

## I. Context & Objective
**Objective (In):** DOCUMENT (not fix) why the logit post-step w+D_eff recompute cannot be eliminated by reusing the accepted Armijo trial. (Out): any code change — this is a won't-fix guard-rail ticket.
**Why:** xc1s.2 folded the triplicated sigmoid z-accumulation (bit-identical, shipped). The ticket ALSO proposed eliminating the post-step recompute on the armijo_improved path by reusing w_trial + a retained sig_trial. IMPLEMENTED AND REVERTED: it is NOT bit-identical.

## II. Input Specification
**Input:** src/logit_calib.cpp Newton loop — accepted-step update 'lambda[j] += alpha*b[j]' vs Armijo trial 'lambda_trial[j] = lambda[j] + alpha*b[j]'.

## III. Finding (evidence)
- Assumption was: on armijo_improved, lambda(post) == lambda_trial bit-for-bit (same alpha, same b, same lambda), so w==w_trial and sig==sig_trial ⇒ reuse is bit-identical.
- REALITY: 'a += x*y' (compound, may FMA to one rounding) differs from 'a + x*y' (separate mul+add, two roundings) by ~1 ULP under -ffp-contract/FMA and reassociation. So lambda(post) != lambda_trial by ~1 ULP ⇒ z, sig, D_eff differ ⇒ trajectory perturbed.
- MEASURED: normal fixture max_error 1.00273370643815e-08 -> 1.00273370170119e-08 (~5e-8 relative); collinear (eb79.18 redundant-margin) 9.55252588141775e-09 -> 9.55252583404824e-09. status/iters unchanged, weights match only to ~13 figs. Converges fine but NOT bit-identical.
- Algebraic sig=(w_trial-L)/range is even worse (catastrophic cancellation).

## IV. Decision
DO NOT reuse w_trial/sig_trial for the logit post-step. Keep the full recompute from the updated lambda. logit is not a bottleneck (eb79.22), so the marginal saved O(M*K) pass does not justify a non-bit-identical change to the delicate collinear Newton path. A comment at the post-step site records this.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: CR-H2b
success: bool
data:
  decision: wont-fix
  reason: fma-ulp-non-bit-identical
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Documented (this ticket + the in-code comment at the post-step). No code change. Close as won't-fix.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by xc1s.2 commit db93c3f. This ticket's premise (reuse must be bit-identical, therefore reject) was the WRONG bar — mathematical correctness + self-consistency is sufficient. (B) is now implemented by adopting the accepted Armijo trial state wholesale (self-consistent lambda_trial/w_trial/sig_trial triple). The ~1 ULP/5e-8 FMA-contraction difference is not a regression. No guard-rail needed.

comments.author: Dennis Alexis Valin Dittrich
comments.text: PRINCIPLE NOTE (per user directive): bit-identity is NOT required if a change is mathematically correct. This ticket wrongly used 'not bit-identical' as a rejection reason for the logit trial-state reuse. Correct bar = mathematical correctness + self-consistency + no convergence regression. The reuse was subsequently implemented correctly (adopt lambda_trial/w_trial/sig_trial wholesale) in xc1s.2 commit db93c3f. Recorded repo-wide as memory 'acceptance-bar-mathematical-correctness-not-bit-identical'.

title: [DEFER] r_bridge estimate_M_cell computed twice on AUTO path
description:
# leafblower-eb79.14 + eb79.15: r_bridge perf micro-opts (best_weights memcpy + estimate_M_cell lazy cache)
**Status:** `READY_FOR_EXECUTION`
**Mechanism:** WU-A (eb79.14): replace scalar-loop fill of the best_weights REALSXP with std::memcpy. WU-B (eb79.15): lazy-cache estimate_M_cell (sentinel) so the AUTO+auto-capacity path computes it once, not twice — WITHOUT hoisting past site A's length-validity guard. Single file (r_bridge.cpp). Both output-preserving.
**Forbidden:** hoisting estimate_M_cell UNCONDITIONALLY above site A's CXX.1 length-validity guard (estimate_M_cell OOB-reads on malformed input); any change to computed VALUES (byte-identical output required); touching solver cores; eb79.13 (WONTFIX — profiled, design intent stands).
**Audit:** best_weights byte-identical after memcpy; estimate_M_cell computed once on the both-run path, identical value at both sites; full R suite green + R/Python parity unchanged.

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** In: two redundant/suboptimal r_bridge code fragments. Out: (A) best_weights REALSXP filled by memcpy (matches the nearby weights memcpy at r_bridge.cpp:881); (B) estimate_M_cell (O(n·K)) computed ONCE instead of twice on the AUTO-routing + auto-capacity_mu path. Zero behavior/value change.
* **Why:** Two deferred P4 micro-opts from the 2026-07-02 review. Low-risk cleanup; consistency + one avoided O(n·K) scan.
* **Reference Data (verified 2026-07-02, post-eb79.25 line numbers):**
  - WU-A (eb79.14): r_bridge.cpp:958-961 — `int bw_n = res_best_weights.size(); SEXP bw_sxp=allocVector(REALSXP,bw_n); double* bw=REAL(bw_sxp); for(i) bw[i]=res_best_weights[i];`. REAL(REALSXP) is a contiguous double[]; res_best_weights is std::vector<double> (contiguous). ⇒ `std::memcpy(bw, res_best_weights.data(), (size_t)bw_n*sizeof(double))` is safe + equivalent. Guard: only when bw_n>0 (memcpy of 0 bytes is fine, but keep the existing structure).
  - WU-B (eb79.15): estimate_M_cell called at r_bridge.cpp:401 (site A, inside the capacity_penalty<=0 auto-capacity_mu block, GUARDED by the CXX.1 length-validity skip — comment at :397-400: "filling with malformed input would OOB-read") and r_bridge.cpp:531 (site B, AUTO routing, method=="auto"). BOTH call `estimate_M_cell(n, K, const_cast<const int32_t**>(group_ids.data()), cat_counts.data())` — IDENTICAL args. On a call that is method="auto" AND capacity_penalty<=0, both run ⇒ redundant O(n·K).
  - CANNOT hoist unconditionally (site A's guard prevents OOB on malformed input). SAFE fix = lazy cache: `int m_cell_est_cache = -1;` before both; site A computes as now then stores to the cache; site B: `if (m_cell_est_cache < 0) m_cell_est_cache = estimate_M_cell(...); int M_cell_est = m_cell_est_cache;` — reuses A's value when A ran (both-run path), else computes under B's own conditions. Each site keeps its existing guard; only the second redundant compute is skipped. Value byte-identical.
  - eb79.13 = WONTFIX (profiled: sub-second per-iter at realistic n_lam; dsyevd O(n_lam^3) multi-second only at the pathological n_lam=4096 cap; WL-1 design intent stands).
* **Philosophy:** Sub-agent = Goldfish Memory. All info here.

## II. Input Specification
* **Expected Input:** r_bridge.cpp locals: res_best_weights (std::vector<double>), the estimate_M_cell call sites + group_ids/cat_counts/n/K in scope at both.
* **Format:** C++; no ABI change; no public API change.

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Logic** | WU-A: `if (bw_n > 0) std::memcpy(bw, res_best_weights.data(), (size_t)bw_n * sizeof(double));` (or unconditional memcpy — 0-length is a no-op). `<cstring>` is already included (r_bridge.cpp:9). WU-B: sentinel `int m_cell_est_cache = -1;` declared BEFORE site A; site A stores its computed M_cell_est into the cache AND st.alm.capacity_mu (as now); site B: reuse cache if >=0, else compute + store. Do NOT move estimate_M_cell out of either guarded region. |
| **Format** | Two localized edits in r_bridge.cpp. No new TU. |
| **Boundary** | src/r_bridge.cpp only. No solver-core / Python / test-fixture change (both are output-preserving ⇒ existing tests are the regression net). |
| **Tone** | Match file style; cite eb79.14/eb79.15. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
1. **WU-A (eb79.14):** replace the scalar for-loop (r_bridge.cpp:961) with memcpy per Guards.
2. **WU-B (eb79.15):** add the sentinel cache; site A stores; site B reuses-or-computes per Guards. Confirm identical args at both sites (already verified).
3. **VALIDATE (all 3 estimate_M_cell path combinations — byte-identical vs committed HEAD):** (i) BOTH-RUN: method="auto" + capacity_penalty auto/NULL (A computes, B reuses cache); (ii) B-ONLY: method="auto" + explicit capacity_penalty>0 (site A branch skipped ⇒ sentinel stays -1 ⇒ site B must fall through to a FRESH compute — the silent-regression-risk path); (iii) A-ONLY: method≠"auto" (e.g. "oris") + capacity_penalty auto (B never runs — cache unused, trivially unchanged). Save weights+result from HEAD for each, diff after the change (byte-identical). R CMD INSTALL --preclean; full R suite green; pytest green.
4. Check Guards.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: leafblower-eb79.14+15
success: bool
data:
  bw_memcpy_applied: bool
  mcell_computed_once_on_both_run_path: bool
  output_byte_identical: bool
  r_tests: "PASS n/0"
  py_tests: "PASS n/0"
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] WU-A: best_weights REALSXP filled by memcpy (0-length safe); byte-identical to the scalar fill.
- [ ] WU-B: estimate_M_cell computed ONCE on the method=auto + capacity_penalty<=0 path (sentinel cache); site A's CXX.1 length-validity guard preserved (NOT hoisted); identical M_cell_est value at both sites.
- [ ] Output byte-identical (weights + result) on ALL 3 path combinations: both-run (auto + auto-capacity), B-only (auto + capacity_penalty>0 ⇒ sentinel falls through to fresh compute at site B), A-only (non-auto + auto-capacity). full R suite green; pytest green.
- [ ] Only src/r_bridge.cpp changed; pathspec-form commit, no .beads leak. eb79.13 closed WONTFIX with profiling evidence (separate).
close_reason: Done (commit b14456d, 4-phase loop; plan gate-approved 3/3 iter2 + agy SOUND). estimate_M_cell lazy sentinel cache (m_cell_est_cache=-1): site A stores, site B reuses-else-computes-fresh; site A's CXX.1 OOB guard NOT hoisted. Byte-identical across all 3 path combos (both-run/B-only/A-only) + oris_soft — verified vs HEAD. R fail=0/err=0, pytest 34/0, adversarial PASS.

close_reason: WONTFIX (profiled 2026-07-02, per the ticket's own guard 'design intent stands unless profiling proves the cost is real'). newton_kl per-iter cost at realistic n_lam is sub-second and NOT dsyevd-bound — the O(n*K) Hessian build over large n dominates (measured single-thread: n_lam~100=0.031s/iter, ~300=0.124, ~600=0.189, ~1000=0.173). dsyevd O(n_lam^3) is a few ms at n_lam<=1000 (negligible). The unconditional dsyevd (WL-1 numerical-robustness design) stands; a conditioning-probe/LDLT-fallback gate for the extreme n_lam->4096 edge remains available as opt-in IF a real 4096-cat workload ever emerges.

title: SPECULATIVE: micro-bench bulk_logsumexp kernel for ieppa LSE [ya85 follow-up]
description:
# SPECULATIVE: bulk_logsumexp kernel for ieppa LSE accumulate — measure-first

**Status:** `SPECULATIVE — Phase-0 ceiling gate first; expected outcome NO-GO.`

## I. Context & Objective
* **Objective:** Decide whether vectorizing the log-sum-exp accumulate at `src/ieppa.cpp:653-655` (via a new header-inline `lbw::bulk_logsumexp`) reduces END-TO-END ieppa solve wall-clock beyond noise; author + wire the kernel ONLY if a cheap ceiling check first shows it could plausibly clear the GO threshold, and keep it ONLY if the end-to-end bench proves it AND behavior holds.
* **Why:** yxcg (parent ya85) profiling: only SIMD-addressable hot fragment is the scalar `exp(lv[r]-lv_max)` accumulate inside `apply_single_margin_log` (lambda#2=14.83% self; scalar `exp` ~5.55% under it). Gather (L638-649) dominates the SAME lambda → Amdahl ceiling: exp ≤ ~0.82% of total solve, so even 4× SIMD ⇒ <1% total. **Expected outcome: NO-GO.** Value = a definitive recorded measurement that forecloses re-proposals.

## II. Input / Evidence (current code, master)
* `src/ieppa.cpp` lambda `apply_single_margin_log` (L623):
  - L636 `lv.assign(cells.size(), -inf)`.
  - **L638-649 GATHER — DO NOT TOUCH** (indirect `c=cells[r]`; non-SIMD-able; dominates).
  - L651 `if (!std::isfinite(lv_max)) { record_empty; continue; }` ⇒ lv_max FINITE below; kernel never called with all-(-inf).
  - **L653-655 LSE ACCUMULATE (target):** `double sum=0; for r { if (std::isfinite(lv[r])) sum += std::exp(lv[r]-lv_max); }`.
  - L656 `log_S_kj = lv_max + std::log(sum);` feeds the iterative SOR `lf` update ⇒ trajectory-sensitive.
* `lv[r]` source (L645-647): `s = log_X_init[c]+log_W[c]+cell_lf[c]; if(gk>=0) s-=lf[...]`. log_X_init/log_W finite (X_init>0,W>0 guarded L640). `cell_lf[c]` and `lf[]` are ACCUMULATED across iterations and NOT a-priori bounded ⇒ `s` can be +inf (overflow) or NaN (inf-inf). The scalar `isfinite(lv[r])` guard at L653 EXISTS precisely to drop such lanes. Any SIMD replacement MUST reproduce this exactly.
* `src/lbw_math.hpp`: kernels are `inline`, libmvec-gated via `LBW_HAS_GLIBC_MVEC` (`src/lbw_config.h:6`), `_ZGVdN4v_exp` declared (lbw_math.hpp:8). `ieppa.cpp:2` already `#include "lbw_math.hpp"`. Header-only ⇒ no CMake/CORE_SOURCES change.
* Bench harness: `benchmarks/newton_kl_bench.R`, `benchmarks/stepstone_compare_current.R` exist. Stepstone baseline max|Δw| must be MEASURED on the unmodified tree (do not assume ~1.2e-12 — confirm it as the reference before choosing the guard).

## III. Constraints & Guards
| Type | Guard |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Phase-0 gate (cheap, first)** | BEFORE authoring the kernel: estimate the accumulate's share of total solve (isolated `bench::mark` of the scalar L653-655 over representative `cells.size()`, vs a full-solve timing; or `perf` re-confirmation). If the accumulate is < 1.5% of total solve (cannot reach the 3% GO threshold even at 4× SIMD), CLOSE wont-fix with the recorded number — DO NOT write/wire the kernel. Proceed to Phase 1 ONLY if the ceiling plausibly clears 3%. |
| **Non-finite masking (correctness)** | The kernel MUST mask every NON-FINITE `lv[i]` lane to a 0 contribution — i.e. replicate the scalar `isfinite(lv[r])` guard, covering -inf, +inf, AND NaN. Compute exp on finite lanes, force non-finite lanes' contribution to 0 (SIMD select on `isfinite(lv[i])`). This makes correctness INDEPENDENT of libmvec's exp(-inf)/exp(+inf)/exp(NaN) behavior. (NOTE: this dissolves the libmvec-(-inf) question — masking handles it regardless. It also adds per-lane work that further lowers any speedup — reinforcing the expected NO-GO.) |
| **Numerical / parity** | Parity (R-vs-Py) is reduction-ORDER-invariant (both call the same .so) ⇒ unaffected. REAL gate = STEPSTONE: log_S_kj feeds the iterative lf update; reduction-order can amplify. Gate = stepstone max|Δw| ≤ 10× the MEASURED unmodified baseline (record baseline first; do not hard-code). If exceeded ⇒ REJECT even if faster. |
| **GO threshold** | Keep ONLY if end-to-end ieppa solve median improves ≥ 3% reproducibly (≥2 runs, CI excludes 0) AND stepstone within gate AND parity unchanged AND R suite green. |
| **Inline / scope** | Kernel header-inline in lbw_math.hpp (libmvec path + scalar fallback). No new .cpp. DO NOT touch the gather (L638-649); no lambda refactor; no fusing the two passes; no unrelated kernels. |

## IV. Step-by-Step Logic
0. **Phase 0 — ceiling check (cheap, gating).** Measure the accumulate's fraction of total solve (per the Phase-0 gate). Record it. If < 1.5% ⇒ write the number to the ticket, set decision=`reject-no-win`, CLOSE; STOP (no kernel). Else continue.
1. Measure & record the UNMODIFIED stepstone baseline (max|Δw|, Pearson r) for the numerical gate.
2. Add `inline double bulk_logsumexp(const double* lv, double lv_max, int n)` to lbw_math.hpp: returns Σ over FINITE lanes of `exp(lv[i]-lv_max)`; non-finite lanes contribute 0 (mask). SIMD path (LBW_HAS_GLIBC_MVEC) + scalar fallback whose result is bit-identical to the current L653-655 loop semantics.
3. **Correctness first:** unit-test the kernel vs the scalar loop on arrays including -inf, +inf, NaN, n∈{0,1,2,3,4,5,8,hundreds}; require match to rtol=1e-12 (and exact handling of non-finite). Gate: must pass before wiring.
4. Wire at L653-655 (replace the scalar accumulate; keep L656). `R CMD INSTALL --preclean .`.
5. END-TO-END bench: interleaved before/after full ieppa solve (newton_kl_bench / stepstone driver pattern; OMP_NUM_THREADS=1), ≥2 reps, median+CI.
6. Numerical: `Rscript benchmarks/stepstone_compare_current.R` (max|Δw| vs the Phase-1 baseline gate); Python parity rtol=1e-6; full R suite.
7. **DECIDE:**
   - **GO** (≥3% AND stepstone within gate AND parity unchanged AND R suite green): keep, commit `perf(ieppa): vectorize LSE accumulate via bulk_logsumexp [tiam]`.
   - **NO-GO** (any condition fails): **REVERT the L653-655 wiring** (`git checkout -- src/ieppa.cpp`), rebuild to confirm clean scalar tree, DELETE the unused kernel from lbw_math.hpp (no dead code) UNLESS separately justified, ensure `git status` clean (no half-applied change), record all numbers, close `reject-no-win`.
8. Record numbers in the ticket REGARDLESS of outcome.

## V. Output Schema (Strict)
```toon
task_id: tiam
success: bool
data:
  phase0_accumulate_fraction: float   # accumulate / total solve
  phase0_gate: proceed | closed-below-ceiling
  kernel_unit_test: pass | fail | n/a
  nonfinite_masking_verified: bool     # -inf,+inf,NaN all → 0 contribution
  stepstone_baseline_max_dw: float
  stepstone_after_max_dw: float | n/a
  end_to_end_speedup: float | n/a
  parity_unchanged: bool | n/a
  decision: implement | reject-no-win
  tree_clean_after: bool               # no half-applied change on NO-GO
error_log: null | msg
```

## VI. Definition of Done
- [ ] Phase-0 ceiling fraction measured + recorded; proceed only if ≥1.5%.
- [ ] (If proceeding) Unmodified stepstone baseline recorded BEFORE changes.
- [ ] (If proceeding) Kernel unit-tested vs scalar to rtol=1e-12 incl. -inf/+inf/NaN/n∈{0,1,small,large}; non-finite masking verified (correctness independent of libmvec exp behavior).
- [ ] (If proceeding) End-to-end ieppa bench (interleaved, ≥2 reps) median+CI recorded.
- [ ] Decision evidence-backed vs GO threshold (≥3% AND stepstone ≤10× baseline AND parity unchanged AND R suite green). Expected: reject.
- [ ] **NO-GO path:** wiring reverted, kernel removed (no dead code), `git status` clean, numbers recorded.
- [ ] **GO path:** stepstone within gate, parity rtol=1e-6 unchanged, full R suite green, kernel header-inline, committed.
- [ ] Numbers recorded in ticket regardless of decision (closes the question definitively).
close_reason: reject-no-win at PHASE 0 (measure-first gate). Independent perf (200k-row x 50-rep realistic harvest, OMP=1): apply_single_margin_log lambda = 0.20% of total solve; scalar exp (ALL callers) = 0.11%; the L653-655 accumulate is a sub-fraction <=0.11% — 13x below the 1.5% gate. Even 4x SIMD => <=0.03% end-to-end (noise). Corroborates yxcg (5.55% self in synthetic fixture; smaller on realistic workload where build_cell_table/STRING_ELT/R-overhead dominate). NO kernel written, ieppa.cpp untouched, tree clean. Verified by orchestrator: no bulk_logsumexp in src/, L653-655 unchanged, Makevars clean, 0 commits. Question definitively closed: ieppa LSE accumulate is NOT a worthwhile SIMD target.

title: feat(harvest): two-stage hierarchical calibration — coarse then fine margins with cell-n threshold
description: P5 (low priority): Two-stage hierarchical raking. Stage 1: calibrate to coarse_margins (user-specified subset of K margins). Stage 2: within each coarse cell, calibrate to remaining fine margins only where n_per_cell >= n_min (default 30); sparse cells inherit Stage 1 weights. Handles high-dimensional interaction sparseness (e.g., K=9 where cross-product cells inevitably have n<5). How autumn/anesrake works in practice. Cost: two solver passes, user must specify coarse/fine split, potential Stage-2 disturbance of Stage-1 margins. Defer until P1+P2+auto_collapse cover 80% of cases.
close_reason: ABANDONED 2026-05-07. Feature implemented (epic .1, 12 tickets, 0.2.0/0.2.1) then reverted to baseline 2464a51 after empirical evaluation showed net-zero/negative payoff at production scale (1S/2S median ratio K=6 N=2000: raking 0.76x, sinkhorn 0.24x, greenkhorn 0.73x — all WORSE). Ghosal-Nutz 2022 (arxiv:2212.06000, Math OR forthcoming): unconstrained Sinkhorn rate H(pi_t|pi*)+H(pi*|pi_t)=O(t^-1), dual O(t^-1), marginal entropies O(t^-2). Compare to iEPPA kk1204 empirical errRp~iter^-0.5 trajectory: the capacity clamp is costing one full rate order (from O(t^-1) smooth-operator to O(t^-1/2) piecewise-linear). This quantifies the slow-rate penalty; any iEPPA-preserving fix that restores O(t^-1) would mean proportional wall-time savings.

kk1204 K=20 calibration problem is near-infeasible by construction (K=20 dense margins, target_skew=20, max_weight=3): DEFF=8000-14000 and n_eff=71-118 on ALL solvers (ieppa/newton_kl/auto). This is a fixture pathology, not a solver gap. Use DEFF and n_eff to classify feasibility before selecting algorithms or benchmarking solver quality.

ieppa.cpp BUDGET/STALL reclassification block (inserted after homotopy loop end) MUST come AFTER the INFEAS promotion guard that checks res.status == RK_ERR_NOCONV. If inserted before: infeasible problems exit with BUDGET(4) instead of INFEAS(2), harvest() warns instead of stop(). Fix: extend INFEAS guard to also match BUDGET and STALL. Discovered 2026-04-28 during C2 fix implementation.

jy0m.1 SOTA fix (CORRECTED via agy cross-review + verification; supersedes jy0m1-absolute-bar-evidence 'document the limitation' which was a FALSE-DICHOTOMY error). The genuine SOTA is a per-margin BOX-FEASIBILITY CERTIFICATE at the raking gate: margin (k,j) is provably infeasible iff T_kj*n outside [Sum L_cell, Sum U_cell] over cells_per_cat[k][j] — equivalently T_kj/S_kj outside [min_weight, max_weight] (since L_cell=min_w*X_init, U_cell=max_w*X_init, w_init=1 => SumL=min_w*n_kj, SumU=max_w*n_kj, S_kj=n_kj/n). RIGOROUS necessary condition, ZERO threshold (no fitted magic number), reuses L_cell/U_cell/cells_per_cat already built at raking.cpp:65-75, O(M_cell) once. VERIFIED (R probe): corner (rare r emp 0.014, tgt 0.005, min_w 0.7 => ratio 0.337<0.7) FIRES; FEASIBLE stepstone_small @ default bounds(0,Inf) 0/793 silent (this is the 54.5%-rel-miss case the RELATIVE bar false-fired on — box-cert ignores inter-margin IPF tension because every margin is individually box-feasible at loose bounds); @ tight(0.7,2) 95/793 fire = genuinely box-infeasible (correct, NOT false positive). Superior to BOTH the absolute 1pp bar (misses the corner) AND the relative bar (false-STALLs feasible 54.5%). RESPONSE (my refinement over agy's 'add INFEAS precheck'): a box-infeasible margin DENIES RK_OK (even if errRp<=1pp) => falls through to STALL(5) (constrained optimum, weights VALID = best achievable 0.0098) — NOT hard INFEAS(2)/harvest stop() (too aggressive; best-effort weights usable), NOT 'document'. Matches budget_vs_stall_status_codes semantics + current tight-stepstone STALL behavior. Necessary-not-sufficient (misses JOINT infeasibility) but strict superset improvement. Analogous to oris preentry sum_U (oris.cpp:186-193) which raking LACKS. jy0m.1 re-planned from doc-only to: box-cert guard in the raking feasibility gate (raking.cpp:559 + SRAA :444), deny RK_OK on box-infeasible margin. Also applies to the SRAA path (jy0m.2 STALL emitter). Do NOT re-adopt the 'document the limitation' outcome.

Cell-level norms vs obs-level norms: in leafblower cell-table code, Σ_c r_c² ≠ Σ_i r_i² when n_per_cell[c] varies. Equivalence requires 1/n_c weighting: Σ_c r_c²/n_c = Σ_i r_i². R vectorization byte-identity gotcha (xc1s.13f/g, opus-caught 2026-07-04): rowsum()'s C kernel (do_rowsum in array.c) accumulates group totals in PLAIN double, while base sum() uses LONG DOUBLE (extended precision). So replacing a per-level sum(weights[mask]) loop with rowsum(weights, group) is NOT byte-identical — it diverges at ~1 ULP for any level with 3+ obs and non-dyadic weights (proven: 2000 real weights, old 6547.5614013784488634 vs rowsum 6547.5614013784479539). It is ALSO a precision REGRESSION (double < long double), against the project no-cancellations mandate. CORRECT vectorization that stays byte-identical AND O(n): tapply(x, factor(group, levels=lvls), sum) — split()+base sum() per group preserves both row order AND long-double accumulation. tabulate(match()) is fine for INTEGER counts (exact, no FP). Byte-identity harness MUST include a large-n non-dyadic-weight fixture (3+ obs/level); small/integer-weight fixtures round identically under double and long-double and give a false identical()=TRUE. Applies to weighted_pct.R, diagnose_weights.R, current_miss.R.

eb79.18 FIXED (commit 2b7d083). logit collinear STALL root cause: warm-start solved (AA^T)λ0=A·z_target via ridge-Cholesky (logit_calib.cpp), ACCEPTED-but-BIASED (max|λ0|=2.303=|z_target|, NOT rejected) — put ~z_target on each redundant dual so z_c=Σ over R redundant margins=R·z_target -> σ→0 -> every cell at L by iter0 -> D_eff floor (kDeffFloor=1e-6) -> non-descent Newton -> Armijo exhausts (α=1.63e-4) -> STALL at min_weight. Result: consistent collinear status=0/Σw=n/iter-1; inconsistent STALL; heterogeneous converges. NOTE harder tight-bounds+skewed collinear still BUDGET at 50-Newton-iter cap (kMaxNewtonIters) = SEPARATE main-loop speed limit, filed eb79.22 (contingent LM port). logit convergence_solver_objective (eb79.20, commit b1d3f16) = Σ_c D_L(w_best[c]) where D_L(w)=range·[p·log p+(1−p)·log(1−p)+log2], p=(w−L)/range = range·(log2−H(p)) ∈[0,range·log2]. Reference is the MIDPOINT (not X_init/design): the forward map w=L+range·σ(z), z=Σλ (logit_calib.cpp:300-306) has NO z_target offset inside the sigmoid, so σ(0)=½⇒w=midpoint; lambda_0=z_target is warm-start only. Gradient D_L'(w)=log((w−L)/(U−w))=z matches stationarity exactly. Do NOT switch to design-referenced Deville-Särndal G_L: agy verified (conf 88) per-cell z_target ∉ row(A) + code uses least-squares seed solve ⇒ fixed point is midpoint-referenced. select_solver_objective (calib_dispatch.hpp:175) covers only GREG/CHEBYSHEV, returns NaN for logit — computed inline. l1_weight_change=Σ_i|w_out−w_in|/n (obs-level).

Tang 2024 (arxiv:2403.05054) Theorem 1 K-counting: K indexes INEQUALITY constraints, NOT problem dimensions. For iEPPA box-constraints L ≤ X[c] ≤ U, K_ineq = 2·M_cell (two per cell: upper and lower bounds), not K=20 margin count. Misreading inflates error bound 8·n^(2/(K+1))·(K+1)·exp(-η·Δ/(K+1)) to vacuously large — at 2·M_cell=2e6, exp(-47·Δ) becomes exp(-2.4e-5·Δ·η). Paper's K=O(1) assumption doesn't transfer to box-constraint case.

ACCEPTANCE BAR for solver/numeric refactors: the requirement is MATHEMATICAL CORRECTNESS + SELF-CONSISTENCY + NO CONVERGENCE REGRESSION — NOT bit-identity. Bit-identity is a convenient (strong) verification when available, but a change that is provably a valid evaluation of the SAME mathematical quantity is acceptable even if it differs by FP rounding (~1 ULP / context-dependent FMA contraction / reassociation), as long as it does not regress convergence (status, iteration count, and final error stay within tolerance) and the produced state is self-consistent. Do NOT reject or scope out a mathematically-correct optimization solely because it is not bit-identical. Example (xc1s.2, commit db93c3f): adopting the accepted Armijo trial state (lambda=lambda_trial, w=w_trial, D_eff from sig_trial) in logit_calib.cpp is self-consistent and correct; the ~5e-8 max_error shift vs the recompute form is FMA contraction of the same lambda+alpha*b at two sites — shipped. Counter-anti-pattern: xc1s.2 was FIRST wrongly rejected on a bit-identity bar (filed as won't-fix CR-H2b), then corrected. Note: xc1s.4 (raking W=n vs W=SigmaX, ~1e-13) was correctly SHIPPED under this bar. Verification protocol for non-bit-identical changes: (1) prove same math quantity + self-consistency; (2) full R+Python suites green (fixtures assert tolerances); (3) targeted before/after on sensitive fixtures (e.g. eb79.18 collinear logit) showing status/iters unchanged + error below tol; (4) fresh adversarial review with the mathematical-correctness bar stated explicitly.

ieppa.cpp ALM linearized Newton step X = X_tilde*(1-lambda+mu*z)/(1+rho), rho=mu*X_tilde is CORRECT — do NOT add a -rho term. iEPPA's Bregman generator is the UN-normalized KL / I-divergence D=X*log(X/X_tilde)-X+X_tilde, so dD/dX=log(X/X_tilde) (NOT log+1). Linearizing log~=X/X_tilde-1 in stationarity log(X/X_tilde)+lambda+mu(X-z)=0 gives exactly the code. leafblower-7emq (conf 50, SUSPECTED) proposed -rho citing the design spec, but its derivation used the NORMALIZED KL (gradient log+1) which is the wrong generator. 2-cell scipy-style sim: both forms share fixed point X=clamp(X_tilde,L,U) and convergence rate is a wash. Guard comment added at the step (commit 7c62d50). Closed not-a-bug. Pattern repeat of xiox: formula-bug tickets need first-principles re-derivation + numerical validation; reviewer derivations can use the wrong premise.

lf_correction cycling is mathematically impossible. T1.B fires only when total_X > capacity, forcing shift = log(total_X/capacity) > 0, so lf_correction = -shift/K < 0 always. Sign reversal required for cycling cannot occur by the firing predicate itself. Empirically confirmed: 1602 T1B fires, 0 cycling triplets on stepstone K=9.

chebyshev.cpp Phase-B corrector corr = y*dS_aff + y*dS_aff^2/s is CORRECT and complete — do NOT drop the linear y*dS_aff term. It is the -y part of the full affine dual step dY_aff = -y - y*dS_aff/s, so corr = -dS_aff*dY_aff expands to both terms. corr_hi carries a NEGATIVE linear term because dS_hi=-dX. leafblower-xiox (conf 60) proposed dropping it citing N-W 19.55 but its derivation approximated dY_aff ~ -y*dS/s, dropping the -y. Verified vs CLARABEL LP reference: solver hits Chebyshev optimum to ~1e-11 on converged problems; removing the term does NOT fix the K>=9 stall (that is a separate conditioning/iter-cap issue, see file header L19-21). Guard comment added at the corrector (commit 9e2e913). Closed xiox as not-a-bug.

cholesky_factor_inplace in calib_linalg.cpp applies Gill-Murray-Wright diagonal perturbation (eps_perturb=1e-12) before dpotrf, so it NEVER returns non-RK_OK on near-singular matrices. Tests asserting warnings or errors on collinear dummy matrices will always fail.
